equipment.name: Digestion liquor pumps
equipment.function: Pump strong spent liquor through the liquor heater train into the digesters.
equipment.type_selected: Single-stage high-head centrifugal process pump, between-bearings radially split (API 610 BB2) or heavy overhung OH2, double mechanical seal with quench (API 682 Plan 53/62), VFD.
equipment.why_this_type: Clean but hot caustic liquor at ~700 m3/h and ~120 m head - within one high-head stage at 1,480 rpm; API-style construction for reliability at temperature.
equipment.alternatives: Two pumps in series; multistage BB3 pump.
key_dimensions: Impeller ~600-650 mm dia at 1,480 rpm - engineering estimate
Suction DN 300-350, discharge DN 250-300 - engineering estimate
Pump + motor skid ~5 m x 2 m - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (digester 6 barg + 8 heaters x ~0.5-0.8 bar + static)

equipment.working_principle: A centrifugal impeller adds energy to the liquor; at constant speed the flow-head curve is set by the impeller diameter. The VFD speed is trimmed to deliver the liquor flow demanded by the charge-ratio controller (liquor:bauxite) while overcoming the rising pressure drop of the heaters as they scale. Discharge pressure trends upward between descaling cycles, a useful scaling indicator.
details_to_model: Horizontal pump with centreline-mounted casing on baseplate, bearing housings both ends (BB2), flexible spacer coupling with guard, large motor
Suction strainer (temporary), isolation gate valve, discharge check valve + gate valve, minimum-flow recirculation line back to tank with control valve
Seal support system: Plan 53 pressurised barrier reservoir with level/ pressure switches or quench with steam/ water
Pressure gauges, vibration probes, bearing RTDs
Drip pan to bund
equipment.materials: Carbon steel casing (caustic SCC: PWHT of welds), 12Cr/ duplex impeller and wear rings, 4140 shaft; seal faces SiC/ SiC.
equipment.drive_and_power: 400-550 kW MV motor (6.6 kV) with VFD (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Vibration/ bearing temperature; seal barrier alarms
Auto-start of standby on trip; low-flow protection
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic at 12-16 barg - spray from seal/ flange failure; flange spray guards
High-voltage motor
common_problems: Mechanical seal failure from caustic crystallisation
Cavitation if tank level low and liquor near boiling
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep minimum flow; watch seal-pot levels each shift
sources: API 610 Centrifugal Pumps for Petroleum, Petrochemical and Natural Gas Industries

equipment.name: Digestion slurry charge (booster) pumps
equipment.function: Supply desilicated slurry at positive pressure (~2-4 barg) to the suction of the piston-diaphragm pumps so that the hot (~100 degC, near boiling) slurry does not flash/cavitate in the PD pump suction valves.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal slurry pump, hard-metal (27 % Cr white iron), VFD.
equipment.why_this_type: PD pumps need a pressurised, steady suction; slurry at ~100 degC has little NPSH margin (BPE ~5-7 K, so it boils at ~105-107 degC at atmosphere).
equipment.alternatives: Elevated suction tank giving static head only (often insufficient).
key_dimensions: Discharge ~DN 200 - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate / PD-pump vendor NPSH requirement

equipment.working_principle: A centrifugal slurry pump with thick hard-metal liners pressurises the slurry into a short header feeding the PD pump suction manifold, keeping the slurry well above its vapour pressure inside the suction valves even during the suction stroke acceleration.
details_to_model: Pump at grade beside PD pump, suction from desil tank 3/6 discharge header with knife-gate valves, discharge to PD suction stabiliser
Flush/ drain connections; PI with diaphragm seal
equipment.materials: High-chrome white iron wet end.
instrumentation_and_control: PIC on PD-pump suction pressure -> VFD
Low suction pressure trips PD pump
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry
common_problems: Wear; sanding at low flow
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never run PD pump without charge pump pressure
sources: Weir Minerals GEHO PD pump literature (suction pressure requirements)

equipment.name: Digestion slurry feed pumps (piston-diaphragm)
equipment.function: Pump desilicated slurry at constant flow and high pressure (up to ~22 barg) through the slurry heaters into the digesters.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal triplex single-acting piston-diaphragm pump (GEHO TZPM-type): pistons work in clean propelling oil; elastomer diaphragms separate the oil from the slurry; ball/ cone check valves on the slurry side.
equipment.why_this_type: The slurry must be pushed through ~6 heaters (dP rising as they scale) into ~6 barg digesters - total ~15-22 barg. A PD pump delivers constant flow regardless of rising heater dP, has high efficiency (~85-90 %) and keeps abrasive slurry away from pistons and packings. PD pumps are the established choice for high-temperature digestion feed and are widely used where slurry heaters are installed.
equipment.alternatives: 2-3 hard-metal centrifugal slurry pumps in series with VFD (feasible at ~10-15 barg; lower capex, lower efficiency, flow changes as heaters scale; last stage needs high-pressure casing). If slurry heaters are omitted (slurry heated only by direct steam), centrifugal pumps alone are sufficient.
key_dimensions: Footprint ~10-12 m x 5-6 m, height ~4 m incl. dampeners - engineering estimate
3 diaphragm housings ~1.0-1.5 m dia (spherical/ dome) - engineering estimate
Suction/ discharge manifolds DN 200-250 - engineering estimate
Stroke ~0.4-0.5 m, ~40-60 strokes/min - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate - CONFIRM diaphragm elastomer temperature rating with vendor

equipment.working_principle: An electric motor drives a crankshaft through a gearbox; three cranks 120 deg apart move three pistons back and forth. Each piston pushes and pulls a column of clean propelling oil, which flexes a large rubber diaphragm in its housing. When the diaphragm moves back (suction stroke) the slurry suction check valve opens and slurry fills the chamber; on the forward stroke the suction valve closes, the discharge valve opens and slurry is displaced into the discharge manifold. Because only the diaphragm and the check valves touch the slurry, the precision piston and liner never see abrasive solids. A diaphragm-position control system tops up or bleeds propelling oil so the diaphragm stays in its correct range. A gas-charged pulsation dampener on the discharge smooths the triplex flow pulsations so the heaters and piping do not vibrate.
details_to_model: Power end: large cast crankcase with crankshaft, connecting rods, crossheads, piston rods; gearbox and motor in line on common baseplate; coupling guards
Three horizontal piston/ liner assemblies in front of crankcase, each feeding a dome-shaped diaphragm housing (two bolted halves with diaphragm clamped between)
Diaphragm position rods/ sensors on each housing; propelling oil system with tank, filters, flushing pump
Slurry side: three suction and three discharge valve housings (ball or cone valves) with bolted covers for quick valve change, connected to suction and discharge manifolds
Suction stabiliser (vessel) on inlet; discharge pulsation dampener (vertical bladder vessel, N2 pre-charge) with gauge
Discharge safety relief valve and bursting disc piped back to suction tank; discharge isolation valve; pressure transmitters
Lube oil unit for power end with cooler
Maintenance monorail/ jib crane over valve and diaphragm housings; acoustic enclosure optional
Concrete block foundation with anchor bolts, grout
equipment.materials: Diaphragm housings ductile iron/ cast steel; diaphragms elastomer (NR/ NBR/ EPDM - temperature/ caustic rated); valve seats hardened/ PU-faced; manifolds CS.
equipment.drive_and_power: 250-400 kW induction motor with VFD (flow control) and parallel-shaft gearbox (engineering estimate).
instrumentation_and_control: Flow set by VFD speed (stroke rate) - FIC ratioed to liquor flow
Discharge and suction PT; dampener pre-charge pressure
Diaphragm position monitoring; valve-condition monitoring (pressure-pulse analysis)
Trips: high discharge pressure, low suction pressure, lube oil, diaphragm end-position
hazards_and_safety: Very high stored energy: never open valve covers until discharge is depressurised and isolated, dampener vented
Hot caustic slurry at 15-22 barg
Rotating crank mechanism - guards
Nitrogen-charged dampener
common_problems: Check-valve wear (falling volumetric efficiency, pressure pulsation)
Diaphragm failure (oil contamination of slurry or slurry in oil)
Pulsation-induced vibration if dampener pre-charge lost
operating_tips_and_key_points: Monitor valve condition and change valves on condition
Maintain dampener pre-charge ~60-80 % of operating pressure (vendor to confirm)
Rising discharge pressure at constant flow = heater scaling - schedule heater changeover
sources: Weir Minerals, GEHO piston diaphragm pumps (ZPM/TZPM) product literature - alumina refinery digestion feed
Engineering estimate (sizing). OPEN: confirm diaphragm temperature limits and pump frame for 100 degC caustic slurry with vendor

equipment.name: Slurry heaters (flash-vapour, shell & tube)
equipment.function: Regeneratively heat the desilicated slurry stream from ~100 to ~127-130 degC by condensing flash vapour from flash stages 6 to 1 on the shell side.
equipment.qty_operating: 18 (6 per unit, one per flash stage)
equipment.qty_standby: 3 (1 per unit, 'rotating spare' that can be valved into any position while another heater is descaled)
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal multi-pass shell & tube, TEMA AEL-type (removable channel covers at both ends, fixed tubesheets), slurry in tubes, condensing flash vapour in shell.
equipment.why_this_type: Slurry must be in the tubes so they can be mechanically/ hydro-blasted and acid cleaned; straight tubes with removable channel covers at both ends allow full-length cleaning. Fixed tubesheets are acceptable because the shell side is clean condensing vapour (no shell-side cleaning).
equipment.alternatives: Double-pipe (tube-in-tube) heaters (common for high-temperature plants); direct-contact condensers; omit slurry heaters and heat slurry with live steam only (less scaling, more steam).
key_dimensions: Shell ID ~0.95-1.1 m, tube length ~7.3 m, overall length ~9.5-10 m - engineering estimate
~250-280 tubes, 50.8 mm OD x ~3.4 mm wall, 12 passes (~22 tubes per pass) - engineering estimate
Heat transfer area ~280-330 m2 each - engineering estimate
Vapour inlet nozzle ~DN 400-500; slurry nozzles DN 200; condensate outlet DN 80-100 - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (limit settling/ scaling vs erosion)
IAPWS-IF97 saturation + assumed BPE ~6 K; engineering estimate
Engineering estimate (strongly depends on desilication efficiency)

equipment.working_principle: Flash vapour from the matching flash tank enters the shell through a large top nozzle and an impingement plate, then condenses on the outside of the tubes, giving up its latent heat. The slurry flows back and forth through 12 passes of tubes at 2-3 m/s, picking up heat. Condensate drains from the bottom of the shell into a condensate pot, and non-condensable gases (air, CO2, light organics) are vented from the far end of the shell to the next lower-pressure stage, because even a few percent of non-condensables blankets the tubes and kills heat transfer. Heaters are arranged in series in order of rising vapour pressure (stage 6 vapour heats the coldest slurry, stage 1 vapour the hottest), so the slurry approaches the temperature of each stage. As DSP/ aluminosilicate scale builds inside the tubes, heat transfer falls and pressure drop rises; the spare heater is valved in and the scaled one is taken out for acid cleaning or hydro-blasting.
details_to_model: Horizontal cylindrical shell on two saddles (one fixed, one sliding with slotted holes), shell with possible thin-wall expansion bellows
Front and rear channels (barrel sections) with pass-partition plates inside; bolted flat channel covers with davit or hinge for removal; ~40-60 large studs per cover
Tube-side nozzles: slurry in/ out on front channel (DN 200, flanged, high-rating ASME Class 300) with ceramic/ hardened inlet ferrules in tube ends

Shell nozzles: vapour inlet on top (DN 400-500) over impingement plate; condensate outlet bottom (DN 80-100) to condensate pot; NCG vent at top far end (DN 50); PSV (tube-rupture case) DN 80-150 on top; drain and vent nozzles
Inside (for cutaway): tubesheets (~120-180 mm thick), tube bundle, support plates (no segmental baffles needed for condensing service - just support plates), impingement plate
Heaters stacked 2-3 high in a heater bank steel structure with platforms at each channel-cover level, lifting beams/ monorails above covers
Switching manifold: each heater with tube-side inlet/outlet isolation (metal-seated ball valves) and bypass so the spare can be inserted; vapour inlet butterfly/ gate isolation valve
Insulation (calcium silicate/ mineral wool ~75-100 mm) with aluminium cladding; channel covers left uninsulated or with removable insulation boxes
Thermowells on slurry in/out; PT on shell; level glass/ LT on condensate pot
equipment.materials: Shell, channels and tubesheets carbon steel (SA-516-70 / SA-266) with PWHT for caustic service; tubes seamless carbon steel (SA-179/ SA-192) - duplex 2205 or stainless an option for longer life against acid cleaning and erosion; tube-to-tubesheet expanded and seal welded.
instrumentation_and_control: Slurry outlet TT per heater (approach temperature tracking -> scaling indicator)
Heater switching sequence (DCS step) for spare insertion
hazards_and_safety: Tube rupture: high-pressure slurry into low-pressure shell - shell PSV sized per API 521 tube-rupture case
Opening channel covers: must be fully drained, depressurised, cooled and caustic-flushed; residual flashing caustic
Acid cleaning hazards: inhibited acid, H2 evolution in steel equipment - ventilate, no ignition sources
UHP water jetting (up to ~1,000-2,500 bar) - AS/NZS 4233.1 controls
common_problems: DSP (sodalite/ cancrinite) and gibbsite scale in tubes
Tube erosion at inlet ends (inlet ferrules wear)
Blocked tubes from sanding at low velocity
Non-condensable blanketing if vents closed
operating_tips_and_key_points: Track each heater's approach temperature; changeover on trend, not on failure
Keep NCG vents open (set by orifice/ valve)
Never let slurry stand in heaters - flush with liquor on shutdown
sources: TEMA Standards, 10th ed.; ASME BPVC Section VIII Div.1
Adamson, Bloore & Carr (1963) - regenerative heating in Bayer digestion
Addai-Mensah J. and co-workers, sodalite crystallisation and heat-exchanger scaling in Bayer liquors (Hydrometallurgy/ Light Metals)

equipment.name: Liquor heaters (flash-vapour, shell & tube)
equipment.function: Regeneratively heat strong spent liquor from ~95 to ~127-130 degC using flash vapour from stages 6 to 1 (paired with the slurry heaters).
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal 4-pass shell & tube, TEMA AEL-type, liquor in tubes, condensing vapour in shell; identical design to live-steam liquor heaters for interchangeability.
equipment.why_this_type: Clean liquor scales more slowly than slurry; straight tubes allow hydro-blasting; 4 passes give ~1.8-2 m/s.
equipment.alternatives: Vertical heaters; plate heat exchangers (not used: rapid scaling, gasket attack).
key_dimensions: Shell ID ~1.3-1.4 m, tube length ~7.3 m, overall ~9.5-10 m - engineering estimate
~520-560 tubes, 38.1 mm OD x 3.0 mm wall, 4 passes - engineering estimate
Area ~450-500 m2 - engineering estimate
Vapour inlet DN 500-600; liquor nozzles DN 300 - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (shell rated for live-steam service so heaters are interchangeable)

equipment.working_principle: Same as the slurry heaters: flash vapour condenses on the tubes and heats the liquor flowing inside. Because spent liquor is supersaturated with respect to DSP when heated, sodalite/ cancrinite scale gradually forms on the tube walls; good pre-desilication slows it. Heater outlet temperatures and the approach to vapour temperature are trended, and heaters are cycled through descaling with the rotating spare.
details_to_model: As slurry heaters, but larger shell and fewer passes (4); channel covers at front (inlet/outlet) and rear (return)
Vapour inlet with impingement plate; condensate outlet to pot; NCG vent at top far end; shell PSV
Arranged in the same heater bank as slurry heaters, typically liquor and slurry heater of same stage adjacent and fed from one vapour header branch

instrumentation_and_control: TT liquor out per heater; shell PT; condensate pot LIC; conductivity on condensate
hazards_and_safety: As for slurry heaters
common_problems: DSP scale; tube leaks contaminating condensate with caustic
operating_tips_and_key_points: Liquor-heater scale rate is the best indicator of desilication performance

equipment.name: Live-steam liquor heaters
equipment.function: Raise liquor from ~127-130 degC to ~150-158 degC with medium-pressure live steam so that the combined feed in digester 1 reaches digestion temperature.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 dedicated (the unit's spare liquor heater can be valved in)
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal shell & tube, TEMA AEL, identical to liquor heaters; MP steam on shell.
equipment.why_this_type: Indirect steam heating returns clean condensate to the boilers, unlike direct injection which dilutes the liquor.
equipment.alternatives: Direct steam injection of all heating steam (simpler, but adds ~40-50 t/h water per unit to evaporate).
key_dimensions: As 06-HX-201 (shell ~1.35 m ID x 7.3 m tubes, ~470 m2) - engineering estimate
equipment.working_principle: Saturated MP steam condenses on the tubes; the steam control valve on the shell inlet modulates to hold liquor outlet temperature (or the digester 1 temperature cascade). Condensate passes through a level-controlled pot to the clean condensate system and is checked for caustic (conductivity) before being returned to the boilers.

equipment.materials: As liquor heaters.
instrumentation_and_control: Condensate conductivity -> divert valve to contaminated condensate
hazards_and_safety: High-temperature steam ~190 degC; steam hammer on start-up - warm up slowly, drain lines
common_problems: Tube leak contaminating boiler condensate - must be detected fast
operating_tips_and_key_points: Warm up and drain steam lines before admitting steam

equipment.name: Digester 1 direct live-steam injection heaters
equipment.function: Trim the mixed slurry + liquor temperature at digester 1 inlet to 143-150 degC with direct live-steam injection.
equipment.type_selected: In-line direct steam injection heater (variable-area nozzle) on the slurry line just upstream of digester 1, or steam injection nozzles into the digester 1 inlet mixing tee.
equipment.why_this_type: Fast, scale-free final temperature control.
equipment.alternatives: Steam sparger in digester 1 (hammer risk); more indirect heater area.
key_dimensions: In-line body ~DN 250-300, ~2 m - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Hudson et al. (Ullmann's) low-temperature digestion range; engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: As the A05 steam injection heater but at MP steam; the digestion temperature controller (digester 1 outlet) modulates steam flow. Interlocks shut steam if slurry flow is lost.
details_to_model: In-line heater with actuator, steam isolation and check valve, TT downstream
equipment.materials: CS body, hardened/ ceramic nozzle.
instrumentation_and_control: TIC digester 1 temperature; low-flow steam cut-out
hazards_and_safety: Steam hammer; hot caustic
common_problems: Nozzle erosion
operating_tips_and_key_points: Digestion temperature affects A/C achievable and boehmite extraction - hold set point tightly

equipment.name: Digesters (low-temperature, in series)
equipment.function: Provide ~30-60 min residence at 143-150 degC under pressure for complete gibbsite dissolution and completion of desilication.
equipment.qty_operating: 12 (4 in series per unit x 3 units)
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each digester has a bypass so one can be removed for descaling with reduced residence)
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical pressure vessel (ASME VIII Div.1) with 2:1 semi-elliptical heads, top-entry agitator with pressurised double mechanical seal, inlet dip pipe and side overflow outlet (up-flow).
equipment.why_this_type: Low-temperature digestion needs only modest pressure (~5-6 barg), so large-diameter vertical vessels are economical. Agitation and up-flow minimise short-circuiting and sanding.
equipment.alternatives: Unagitated plug-flow digesters (slurry in at top, out at bottom or vice versa; relies on high velocity and steam mixing); horizontal autoclaves; tube digesters (high-temperature plants).
key_dimensions: ~5.5 m ID x ~10.5 m tangent-to-tangent; ~260 m3 gross, ~220-240 m3 working - engineering estimate
Overall height incl. heads and agitator drive ~17-18 m; top of vessel at ~+20-24 m on structure/ skirt - engineering estimate
Shell thickness ~25 mm (calc: 9 barg, 175 degC, SA-516-70 S~138 MPa, E=1 -> ~18 mm + 6 mm CA) - engineering estimate
Agitator: 2 pitched-blade/ hydrofoil impellers ~1.8-2.0 m dia - engineering estimate
Nozzles: inlet DN 400-450; outlet DN 400-450; steam DN 200; PSV 2 x DN 150-200; manways 2 x DN 600 - engineering estimate

operating_parameters.basis: Hudson et al., Ullmann's; Adamson et al. (1963); engineering estimate
Engineering estimate (liquor vapour pressure ~2.5-3 barg at 145 degC, IAPWS-IF97 with BPE ~5-7 K, plus margin)
Engineering estimate (before dilution; pregnant liquor after dilution 0.68-0.72)

equipment.working_principle: The heated liquor and the heated slurry, trimmed with live steam, enter digester 1 through a dip pipe that discharges low in the vessel. The agitator keeps the solids suspended and the temperature uniform while gibbsite reacts with free caustic to form sodium aluminate in solution. Slurry rises through the vessel and leaves by a side nozzle near the top, then enters the next digester's dip pipe - this up-flow series arrangement approximates plug flow and gives each particle the needed residence time. The vessels are kept full and pressurised above the liquor's vapour pressure so that the liquor does not boil; boiling would cause slugging and erosion. Pressure is controlled at the first flash tank let-down valve, and level is effectively 'full' (radiometric level confirms no vapour space). As the slurry passes through, A/C rises toward the target (~0.72); excessive A/C or temperature loss would risk gibbsite reverting on the walls.
details_to_model: Vertical cylindrical vessel with 2:1 SE top and bottom heads, on a cylindrical skirt (with skirt access opening and vent holes) or 4 leg/ lug supports on a structural steel platform
Top head: agitator mounting nozzle (DN 600-800 flange) with agitator stool, gearbox and vertical motor; double mechanical seal with barrier-fluid pot (Plan 53) on agitator stool; lifting lug/ davit
Top head nozzles: dip-pipe inlet nozzle (internal pipe to ~1/3 height, wear-resistant end), vent/ NCG nozzle to flash train, 2 PSV nozzles to relief header, top manway DN 600 with davit

Shell: side outlet nozzle near top (overflow), live-steam nozzle on digester 1, 3-4 thermowells at different elevations, pressure tap, lower manway DN 600, nozzle for radiometric source holder (or external source holder on bracket)
Bottom head: drain nozzle DN 150-200 with metal-seated ball valve to dump header; sand flushing connection
Internal (cutaway): agitator shaft with 2 impellers, steady bearing at bottom (optional), 4 baffles, dip pipe, wear plate below dip pipe
External radiometric level/ density gauges: source holder (lead-shielded, with lock) on one side and long scintillation detector on opposite side
Insulation ~100 mm mineral wool + aluminium cladding with visible bands; insulation removable boxes around nozzles
Platforms at top head (with grating and handrails) connected between all four digesters, stair tower at end of row, intermediate platform at manway/ instrument level
Transfer piping between digesters: large-radius bends, wear-back tees, flanged spools with spray guards; pipe supports from structure
Nameplate, earthing bosses, painted identification bands
equipment.materials: Carbon steel SA-516-70 (normalised), corrosion allowance ~6 mm, full PWHT for caustic service (NACE SP0403); agitator shaft/ impellers CS or 2205 duplex; dip pipe hard-faced/ ceramic-lined tip.
equipment.drive_and_power: 45-90 kW top-entry agitator per digester (engineering estimate), on essential supply.
instrumentation_and_control: TT at 3-4 levels, TIC on digester 1 (cascade to steam)
PT/ PIC on last digester (let-down valve to flash tank 1)
Radiometric level/ density on each digester
Agitator torque/ kW; seal barrier pressure/ level alarms
Liquor sampling (cooled, pressurised sampler) for A/C, C, SiO2 at exit
SIS: high pressure, high temperature, loss of agitator, loss of feed -> steam trip
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry at 145 degC and ~5-6 barg: any leak flashes violently (~7-8 % of the liquor flashes to steam) causing scalds plus caustic burns - spray shields on all flanges, exclusion zones
Overpressure if outlet blocked while steam is on - PSVs and SIS

Confined space entry for descaling: full isolation (positive isolation with spades/ blinds), radiometric source shutters locked, agitator LOTO, ventilation, rescue plan; scale may fall from walls/ head
Caustic stress corrosion cracking - regular inspection (wet fluorescent magnetic particle on welds)
Hot surfaces, working at height
common_problems: Scale (gibbsite/ DSP) on walls and agitator, reducing working volume
Sand accumulation in bottom head
Erosion at inlet dip pipe and outlet nozzles
Seal failures on agitators
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch the digester exit A/C vs target: too high risks reversion and losses; too low wastes liquor capacity
Keep pressure margin above vapour pressure; flashing in digesters causes vibration and erosion
Plan descaling outages with the flash train (often during a unit shutdown every ~6-12 months - engineering estimate)
sources: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div.1 (UG-27 thickness, UG-99 hydrotest)
Hudson L.K. et al., Aluminum Oxide, Ullmann's Encyclopedia (low-temperature digestion ~140-150 degC)
Adamson, Bloore & Carr (1963) Basic principles of Bayer process design

equipment.function: Supply MP steam to live-steam heaters and injection heaters at controlled pressure and near-saturation temperature.
equipment.type_selected: Pressure-reducing and desuperheating (PRDS) station with spray-water desuperheater, steam header with drip legs and traps.

details_to_model: Control valve station with isolation and bypass, desuperheater spray nozzle, downstream straight run, TT/PT, safety valve, header with drip legs, steam traps, expansion loops on pipe rack
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (ASME B31.1/ B31.3).
instrumentation_and_control: Steam flow FT to each unit
hazards_and_safety: High-energy steam line rupture; water hammer
common_problems: Trap failures causing hammer

Live-steam header and PRDS on rack. Clearances for channel-cover removal (~3 m at each heater end) and crane access roadway (~6 m) along each bay. Relief header slopes to the shared dump tank at the end of the area. Safety showers at every level/ stair landing.

areas.purpose: Cool the digested slurry from ~145 degC to its atmospheric boiling point (~105-108 degC) in pressure steps, producing flash vapour at successively lower pressures that heats the incoming slurry and liquor (regenerative heat recovery), and collect the condensate for reuse.
areas.process_description:
1) Digested slurry from the last digester is let down through a severe-service control valve (which holds digester pressure) into flash tank 1.
2) In each of 6 pressurised flash tanks per unit, the pressure is lower than the vapour pressure of the incoming slurry, so part of the water boils instantly (flashes) until the slurry cools to the boiling temperature at that pressure. The slurry is cooled ~5-7 K per stage; ~2 % of its mass evaporates per stage.
3) Vapour leaves each tank top through a disengagement space/ baffle to the matching pair of heaters (slurry heater + liquor heater) in A06; slurry from the tank bottom passes through a level-control (let-down) valve to the next, lower-pressure tank.
4) Indicative stage table (engineering estimate; slurry exit T / vapour saturation T / pressure): FT1 139/133 degC, ~2.95 bar a (~1.9 barg); FT2 133/127, ~2.45 bar a; FT3 127/121, ~2.05 bar a; FT4 121/115, ~1.69 bar a; FT5 115/109, ~1.39 bar a; FT6 109/103, ~1.13 bar a; then atmospheric blow-off tank ~105-107 degC. (Vapour is saturated at a lower temperature than the slurry because of the boiling-point elevation of ~5-7 K of the caustic liquor; pressures from IAPWS-IF97.)
5) Blow-off (atmospheric) tank: final flash; vapour to a vent condenser or the mill-liquor heater (A04); slurry pumped to the dilution tank (clarification area) where it is diluted with first-washer overflow before settling.
6) Condensate: heater condensate from each stage drains via condensate pots and cascades to the next lower-pressure pot (re-flashing), finally collected as 'process condensate' (~75-80 t/h per unit), monitored by conductivity for caustic contamination, and used for residue washing/ hydrate washing or polished for boiler feed. Live-steam condensate is kept separate ('clean condensate') and returned to the boilers after conductivity checks.
7) Non-condensable gases from heater shells are vented stage-to-stage and finally from the last stage to the vent condenser (odour/ VOC control).
8) Scale control: gibbsite (from alumina supersaturation as slurry cools) and DSP scale form on flash tank walls, inlet boxes and interstage lines/ valves. Interstage lines and valves are inspected and descaled at unit shutdowns (~6-12 months, engineering estimate) by UHP water jetting/ mechanical means; erosion-resistant inserts are replaced.
High-temperature plants: typically 8-12+ flash stages from ~250 degC, much higher first-stage pressures (~20-30 bar), and titanate/ boehmite scales.

equipment.working_principle: Hot slurry enters through the let-down valve at a pressure above the tank's saturation pressure. As it enters the lower-pressure tank, some water boils instantly, absorbing latent heat and cooling the slurry to the saturation temperature at the tank pressure (adjusted for boiling-point elevation). The violent two-phase jet strikes a replaceable impact box rather than the shell. Vapour rises through the disengagement height, where droplets fall back, and leaves through the top nozzle to the heaters; the heaters condense it, and this condensation is what holds the tank pressure down. Slurry collects in the cone and passes to the next tank through a level-control valve. The more stages, the closer the liquor/slurry can be heated to the digestion temperature, but the more equipment is required.
details_to_model: Vertical vessel: 2:1 SE top head, cylindrical shell, 60 deg cone bottom with knuckle, supported on 4 lugs/ a ring girder on a steel structure (cone hangs below platform) or on legs
Inlet: side nozzle at ~mid-shell entering an internal impact/ wear box (bolted replaceable hard-faced plates or ceramic tiles), sometimes tangential; reinforcing pad around nozzle
Top: vapour outlet nozzle DN 700-900 with internal baffle/ hood to deflect droplets, PSV nozzle(s), vent/ NCG nozzle, top manway DN 600 with davit
Shell: manway DN 600 near inlet box (for inspection), radiometric level source holder and detector (vertical strip), PT, 2 thermowells
Cone: outlet nozzle DN 350-400 with internal vortex breaker (cross plate), drain nozzle, flushing nozzles (2-3 liquor flush connections into cone)
Wear liners at inlet zone shell (sacrificial plate welded inside), ultrasonic thickness test points marked on exterior
Insulation ~75-100 mm with aluminium cladding
Platforms at top head and at inlet/ manway level, ladders/ stairs, handrails; tanks connected by interstage piping descending stage to stage
Vapour line from top to heater bank (large, insulated, sloped, with low-point drains)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel SA-516-70, CA ~6 mm, full PWHT for caustic service; inlet box hard-faced/ ceramic; internal baffle CS.
instrumentation_and_control: Radiometric level LT/ LIC -> interstage let-down valve
PT per stage (stage pressures follow heater condensation)
PSV per tank (blocked vapour outlet/ upstream valve failure cases)
Vapour carry-over detection: condensate conductivity at the paired heaters
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry under pressure; leaks flash violently
Erosion thinning at inlet zone - risk of sudden rupture; routine UT thickness surveys
Vacuum collapse risk if not FV-rated when vapour condenses during shutdown
Confined space entry; radiometric source isolation; scale falling
Opening flanges with trapped hot slurry - verify drained and vented
common_problems: Inlet-zone erosion and wear-box failure
Gibbsite/ DSP scale on walls and outlet cone (reduced volume, level gauge errors)
Carry-over of slurry into vapour lines at high level, contaminating heater condensate
Level control instability due to two-phase flow
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep levels low-mid band - high level causes carry-over into heaters (caustic in condensate)
Rising stage pressure indicates the matching heater is losing duty (scaled/ NCG blanketed)
Trend wall thickness at inlet zone at every shutdown
sources: Adamson, Bloore & Carr (1963) - flash heat recovery in Bayer digestion

Digestion flowsheet choice: this design uses double-stream regenerative heating with BOTH slurry heaters and liquor heaters (paired per flash stage). Many low-temperature refineries heat only the liquor indirectly and heat the slurry by direct live-steam injection (no slurry heaters, centrifugal feed pumps only). Digestion feed pump type: piston-diaphragm (GEHO TZPM-type) selected because of slurry-heater pressure drop (~15-22 barg). Confirm diaphragm elastomer temperature rating for ~100 degC caustic slurry, pump frame size for ~300 m3/h, and whether 2-3 centrifugal pumps in series would be preferred.

Number of digestion units (3) and digesters per unit (4 x ~240 m3 working, ~45 min) are engineering estimates; confirm against a real low-temperature plant reference (e.g., Darling Range or East Coast India refinery data) and with bauxite digestion kinetics test work.
Digester agitation: top-entry agitators were assumed; some low-temperature plants use unagitated plug-flow digesters. Confirm.
Bauxite factor changed to 2.65 t/t dry (from 2.4-2.6). Confirm available-alumina definition (whether DSP alumina loss is already deducted) and project bauxite assays.

Grinding circuit: single-stage ball mills with 1 mm screens assumed; Bond work index of the project bauxite (caprock/ laterite hardness) and screen capacity per unit need test work; alternatives (rod+ball, SAG) depend on ore clay content.
Number of flash stages (6 + blow-off) is an economic optimisation (heater area vs steam); confirm with SME and heat balance software.
PWHT requirements for large atmospheric API 650 tanks in ~15 % NaOH at ~100 degC per NACE SP0403 caustic chart - confirm owner's materials philosophy (full PWHT of nozzles/ attachments vs shell).
Descaling intervals for slurry heaters (1-4 weeks), liquor heaters (3-8 weeks), digesters/flash tanks (6-12 months) are estimates; depend strongly on reactive silica and desilication efficiency.
Acid cleaning chemistry (inhibited H2SO4 strength/ temperature) to be confirmed with chemical-cleaning vendor and refinery practice.
Final flash vapour use (mill-liquor heating vs condenser) and VOC/odour control strategy (thermal oxidation of NCG?) depend on site environmental conditions.
Area numbering for interfaces outside A04-A07 (stockyard, evaporation, clarification, power house) to be aligned with the master area list.

areas.area_name: Sand removal, settling & washing (clarification and CCD residue washing)
areas.purpose: Separate the coarse sand and the fine residue (red mud) from the digested slurry, deliver a clear pregnant (green) liquor to security filtration, and recover soluble soda and dissolved alumina from the residue by counter-current decantation (CCD) washing before the residue is filtered and stored.
areas.process_description:
1) FEED: Digested slurry leaves the last blow-off flash tank of digestion (A07) at about 103-108 degC, at atmospheric pressure and close to boiling. It is supersaturated in alumina (A/C about 0.68-0.72) and contains roughly 70-90 g/L residue solids. A08 must be fast: from the digester to the end of security filtration the liquor is metastable. Gibbsite can autoprecipitate in settlers, tanks and launders, which loses product and builds scale, so the aim is short residence time and high temperature.
2) SAND REMOVAL: Cyclone feed pumps send the slurry to clusters of hydrocyclones that cut at about 100-150 um. Underflow (sand, mostly quartz plus coarse goethite, hematite and laterite gravel) drops to a 3-stage counter-current screw-classifier train and is washed with hot wash water. Washed sand is dewatered on a vibrating screen and conveyed to a stockpile. It is used to build RSA embankments, drainage layers and roads. Cyclone overflow (fine residue plus liquor) flows to the settler feed (dilution) tank. Sand content varies strongly with bauxite source. It is low in India East Coast khondalite bauxite and high in Darling Range ore, where residue is reported as roughly half sand. The circuit is sized for 10-15% of residue as sand.
3) DILUTION AND FLOCCULATION: The first-washer overflow (weak liquor) dilutes the cyclone overflow in the settler feed tank. This lowers viscosity and sets pregnant liquor concentration and A/C. Flocculant is added in stages: hydroxamate-modified polyacrylamide for overflow clarity (it captures fine iron and titanium minerals and DSP), and high-MW sodium polyacrylate for settling rate. Both go in at the feed pipe and feedwell.
4) SETTLING (clarification): High-rate settlers (decanters) separate residue from liquor. Overflow is pregnant liquor (green liquor) at about 10-50 mg/L suspended solids and goes to security filtration (A10). Underflow at about 30-40 wt% solids is pumped to Washer 1.
5) CCD WASHING: Six washer stages operate, with a 7th installed for descaling rotation. Mud moves forward (W1 to W6) by underflow pumping. Wash liquor moves backward: hot wash water, made of RSA return lake water, condensate and press-filter filtrate, enters W6. Each washer's overflow joins the feed of the washer before it. W1 overflow returns to the settler feed tank. Soluble Na2O and Al2O3 concentrations fall by about one stage-factor per washer (ideal-mixing model). Final underflow leaves W6 at 45-55 wt% solids with residual liquor of about 3-8 g/L total soda as Na2CO3, and is pumped to residue filtration (A09).
6) CHEMISTRY in this area: (a) Supersaturated pregnant liquor, NaAl(OH)4 in NaOH, can revert by Al(OH)4- -> Al(OH)3 + OH-. This is avoided by keeping liquor hot and residence short. (b) Desilication product (DSP, sodalite type Na8[Al6Si6O24]X2 with X = 2OH-, CO3 2-, SO4 2- or Cl-) has largely formed in pre-desilication and digestion and leaves with the mud. It is the main CHEMICAL soda loss: about 0.6-0.7 kg Na2O per kg reactive SiO2 (stoichiometric for sodalite). Washing cannot recover it. (c) Washing recovers only SOLUBLE (mechanical) soda entrained in the liquor that wets the mud. (d) In the later washers, where liquor is weaker and cooler, some gibbsite can precipitate (soluble alumina loss), and carbonate and oxalate can build scale. This is managed by washer temperature and by rotating the spare washer.
7) WATER BALANCE: All wash water entering W6 ends up in the liquor circuit and must be removed by evaporation (A12/A13). The wash ratio therefore trades soda recovery against evaporator steam. This is a key point for trainees.
8) HIGH-TEMPERATURE (boehmitic) plants differ: digestion runs at 240-260 degC, there is typically more DSP and cancrinite, slurry is cooled by more flash stages, and settler feed liquor is more concentrated. The settling and CCD principles are the same.

streams.name: Digested (blow-off) slurry to sand cyclones
streams.flow: About 2,700-3,000 m3/h liquor + about 265 t/h dry residue solids (incl. sand)
streams.pressure: Atmospheric at tank; about 1.5-2.5 bar g at cyclone inlet
streams.composition: Caustic about 240-280 g/L as Na2CO3 (pre-dilution), A/C about 0.70-0.74, residue solids about 70-90 g/L
streams.basis: Engineering estimate from 240 t/h alumina, 80 g/L yield and 1.1 t residue/t alumina

streams.name: Sand cyclone underflow
streams.flow: About 25-40 t/h dry sand (design 45 t/h) at about 50-65 wt% solids
streams.basis: Engineering estimate (10-15% of residue as sand); sand content is ore-specific

streams.name: Washed sand to stockpile
streams.flow: About 25-40 t/h dry sand at about 85-90 wt% solids
streams.composition: Residual soluble soda target < about 1-3 kg Na2O/t sand

streams.name: Settler feed (diluted slurry)
streams.flow: About 3,300-3,500 m3/h liquor + about 230-250 t/h fine residue
streams.composition: Caustic about 230-260 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C about 0.68-0.72, solids about 60-80 g/L
streams.basis: Engineering estimate consistent with provisional liquor numbers

streams.name: Settler overflow = pregnant (green) liquor
streams.flow: About 3,000-3,400 m3/h (240 t/h alumina / 70-85 g/L yield, plus losses)
streams.composition: Caustic 230-260 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C 0.68-0.72, suspended solids about 10-50 mg/L
streams.basis: Computed from plant-wide numbers; solids range from published practice (engineering estimate)

streams.name: Settler underflow
streams.flow: About 230-250 t/h dry solids at 30-40 wt% (about 600-750 m3/h slurry)

streams.name: Wash water to last washer
streams.composition: Total soda about 1-10 g/L as Na2CO3 (lake water/filtrate), pH 12-13
streams.basis: Engineering estimate; set by evaporation capacity

streams.name: First washer overflow (weak liquor) to dilution
streams.composition: About 80-140 g/L caustic as Na2CO3 (engineering estimate)

streams.name: Final washer underflow to residue filtration
streams.flow: About 265 t/h dry solids (incl. any returned sand fines/TCA) at 45-55 wt% (about 330-400 m3/h)
streams.composition: Liquor about 3-8 g/L total soda as Na2CO3
streams.basis: IAI BR Guidance 2015 (CCD underflow >40%, practical limit about 50%, advanced thickeners 48-55%); soda value engineering estimate

streams.name: Flocculant solutions
streams.flow: Settler about 100-300 g/t, washers about 30-100 g/t each (dry polymer basis), diluted to 0.02-0.1%
streams.composition: Sodium polyacrylate (high MW); hydroxamated polyacrylamide for settler

equipment.name: Sand cyclone feed pumps (blow-off slurry pumps)
equipment.function: Pump hot digested slurry from the last flash tank to the sand cyclone clusters at the required inlet pressure.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal heavy-duty centrifugal slurry pump, metal-lined (high-chrome) or hard-metal single casing, overhung, belt or direct drive with VSD (Weir Warman AH/MC or equivalent class)
equipment.why_this_type: Large-volume abrasive slurry service at low-to-moderate head. Hard-metal pumps withstand quartz sand, and hot caustic rules out natural rubber.
key_dimensions: Each about 1,500-1,800 m3/h at about 25-35 m head (engineering estimate)
Suction about 500-600 mm (20-24 in), discharge about 400-450 mm (16-18 in)
Impeller dia about 1.2-1.5 m; pump + baseplate + motor footprint about 6 m x 2.5 m

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (cyclone inlet 1.0-1.5 bar + static + losses)

equipment.working_principle: A rotating closed impeller with heavy, thick vanes gives the slurry kinetic energy, and the volute converts it to pressure. Wear parts (impeller, throatbush, frame-plate liner and volute liner) are high-chrome white iron (about 27% Cr), which resists abrasion by quartz sand. Because the slurry is at its boiling point, available NPSH is only the static head between the flash tank level and the pump. For that reason the pumps sit at the lowest elevation, directly below the tank, with a short, large-bore suction. The VSD holds cyclone inlet pressure constant as feed density varies. Gland sealing uses flushed packing with condensate or a double mechanical seal, and dilution of the process must be minimised.
details_to_model: Overhung pump with a split, bolted outer casing showing heavy flange bolts around the perimeter; large suction on the impeller axis and tangential discharge pointing up
Bearing housing (cartridge) on a pedestal, adjusting screw for impeller clearance at the rear of the bearing assembly
Overhead belt drive (motor mounted above pump) with belt guard, OR direct coupled motor with coupling guard; motor about 2 m long
Suction spool with knife-gate isolation valve (rising stem, handwheel/actuator), drain valve and flushing connection; discharge with pinch or knife-gate valve, pressure gauge with diaphragm seal
Gland water line with rotameter and needle valve (packed gland) or seal-water panel
Common concrete plinth with drip/drain trench, bunded pump bay, safety shower nearby
Insulated suction pipe (aluminium cladding), personnel-protection cages
Lifting lugs on casing halves; monorail/hoist beam above the pump bay for liner change
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry at near boiling: flashing on loss of containment, severe caustic plus thermal burns (full face shield, caustic-resistant PPE)
Gland or flange leak spray: install flange guards/spray shields
Isolation and drainage before liner change: double block and drain, LOTO, confirm cooled and depressurised
Rotating belt drives: guards
Water hammer on pump trip with a long discharge line
sources: Engineering estimate based on typical Bayer blow-off pump practice
IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015) for circuit context
equipment.materials: High-chrome white iron (about 27% Cr, e.g. Warman A05) wet-end; ductile iron or carbon steel outer casing; carbon steel shaft sleeve with hard coating
equipment.drive_and_power: LV/MV induction motor 450-750 kW with VSD; V-belt or direct coupling
instrumentation_and_control: VSD speed control on cyclone inlet pressure
common_problems: Cavitation from low NPSH or flashing
Rapid wear of throatbush/impeller due to sand
Scale build-up in casing
Gland leaks
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never run the pump against a closed discharge in hot slurry, because it flashes in seconds
Keep flash tank level above the minimum for NPSH
Flush the line with dilute liquor before a planned stop to avoid sanding
equipment.alternatives: Vertical cantilever pumps from a sump (smaller plants)

equipment.name: Sand cyclone clusters
equipment.function: Classify coarse sand (+100-150 um) out of the digested slurry ahead of the settlers, protecting settlers, rakes and pumps and producing a sand by-product.
equipment.qty_standby: 2-3 spare cyclones per cluster (isolated by knife gate)
equipment.type_selected: Radial manifold cluster of 500-660 mm diameter hydrocyclones, ceramic- or high-chrome-lined (Weir Cavex / FLSmidth Krebs gMAX class)
equipment.why_this_type: Compact, no moving parts, sharp enough cut at 100-150 um, easy online exchange of individual cyclones.
key_dimensions: Cyclone body ID about 500-660 mm, overall cyclone height about 3-4 m (engineering estimate)
Cluster manifold dia about 3-4 m, 8 positions; overall cluster height about 6-7 m
Inlet about 250 x 125 mm rectangular; vortex finder about 200-250 mm; apex (spigot) about 100-150 mm
equipment.working_principle: Slurry enters tangentially and forms a vortex. Centrifugal force throws coarse, dense sand particles to the wall, where they spiral down and discharge through the apex as underflow. Fine mud and most of the liquor reverse into the inner upward vortex and leave through the vortex finder as overflow. The cut size is set by cyclone diameter, inlet pressure, vortex finder and apex dimensions, and slurry viscosity. Hot, low-viscosity liquor improves the separation. A 'roping' apex indicates overload.
details_to_model: Circular distributor (manifold) with a central bottom feed and 8 radial knife-gate valves, each feeding one cyclone mounted inclined or vertical
Each cyclone: cylindrical inlet head with tangential inlet, conical sections (2-3 flanged cone segments), apex/spigot with rubber/ceramic insert, vortex finder rising to overflow launder
Circular overflow launder (annular trough) collecting all vortex finders, with large outlet pipe to settler feed tank
Underflow collection launder/hopper below, discharge chute to classifier
Pressure gauge on manifold with diaphragm seal
Steel support structure with access platform at cyclone-head level, grating, handrails, toe boards, caged ladder or stair
Chain block/monorail for cyclone change-out
Covered launders with vapour vents (hot liquor)
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic splash from apex 'spray' discharge; underflow hood required
Steam/vapour around launders
Working at height on cluster platform
Isolate the valve and drain the cyclone before changing it
sources: Engineering estimate; vendor sizing practice for 500-660 mm hydrocyclones
Power G., Graefe M., Klauber C., Hydrometallurgy 108 (2011) 33-45 - sand separation and use (not retrieved this session)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell with ceramic (alumina/SiC) or high-chrome wear liners; natural rubber unsuitable at 100+ degC in caustic, so EPDM/specialised elastomer is used only where rated
common_problems: Apex blockage by gravel/scale
Roping in overload
Liner wear and scaling at vortex finder
operating_tips_and_key_points: Adjust the number of cyclones online to hold the pressure
Check underflow discharge shape (umbrella spray, not rope)
equipment.alternatives: Rotary sand traps or sand separators (gravity), as in older plants and as Wikipedia notes for liquor clarification

equipment.name: Sand washing screw classifiers (3-stage counter-current)
equipment.function: Wash entrained caustic liquor from sand and dewater it, recovering soda and alumina; produce clean sand for construction use.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (bypass to settler feed or temporary sand cyclone return during maintenance)
equipment.type_selected: Inclined twin-spiral screw (spiral) classifiers, high-weir type
equipment.why_this_type: Robust and simple. Classifying, washing and dewatering happen in one machine, it tolerates gravel, and it is proven in Bayer sand washing.
key_dimensions: Spiral dia about 1.5-2.0 m, tank length about 10-12 m, incline about 14-18 degrees (engineering estimate)
Pool area at lower end about 15-25 m2
Each about 25-35 t overall
equipment.working_principle: Sand slurry enters a pool at the lower end of an inclined trough. Coarse sand settles and is conveyed up the incline by slowly rotating helical spirals, draining as it rises out of the pool. Fines and liquor overflow the weir at the lower end. Wash liquor flows counter-current: fresh hot wash water is added at stage 3. Stage 3 overflow becomes wash liquor for stage 2, stage 2 overflow serves stage 1, and stage 1 overflow returns to the settler feed tank. Dewatered sand discharging from stage 3 carries only weak liquor.
details_to_model: Long inclined steel trough with rectangular pool section at lower end and adjustable overflow weir with launder
Two parallel helical spirals on hollow shafts, bolt-on wear shoes (hardened/Ni-hard) on flights
Upper-end drive: motor + gearbox (shaft-mounted reducer) with guard; lower bearing with lift mechanism (screw jack/hydraulic) to raise the spirals out of sand on restart
Feed box at mid-pool; wash water spray bars over the rising sand bed
Sand discharge chute at upper end dropping onto next stage or dewatering screen
Covers over pool and vapour extraction duct; access walkways along both sides, stairs
Tank drains and flushing connections
hazards_and_safety: Rotating spirals: interlocked covers, LOTO before entry
Hot caustic splash and vapour
Confined space if the trough is entered for wear-shoe replacement
sources: Engineering estimate; classical Bayer sand washing practice
equipment.materials: Carbon steel trough (PWHT of welds for hot caustic per NACE SP0403), hardened wear shoes
equipment.drive_and_power: Electric motor 15-37 kW per classifier with helical-bevel reducer; hydraulic or electric lift
common_problems: Spiral overload on restart after a sand-up
Wear of flight shoes
Scale on weir
operating_tips_and_key_points: Lift the spirals before stopping with a full sand load
Keep wash water hot to keep viscosity low
equipment.alternatives: Sand washing hydrocyclones + horizontal belt filter or dewatering screen; bucket-wheel sand washers

equipment.name: Sand dewatering screen
equipment.function: Final dewatering of washed sand to a conveyable, stackable product.
equipment.type_selected: Linear-motion high-frequency dewatering screen with polyurethane panels (0.5-1.0 mm aperture)
equipment.why_this_type: Produces about 85-90 wt% solids sand for conveying.
key_dimensions: Deck about 1.8-2.4 m wide x 4.8-6.0 m long (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Twin unbalanced-mass vibrator motors produce a linear stroke. Sand forms a bed that acts as its own filter while water drains through the polyurethane panels, and the deck slopes slightly upward towards the discharge to hold the bed.
details_to_model: Box-like screen body on coil or rubber springs, two exciter motors on top cross-beam
Modular PU panels in grid, side plates with reinforcing ribs
Under-pan sloping to a filtrate pipe returning to classifier stage 3
Discharge lip over conveyor 08-CV-001; enclosure with vents
hazards_and_safety: Vibration and noise
Pinch points at springs
equipment.materials: Carbon steel with PU panels
common_problems: Panel blinding
Spring failure
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check panel wear and blinding each shift
equipment.alternatives: Stacking sand to drain on a pad

equipment.name: Sand conveyor and sand stockpile
equipment.function: Convey washed sand to a covered stockpile/loadout for trucking to the RSA (embankment, drainage layers, roads).
equipment.type_selected: Troughed belt conveyor (CEMA C/D idlers), 750-900 mm belt; bunded concrete stockpile pad with drainage sump
equipment.why_this_type: Low capacity and short distance.
key_dimensions: Belt width 750-900 mm, length about 50-150 m (engineering estimate)
Stockpile pad about 40 x 30 m, 3-5 days storage
equipment.working_principle: A troughed belt on idlers, driven by a head pulley, carries the sand. Drainage from the stockpile pad (weak caustic) is collected in a sump and returned to the process.
details_to_model: Galvanised truss gallery with walkway on one side, handrails, pull-wire emergency stop along length
Head drive (motor, fluid coupling, gearbox) with guarding; tail pulley with gravity or screw take-up
Belt scrapers at head; skirtboards at loading
Stockpile pad with push walls, drain grate and sump pump; front-end loader
hazards_and_safety: Nip points at pulleys
Alkaline sand (pH > 11): skin and eye irritation
Mobile plant at stockpile
sources: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials (practice)
equipment.materials: Galvanised steel structure, rubber belt
instrumentation_and_control: Pull-wire switches, belt drift and speed switches
common_problems: Carry-back of sticky sand
operating_tips_and_key_points: Monitor sand soda, because it decides whether sand can be used in construction
equipment.alternatives: Direct truck loadout

equipment.name: Settler feed (dilution) tank
equipment.function: Combine the cyclone overflow with first-washer overflow and dilute the slurry to the target pregnant liquor concentration. Also acts as the first flocculant contact point.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated cylindrical vertical tank with fixed roof, insulated
equipment.why_this_type: Short residence (2-5 min) mixing vessel that minimises time for autoprecipitation.
key_dimensions: About 8-10 m ID x 8-10 m high (engineering estimate)
Live volume about 300-500 m3
equipment.working_principle: A top-entry agitator mixes the two streams uniformly. The overflow box, or gravity distributors, splits the flow equally to the operating settlers.
details_to_model: Top-entry agitator (2 pitched-blade impellers) with gearbox on roof bridge
Inlet nozzles: cyclone overflow, washer 1 overflow, sand classifier overflow, flush; outlet distributor box with 3 gates (one per settler)
Insulation with aluminium cladding, roof manway, vent, level radar
Stair tower to roof, handrails
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic vapour
Confined space entry for descaling
equipment.materials: Carbon steel, PWHT welds (NACE SP0403 caustic service)
instrumentation_and_control: Density/caustic analyser on outlet (online titrator or conductivity-based)
common_problems: Scaling and sanding
operating_tips_and_key_points: Control dilution with W1 overflow to hold pregnant liquor caustic/A/C on target
equipment.alternatives: Inline dilution in pipe/launder

equipment.name: High-rate settlers (mud decanters / clarifier-thickeners)
equipment.function: Separate fine residue from pregnant liquor, giving clear overflow for security filtration and thickened underflow for washing.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 (rotation for descaling, about every 3-12 months; engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: High-rate thickener with deep feedwell (energy-dissipating, flocculant-dilution type), centre-column supported hydraulic rake drive, fixed insulated roof
equipment.why_this_type: Synthetic flocculants allow 3-10x the unit-area capacity of old Dorr tray settlers, cutting liquor holdup (autoprecipitation and soda inventory). A spare unit is needed because gibbsite and DSP scale accumulates.
key_dimensions: ID about 35-40 m; sidewall about 6-8 m; floor slope about 1:6 to 1:4 (engineering estimate)
Feedwell about 5-7 m dia x 3-4 m deep
Centre column about 2.5-3.5 m dia (access to underflow cone)
Mud bed depth typically 1-3 m

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (3,300 m3/h over 2 x 35-40 m)

equipment.working_principle: Slurry enters the feedwell, where velocity is dissipated and flocculant is mixed in so fine particles aggregate into large, fast-settling flocs. Flocs settle through a hindered-settling zone into a compression bed. Clear liquor rises and overflows the peripheral launder weirs. Slowly rotating rake arms (about 1 rev per 10-20 min) with angled blades move the compacted mud towards the central discharge cone and break up channels so water can escape the bed. Hydroxamate flocculant is selective for iron oxide fines and controls overflow clarity. Polyacrylate builds large flocs for settling rate. Bed level and rake torque are the key controls. Too high a bed raises torque and risks solids carry-over; too low a bed gives a thin underflow.
details_to_model: Large flat-bottomed cylindrical steel tank on a concrete ring wall/raft; shallow conical floor with grout fill, underflow cone at centre
Underflow tunnel or under-tank chamber with underflow pipes, knife-gate valves and pumps (08-PP-002); tunnel lighting, ventilation, escape stairs
Centre column (fixed) carrying the rake drive at the top on a drive platform with hydraulic power unit and lift cylinders
Rake: 2 long + 2 short truss arms with angled blades/ploughs, scraper at cone, optional pickets; rake lift 600-900 mm
Access bridge from tank wall to centre platform (walkway with handrails), roughly 18-20 m span supported on the column
Feedwell hanging off the bridge/column, multiple flocculant sparge points, feed pipe running along the bridge
Peripheral internal overflow launder with V-notch weirs, launder outlet box to green liquor tank; launder covered
Fixed conical roof (sheet roof on rafters) with vapour vents, inspection hatches, sampling ports
Wall insulation (mineral wool about 75-100 mm + aluminium cladding)
Instrumentation: bed level sonar/nuclear profiler hanging off bridge, rake torque display at drive, overflow turbidity, nuclear density gauge on underflow line
Stairs (zig-zag) on tank wall, intermediate landings, roof walkways
Scour/flush nozzles in cone; emergency dump connection to spill tank
Bund wall around thickener farm
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic liquor near boiling: burns, flashing
Confined-space entry during descaling: tank must be drained, cooled, ventilated, gas tested and LOTO applied to rake drive; entrapment in soft mud
Fall from bridge/roof
Rake drive overload or rake collapse: torque trip, lift on high torque
Underflow tunnel: confined/low-lying space, flooding risk, toxic atmosphere possible
Vapour plumes reduce visibility on roof
sources: IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015) - high-rate decanters, super thickeners, CCD practice
Engineering estimate for dimensions and loadings
Hydroxamate flocculant practice: Cytec/Solvay HX series literature (TMS Light Metals papers on hydroxamate flocculants, not retrieved this session)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A516-70 or equivalent), welds PWHT for caustic SCC (NACE SP0403 caustic chart); no internal lining; rake structural CS
equipment.drive_and_power: Hydraulic planetary rake drive, about 15-30 kW HPU; rated torque about 1-3 MNm (engineering estimate)
instrumentation_and_control: Bed level (sonar or nuclear profiler) and bed mass (pressure)
Underflow density (nuclear) and flow (magflow) controlling underflow pump speed
Flocculant ratio control on feed solids
common_problems: Gibbsite autoprecipitation and DSP scaling on walls, launders and rakes
Rat-holing/channelling in bed
Rake torque excursions
Poor overflow clarity from flocculant under- or over-dosing, temperature drop or sand carry-over
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hold the bed low enough to limit liquor residence (autoprecipitation) but high enough for underflow density
Respond to rising torque by raising the rake and increasing underflow
Adjust hydroxamate dose to overflow clarity, because it directly sets security filter load
Plan descale rotation and keep the standby settler full of hot liquor if possible
equipment.alternatives: Conventional settlers (low-rate, Dorr multi-tray); deep cone settlers

equipment.name: Settler underflow pumps
equipment.function: Withdraw thickened mud from each settler and pump it to Washer 1.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal slurry pumps, hard-metal, VSD
equipment.why_this_type: Moderate density (30-40 wt%) hot slurry; VSD gives density control.
key_dimensions: Each about 300-450 m3/h at 25-40 m head; 250/200 mm class (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Centrifugal slurry pump. Speed is controlled from underflow density and bed level.
details_to_model: Located in underflow tunnel/under-tank chamber
Suction from cone with 2 knife-gate valves, flush water connection, density gauge on discharge
Recycle line back to feedwell for start-up/bed fluidising
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry
Confined tunnel location
equipment.materials: High-chrome wet-end
common_problems: Line blockage on stop; flush immediately
operating_tips_and_key_points: Flush suction and discharge on every stop
equipment.alternatives: Peristaltic hose pumps for very high density

equipment.name: CCD residue washers W1-W6 (+W7 spare)
equipment.function: Counter-current wash the residue to recover soluble soda and alumina and thicken the final underflow for filtration.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 (W7 installed; rotated into any position for descaling)
equipment.type_selected: High-compression (deep-bed) thickeners with steep floor, flocculant-dilution feedwell, centre-column hydraulic rake drive; W1-W3 roofed and insulated, W4-W6 open top or roofed depending on climate
equipment.why_this_type: Higher underflow density per stage (45-55 wt%) reduces liquor carried forward and therefore the stages and wash water needed. The IAI guidance shows a typical 6-washer CCD arrangement.
key_dimensions: ID about 30-38 m; sidewall about 8-12 m; floor slope about 15-20 deg (engineering estimate)
Feedwell about 5-6 m dia

equipment.working_principle: Each washer is a thickener. Underflow mud from stage n is mixed with overflow from stage n+2 in the feedwell of stage n+1, so the mud always meets progressively weaker liquor as it moves forward, and wash water moves backward. With ideal mixing, the fraction of soluble soda remaining after N stages falls roughly as (1/R)^N, where R is the ratio of overflow liquor to underflow liquor at each stage. Raising underflow density (lower liquor per tonne of mud) improves washing efficiency more than adding wash water. Flocculant (polyacrylate) is added at every feedwell. The final washer, or a dedicated superthickener, delivers dense underflow to residue filtration.

Confined space for descaling (DSP/gibbsite/calcium carbonate scale): mechanical or hydro-blasting
Bund/sump hazards; alkaline spill containment
Rake drive overload or collapse
sources: IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015) - CCD, deep cone washers, high-rate decanters, super thickeners

Balance wash water with evaporation capacity

areas.layout_notes: Thickener farm located immediately downstream of digestion blow-off/flash tanks to minimise pipe length and residence time. Arrangement (engineering estimate): sand cyclone structure and classifier building (about 40 x 25 m) next to the last flash tank; settler feed tank beside it; three settlers (35-40 m) in a row and seven washers (30-38 m) in two rows, centre-to-centre spacing about 45-50 m, connected by a central pipe rack (about 8-10 m high, 2-3 tiers) carrying underflow, overflow, flocculant, wash water, steam and flush lines. Total farm footprint about 450 m x 120 m. Tanks on concrete ring walls with grade-level or slightly sunken underflow chambers/tunnels for pumps (tunnels need ventilation and two escape routes). Bunded to contain 110% of the largest tank, sloping to sumps. Flocculant building (about 30 x 15 m) central to the farm. Security filtration building (A10) adjacent to settlers. Residue filtration (A09) at the downstream end of the washer train, nearest the RSA road/conveyor.
interfaces: A07 Digestion: blow-off slurry from last flash tank (temperature, solids, A/C)
A10 Security filtration: settler overflow (green liquor) and return of filter cake/sluice slurry to settler feed or W1
A09 Residue filtration: W6 underflow forward; filtrate and RSA return water back as wash water
Evaporation area: wash water added here must be evaporated (plant water balance)
Lime/causticisation area: lime for TCA (A10) and any washer causticisation
Utilities: LP steam, condensate, process water, instrument air, power
RSA (A09): washed sand for embankments

areas.purpose: Dewater washed residue to a high-solids filter cake for dry stacking, with cake washing to minimise soluble soda loss and alkalinity. Transport the cake to a lined, engineered residue storage area (dry stack) managed to GISTM/ICOLD/ANCOLD practice, and return alkaline water to the refinery so no untreated discharge leaves site.
areas.process_description:
1) FILTER FEED: W6 underflow (45-55 wt% solids, 3-8 g/L soda as Na2CO3) is collected in an agitated filter feed tank (about 6-12 h buffer).
2) PRESS FILTRATION: Recessed-chamber membrane filter presses are filled by feed pumps at rising pressure up to about 7-10 bar g (engineering estimate). The cake is optionally washed with hot water to displace residual liquor, membrane-squeezed at about 15-16 bar g, and air-blown. Plates are then opened and the cake drops onto collecting belt conveyors. Cake reaches about 70-78 wt% solids (22-30% moisture). Published references: press filter cake >70% solids (IAI 2015); Alunorte press cake about 22% moisture; CHALCO Zhongzhou 27-30% moisture with 600-800 m2 plate area presses; typical 23-27% moisture (Wikipedia, Red mud).
3) FILTRATE: Filtrate (low soda) is collected and returned as wash water to the CCD (08-TK-021). This closes the soda loop.
4) CAKE HANDLING: Conveyors take the cake to a truck loadout bin. Articulated dump trucks haul it 2-5 km (engineering estimate) to the active RSA cell.
5) DRY STACKING AND MUD FARMING: Cake is spread in thin layers (about 0.3-0.5 m) by dozer. It is turned and conditioned by amphirol and/or harrow to speed drying and atmospheric carbonation, then compacted. Thin-layer stacking uses 0.3-0.5 m layers dried to about 70% solids before the next layer, and EGA Al Taweelah places residue in 300 mm layers with 5 m lifts (IAI 2015).
6) NEUTRALISATION / ALKALINITY REDUCTION, base case: (a) cake washing in the press; (b) atmospheric carbonation of the stack surface during farming, where CO2 + 2OH- -> CO3 2- + H2O and Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O -> 2NaHCO3, with tricalcium aluminate and other alkaline solids buffering pH so it falls only gradually; (c) all lake water and underdrainage is returned to the refinery. Option, with a CO2 source and a provision on the layout: CO2 carbonation of filter feed (the Alcoa Kwinana concept; literature reports residue pH reduced from about 13 to about 10.5 using CO2 from a neighbouring ammonia plant, not retrieved this session). Option for a coastal site: seawater neutralisation of residue or lake water. Mg2+ and Ca2+ in seawater precipitate hydroxide and carbonate alkalinity as brucite, hydrotalcite and calcite, giving pH 8-8.5 (IAI 2015; QAL supernatant <8.5 pH, <30 mg/L solids, <5 mg/L Al, 50 m diffuser).
7) RSA: The stack is built in cells on a composite-lined base (HDPE geomembrane over compacted low-permeability clay), with a sand/gravel underdrainage layer and slotted pipes to sumps, perimeter starter embankments of compacted fill and later compacted residue, upstream or centreline raises in 2-5 m lifts, a decant/stormwater pond (residue lake), seepage interception and groundwater monitoring bores. Governance follows the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management (GISTM, 2020: 6 topic areas, 15 principles, 77 requirements), ICOLD bulletins on tailings dams and ANCOLD Guidelines on Tailings Dams. Consequence classification uses GISTM Annex 2.
8) Wet disposal (lagooning at 18-22% solids, IAI 2015), the historical Indian and global practice, is NOT selected because of footprint, seepage and dam-break risk (Ajka 2010: about 1 Mm3 released, 10 deaths).

equipment.why_this_type: Gives the highest cake solids (>70%) for a safe, trafficable dry stack, as GISTM and IAI best practice prefer. Proven at Alunorte and many Chinese plants. Rotary vacuum drum filters (about 60% solids) need more farming.

Cake thickness about 35-45 mm
Loaded mass about 200-300 t
equipment.working_principle: A pack of polypropylene plates is closed hydraulically against a fixed head. Each pair of plates forms a chamber lined with filter cloth. Slurry is pumped in. Liquor passes through the cloth and plate drainage surface to filtrate ports, and solids build up as cake until the chambers are full. Alternate membrane plates are then inflated with water to about 15-16 bar to squeeze the cake. An optional wash displaces residual liquor, then compressed air blows the core and cake. The press opens, a plate shifter separates the plates one by one or in groups, and the cake falls through open drip trays onto conveyors below. Cloths are washed with high-pressure spray about every 10-30 cycles.
details_to_model: Fixed head (with feed, filtrate, wash, air and squeeze-water nozzles) and moving head on rollers; long hydraulic main cylinder and power pack at the closing end
Overhead twin beams (or side bars) carrying about 150 plates; alternating chamber/membrane plates (light grey PP) with cloths and visible corner filtrate ports
Automatic plate shifter carriage(s) running along the beam; overhead travelling cloth-washer gantry with spray bar
Bomb-bay drip trays (hinged doors) under the plate pack, hydraulic actuators
Light curtains/safety gates along both sides, walkways at plate level, emergency stops
Filtrate collection manifolds and sight glasses (open discharge taps on older styles)
Squeeze-water and blow-air manifolds with automated valves; instrument panels

Building: steel-framed, about 120 x 35 m, height about 25 m, overhead crane 09-CR-001 for plate change, plate laydown area
hazards_and_safety: Crush/pinch between plates and moving head: guarding, light curtains, LOTO, no hands in pack

Alkaline slurry spray from cloth leaks ('squirts') and hot filtrate
Working at height on press floors; open cake chutes

Noise from air blow and plate shifting
sources: IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015): press filters >70% solids, Alunorte 22% moisture, Zhongzhou 600-800 m2, >95% efficiency
Wikipedia 'Red mud': filter cake 23-27% moisture, can be washed
equipment.materials: Steel frame (painted), polypropylene plates, PP multifilament/monofilament cloth; EPDM/TPE membranes
equipment.drive_and_power: Hydraulic power pack about 30-55 kW per press; plate shifter about 5-11 kW; cloth washer HP pump separate

areas.purpose: Remove the last fine residue particles (iron and titanium minerals, DSP) from the settler overflow so that the pregnant liquor sent to precipitation is near solids-free. areas.process_description:
1) Settler overflow (green liquor, about 10-50 mg/L solids, about 100 degC) flows by gravity to the unfiltered liquor tank. Security filter feed pumps deliver it to a bank of horizontal pressure leaf filters (Kelly type).
2) FILTER AID: Tricalcium aluminate (TCA, Ca3Al2(OH)12, also written 3CaO.Al2O3.6H2O) is made on site by reacting slaked lime with aluminate liquor: 3Ca(OH)2 + 2Al(OH)4- -> Ca3[Al(OH)6]2 + 2OH-. TCA forms hard hexagonal or cubic crystals that make a porous, incompressible precoat and cake.
3) CYCLE (engineering estimate): (a) fill the filter with liquor; (b) precoat by recirculating TCA slurry until the filtrate is clear (about 10-20 min); (c) filter with TCA body feed until differential pressure reaches about 3-4 bar or the time limit (about 4-12 h); (d) drain the heel back to the feed tank; (e) sluice cake off the leaves with dilute liquor/wash liquor sprays while the leaves rotate or the sluice header oscillates; (f) send sluiced cake slurry to the cake tank and pump it back to the settler feed tank or Washer 1, so residue and TCA leave via the CCD; (g) return to service. Periodically the leaves are pulled and cloths descaled or replaced.
4) Filtrate turbidity is monitored on each filter. Filtered pregnant liquor goes to the filtered liquor tank and on to heat interchange/precipitation.
5) Target filtrate solids < about 5-10 mg/L, typically < 5 mg/L (engineering estimate). The trade-off is TCA dosing: lime consumption plus a small alumina loss to TCA.

equipment.working_principle: Liquor fills the shell around the leaves. Under pressure it passes through the cloth on both faces of each leaf into the leaf's internal drainage space and leaves through the leaf outlet nozzle into a common filtrate manifold. The TCA precoat forms the true filtration surface: a rigid, permeable layer that traps fine residue and keeps the cloth from blinding. Body feed keeps the growing cake porous. When pressure drop reaches the limit, the filter is isolated and drained, and the cake is sluiced off with liquor sprays as a slurry. The leaves are then precoated again. Several filters in staggered cycles give continuous overall flow.
