open_questions: Research limitation: WebSearch was disabled in this session and most vendor and journal sites could not be fetched. Only the IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015 PDF), Wikipedia 'Red mud' and the GISTM landing page were retrieved. Every other number is marked 'engineering estimate' or cites literature from prior knowledge (Power/Graefe/Klauber 2011; Kwinana carbonation; Kelly/TCA practice). SME verification is requested, especially for thickener diameters and loadings, Kelly filter area and flux, and press cycle times.

Bauxite basis conflict: the provisional spec (45-50% Al2O3, about 40% available) matches India East Coast bauxite, not Darling Range (about 30% available, high quartz sand). Sand circuit sizing and residue tonnage depend strongly on which ore is chosen.
Site location (coastal or inland) decides whether seawater neutralisation is an option. Base case is inland: dry stack with atmospheric carbonation, and CO2 carbonation as a future provision.
Climate (monsoon or Mediterranean) drives RSA water balance, pond size and wet-season trafficability; a hydrological basis is needed.
Residue filtration technology: membrane filter presses selected; alternatives are vacuum drum filters (Alcoa/Worsley style) or paste thickening. Confirm with the owner's risk appetite under GISTM.
Applicable national regulations (e.g. India CPCB red mud guidelines, Western Australian DMIRS/ANCOLD) and the GISTM consequence classification need to be defined.
Security filtration: Kelly leaf filters selected; Alcoa-style sand filters or candle filters could be preferred. Confirm against product Fe specification.
Residue reuse (cement, iron recovery, road base) could reduce RSA volume; not included in base design.

areas.purpose: Cool polished pregnant (green) liquor from ~100-106 degC to the precipitation fill temperature (72-78 degC for the agglomeration stage), recovering the heat into cold spent liquor that returns to evaporation and digestion. A11 also holds the spent-liquor surge tank, a cooling-water trim cooler for tight control of the fill temperature, and the hot-caustic clean-in-place (CIP) system for the exchangers. The temperature set here is the main lever on precipitation supersaturation, agglomeration and particle-size control.
areas.process_description: 1) Polished pregnant liquor (PL) arrives from the A10 security/polishing filtration filtrate tank at 100-106 degC. Typical composition is C ~240-250 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C 0.68-0.72 and solids <10-15 mg/L. Four feed pumps (3 operating, 1 standby) send it through duplex basket strainers. 2) The PL passes counter-current through banks of gasketed plate heat exchangers (PHEs). Spent liquor from the A11 spent-liquor tank (55-62 degC) is on the cold side. Six PHEs carry the duty and two are offline at any time for hot-caustic cleaning. The PL leaves at 76-82 degC and the spent liquor at 82-90 degC. The duty is ~95-110 MW for a PL flow of ~3,000-3,300 m3/h (engineering estimate: rho ~1.30 t/m3, cp ~3.2-3.3 kJ/kg.K, dT ~25-28 K). 3) Cooling below the dew point of the regenerative exchangers is done in a cooling-water trim cooler (1 operating + 1 standby). It sets the agglomeration fill temperature to ±0.5-1 degC. The fill temperature is a cascade master over both the trim-cooler cooling water and a PHE bypass valve. 4) Chemistry: as PL cools, the gibbsite equilibrium solubility falls steeply, so the liquor becomes supersaturated. The relative supersaturation is (A - A*)/C. Some gibbsite autoprecipitates (spontaneous nucleation) on the cooled PL-side plate surfaces, so the PL side of the PHEs scales with gibbsite in hours to days. The spent side is undersaturated in gibbsite as it is heated and scales much more slowly, mainly with DSP or sodium aluminosilicate and oxalate. Gibbsite scale is redissolved by circulating hot, low-A/C caustic (C ~250-300 g/L, 85-95 degC) for 2-6 h on a rotating schedule. 5) The heated spent liquor goes to A? Evaporation and to digestion slurry heating (interface). 6) Low-temperature (gibbsitic) and high-temperature (boehmitic) plants differ only slightly here. In a high-temperature plant the PL leaves the digestion flash train and clarification at a similar ~100-106 degC, so the interchange duty is similar. Its higher digestion A/C (0.72-0.75+) gives a higher precipitation driving force, and European high-caustic plants cool further (to ~60-65 degC fill) to make floury or high-yield hydrate.

equipment.name: Pregnant liquor heat-interchange feed pumps
equipment.function: Take polished PL from the A10 filtrate tank and push it through the strainers, PHEs and trim cooler up to the precipitator inlet box at the top of the agglomeration tanks (~32-35 m).
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal process pump (ISO 5199 / ASME B73.1-type heavy duty), back pull-out, double mechanical seal with flush (API 682 Plan 53/54-type) or a dynamic expeller seal, VSD driven
equipment.why_this_type: Clear liquor (solids <15 mg/L), so a process pump is more efficient than a slurry pump. A VSD gives flow control without throttling across the scaling-prone PHEs.
key_dimensions: Discharge DN350-400, suction DN450-500 (engineering estimate)
Baseplate ~4.5 m x 1.5 m incl. motor (engineering estimate)
Motor ~250-355 kW, 4-pole, 6.6 kV or 3.3 kV (engineering estimate)

equipment.working_principle: A centrifugal impeller adds velocity to the liquor and the volute converts it to pressure. The pumps run in parallel on a common discharge header, and the number running plus the VSD speed is set to hold the PL flow setpoint coming from the plant-wide liquor balance. Each pump has a minimum-flow recirculation line back to the source tank to avoid overheating at low flow. The liquor is near saturation and above 100 degC, so suction pressure must be kept above vapour pressure (NPSH margin) and dead legs avoided, because cooling liquor in stagnant pipe scales with gibbsite. Mechanical seals need clean, compatible flush liquid (condensate or barrier fluid) so caustic crystals do not form on the seal faces.
details_to_model: 4 pumps in a row on a concrete plinth inside a bunded pump bay, ~3.5 m centres

Each pump: suction isolation knife-gate or butterfly valve (DN500), suction spool with flanged temporary strainer, eccentric reducer flat-on-top, pump casing, coupling guard (yellow), TEFC motor with terminal box and VSD cable tray
Discharge: check valve, butterfly/gate isolation valve with gear operator and handwheel, pressure gauge plus pressure transmitter, min-flow line DN150 with control valve back to the tank
Seal plan pot (vertical cylinder ~0.3 m dia x 0.8 m) on a stand beside each pump, with level gauge and small tubing
Casing drain valves to a trench drain covered by grating
Common discharge header DN600 rising to the pipe rack with a magnetic flowmeter (full-bore, lined)
Lagging (aluminium-jacketed mineral wool) on suction/discharge piping for personnel protection (>60 degC)
Spray shields (flange guards) on every flange in caustic service
Local start/stop/E-stop station on a post beside each motor
Monorail or mobile-crane access for motor and rotating-assembly removal
hazards_and_safety: Hot (100+ degC) caustic liquor: severe alkali burns plus thermal burns; it can flash if released at low pressure. Require face shield, chemical goggles, PVC/neoprene gauntlets and caustic-resistant clothing
Flange guards on all flanged joints; safety shower and eyewash within 10 s / ~15 m (ANSI Z358.1)
Isolation: double block-and-bleed or positive isolation (spade) before opening; drain and flush to sump
Rotating equipment: coupling guards (ISO 14120), LOTO at the MCC/VSD
Hot surfaces: personnel-protection lagging
instrumentation_and_control: Bearing temperature and vibration (online or portable route)
FIT on common header (magflow), FIC to VSD
equipment.materials: Casing ductile iron or carbon steel; impeller and wear rings CD4MCuN duplex or 316 SS; shaft sleeve 316/duplex; seal faces SiC/SiC. Carbon steel piping is suitable for caustic below ~ the NACE SP0403 PWHT line; check welds and stress relieve where required.
common_problems: Gibbsite scale in stagnant branches and min-flow lines
Seal failure from crystallisation
Cavitation if the source tank level is low (hot liquor near saturation pressure)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never leave a standby pump with its isolations open and no flow, or it scales solid; flush it with condensate or rotate duty weekly

equipment.name: Liquor strainers ahead of PHEs
equipment.function: Protect the narrow PHE channels from scale flakes, gasket debris and fine hydrate. 11-ST-001/002 (1 operating + 1 standby, automatic backwash) serve spent liquor; 11-ST-003/004 (duplex basket) serve PL.
equipment.type_selected: Spent liquor: automatic self-cleaning (backwash/rotating-arm) strainer, ~1.5-3 mm screen. PL: duplex basket strainer with changeover valve.
equipment.why_this_type: The spent liquor carries thickener-overflow fines and scale flakes, so continuous self-cleaning avoids frequent manual entry. The PL is already polished, so a manual duplex basket is adequate as a guard.
key_dimensions: Body DN500-600, ~1.0-1.2 m dia x 2.0-2.5 m tall (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Liquor passes through a cylindrical wedge-wire or perforated screen, and particles larger than the aperture stay on the screen. In the self-cleaning type a rotating suction arm or a short reverse flow sweeps the screen when the differential pressure reaches its setpoint, and the debris goes to a drain or the spent-liquor tank. The duplex PL basket is switched manually to the clean side so the dirty basket can be removed after isolation and draining.
details_to_model: Vertical cylindrical body on legs, top bolted cover with davit arm for lifting the basket (duplex type: two bodies side by side joined by a 3-way changeover plug valve with lever)
Self-cleaning type: gear motor on top, backwash outlet DN100 with actuated ball valve, differential-pressure transmitter tubing across inlet and outlet
Drain and vent valves; flange guards
Inlet and outlet flanges in line with the header
hazards_and_safety: Opening a basket that is still pressurised or hot can spray hot caustic: verify zero pressure and drain first
Heavy basket lifting: use the davit
instrumentation_and_control: dPIT across each strainer, alarm high
equipment.materials: Carbon steel body (caustic-service welding procedures); 316 SS screen

equipment.name: Pregnant liquor / spent liquor heat interchangers (regenerative PHEs)
equipment.function: Cool PL from 100-106 to 76-82 degC while heating spent liquor from 55-62 to 82-90 degC. This recovers ~95-110 MW that would otherwise be rejected to cooling towers.
equipment.type_selected: Large gasketed plate-and-frame heat exchangers (single-pass counter-current, 1-pass/1-pass, large-port plates ~2-3.5 m2 each), plates 316L SS, peroxide-cured EPDM clip-on gaskets; frame designed to ASME VIII Div 1 / PED
equipment.why_this_type: PHEs give high U (thin turbulent channels) and close approach temperatures (~10-20 K) in a compact footprint, and they open for inspection. Cleaning by hot caustic recirculation is fast. A 2-of-8 standby allows continuous cleaning rotation. Australian low-temperature refineries commonly use PHEs for this duty; check this with the SME. ALTERNATIVE: multi-stage vacuum flash cooling of PL (see 'alternatives').
equipment.alternatives: (a) Vacuum flash coolers: 4-6 flash vessels in series, each taking ~4-6 K off the PL. The flash vapour condenses in shell-and-tube spent-liquor heaters (or a barometric condenser on the last stage), and the last stages run under vacuum (~0.25-0.45 bar abs, allowing for the liquor boiling-point elevation of ~5-8 K). Advantages: no heat-transfer surface in contact with supersaturated PL, so no gibbsite fouling; the small evaporation (~1-3% of water) concentrates the liquor and slightly raises yield. Disadvantages: large vessels and vacuum systems, a poorer approach temperature, and condensate that must be recovered. It is widely used in older and high-temperature (European) plants and is a valid design choice. (b) Spiral heat exchangers: tolerate solids better but cost more per m2 at this scale. (c) Shell-and-tube: low U with viscous liquor, so very large. All values are engineering estimates.
key_dimensions: Effective area ~700-950 m2 per unit; total installed ~5,600-7,600 m2 (engineering estimate: Q~100 MW, LMTD ~18-20 K, design U ~1,000-1,500 W/m2.K incl. fouling)
Frame ~3.5-4.2 m high x 1.3-1.6 m wide x 6-9 m long incl. carrying bar (engineering estimate)
Port size DN400-500 (engineering estimate)
~300-450 plates per unit at ~2.2-3 m2 per plate (engineering estimate)
Units arranged in 2 banks of 4, ~3 m apart, with a ~5 m service aisle for plate removal

engineering estimate; strongly dependent on PL A/C and temperature

equipment.working_principle: A PHE is a pack of thin corrugated stainless plates clamped between a fixed frame plate and a movable pressure plate by long tie bolts. Gaskets in each plate groove route the two liquors into alternate channels, so every plate has hot PL on one side and cold spent liquor on the other, flowing in opposite directions (counter-current). The chevron corrugations make the flow turbulent at low velocity, giving high heat-transfer coefficients and letting the outlet of one stream approach the inlet of the other within a few kelvin. Because the PL becomes more supersaturated as it cools, gibbsite nucleates and grows on the PL-side plates, U falls and the pressure drop rises. The unit is therefore valved out and hot, low-ratio caustic is circulated to dissolve the scale, then it is returned to service. Plate packs can be opened by sliding the pressure plate back along the carrying bar for inspection, gasket replacement or off-line high-pressure jetting.
details_to_model: Fixed frame plate (thick painted carbon steel, ~250 mm) with 4 corner nozzles (DN400-500): PL in at top and out at bottom, spent in at bottom and out at top (counter-current). Each nozzle has a flanged spool, a butterfly isolation valve with gear operator, and a flange guard
Movable pressure plate with roller hanging from the top carrying bar; bottom guide bar; 12-20 tie bolts (M48-M64) with nuts, bolt protection sleeves
Plate pack visible as a ribbed block of hundreds of thin plates (stainless, grey) with slightly visible black/green gasket edges
Perforated stainless or polycarbonate spray shield wrapped around the plate pack (mandatory)
End support column at the far end of the carrying bar
Drain valves at bottom ports and vent valves at top ports; CIP connections (DN150 tees with valves) on PL inlet and outlet
Temperature elements (thermowells) and pressure gauges/transmitters on all 4 nozzles; dP transmitter across PL side
Drip tray / bunded slab beneath, sloping to a trench
Pipe manifolds: PL and spent headers DN600-900 running along the bank on low sleepers; isolation valves accessible from grade or a low platform
Clear withdrawal space beside each pack for plate removal; mobile plate-handling trolley
hazards_and_safety: Gasket blow-out or plate crack sprays hot caustic up to several metres: spray shields fitted, exclusion while bringing units online
Over-pressure from blocked-in liquor heated by the other side (thermal expansion): thermal relief valve on each side when isolated
CIP caustic is stronger and hot: same PPE as for PL
Stored energy in tie bolts: only trained fitters tighten or loosen, using the vendor's torque/dimension sequence
Hot surfaces >60 degC: shields act as personnel protection
instrumentation_and_control: TIT on all four nozzles of each unit; PL outlet temperature to the fill-temperature cascade
dPIT on the PL side as the fouling indicator, triggering CIP scheduling
FIT on PL and spent headers; flow split by butterfly control valves
Automated on/off butterfly valves for unit isolation in sequence-controlled CIP (PLC)
equipment.materials: Plates 316L SS, 0.6-0.8 mm (check caustic SCC margin; nickel or 904L for hotter duty). Gaskets EPDM peroxide-cured (caustic resistant to ~150 degC). Frame painted carbon steel. Nozzle linings/sleeves 316L.
common_problems: Gibbsite fouling on the PL side (rapid)
DSP or oxalate scale on the spent side (slow)
Gasket hardening or leaks after many CIP cycles
Plate cracking from caustic SCC or from pressure shocks
Fines from thickener overflow plugging the inlet port area
operating_tips_and_key_points: Fill temperature is the precipitation 'accelerator pedal'. Change it slowly (≤1 degC per shift), because a sudden drop causes nucleation (a 'fines event')
Track U per unit and clean on a trend, not only on a schedule
Always warm up or cool down a returning unit slowly to avoid thermal shock to the gaskets
equipment.drive_and_power: None (static); automated valves are pneumatic or electric

Spent liquor is undersaturated with respect to gibbsite at higher temperature, but it can still deposit fine hydrate and oxalate, so the tank is periodically emptied and cleaned. equipment.name: PHE hot-caustic clean-in-place (CIP) system
equipment.function: Dissolve gibbsite (and some DSP or oxalate) scale from the PHEs offline by circulating hot, strong, low-A/C caustic, then return the spent wash to the liquor circuit.
equipment.type_selected: Insulated agitated CIP tank (~150-300 m3) with steam-heated plate or shell-and-tube heater, two centrifugal CIP pumps, automated valve manifold to each exchanger
equipment.why_this_type: Gibbsite dissolves rapidly in hot caustic far from saturation. In-place cleaning avoids opening plate packs (gasket damage, long downtime).

equipment.working_principle: An exchanger is first isolated on both sides and drained to the spent-liquor tank. Hot caustic is then circulated through the fouled PL side, often counter to normal flow, until the A/C rise in the return flattens, which shows the gibbsite has dissolved. The used solution, now enriched in alumina, is bled to the spent-liquor or digestion circuit so no caustic is lost. The exchanger is flushed with spent liquor and returned to service. Some plants occasionally use an inhibited acid wash for stubborn DSP or oxalate scale; this requires a separate procedure and neutralisation.

areas.layout_notes: A11 sits between A10 (clarification/polishing) and A12 (precipitation), ideally under or beside the main liquor pipe rack, so the PL header runs short and level to the agglomeration tanks. Proposed footprint ~70 m x 40 m (engineering estimate): (1) a bunded pump bay with an open-sided shed and 10-20 t crane (PL and spent pumps, 8 pumps in two rows); (2) a PHE bay with 2 rows of 4 interchangers plus 2 trim coolers, on a bunded, sloped concrete slab with 5 m service aisles and mobile-crane access for plate handling; (3) the CIP skid and tank; (4) the spent-liquor tank (~24 m dia) in its own bund on the precipitation side. Headers DN600-900 run on a 2-level pipe rack (elevation ~6 m and ~9 m) to the precipitation distribution box at the top of the agglomeration tanks (~32-35 m). The spent-liquor tank receives the tertiary thickener overflow by gravity, so it should sit lower than and near A13. Safety showers and eyewashes are placed at each pump row and at the PHE bay entrances.

areas.purpose: Crystallise gibbsite (Al(OH)3) from the cooled, supersaturated pregnant liquor onto recycled seed, to (a) recover alumina (yield ~75-88 g/L Al2O3, design ~80 g/L), (b) produce hydrate with the size distribution, strength and soda needed for sandy smelter-grade alumina, and (c) return spent liquor (A/C ~0.35-0.40) to the liquor circuit. Design: Australian-style two-stage process. A hot agglomeration stage with a low charge of fine seed is followed by a growth stage with a high charge of coarse seed and interstage cooling.
areas.process_description: Chemistry: Na+ + Al(OH)4- (aq) -> Al(OH)3 (s, gibbsite) + Na+ + OH-. This is the reverse of gibbsite digestion. It is slow and seeded, and is driven by supersaturation (A - A*), where A* is the gibbsite equilibrium solubility. A* falls with temperature and rises with caustic concentration (Rosenberg and Healy 1996 solubility model). The growth rate is roughly second order in supersaturation, with an activation energy of ~60 kJ/mol (Misra and White 1971). Crystallisation is mildly exothermic, so the slurry must be actively cooled to keep the falling temperature profile. Three mechanisms act together: (i) secondary nucleation, which creates new fine particles (<1-5 µm) and is favoured by low temperature and high supersaturation; (ii) agglomeration, in which fine particles cement together into ~20-60 µm agglomerates and which is favoured by high temperature (>70 degC), high supersaturation and low seed surface area; (iii) growth, which is layer deposition on existing surfaces and controls the yield. STEP 1, agglomeration stage (2 lines x 3 tanks): cooled PL at 72-78 degC from A11 is split equally to the two lines at a distribution box. Washed fine seed from A13 (fine seed charge ~30-80 g/L, engineering estimate) is added to tank AG-1. High supersaturation with little seed area promotes agglomeration of the fines into strong mosaic particles. Residence ~6-9 h (engineering estimate). STEP 2, growth stage (2 lines x 12 tanks): coarse seed from A13 (filtered cake repulped in a small PL stream; charge ~350-600 g/L of PL, ~10-25 m2/L seed area, engineering estimate) enters G-1. Slurry flows through 12 tanks in series by bottom-draw airlifts and top launders. Two interstage cooling stations per line take the temperature from ~70-74 degC at G-1 to ~56-60 degC at G-12, maintaining supersaturation as A falls and maximising yield. Growth residence ~25-30 h (engineering estimate). Total ~33-38 h. STEP 3: slurry from G-12 (A/C ~0.35-0.40, solids ~550-700 g/L, ~33-40 % w/w) gravitates to A13 classification. A crystal growth modifier (CGM, a surfactant/oil emulsion) may be dosed to suppress fines and coarsen the product. Precipitation needs no extra heat: the falling temperature profile is set by A11 and the interstage coolers. Contrast with European 'floury' or high-yield practice: higher caustic (~300 g/L), lower fill temperature (~60-65 degC), single stage, finer product. Boehmitic (high-temperature) plants use the same precipitation principles but can reach a higher PL A/C, so yield is higher for the same spent A/C. One tank per line is normally bypassed in rotation for descaling.

equipment.name: Agglomeration precipitators (AG-1..3, Line A = 001-003, Line B = 004-006)
equipment.function: Provide 6-9 h of hot, agitated contact between fresh supersaturated PL and a low charge of fine seed, so that fines cement into strong agglomerates that become the cores of the product particles.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical, flat-bottomed (with grout/concrete fillet) carbon-steel tank, 14 m ID x ~31 m shell, fixed cone roof with agitator bridge; top-entry mechanical agitator (12-AG); bottom-draw airlift transfer
equipment.why_this_type: Large (~4,500 m3) tanks keep the tank count and piping manageable for ~3,000 m3/h PL. Mechanical hydrofoil agitation keeps the high solids suspended at ~15-30 W/m3 and needs less energy than full airlift agitation. Flat bottoms with fillets suit large mechanically agitated tanks; conical bottoms suit air-agitated or airlift designs (alternative).
equipment.alternatives: Pachuca or air-agitated precipitators with a central draft tube and airlift (older Pechiney/Alcan-type practice; no rotating parts in the slurry but high air consumption and a conical bottom). Draft-tube mechanical agitation (impeller in a central draft tube) gives strong axial circulation at lower power but the draft tube scales. Gravity-overflow series (no airlifts) can short-circuit coarse particles.
key_dimensions: ID ~14.0 m; shell height ~31 m; working level ~29-29.5 m; working volume ~4,400-4,600 m3 (engineering estimate)
Roof cone ~1:12 rising to an agitator bridge at ~32-33 m above grade
Shell thickness ~28-32 mm bottom strake tapering to ~10-12 mm top (API 650 one-foot method, SG ~1.55, engineering estimate)
Bottom fillet: 45 deg grout or concrete ring ~1.0-1.5 m high at the shell/floor junction to prevent dead zones
Tank centres ~18 m (4 m clear between tanks for stair towers and launders)

operating_parameters.value: 72-78 (drops ~1-3 K through the stage from heat loss vs heat of crystallisation)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (3 x 4,500 m3 / ~1,550-1,650 m3/h per line)

equipment.working_principle: PL arriving at 72-78 degC is strongly supersaturated, and only a small surface area of fine seed is offered. Gibbsite deposits quickly on the fines and, because the particle number is high and the supersaturation is high, colliding particles are bridged by new gibbsite and 'cemented' into agglomerates. A higher temperature favours this cementing over new nucleation. The agitator keeps everything suspended with enough shear to make particles collide but not so much that the young agglomerates break apart. Slurry leaves each tank through a bottom-draw airlift into the launder feeding the next tank, so coarse particles cannot accumulate in the bottom. After the third tank the slurry passes to growth tank G-1, where the coarse seed charge is added.
details_to_model: Shell with horizontal strakes ~2.5 m high (12-13 strakes), external vertical stiffeners not needed; wind girder near the top

Cone roof with a central steel agitator bridge (two box girders spanning the full 14 m, supported by the shell) carrying the gearbox and motor; bridge has grating deck, handrails and toe-boards (AS 1657 / ISO 14122)

Roof: 2-3 DN900 roof hatches (descaling access and inspection), slurry inlet box/chute from the launder (~1.5 x 1.5 m) entering through the roof, PL and seed inlet nozzles DN600 for AG-1, radar level nozzle with a large-diameter stilling well or non-contact radar, 2 vents DN400 with goosenecks

Shell: 2 x large access doors at grade (~1.2 x 1.8 m oval or 1,500 mm round, hinged, bolted) for descaling and excavator entry, 180 deg apart; 1-2 DN900 manholes at ~15 m reachable from the stair tower; drain/emptying nozzle DN300 at the floor with knife-gate valve; 3-4 thermowells at heights ~3, 12, 20, 27 m; sample points at mid-height with DN50 ball valves inside a splash box

Airlift riser (12-AL) pipe DN600-900 running inside the tank against the wall from ~0.5-1 m above the floor to above the liquid level, then discharging through the shell into the launder box; air injection pipe DN50-100 down the outside with a flanged connection and valve station
Bypass launder connection (gate or flap) for taking the tank out of series
Overflow (emergency) nozzle DN600 at ~29.8 m to a closed overflow pipe running to the bund
Wall internal baffles: 4 x full-height baffles ~1.0-1.2 m wide (T/12) offset ~0.15 m from the wall, at 90 deg spacing, braced to the shell
Spiral stair or shared stair tower between tank pairs, with landings; roof perimeter handrail; earthing bosses; nameplate
External surface: uninsulated or partially insulated (site-dependent); many plants leave precipitators uninsulated to aid cooling (engineering judgement)
Concrete ringwall foundation with oiled-sand or bitumen bedding, under-floor leak detection telltales; bunded tank farm with sumps
Visual wear and scale: buff/white hydrate crust on the inside walls, launders and roof hatches when modelling the 'cleaning' state
hazards_and_safety: Descaling entry is a confined space with falling scale slabs: permit, positive isolation (spades on all inlets, airlift air isolated and vented, agitator LOTO and gearbox locked), forced ventilation, continuous gas test (generally O2 only), standby person, rescue tripod at the roof hatch
Hot caustic slurry at 70-78 degC: chemical and thermal burns; full caustic PPE at sample points and roof hatches
Working at height (>30 m) on roofs and bridges: handrails, no climbing outside guards, permits for roof hatch work
Tank overflow or launder spill of thousands of m3 of caustic slurry: bund to 110% of the largest tank, high-high level trip on the feed
Hydrate splash makes walkways slippery; housekeeping
Do not open the bottom access doors of a non-empty tank (pressure of ~30 m of slurry)
instrumentation_and_control: Radar level LIT plus high-high level switch
Slurry density or solids: nuclear density gauge on the airlift discharge or periodic manual sampling
Agitator power and torque monitoring (scale build-up and sanding indicator)
Lab samples every 2-4 h for A/C, solids, PSD (laser diffraction), seed surface area
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A516-70 / AS 1548 PT460 / IS 2062 E350). Caustic SCC: at 70-78 degC in ~15-18 wt% NaOH-equivalent liquor, check against the NACE SP0403 caustic soda service chart and stress-relieve nozzle and attachment welds if required. Corrosion allowance 3 mm. Agitator wetted parts CS with 3-6 mm corrosion/erosion allowance.
common_problems: Gibbsite scale on walls, baffles, roof underside, launders and agitator shafts/blades. It builds ~100-300 mm/yr (engineering estimate), cuts working volume and unbalances agitators. Tanks are descaled every ~12-36 months (engineering estimate) by high-pressure water jetting (UHP ~1,000-2,500 bar), mechanical breaking (excavator with hammer) or caustic dissolution
Sanding: solids settle if the agitator trips and can 'bog' the impeller, so restarting needs a high-torque drive or air lancing
Short-circuiting if baffles or airlifts fail
Fines nucleation events from too-low temperature or a high-A/C PL spike
Oxalate co-precipitation (destabilised oxalate) gives fine, high-soda hydrate
operating_tips_and_key_points: Agglomeration needs high temperature AND low seed surface. Adding too much fine seed or running too cold gives growth or nucleation instead of agglomeration
Never stop agitation on a full tank unless it is planned: if the agitator trips, start emptying or air-lancing within minutes to hours
PSD (particle size distribution) moves in slow cycles of weeks. Respond to trends with small changes to fine seed charge and fill temperature
sources: Misra C., White E.T., 'Kinetics of crystallization of aluminium trihydroxide from seeded caustic aluminate solutions', Chem. Eng. Prog. Symp. Ser. 67(110), 1971
Ilievski D., White E.T., 'Agglomeration during precipitation: agglomeration mechanism identification for Al(OH)3 crystals in stirred caustic aluminate solutions', Chem. Eng. Sci. 49 (1994)
Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry
Donaldson D., Raahauge B.E. (eds), Essential Readings in Light Metals Vol. 1 Alumina and Bauxite, TMS/Wiley 2013 (compiled Light Metals precipitation papers)
Engineering estimate for all sizes and counts

equipment.name: Growth precipitators (G-1..G-12; Line A = 007-018, Line B = 019-030)
equipment.function: Grow hydrate on a large coarse-seed surface over ~25-30 h with falling temperature, to reach the target yield (A/C to ~0.35-0.40) and build product particle size.
equipment.type_selected: Same as agglomeration tanks: 14 m ID x ~31 m, ~4,500 m3 working, flat bottom with fillet, cone roof, top-entry mechanical agitator, bottom-draw airlift transfer
equipment.why_this_type: Standardising on one tank size and one agitator size minimises spares and lets tanks be repurposed. Residence ~25-30 h at ~1,850-2,100 m3/h slurry per line needs ~11 x 4,500 m3 per line.
equipment.alternatives: Fewer, larger tanks (~6,000-8,000 m3) reduce the count but need larger agitators and footprints. A single-stage 'European' layout instead of two-stage.
key_dimensions: As 12-TK-001..006: ID ~14 m, shell ~31 m, working ~4,500 m3 (engineering estimate)
Total precipitation working volume ~135,000 m3 (30 tanks) (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: design basis; yield = C x (A/C_PL - A/C_spent), e.g. 245 x (0.70-0.37) = 81 g/L

equipment.working_principle: In growth the seed surface is large, so the supersaturation is spent mainly on deposition onto existing particles rather than on new nuclei or agglomeration. The growth rate falls as A approaches A*, so the slurry is cooled in steps (interstage cooling). This lowers A* and restores the driving force, so the tail of the train still precipitates. Since the rate also falls with temperature (activation energy ~60 kJ/mol), there is an economic optimum: too cold and growth is slow and nucleation and soda pick-up increase; too hot and the yield is lost. Slurry moves tank to tank by airlifts drawing from near the floor, so the oldest, coarsest particles move forward and a plug-flow-like residence-time distribution builds up over 12 tanks in series.
details_to_model: Identical tank model to agglomeration (reuse asset) with different inlet arrangements: G-1 has coarse seed inlet DN500 and slurry inlet box; G-4 and G-8 have an interstage cooler suction nozzle DN500-600 on the shell at ~1.5-2.5 m above the floor with knife-gate valve; G-5 and G-9 have the cooler return nozzle on the roof or upper shell
G-12 has the outlet launder or overflow box to the classification feed launder
Each line arranged as 2 rows (serpentine): Line A row 1 = AG-1..3 + G-1..4, row 2 = G-5..12 returning; Line B mirror image
Common elevated launder gallery at roof level (~31-32 m) between rows, steel-trestle supported, with a walkway along it
Stair towers (enclosed or open) every 2-3 tanks connecting grade, mid-landing (~15 m) and roof level
Pipe and cable racks along the outside of each row at ~6 m
hazards_and_safety: As agglomeration tanks: confined space, falling scale, working at height, hot caustic slurry (56-74 degC), large spill potential
Descaling with UHP water jetting (>1,000 bar): injection injuries, exclusion zones, dead-man controls
instrumentation_and_control: Line temperature profile display; A/C profile from lab or online analyser (thermometric titration autoanalyser) on selected tanks
common_problems: Scale (less than agglomeration in G-1..4, more in cold tail tanks where fines nucleate)
Loss of yield if interstage coolers are fouled
Fines build-up, then excess fine seed, then PSD cycle
operating_tips_and_key_points: Yield control: PL A/C (from digestion), fill temperature, end temperature (interstage coolers), seed charge and residence (number of tanks online)
Bypass a tank only via the launder bypass: never stop flow through a tank with the agitator still running unless the descaling procedure is followed
sources: Rosenberg S.P., Healy S.J., 'A thermodynamic model for gibbsite solubility in Bayer liquors', 4th International Alumina Quality Workshop, Darwin, 1996
Hudson L.K. et al., Ullmann's 'Aluminum Oxide'
Wefers K., Misra C., 'Oxides and Hydroxides of Aluminum', Alcoa Technical Paper No. 19 (Revised), 1987
Engineering estimate for sizes and counts

equipment.name: Precipitator agitators
equipment.function: Keep the hydrate slurry (up to ~700 g/L) fully suspended and the tank well mixed, with enough shear for particle collision but low enough tip speed to limit attrition and breakage of agglomerates.
equipment.qty_operating: 28-30 (one per tank; the agitator of a tank being emptied is stopped)
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (spare gearbox, motor and impeller set held in store)
equipment.type_selected: Top-entry, centre-mounted, long-overhung shaft (no bottom steady bearing) with 2 axial-flow hydrofoil impellers (e.g. Metso/Outotec OKTOP, SPX Lightnin A310/A510 family, EKATO, Philadelphia Mixing Solutions types), driven by a bevel-helical or planetary gearbox with integral thrust bearing (drywell) and a TEFC motor; VSD or soft-starter
equipment.why_this_type: Hydrofoils give high axial pumping per kW (flow number) at low tip speed (~3-5 m/s), so attrition is low. Having no steady bearing avoids failures in scaling slurry. Two impellers cover the ~29 m liquid height (H/T ~2.1).
equipment.alternatives: Airlift (draft-tube) agitation: no moving parts in the slurry but high air consumption, a conical bottom, and draft-tube scaling. Mechanical draft-tube circulators.
key_dimensions: Impeller diameter ~5.0-6.0 m (D/T ~0.36-0.43), 3 or 4 blades (engineering estimate)
Lower impeller ~1/3 D above the floor (~1.8-2.5 m), upper impeller at ~45-60% of liquid height (engineering estimate)
Shaft hollow tube ~350-600 mm OD, ~28-30 m long, in 2-3 flanged sections (engineering estimate)
Gearbox ~2.5 x 2.0 x 2.0 m, ~15-25 t (engineering estimate); motor 90-160 kW, 4-pole
Overall drive height above bridge ~4-5 m
equipment.working_principle: Each hydrofoil impeller works like a slow ship's propeller, pushing slurry downward along the tank axis. The flow turns at the floor, sweeps outward and upward along the walls (the baffles stop the bulk from swirling), and returns to the impeller. This 'down-pumping' loop lifts settled particles from the floor (the just-suspended condition, Zwietering criterion) and circulates the whole volume several times per hour. Power draw is roughly ρ·Np·N³·D⁵, so small speed changes cause large power changes. The gearbox reduces the motor speed of ~1,480 rpm to ~10-18 rpm and carries the large downward thrust and bending moment of the long overhung shaft in its output bearings. Scale on the blades adds mass, unbalance and power, so torque and vibration trends show when a shaft needs cleaning.
details_to_model: Drive on the bridge: motor (horizontal or vertical, with fan cowl and terminal box) coupled to a right-angle bevel-helical gearbox; output flange; drywell lantern with access windows guarded by mesh; lifting lugs
Shaft coupling flange (rigid) under the gearbox; shaft seal: simple roof-penetration dust/vapour shroud (no pressure seal) with flexible boot
Shaft visible inside the tank: 2-3 bolted flanged sections; two hydrofoil impellers each with 3-4 twisted, tapered blades bolted to a hub; blade tips may have replaceable wear tips
Optional VSD cabinet in the MCC; local control station on the bridge (start/stop/E-stop, ammeter)
Lubrication: gearbox oil cooler (small fan-cooled or water-cooled heat exchanger) and oil level sight glass; grease points
Lifting: removable bridge hatch and davit points so a mobile crane (~200-300 t class at ~35 m reach) can lift the drive; shaft sections lifted through a roof hatch
Vibration sensors on gearbox housing (accelerometer cable to junction box)
Guarding: mesh guard around couplings and drywell (ISO 14120)
hazards_and_safety: Rotating shaft in the tank: an entrant could be struck. Isolate and lock the motor AND mechanically lock the shaft (pin or brake), because flowing slurry can turn the impeller (windmilling)
Heavy lifts at height (gearboxes ~20 t): lift plans, exclusion zones
Hot gearbox oil; noise ~80-85 dB(A) near the drive
Never start an agitator buried in settled solids at full speed: shaft or gearbox overload
instrumentation_and_control: Motor current/kW to DCS; torque calculation
Gearbox oil temperature and level switch; bearing vibration (online for critical units)
Run/trip status; trip alarm triggers the sanding-response procedure
equipment.materials: Shaft and impellers carbon steel (or high-strength low-alloy) with 3-6 mm erosion allowance; blades may be rubber- or polyurethane-coated at tips; gearbox cast iron/steel
common_problems: Scale build-up on blades and shaft causes unbalance, vibration and gearbox bearing failure
Gearbox output bearing wear
Fatigue cracks at blade roots
Sanded impeller after power failure
operating_tips_and_key_points: Restart after a trip within the allowed time or use the sanded-start procedure (low speed with high torque, or air lancing)
Trend kW per tank: a rising kW means scale is building on the blades
equipment.drive_and_power: 90-160 kW TEFC motor, 6.6 kV or 690 V, VSD optional (engineering estimate)
sources: Paul E.L., Atiemo-Obeng V.A., Kresta S.M. (eds), Handbook of Industrial Mixing, Wiley 2004 (hydrofoil design, solids suspension, Zwietering)
Vendor product literature (Metso/Outotec OKTOP, SPX Lightnin, EKATO) - general ranges only

equipment.name: Transfer airlifts and inter-tank launders (incl. bypass launders and gates)
equipment.function: Move slurry from the bottom of each precipitator to the top of the next one in series, without pumps, and allow any tank to be bypassed.
equipment.qty_operating: 28-30 airlifts (one per tank); ~2 x 15 launder sections plus bypass launders
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (redundant air injection points per airlift recommended)
equipment.type_selected: Airlift riser DN600-900 (one per tank) inside the tank against the wall; open rectangular steel launders (with removable covers) sloping ~0.5-1% between tanks; slide gates or flap gates for bypass
equipment.why_this_type: Airlifts have no moving parts in slurry, tolerate scale, and draw from the bottom so coarse particles cannot accumulate (the older Bayer standard). Launders allow visual inspection and easy cleaning.
key_dimensions: Riser DN600-900, length ~30 m (engineering estimate)
Air injection at ~6-12 m submergence via a DN80-100 air line and annular or spider injector (engineering estimate)
Launder ~0.8-1.2 m wide x 0.8-1.0 m deep, slope ~1:100, roof-level steel trestles (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Compressed air injected into the riser pipe forms bubbles, so the mixture inside the riser is lighter than the slurry outside. The heavier slurry outside pushes the mixture up and out of the top into the launder. Flow rises with air rate until slugging sets in. The launder then carries the slurry by gravity to the next tank's inlet box. Each tank's launder has an inlet gate and a bypass gate: closing the inlet and opening the bypass routes slurry straight past the tank so it can be emptied and descaled while the line keeps running.
details_to_model: Riser emerging through the shell or roof edge into a launder head box (~1.5 x 1.5 x 1.5 m) with a splash cover and vent

Air supply station on the shell exterior at grade or mid-landing: isolation ball valve, globe throttle valve, rotameter or flow transmitter, pressure gauge, non-return valve, quick-connect for air lance

Launders: U or rectangular channel with stiffener ribs, bolted removable grating or plate covers, supported on steel trestles between tank roofs; slide gates with rising-stem handwheels at each tank junction; bypass launder parallel to the main launder
Walkway along launders with handrails
Scale visible as buff crust inside launders
hazards_and_safety: Compressed air: never disconnect a pressurised hose
Open launder of hot caustic slurry at height: keep covers on, splash guards, handrails
Gate operation in hot caustic splash zone: PPE
instrumentation_and_control: FT on air to each airlift (or manual rotameter)
Launder level switches at critical points (overflow alarm)
equipment.materials: Riser carbon steel, sometimes rubber-lined at the bottom inlet; launders carbon steel 8-10 mm
common_problems: Riser scale-up reduces capacity
Air injector blockage
Launder overflows when a gate is mis-set
sources: Engineering estimate; common Bayer practice (see Donaldson and Raahauge 2013 compilation)

equipment.name: Precipitation airlift air blowers/compressors
equipment.function: Supply oil-free low-pressure air to all transfer airlifts and to air lances for sanded-tank recovery.
equipment.type_selected: Oil-free rotary screw compressors (or multistage centrifugal blowers) with inlet filter-silencer, aftercooler and air receiver
equipment.why_this_type: Delivers 1.5-3 barg air reliably in the required flow range. Oil-free air avoids oil reaching the liquor (it would act as an organic contaminant).
key_dimensions: Package ~5 x 2.5 x 2.5 m each in an acoustic enclosure; receiver ~10-20 m3 vertical vessel (engineering estimate)
Motor ~200-400 kW each (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Twin helical rotors trap and compress air without oil in the compression chamber (timing gears keep the rotors apart). Air is cooled, collected in a receiver to steady the pressure, and distributed via a ring main along the precipitator rows.
details_to_model: Compressor house (steel portal frame, cladding, roll-up door, louvres) with 4 packages, receiver outside, dryer optional, ring main DN300 on pipe rack with drops to each tank
Inlet filters and silencers on the roof or wall
hazards_and_safety: Noise >85 dB(A) inside enclosure; hearing protection zone
Pressure vessel (receiver) to ASME VIII / AS 1210 with safety valve
Hot surfaces
instrumentation_and_control: Header pressure control (load/unload, VSD lead unit)

equipment.name: Interstage cooler slurry pumps (4 stations x 1 operating + 1 standby)
equipment.function: Draw precipitation slurry from G-4 and G-8 of each line, pump it through the interstage coolers and return it to the next tank.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal heavy-duty centrifugal slurry pump, rubber- or high-chrome-lined (e.g. Weir Warman AH, Metso MDM/HM, KSB GIW type), with VSD, gland water or expeller seal
equipment.why_this_type: Hydrate slurry is abrasive (~35-40% w/w solids), so replaceable wear liners and slow speed are needed. A VSD sets the loop flow and therefore the cooling.
key_dimensions: Discharge DN450-500, suction DN500-600 (engineering estimate)
Motor ~250-450 kW (engineering estimate)
Pump plus motor ~6 x 2 m on a common baseplate or overhead V-belt drive

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (return to tank top ~31 m from a suction at ~2 m; PHE dP ~0.5-1 bar)

equipment.working_principle: Same centrifugal principle as the liquor pumps, but with a large, thick, slow impeller and replaceable liners. The low speed limits wear and hydrate attrition. Gland seal water (condensate) or an expeller keeps abrasive solids out of the shaft packing. If the pump stops, the cooler must be flushed with liquor or water quickly, or settling solids will block the wide-gap channels.
details_to_model: Pumps at grade beside G-4/G-8 in a bunded area; large knife-gate suction valve (DN600) at the tank nozzle, flexible rubber spool/expansion joint, suction drain and flush connections
Slurry pump: split casing with bolts, liner, impeller adjustment mechanism at bearing housing, gland water line with rotameter, coupling or V-belt drive with guard
Discharge pinch or knife-gate valve, pressure gauge with diaphragm seal, flushing connection
Cooler return line rising up the tank side to the roof with pipe supports and rubber-lined bends
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry: worn casing or liner can burst; inspect wear
Flushing and draining procedures before opening
Rotating equipment guarding, LOTO
instrumentation_and_control: Magflow on loop flow, PT discharge, VSD speed, motor current
equipment.materials: Natural rubber or high-chrome (27% Cr white iron) liners and impeller; CS casing
common_problems: Wear of liners and impeller
Scale in suction nozzle
Gland water dilution of liquor (use minimal flow or expeller seals)
sources: Weir Minerals Warman / KSB GIW slurry pump literature (general)
Wills' Mineral Processing Technology, 8th ed. 2016 (slurry pumping)

equipment.name: Interstage coolers (4 stations x 3 units: 2 operating + 1 cleaning)
equipment.function: Remove the heat of crystallisation plus the desired sensible heat from the precipitation slurry so the growth train follows the target temperature profile (~72 to ~58 degC).
equipment.type_selected: Wide-gap (free-flow) plate heat exchangers: slurry side with ~8-16 mm free-flow channels and no contact points, cooling-water side with standard narrow-gap plates; 316L plates, EPDM gaskets
equipment.why_this_type: Wide-gap channels pass ~600-700 g/L hydrate slurry without plugging and are much more compact than shell-and-tube. Cooling water allows control independent of liquor-heat recovery.
equipment.alternatives: (a) Vacuum flash interstage coolers: slurry flashes in a vessel under vacuum, vapour condenses in a barometric condenser or a surface condenser. There is no heat-transfer surface in slurry and a small concentrating effect, but it needs vacuum equipment and large vessels. (b) Spiral heat exchangers, which are very tolerant of solids. (c) Older plants used vertical shell-and-tube coolers or cooling in the precipitators themselves via internal cooling elements. All engineering judgement.
key_dimensions: ~200-350 m2 per unit (engineering estimate; station duty ~11-17 MW, LMTD ~25-30 K, U ~1,000-1,500 W/m2.K)
Frame ~3.5 m high x 1.5 m x 5-7 m; ports DN400-500 slurry, DN400 CW (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (≈2,000 m3/h x SG 1.5 x cp ~2.5-2.7 kJ/kg.K x dT 5-7 K)

equipment.working_principle: Same plate-and-frame principle as the A11 PHEs. On the slurry side the plates are pressed with deep corrugations and no contact points, leaving a wide open channel that hydrate particles pass through without bridging. Cooling water flows counter-current in narrow channels on the other side. Cooling the supersaturated slurry deposits gibbsite scale on the slurry side, so one unit per station is always offline for hot-caustic or high-pressure water cleaning. The slurry outlet temperature is controlled by the cooling-water flow and the pump speed.
details_to_model: Same visual vocabulary as the A11 PHEs (frame, carrying bar, tie bolts, spray shield) but with fewer, thicker plates and visibly larger slurry ports
Isolation knife-gate valves on slurry nozzles (not butterflies), butterfly valves on CW nozzles
Flush water/condensate connections and drain valves to a bunded trench
Thermowells on all nozzles; CW control valve; dP gauge on slurry side
Shelter roof over each station; mobile-crane access for plate handling
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry spray from gasket failure: spray shields
Abrasion of plates near ports can lead to leaks into the cooling water: CW return pH/conductivity monitoring
Thermal relief on blocked-in sides
instrumentation_and_control: TIC slurry outlet (cascade to CW valve)
AIT pH or conductivity on CW return
Interlock: CW and slurry flows confirmed before opening valves
equipment.materials: 316L plates (thicker gauge on slurry side), EPDM gaskets, CS frame
common_problems: Gibbsite scale and blockage at port distribution areas
Gasket erosion
Loss of cooling in summer (cooling-tower approach) limits yield
operating_tips_and_key_points: Interstage cooling is the main summer bottleneck. Watch cooling-tower supply temperature against end-of-train temperature
Flush the slurry side with liquor before any shutdown longer than a few minutes
sources: Alfa Laval WideGap PHE product literature (general; alumina-specific page blocked)

equipment.name: Precipitator emptying (drain-down) pumps
equipment.function: Empty a bypassed precipitator to the next tank or to the emptying header before descaling; return slurry after maintenance.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal slurry pump, rubber-lined, on a fixed plinth connected to a drain header (or a skid-mounted, diesel-driven mobile unit)
equipment.why_this_type: Robust for settled, coarse hydrate, and allows a tank to be fully emptied below the airlift's minimum level.
key_dimensions: ~300-600 m3/h, 30-40 m head, 110-200 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Takes slurry from the floor drain nozzle of the tank being emptied and pumps it to a running tank downstream. Flushing water or liquor is used to clear the line after each use.
details_to_model: Drain header DN300 along the base of each row with knife-gate branch valves to each tank
Pump at the line end with suction flexible hose connection points
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry; line blockages under pressure; hose whip

equipment.name: Crystal growth modifier (CGM) dosing skid
equipment.function: Dose a surfactant or oil-based crystal growth modifier to the PL or agglomeration inlet to reduce fines, coarsen product and help control PSD cycles.
equipment.type_selected: IBC/bulk tank plus metering diaphragm or progressive cavity pumps with flowmeters, injection quills
equipment.why_this_type: Low-flow, accurate metering of a viscous chemical
key_dimensions: Bulk tank ~20-40 m3, skid ~3 x 2 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Positive-displacement metering pumps inject the modifier at a rate proportional to PL flow. The modifier adsorbs on gibbsite surfaces and changes the balance between nucleation, agglomeration and growth.
details_to_model: Bunded skid with tank, pumps, pulsation damper, calibration column, injection quill on the PL header

areas.layout_notes: Precipitation is the largest tank farm in the refinery after residue. It has 30 tanks of ~14 m dia x ~31 m: 2 lines x (3 agglomeration + 12 growth). Each line is laid out as a 2-row serpentine (7 + 8 tanks) at ~18 m centres, with a ~10-12 m aisle between rows carrying the roof-level launder gallery, pipe rack and stair towers. Lines A and B sit side by side, separated by a ~20-25 m access road for mobile cranes (~200-300 t class) and descaling equipment. Approximate block footprint ~150 m x 120 m (engineering estimate). The interstage cooler stations sit at grade at the ends or middles of the rows near G-4/G-5 and G-8/G-9. The compressor house sits at one end. The PL distribution box is on a steel tower or on the AG-1 roofs, fed from the A11 rack. Precipitation should be upstream (higher) of A13 so G-12 slurry gravitates to classification. Tank roofs are at ~31-33 m, and drives and bridges peak at ~36-38 m. Bunds (110% of the largest tank) have sumps at low corners. The cooling-tower block (utilities) is placed nearby but downwind to avoid drift onto the walkways.
interfaces: A11: cooled PL (72-78 degC) and fill-temperature control
A13: fine seed and coarse seed returns; G-12 slurry out to classification

Utilities: precipitation cooling-tower water (~5,000-7,000 m3/h), compressed air (airlifts), instrument air, power (~30 agitators x 90-160 kW plus pumps and compressors; precipitation area load ~6-10 MW, engineering estimate), condensate for seal and flush
Oxalate removal area: oxalate behaviour depends on fine-seed washing in A13
Maintenance: descaling contractors, UHP water jetting units, mobile cranes, scale disposal (scale is recycled to digestion or sold)

areas.purpose: Separate the end-of-precipitation hydrate by size into (1) coarse product hydrate (to A14 filtration and calcination), (2) coarse (growth) seed recycled to G-1, and (3) fine seed recycled to agglomeration after washing to remove co-precipitated sodium oxalate. Also recover clear spent liquor (thickener overflow) for A11. Classification sets the product PSD and the seed balance.
areas.process_description: 1) G-12 slurry from each line (~1,800-2,200 m3/h, 550-700 g/L solids, 56-60 degC) flows by gravity launder into a primary cyclone feed tank (one per line). 2) Primary classification: slurry pumps feed a primary cyclone cluster. The cut size d50c is ~80-110 µm (engineering estimate), set so that the underflow solids rate equals the product rate (~380-400 t/h total). Underflow (coarsest particles, ~55-65 % w/w solids) goes to the A14 product slurry tanks. Overflow goes to a secondary cyclone feed tank. 3) Secondary classification: secondary cyclones (finer cut, d50c ~40-60 µm, engineering estimate) make an underflow of coarse seed (~1,050-1,800 t/h) and an overflow carrying fines (<~45 µm) and most of the liquor. 4) Coarse seed is dewatered on vacuum disc filters to remove spent liquor, which would otherwise dilute the supersaturation in growth. The cake is repulped with a PL side-stream in coarse seed repulp tanks and pumped to G-1. 5) Secondary overflow goes to two tertiary (fine seed) thickeners. Clear overflow (spent liquor) gravitates to 11-TK-001. Thickened underflow (fine seed, ~400-700 g/L) is pumped to fine seed drum filters. 6) Fine seed washing: on the drum filters the cake is washed with hot condensate (~85-95 degC). Sodium oxalate that co-precipitated on the fine seed during the cool end of precipitation dissolves, and the oxalate-rich wash filtrate goes to the oxalate removal area. This is critical in high-organic Darling-Range-type liquors. The washed fine seed is repulped with PL and pumped to AG-1. 7) Seed balance: if fines accumulate (nucleation event), excess fine seed can be sent to the product stream, to the CIP or digestion return, or held in the fine seed tank. Classification therefore 'tunes' the PSD cycle. Alternative older design: three-stage gravity classifiers (primary, secondary and tertiary thickener/classifier vessels with rakes), still widely used.

equipment.name: Primary cyclone feed tanks (one per line)
equipment.function: Receive G-12 slurry by gravity and provide pump suction head and a little surge for the cyclone feed pumps.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical agitated carbon-steel tank with conical or sloped bottom, open or vented roof, top-entry agitator

key_dimensions: ~300-500 m3 working each; ~8-9 m ID x 8-9 m (engineering estimate)
Agitator ~30-55 kW
equipment.working_principle: A buffer pump-box: level control varies the speed of the duty cyclone feed pumps to keep the tank between limits, giving a stable cyclone inlet pressure.
details_to_model: Launder inlet box with splash plate, top-entry agitator on a bridge, 2-3 suction nozzles DN500 near the bottom with knife-gate valves, radar level, overflow to bund, drain nozzle, access stair and roof platform, manway

equipment.materials: Carbon steel, rubber-lined bottom cone optional

equipment.name: Primary cyclone feed pumps (2 per line operating + 1 standby per line)
equipment.function: Feed G-12 slurry to the primary cyclone clusters at a constant inlet pressure.
equipment.type_selected: Heavy-duty horizontal centrifugal slurry pump, rubber- or high-chrome-lined, VSD
equipment.why_this_type: Abrasive hydrate slurry; VSD holds cyclone pressure as wear changes the pump curve.
key_dimensions: DN400-450 discharge; motor ~250-400 kW (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (cyclone cluster on structure at ~15-20 m + inlet pressure ~1 bar)

equipment.working_principle: As for the slurry pumps in A12. The pump speed is controlled to hold the cyclone manifold pressure setpoint.
details_to_model: As other slurry pumps: knife-gate suction valves, expansion joints, slurry pump with liners, gland water, VSD motor, guards, discharge pinch valves, PT with diaphragm seal
Riser pipes DN450 up the cyclone structure, rubber-lined long-radius bends

equipment.name: Primary hydrocyclone clusters (product classification)
equipment.function: Separate the coarsest hydrate (product, ~380-400 t/h total) from the circulating seed and liquor.
equipment.qty_operating: 2 clusters (one per line), each ~6 of 8 cyclones operating
equipment.type_selected: Radial manifold cyclone cluster ('cyclopac'/'nest') of large hydrocyclones ~650-760 mm (26-30 in) dia, polyurethane- or rubber-lined (e.g. FLSmidth Krebs gMAX, Weir Cavex type), each with an inlet knife-gate valve
equipment.why_this_type: Compact, no moving parts, sharp enough cut for hydrate, and easy to adjust (number of cyclones online, apex size, pressure). Modern alternative to gravity classifiers.
equipment.alternatives: Gravity primary classifier (large conical tank with rake, upward liquor flow; e.g. 15-25 m dia), as used in many older Bayer plants: gentler on particles (less attrition) but large and slow to respond.
key_dimensions: Cyclone ~660-760 mm ID, overall height ~3.5-4.5 m each; inlet ~250 x 150 mm rectangular; vortex finder ~250-300 mm; apex (spigot) ~120-180 mm (engineering estimate)
Cluster manifold ~3.5-4.5 m dia, overall cluster ~7-8 m dia x ~6 m high (engineering estimate)
Mounted on a steel structure with the cyclone deck at ~15-20 m

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (vendor range for 650-760 mm units)

equipment.working_principle: Slurry enters tangentially at high velocity and spins in the cylindrical section, creating a strong centrifugal field (hundreds of g). Coarse, heavy particles are thrown to the wall and spiral down the cone to the apex (underflow). Finer particles and most of the liquid move to the central upward vortex and exit through the vortex finder (overflow). The particle size with 50% chance of reaching either outlet is the cut size. It depends on cyclone diameter, inlet pressure, slurry density and viscosity, and vortex-finder and apex sizes. A 'roping' (rope-shaped) underflow means the apex is overloaded and coarse particles are being lost to the overflow; a 'spray' discharge is normal.
details_to_model: Circular steel manifold (distributor) with a central bottom feed inlet DN450 and radial branches; each branch has a knife-gate or pinch valve with actuator to a cyclone inlet head

Cyclones arranged radially and inclined slightly or vertical; each consists of inlet head, cylinder section, 1-2 cone sections, apex housing with replaceable spigot (bolted flanges and clamp rings visible)
Overflow pipes from each cyclone top (vortex finder outlet, gooseneck) into a circular overflow launder or collection box above the manifold, with a vent/siphon breaker
Underflow collection launder (annular, open-top with splash cover) beneath the apexes discharging to a chute to the A14 product tank
Pressure gauge on manifold (diaphragm seal), PT, sampling point
Steel support structure with grating deck, handrails, stair access, monorail and hoist (~2-5 t) for cyclone change-out
Wear indicators, labels 'C1-C8'
hazards_and_safety: Pressurised hot caustic slurry at height: liner wear-through causes jets; inspect liners
Spray from the apex: splash enclosure
Working at height and manual handling of heavy cyclone sections (~200-500 kg): use the hoist
instrumentation_and_control: Optional underflow rope or spray detection sensors
Overflow and underflow sampling for PSD
equipment.materials: Steel casing with gum rubber or polyurethane liner; ceramic (alumina) apex liners optional
common_problems: Apex blockage by scale chunks
Liner wear at inlet and apex
Roping at high solids loads
operating_tips_and_key_points: Product rate is set by the number of cyclones in use and the apex size. Change one variable at a time and check the product PSD
sources: Wills' Mineral Processing Technology, 8th ed., Wills and Finch 2016 (hydrocyclone theory)
FLSmidth Krebs gMAX and Weir Cavex product literature (general size ranges)

equipment.name: Secondary cyclone feed tanks and pumps
equipment.function: Collect primary cyclone overflow and pump it to the secondary cyclone clusters.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated pump-box tanks (~300-400 m3) plus horizontal slurry pumps with VSD
equipment.why_this_type: As primary feed
key_dimensions: Tanks ~8 m ID x 8 m; pumps ~800-1,000 m3/h, 30-40 m, 250-355 kW (engineering estimate)
details_to_model: Identical visual set to primary feed tanks and pumps; the tanks sit under the primary cyclone structure so overflow gravitates in
hazards_and_safety: As primary

equipment.name: Secondary hydrocyclone clusters (seed classification)
equipment.function: Split primary overflow into coarse seed (underflow) and fines plus liquor (overflow).
equipment.type_selected: Radial cyclone cluster with ~500-660 mm (20-26 in) lined hydrocyclones
equipment.why_this_type: Smaller diameter for a finer cut; same proven technology
key_dimensions: Cyclone ~500-600 mm ID x ~3-3.5 m tall; cluster ~6-7 m dia (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: As for primary cyclones, with a finer cut.
details_to_model: As primary cluster; the underflow launder discharges to the coarse seed filter feed distributor
Overflow pipe to the tertiary thickener feed launder
hazards_and_safety: As primary

equipment.name: Coarse seed filters
equipment.function: Dewater coarse seed (secondary cyclone underflow) to a cake of ~8-15% moisture, removing spent liquor before the seed is returned to growth.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary vacuum disc filter (8-10 discs, ~3.9-4.5 m dia), polypropylene sector bags, snap-blow cake discharge, bottom-feed agitated trough
equipment.why_this_type: Disc filters give the largest filter area per floor area for very fast-filtering coarse hydrate. Snap-blow discharge is reliable. No washing is needed for coarse seed.
equipment.alternatives: Horizontal belt or table filters (larger footprint); vacuum drum filters; or no seed filtration (cyclone underflow direct to G-1, simpler but dilutes supersaturation and lowers yield).
key_dimensions: ~120-180 m2 filter area per unit (engineering estimate)
Disc dia ~3.9-4.5 m, 8-10 discs on a central hollow shaft, trough ~6-8 m long x 4.5 m wide x 3 m deep, unit ~9 x 5 x 5 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Each disc is made of ~20-30 sectors covered with filter-cloth bags, connected through the hollow central shaft to a control valve (filter head). As a sector dips into the agitated slurry trough, vacuum pulls liquor through the cloth and a cake forms on both faces. Above the slurry the sector stays under vacuum and air is drawn through the cake, dewatering it. Just before the scraper the control valve switches the sector to a brief compressed-air 'snap blow' that inflates the cloth and drops the cake into chutes between the discs. Filtrate and air go to a receiver (separator), where liquor drains to a filtrate pump and air goes to the vacuum pump.
details_to_model: Steel trough with paddle or rocker agitator underneath (geared motor at the side); slurry feed distributor along the trough; overflow weir box
Central shaft with discs, each sector visible as a wedge-shaped bag with clamping strips; filter head (control valve) at one or both ends with large DN300-400 vacuum pipes
Cake scrapers or deflectors between discs, discharge chutes down to the repulp tank or conveyor below
Drive: geared motor with VSD at shaft end; guards
Hood or covers with vapour extraction; inspection doors
Cloth-wash spray headers (low pressure) above discs
Filter floor ~10-12 m above grade (gravity discharge to repulp tanks below); maintenance hoist ~5-10 t over each filter
hazards_and_safety: Rotating discs and scrapers: guards and LOTO before cloth changes
Hot caustic vapour and splash inside hood
Vacuum system: implosion of receivers; snap-blow compressed air
Slippery floors
equipment.materials: Carbon steel trough and frame; PP sectors; PP monofilament cloth; 316 SS control valve wear plates
common_problems: Cloth blinding with fines or scale
Sector bag tears
Cake not discharging (low snap-blow pressure)

equipment.name: Coarse seed repulp tanks and coarse seed charge pumps
equipment.function: Repulp coarse seed cake with a PL side-stream and pump it to G-1 of each line.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated CS tanks (~200-400 m3) with high-power agitators for dense slurry; horizontal slurry pumps with VSD
equipment.why_this_type: Dense, coarse seed slurry (~1,000-1,200 g/L) needs vigorous agitation and robust pumps
key_dimensions: Tank ~7-8 m dia x 7-8 m; agitator ~55-90 kW; pump ~800-1,100 m3/h, 40-50 m head, 300-450 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Filter cake falls from the disc filters into the tank, where agitation and a metered PL addition form a pumpable slurry. Flow control on the seed pump, cascaded from the seed-charge setpoint (ratio to PL flow), sets the growth-stage seed charge.
details_to_model: Tank under the disc filter discharge chutes; top-entry agitator; PL inlet; suction nozzles; seed line DN400-500 rising to the precipitation launder gallery; magflow and nuclear density gauge on the seed line
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry; confined space; rotating equipment
instrumentation_and_control: Seed mass flow = magflow x density (DCS)

equipment.name: Tertiary (fine seed) thickeners
equipment.function: Settle fine hydrate from the secondary cyclone overflow, producing clear spent liquor overflow and a thickened fine seed underflow.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each sized for ~60-70% of flow to allow short outages)
equipment.type_selected: High-rate or conventional bridge-supported / centre-column thickener, flat or shallow-cone floor, with feedwell, rake drive and flocculant dosing
equipment.why_this_type: Fine hydrate settles slowly. Thickening recovers fine seed and clarifies spent liquor in one unit.
equipment.alternatives: Tertiary gravity classifier (older design); cyclones plus clarifier; fine seed filtration directly (no thickener).
key_dimensions: ~35-45 m dia each, side wall ~4-6 m, centre depth ~6-8 m (engineering estimate: rise rate ~1-2 m/h on ~1,300-1,600 m3/h per thickener)
Centre column or bridge with rake drive ~2.5 m dia; feedwell ~6-8 m dia x 3-4 m deep
equipment.working_principle: Feed enters a central feedwell that dissipates energy and mixes in flocculant, so fine particles form flocs that settle quickly. Clear liquor rises to a peripheral overflow launder. Solids settle, compact into a bed, and are raked slowly toward the central underflow cone, where pumps withdraw them. The rake drive measures torque: high torque warns of a heavy bed or scale, and the rakes are lifted automatically if torque keeps rising.
details_to_model: Large circular concrete or steel tank with peripheral overflow launder (V-notch weirs and scum baffle) and a launder outlet box
Access bridge spanning from the edge to centre (~20 m) with walkway, handrails, flocculant and feed pipes
Central drive unit: large slewing ring gear, hydraulic or electric motors, rake lift mechanism, torque indicator
Rake arms (2 long + 2 short) with angled blades/ploughs and scraper, feedwell hanging below the drive
Underflow cone outlet with 2 underflow pumps in a tunnel or below-grade pit (or at grade beside an elevated tank on steel legs)
Insulation optional; vapour forms on surface (hot liquor)
hazards_and_safety: Large open surface of hot caustic liquor: drowning or immersion hazard, handrails on the bridge
Underflow tunnel: confined space, flooding risk
Rake drive pinch points
instrumentation_and_control: Underflow density (nuclear) controls the underflow pump VSD
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (or concrete with caustic-resistant coating), CS rakes
common_problems: Scale on rakes and walls; high torque
Fines carry-over to spent liquor (it then scales PHEs and evaporators)

equipment.name: Tertiary thickener underflow pumps
equipment.function: Withdraw fine seed underflow to the fine seed filters.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal slurry pumps with VSD (density control)
equipment.why_this_type: Dense fine slurry
key_dimensions: ~150-250 m3/h each, 25-35 m head, 45-90 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Speed control holds the underflow density setpoint, which in turn controls the thickener bed inventory.
details_to_model: Pumps in a tunnel or pit beside the cone; dilution/flush water connection; knife-gate valves; density gauge
hazards_and_safety: Confined space in tunnels; flood alarm

equipment.name: Fine seed filters with oxalate wash
equipment.function: Dewater fine seed and wash it with hot condensate to dissolve co-precipitated sodium oxalate (to the oxalate removal plant) before the seed is returned to agglomeration.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary vacuum drum filter with cake-wash spray headers and scraper or belt discharge
equipment.why_this_type: Drum filters allow a well-defined wash zone on the cake, which a disc filter does not offer. Throughput is moderate.
equipment.alternatives: Horizontal belt filter (better counter-current washing, larger footprint); repulp-and-thicken washing.
key_dimensions: ~50-80 m2 each, drum ~3.5-4 m dia x 5-6.5 m face (engineering estimate)
Overall ~8 x 5 x 5 m
equipment.working_principle: The drum rotates partly submerged in the slurry trough. Vacuum through internal drainage pipes forms a cake on the cloth. As the cake rises, hot condensate sprays wash the cake; sodium oxalate is far more soluble in water than in strong spent liquor, so it dissolves and is drawn through as a separate wash filtrate. The filter valve keeps mother and wash filtrate apart so the oxalate-rich wash goes to oxalate removal. The cake is then dewatered and scraped off at the discharge point.
details_to_model: Cylindrical drum with longitudinal filtrate-pipe ribs and cloth caulked into grooves (or wire-wound), trough with oscillating agitator, filter valve at one trunnion end with 2 outlet pipes (mother and wash filtrate), 2-3 wash spray headers with flat-fan nozzles above the drum, scraper blade and discharge chute, drive gearmotor and girth gear, hood with vapour extraction
hazards_and_safety: Rotating drum nip points; hot water and caustic sprays; vapour
instrumentation_and_control: Wash flow ratio to solids; drum speed; vacuum; trough level
Wash filtrate conductivity or oxalate analysis (lab)
equipment.materials: CS drum and trough; 316 SS spray headers; PP cloth
common_problems: Cloth blinding by fines
Poor oxalate removal if wash ratio is low; oxalate then destabilises in precipitation (fines, high soda)
sources: Hind A.R., Bhargava S.K., Grocott S.C., 'The surface chemistry of Bayer process solids: a review', Colloids and Surfaces A 146 (1999) 359-374 (organics and oxalate in Bayer liquors)
