equipment.working_principle: Seed mass flow is calculated from magflow x density and ratioed to PL flow.
details_to_model: Tank with agitator, PL repulp inlet, suction nozzles, seed line to AG-1 head boxes, density gauge, magflow
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry

equipment.name: Oxalate wash filtrate tank and pumps
equipment.function: Collect oxalate-rich wash filtrate from fine seed filters and send it to the oxalate removal area.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical CS tank ~150-300 m3 with centrifugal process pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Simple surge
key_dimensions: ~6-7 m dia x 6-8 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Surge tank with level-controlled transfer.
details_to_model: Tank, radar level, pump pair, line to the oxalate area on the rack
hazards_and_safety: Hot dilute caustic

equipment.name: Seed filter vacuum system (liquid-ring vacuum pumps, filtrate receivers, filtrate pumps, seal tank)
equipment.function: Provide vacuum to the disc and drum filters, separate filtrate from air, and return filtrate to the spent-liquor tank (or wash filtrate to 13-TK-008).
equipment.qty_operating: 8 vacuum pumps (1 per operating filter + 1 extra on drums)
equipment.type_selected: Liquid-ring vacuum pumps (e.g. Nash/Gardner Denver type) with seal water recirculation; vertical filtrate receivers (ASME VIII, external pressure) with barometric legs or filtrate pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Liquid-ring pumps tolerate wet, vapour-laden and slightly caustic gas and are robust.
key_dimensions: Vacuum pump ~10,000-25,000 m3/h each, 250-500 kW (engineering estimate)
Receivers ~2.5-3.5 m dia x 4-6 m tall (engineering estimate)
Barometric legs ~10-11 m to a seal tank (if used)
equipment.working_principle: An eccentric impeller in a casing partly filled with water flings the water outward into a ring. The cells between the blades grow (suction) and shrink (compression) as the impeller turns, pumping gas. The filtrate receiver is a vessel where liquid drops out of the vacuum air stream; the liquid leaves by a barometric leg into a sealed tank or by a filtrate pump, and the air goes to the vacuum pump. Hot caustic filtrate near its boiling point under vacuum flashes, so receivers are sized for vapour disengagement.
details_to_model: Vacuum pump hall: large horizontal liquid-ring pumps with motors, discharge separators/silencers, seal-water heat exchangers
Receivers: vertical dished-head vessels with tangential inlet, top vacuum outlet, sight glass, level transmitter, bottom outlet; stiffening rings (external pressure)
Barometric seal tank at grade or filtrate pumps (end-suction)
Large vacuum piping DN400-600 with isolation butterfly valves
hazards_and_safety: Implosion if receivers are mis-designed: ASME VIII external-pressure rating
Noise from vacuum pumps (>85 dB(A))
Caustic carry-over into seal water raises pH
instrumentation_and_control: Vacuum PT per filter; receiver level control; seal-water flow switches
equipment.materials: CS receivers (caustic service), SS or CI pumps
sources: ASME BPVC VIII Div 1 (external pressure design)

equipment.name: Hydrate flocculant make-up and dosing skid
equipment.function: Prepare and dose flocculant to the tertiary thickener feedwells.
equipment.type_selected: Powder or emulsion make-up system with mixing and storage tanks, progressive-cavity dosing pumps, in-line dilution
equipment.why_this_type: Standard thickener reagent system
key_dimensions: Skid ~6 x 3 m; mixing tank ~10-20 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Flocculant is wetted and aged to full activity, then diluted and dosed in proportion to thickener feed.
details_to_model: Hopper with screw feeder, wetting head, agitated tanks, dosing pumps, dilution water rotameters
hazards_and_safety: Spilled flocculant is extremely slippery

areas.layout_notes: A13 sits immediately downstream (and at a lower grade) of the precipitation G-12 tanks, so slurry gravitates from G-12 via launders to the primary cyclone feed tanks. The classification building is a multi-level steel structure (~40 x 30 m, ~25-28 m high, engineering estimate): grade has the feed tanks, slurry pumps and repulp tanks; ~10-12 m has the seed filter floor (disc and drum filters) above the repulp tanks for gravity discharge; ~18-22 m has the primary and secondary cyclone decks above their feed tanks. Overhead cranes (10-20 t) serve the filter floor, and monorails serve the cyclones. The vacuum pump hall is at grade on one side. The two tertiary thickeners (~40 m dia) sit beside the building, higher than the spent-liquor tank (11-TK-001) so overflow gravitates to it. The A14 product filter building adjoins on the calcination side so primary underflow pipe runs are short. Floors are bunded and sloped to sumps, and safety showers are placed at every level.
interfaces: A12: G-12 slurry in; fine seed to AG-1; coarse seed to G-1; PL side-stream for repulping
A11: tertiary overflow and filtrates to spent-liquor tank 11-TK-001
A14: primary cyclone underflow (product hydrate slurry)
Oxalate removal area: oxalate wash filtrate
Utilities: hot process condensate (wash), compressed air (snap blow), cooling water (vacuum pump seal coolers), flocculant reagent
Digestion: excess fine seed or scale returns (if routed)

areas.purpose: Filter the product hydrate (primary cyclone underflow), wash out entrained spent liquor with hot condensate to minimise soluble soda carried to calcination and recover caustic, and deliver a cake of ~6-10% free moisture to the calciner hydrate storage at ~380-400 t/h dry.
areas.process_description: 1) Primary cyclone underflow (~55-65 % w/w solids, ~190-210 t/h dry per line) enters the agitated product slurry tanks. 2) Filter feed pumps deliver slurry to horizontal rotating table (pan) vacuum filters, 4 operating + 1 standby. 3) On each filter the cake forms in ~30-60 s, then the mother liquor (spent liquor) is drawn off to the mother-filtrate receiver and returned to 11-TK-001. 4) Two-stage counter-current displacement washing: hot condensate (85-95 degC) on the final wash zone; that wash filtrate is recycled as the first wash. Weak wash filtrate is returned to the liquor circuit (spent-liquor tank or residue washing, per water balance). 5) The cake is dewatered by air drawn through it (dry zone), then discharged by a helical scroll to a collecting conveyor. Residual cake heel is loosened by a low-pressure air or water blow, and the cloth is washed by high-pressure sprays each revolution. 6) The cake (6-10% free moisture, soluble Na2O typically <0.05% engineering estimate) travels by belt conveyor with a belt scale and automatic sampler to hydrate storage or calciner feed bins (A15). Total Na2O in the final SGA (~0.30-0.45%) is mostly occluded in the crystal lattice from precipitation and is not removed by washing. Washing only removes surface liquor.

Agitator ~55-90 kW

equipment.name: Product hydrate filters
equipment.function: Form, wash (2-stage counter-current, hot condensate) and dewater the product hydrate cake and discharge it to the product conveyor.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal rotating table (pan) vacuum filter: annular table of radial cells under a shared cloth, rotary valve, helical scroll cake discharge (Dorr-Oliver/FLSmidth, Gaudfrin type), ~70-100 m2 each
equipment.why_this_type: The horizontal cake allows excellent displacement washing with sharp separation of mother, wash and weak filtrates. It suits fast-draining, granular hydrate at high throughput, has a long industry record for product hydrate, and gives a clean continuous discharge.
equipment.alternatives: Horizontal vacuum belt filter (similar washing, longer footprint, more cloth tracking issues); rotary drum filter with washing (less effective washing on a curved cake); tilting-pan filter (very good washing, more complex mechanics).
key_dimensions: Effective area ~70-100 m2 per filter (engineering estimate: ~400-420 t/h / (4 x 1.0-1.5 t/m2.h))
Table outer dia ~10.5-12.5 m, inner dia ~3-4 m, cell depth ~150-250 mm, rim height ~200 mm (engineering estimate)
~24-36 radial cells
Overall with drive, valve and hood ~14 x 14 m footprint; table top at ~6-8 m (filter floor) above grade
equipment.working_principle: The table is a large horizontal ring divided into radial cells, each with a drainage grid and cloth, and each piped to a central rotary valve beneath. As the table rotates, every cell passes through fixed zones defined by the valve: (1) feed, where slurry is spread evenly by a feed box and vacuum draws the mother liquor to the mother receiver; (2) first wash, where recycled wash filtrate displaces remaining mother liquor; (3) final wash, where hot condensate displaces the first-wash liquor (the wash filtrates are kept separate for counter-current reuse); (4) dry zone, where air is pulled through to drain the cake to 6-10% moisture; (5) discharge, where a slowly rotating helical scroll (screw) set a few mm above the cloth sweeps the cake radially outward over the rim into a hopper or chute, and a low-pressure blow-back through the valve lifts the heel; (6) cloth wash, where high-pressure sprays clean the cloth before the cell returns to the feed zone. Displacement washing works best with a level, crack-free cake, which is why the horizontal geometry is used.
details_to_model: Large circular annular table (ring) on a slewing bearing/rollers with a peripheral girth rack, visible radial cell divisions (raised ribs) and PP cloth clamped with caulking strips
Central rotary vacuum valve under the table (large cylindrical valve body with multiple ports DN300-400) connected to 3-4 separate filtrate headers going to receivers
Drive: 2 geared motors with pinions on the girth rack (VSD), guarded
Feed box: radial distributor or slotted pipe over the feed zone, with a flexible flapper for even spreading
Wash headers: 2-3 radial bars with weir-type overflow distributors or flat-fan nozzles over wash zones, each with flow meter and control valve
Discharge scroll: helical screw (~0.6-0.8 m dia) spanning radially from inner to outer edge, driven by its own gearmotor, with height-adjust jacks
Discharge hopper or chute at outer rim to the collecting conveyor below
Cloth wash spray bar and LP blow-back air header
Hood/canopy over the table with vapour extraction duct to an exhaust fan or scrubber; hinged inspection doors; lighting
Filter floor (grating or concrete) around the table with handrails and stairs; overhead travelling crane (~10-20 t) in the filter building for scroll and valve maintenance
Filtrate receivers, vacuum pipes and filtrate pumps on the floor beneath
hazards_and_safety: Rotating table and scroll: nip points at the rim and scroll; fixed guards, interlocked access gates and LOTO for cloth changes (ISO 14120 / AS 4024)
Hot condensate sprays (85-95 degC) and caustic mist under the hood: face shield and goggles
Vacuum line opening while under vacuum
Slips on hydrate-covered floors; housekeeping and wash-down
Confined-space-like conditions under the hood or inside the valve pit
instrumentation_and_control: Feed flow per filter (cake thickness control) and table speed (VSD)
Wash flow FIC ratio to solids rate
Cake moisture (online NIR or microwave analyser optional) and lab soluble-soda analysis
Scroll motor current; table drive torque
Interlocks: hood doors, scroll guard, E-stop pull cords
equipment.materials: Table and cells carbon steel with epoxy or rubber coating or 304/316 SS cell grids; PP monofilament cloth; rotary valve with replaceable wear plates (SS or ceramic); scroll flights with hard-facing
common_problems: Cloth blinding by fines (when fines rise in product) leading to wet cake and high soda
Uneven cake (feed distribution) causing wash channelling
Scroll wear causing a thick heel
Rotary valve wear causing cross-leak between zones
operating_tips_and_key_points: Wet or high-soda cake usually signals a PSD problem upstream (more fines) rather than a filter fault
Keep the wash water hot (>85 degC): hot water lowers viscosity and improves displacement and drainage
equipment.drive_and_power: Table drive 2 x 11-30 kW; scroll 15-37 kW; vacuum pump per filter 250-600 kW (engineering estimate)
sources: Wills and Finch 2016 (vacuum filtration, horizontal filters)
FLSmidth / Dorr-Oliver Eimco and Gaudfrin horizontal table filter literature (general)

areas.layout_notes: The product filter building (~60 x 30 m, ~20 m to eaves, engineering estimate) adjoins A13 and is as close as possible to the A15 hydrate storage and calciners, keeping conveyors short. Filter floor (~6-8 m): 5 table filters in a row at ~16 m centres with hoods, and feed and wash headers. Collecting conveyor 14-CV-001 runs under the filter discharge chutes at ~3-4 m, then turns to an inclined transfer conveyor gallery to A15. A 20 t overhead crane covers the filter floor, with a ground-floor drop zone. The building is open-sided or louvred for ventilation, with floors bunded and sloped to sumps, and safety showers at each floor and stair.

areas.purpose: Convert washed product hydrate (gibbsite, Al(OH)3) into smelter-grade alumina (SGA) by drying, dehydration (calcination) and cooling in two identical gas suspension calciner (GSC) trains with holding vessels. The area sets product LOI, BET surface area and alpha-alumina content. It cannot remove soda or fix poor particle strength: Na2O and particle size come from precipitation and hydrate washing (A13/A14). It is also the refinery's largest single user of fuel and source of CO2.
areas.process_description:
TECHNOLOGY CHOICE: The reference plant uses the FLSmidth-type Gas Suspension Calciner with Holding Vessel (GSC-HV), 2 trains x 3,500 t/d nameplate. The alternative is the Metso Outotec (ex-Lurgi) Circulating Fluid Bed (CFB) calciner. Both are proven at 3,000-4,500 t/d per unit and use similar fuel (about 2.7-3.1 GJ/t). GSC was chosen because (a) its stages match the training curriculum: venturi flash dryer, 2 preheater cyclone stages, stationary furnace, holding vessel, 4 cooling-cyclone stages, fluid bed cooler, ESP; (b) the whole gas path runs under suction from one ID fan, so there are no high-pressure primary-air blowers and dust cannot leak outward; (c) it holds little material, so it starts and stops quickly. The CFB differences are noted under 'alternatives'.
STEP 1 - Feed: Washed hydrate filter cake from the product hydrate pan/table filters (A14) falls by chute or short belt into each train's calciner feed bin. The cake is 6-10 % free moisture, about 0.20-0.30 % Na2O on a dry hydrate basis, 50-80 degC, d50 about 80-100 um. Twin variable-speed screw feeders meter it into the venturi flash dryer.
STEP 2 - Drying (stage A01/P01): Gas leaving preheater cyclone P02 at about 350-420 degC enters through a venturi throat at the bottom of the dryer riser. It lifts the hydrate, and the free moisture flashes off within about 1-2 s. Two dryer cyclones (P01) separate the solids at about 140-170 degC. The gas (about 140-170 degC, about 40-55 vol% H2O) goes to the ESP, then the ID fan, then the stack.
STEP 3 - Preheating and dehydration (P02): P01 solids enter the riser duct from the furnace cyclones. There they meet gas at about 950-1050 degC and are heated to about 320-400 degC in seconds. Most of the chemically bound water leaves here: 2 Al(OH)3 -> Al2O3 + 3 H2O(g). The reaction is endothermic, about +205 kJ/mol, i.e. about 2.0 GJ/t Al2O3 (thermochemical calculation from standard heats of formation). Fine particles heated fast go gibbsite -> chi-alumina. Coarse particles in humid gas partly go to boehmite (AlOOH) first.
STEP 4 - Calcination (P04 furnace): Partly dehydrated solids enter the lower cone of the refractory-lined stationary furnace. Combustion air arrives from cooling cyclone C01, preheated to about 750-900 degC. Natural gas is injected through a ring of burners in the cone and burns with the solids in suspension. Gas and solids leave the top at about 950-1050 degC (set point controls LOI and BET). Excess O2 is about 2-4 %. Gas residence time in the furnace is only a few seconds. The furnace separation cyclones (P04) split solids from gas; the gas goes to P02 (step 3).
STEP 5 - Holding vessel (HV): Solids from P04 drop into an air-fluidised, refractory-lined holding vessel. They stay about 10-30 min (engineering estimate) at about 920-1000 degC, so the last hydroxyl removal finishes there. The HV lets the furnace run 50-100 degC cooler than a GSC without an HV for the same LOI (vendor claim). That gives higher BET, lower alpha-alumina and lower fuel use. HV off-air returns to the furnace.
STEP 6 - Suspension cooling (C01-C04): Hot alumina passes counter-current through 4 cooling-cyclone stages. Ambient air, drawn in at the C04 riser by the ID fan, picks up heat stage by stage and becomes the furnace combustion air. Alumina cools from about 950 degC to about 250-320 degC. Air heats from ambient to about 750-900 degC.
STEP 7 - Fluid bed cooler (FBC): Alumina from C04 enters a multi-compartment air-fluidised bed. Water-cooled tube bundles immersed in the bed bring it to about 70-90 degC. The heat goes through plate heat exchangers to make hot wash water for the hydrate filters, with a cooling tower as trim. Warm FBC exhaust air goes into the C04 air inlet so its heat is recovered.
STEP 8 - Product: The FBC overflows into airslides that feed the dense-phase conveyors to the product silos (A16). An auto-sampler takes hourly samples for LOI, MOI, BET, alpha, PSD, Na2O and impurities.
PHASE CHEMISTRY: gibbsite -> chi/boehmite -> gamma -> delta -> theta (the transition aluminas, BET 60-80 m2/g in SGA) -> alpha (corundum, forms significantly above about 1100-1200 degC; held below about 10 % in SGA because alpha dissolves slowly in cryolite and lowers HF scrubbing capacity at the smelter). Raising calcination temperature lowers LOI and BET and raises alpha. Holding the solids longer at moderate temperature (the HV) lowers LOI and keeps BET high.
HIGH-TEMPERATURE (BOEHMITIC) PLANTS: they use the same calciner technology. The differences are upstream (digestion at 240-270 degC with flash/heat-recovery trains); hydrate quality depends on precipitation practice, not on the digestion route.
GAS SIDE: the whole GSC gas path is at negative pressure, about -0.5 kPa at the C04 air inlet down to about -8 to -11 kPa at the ID fan inlet (engineering estimate). The ESP outlet dust limit is 30-50 mg/Nm3 (typical licence). The off-gas is very humid (dew point about 80-85 degC), so all ducts, the ESP and the stack must run well above about 120 degC.

streams.from_to: 15-EP hoppers -> 15-SC/15-PV dust return -> P02 riser / furnace

streams.name: Calcined SGA product
streams.flow: 146 t/h per train at 3,500 t/d nameplate; plant 241 t/h at 8,300 h/yr

streams.name: FBC cooling water (closed loop)
streams.basis: engineering estimate: 146 t/h x ~1.0 kJ/kgK x ~200 K

streams.name: FBC/HV fluidising air
streams.from_to: 15-BL blowers -> FBC/HV plenums -> exhaust to C04 inlet / furnace

equipment.name: Calciner hydrate feed bin
equipment.function: Buffers wet hydrate from the pan filter, decoupling filter cake discharge pulses from steady calciner feed.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical steel bin with steep conical (or wedge/transition) mass-flow hopper, load-cell mounted
equipment.why_this_type: Wet hydrate (6-10 % moisture) is cohesive and bridges; a steep, low-friction mass-flow hopper feeding twin screws gives first-in-first-out flow and a measurable inventory for feed control.
key_dimensions: Diameter ~6-8 m, cylinder ~6-8 m, cone ~5-7 m (engineering estimate)
Live capacity ~150-300 t (~0.6-1.2 h at 240 t/h) (engineering estimate)
Hopper half-angle ~15-25 deg from vertical, lined (engineering estimate per Jenike flow-function testing)
equipment.working_principle: Filter cake falls into the bin from the pan filter discharge chute or belt. The bin sits on 3-4 load cells, so the control system always knows the inventory. The calciner feed rate is set by screw speed and checked against the rate the bin weight falls when filter feed is stopped. A steep, smooth cone gives mass flow: all material moves together, with no dead zones where wet hydrate can cake and later collapse. The bin is vented into the dryer inlet, which is under negative pressure. This keeps steam and dust inside the system.
details_to_model: Cylindrical shell with roof; top inlet chute from pan filter discharge with inspection door; vent nozzle (DN 300-500) ducted to dryer inlet
Cone lined with UHMWPE or 304/2B stainless wear plates (bolted with countersunk bolts); 2 outlet flanges at cone bottom (rectangular slots) to twin screw feeders
3-4 load cells on bracket lugs at ring girder supported on structural steel at ~30-40 m level of calciner tower
Radar level transmitter on roof, high-high level switch, 2-3 air-blaster or vibrator pads on cone, poke/inspection ports with hinged covers
Roof manhole (DN 600) with handrail perimeter platform, ladder from tower floor
Thermal insulation not normally fitted; external stiffeners on cylinder
hazards_and_safety: Confined space; engulfment by collapsing hydrate bridges: never enter without isolation, permit, standby and bridging cleared from above
Mildly caustic wet hydrate (residual soda) irritates skin and eyes
Air blasters must be isolated and depressurised before entry
common_problems: Rat-holing/bridging with high-moisture cake
Lumps from filter cloth failures blocking screws
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hydrate moisture above ~10 % hurts dryer exit temperature and P01 flow: fix the filters first
Keep bin level steady; a bin running empty lets air bypass into the dryer and upsets the draft
instrumentation_and_control: Feed rate from screw speed SIC + loss-in-weight check
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell, UHMWPE or stainless cone liner
sources: Jenike A.W., Storage and Flow of Solids, Bulletin 123 (hopper design method)
FLSmidth GSC vendor literature (feed system arrangement)

equipment.name: Hydrate feed screw feeders
equipment.function: Meter wet hydrate from feed bin into the venturi flash dryer while forming a material plug gas seal.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each screw sized ~60-70 % of train feed so one can carry the train at reduced rate)
equipment.type_selected: Twin variable-speed screw feeders with plug-forming discharge section
equipment.why_this_type: Screws handle sticky cake, give a speed-proportional feed rate and, with a short shaftless/choke section, a material seal against the dryer's negative pressure.
key_dimensions: Screw diameter ~600-800 mm, length ~5-8 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A rotating helical flight in a U-trough or tube pushes hydrate forward a fixed volume per turn, so feed rate is roughly proportional to speed. Near the outlet a tubular section keeps the screw full. That plug of hydrate seals the bin from the dryer suction. The screw discharges into a feed chute entering the dryer riser just above the venturi throat.
details_to_model: Trough/tube casing with bolted inspection covers
Inlet flange to bin outlet, discharge chute with expansion bellows into dryer riser
Gear motor (helical-bevel) on drive end with coupling guard; end bearings with grease lines
Zero-speed sensor on tail shaft; pull-cord not applicable (enclosed)
Wear-resistant hard-faced flights (visible when cover removed)
hazards_and_safety: Moving machinery: never open inspection covers while running; lock-out at MCC
Hot gas blow-back at dryer inlet if the plug is lost
common_problems: Flight wear and hydrate build-up on shaft
Feed surges when bin bridges
instrumentation_and_control: VFD speed control from calciner feed-rate controller
equipment.materials: Carbon steel casing, hard-faced or AR400 flights
sources: CEMA 350 Screw Conveyors for Bulk Materials

equipment.name: Venturi flash dryer (stage A01) with dryer burner
equipment.function: Flash-dries wet hydrate (removes free moisture) using waste heat in gas from preheater cyclone P02; dryer burner gives heat for start-up and trim.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical refractory/abrasion-lined venturi riser dryer with side-mounted gas-fired hot-gas generator
equipment.why_this_type: The venturi gives the high velocity needed to break up and lift wet agglomerates; suspension drying is fast and needs no moving parts.
key_dimensions: Venturi throat ~1.8-2.5 m dia; riser ~3.5-4.5 m dia, height ~15-25 m to P01 inlet ducts (engineering estimate for 3,500 t/d)
Hot gas generator (dryer burner chamber) ~3-4 m dia x 6-8 m long, rated ~10-25 MW (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate consistent with GSC literature
engineering estimate; must stay well above off-gas dew point ~80-85 degC

equipment.working_principle: Hot gas speeds up through a converging-diverging venturi at the base of the riser. Wet hydrate drops in just above the throat. The turbulence breaks up lumps and the gas carries the particles upward. Heat moves very fast to the small particles, so free water evaporates in about a second. The gas cools from about 400 degC to about 150 degC. Gas and dry hydrate leave the top of the riser into the P01 cyclones. During start-up and heat-up, before P02 gas is hot enough, or with very wet feed, the dryer burner adds hot flue gas to the inlet.
details_to_model: Vertical cylindrical riser rising from the venturi cone; bottom gas inlet elbow from P02 gas duct (large rectangular-to-round transition, ~3 m)
Feed chute entering at ~45 deg just above throat, with flushing/inspection door
Riser top: bifurcated outlet ducts (2) to the two P01 cyclone tangential inlets
Hot-gas generator: horizontal refractory-lined burner chamber with burner front (gas train, flame scanner, combustion-air fan) joined to the inlet duct
Lining ~100-150 mm abrasion-resistant castable on anchors; external shell stiffening rings; thermocouples at inlet, throat and outlet; pressure taps at throat (venturi dP)
Inspection doors at 2-3 levels with platforms; metallic/fabric expansion joints on ducts; spring supports/hangers
hazards_and_safety: Hot surfaces (shell 80-150 degC), hot gas leakage at doors (system is under suction, but opening doors under upset/positive pressure ejects hot dust)
Burner: purge and flame-supervision per NFPA 85/86 / EN 746-2
Steam and hot dust on blockage clearing
common_problems: Wet feed collapse (dryer 'choking') when outlet temperature drops; build-up at feed point
Erosion of throat lining
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch dryer outlet temperature: it is the first warning of feed moisture or feed rate changes
instrumentation_and_control: Dryer burner on BMS with UV/IR scanner
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell, abrasion-resistant castable
sources: FLSmidth GSC vendor literature (flash dryer stage)
Raahauge B.E. & Williams F.S. (eds), Smelter Grade Alumina from the Bayer Process, Springer 2022

equipment.name: Dryer (P01) separation cyclones
equipment.function: Separate dried hydrate from the cooled off-gas; underflow goes to the P02 riser and gas to the ESP.
equipment.type_selected: High-efficiency tangential-inlet cyclones with central vortex finder and pendulum flap valve on dip-leg
equipment.why_this_type: Standard suspension-preheater technology from the cement and alumina industries; high efficiency at P01 limits the dust load on the ESP.
key_dimensions: Cylinder ID ~5.0-6.5 m each, overall height cylinder+cone ~15-20 m (engineering estimate)
Inlet duct rectangular ~2.5 x 4 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Gas enters tangentially and spins down the cylinder and cone. Centrifugal force throws the particles to the wall, and they slide down into the dip-leg. The gas reverses at the cone bottom and leaves upward through the central vortex finder. A counterweighted pendulum flap in the dip-leg opens only under the weight of solids. That stops gas short-circuiting up the dip-leg, which would ruin separation.
details_to_model: Cylinder + cone shell with involute (scroll) inlet; vortex finder pipe projecting into cylinder; top gas outlet duct to common off-gas duct
Dip-leg with pendulum flap valve housing (external counterweight arm, limit switch), inspection doors above and below flap
3-6 air blasters on cone (tanks + discharge nozzles), poke holes with caps
Thin lining (gunite/abrasion castable ~50-75 mm) on cold stage
Support lugs on cyclone cylinder bearing on tower beams; platforms at inlet level and flap level
Thermocouple and pressure tap on outlet duct; cone draft (pressure) tap for blockage detection
hazards_and_safety: Cyclone blockage clearing: hot dust can burst out of doors; use remote lances, face shields, aluminised clothing; never stand in line with doors
Confined space entry only after cool-down, gas test, isolation of air blasters and fan
common_problems: Cone build-up from condensation if outlet temperature is low
Flap valve sticking open (gas bypass) or shut (blockage)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel; abrasion castable
sources: Cement/alumina suspension preheater practice (e.g., Duda, Cement Data Book)

equipment.name: Preheater (P02) cyclones and riser
equipment.function: Heat dried hydrate to ~320-400 degC with furnace gas, removing most chemically bound water, and cool the gas before it goes to the dryer.
equipment.type_selected: Refractory-lined tangential cyclones with heat-resistant vortex finders and pendulum flaps
equipment.why_this_type: Gas-solid suspension heat exchange in risers + cyclones is near counter-current overall and very efficient.
key_dimensions: Cylinder ID ~5.5-6.5 m each, height ~16-22 m (engineering estimate)
Riser duct (from P04 gas outlets) ~3-4 m ID (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Dried hydrate from P01 is injected into the hot riser duct carrying gas from the furnace cyclones. Heat transfer to fine particles in suspension takes a second or less. The hydrate loses most of its 34.6 % theoretical combined water and turns into chi-alumina or boehmite, absorbing much of the reaction heat. The P02 cyclones then separate the solids, which drop into the furnace. The gas, now about 350-420 degC, goes on to the dryer.
details_to_model: As for P01 but with full refractory lining (~150-230 mm insulating + dense castable/brick)
Segmented vortex finder of heat-resistant cast steel hung from the roof (visible from roof hatch)
Pendulum flap on dip-leg, with refractory-lined flap box, plus a splash box at the riser injection point
Riser-to-cyclone ducts with expansion joints; ducts and cyclones carry many TC and pressure points
Shell IR-scanner coverage and hot-spot painted temperature indicator patches
hazards_and_safety: Shell up to ~150-250 degC: personnel guards near walkways
Hot meal (300-400 degC) flushes like a liquid if a blockage releases
common_problems: Refractory damage at inlet scroll; vortex finder segment loss
Build-up at riser injection point
instrumentation_and_control: TT gas outlet P02 (key profile reading)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell; refractory; heat-resistant cast steel (e.g., 25Cr-20Ni class) vortex finder
sources: Wefers K. & Misra C., Oxides and Hydroxides of Aluminum, Alcoa Technical Paper 19 (1987) (dehydration sequence)

equipment.name: Calciner furnace (P04) with main burners
equipment.function: Burn fuel in preheated air with the alumina in suspension, raising solids to calcination temperature (950-1050 degC).
equipment.type_selected: Stationary, refractory-lined, vertical cylindrical suspension furnace with conical bottom air inlet and ring of gas burners (fuel-oil-capable lances optional)
equipment.why_this_type: Combustion in suspension with the material is very efficient. There is no moving kiln shell, and the refractory load is small compared with rotary kilns (rotary kilns used ~4.5-5 GJ/t vs ~3 GJ/t for stationary calciners).
key_dimensions: Shell ID inside lining ~5.5-6.5 m; cylindrical height ~20-28 m plus bottom cone ~6-8 m (engineering estimate from ~200 m3/s actual gas at ~6-8 m/s)
Refractory total ~250-350 mm (insulating brick/board + dense high-alumina castable/brick) (engineering estimate)
Burners: ~6-12 per furnace in 1-2 rings (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: GSC-HV practice (Raahauge & Williams 2022; vendor literature); without holding vessel 1050-1150 degC

equipment.working_principle: Preheated air from cooling cyclone C01 rises into the furnace through the bottom cone at high velocity. Natural gas injected through burner lances mixes with this hot air and burns, while the partly dehydrated alumina from P02 is fed in at the cone. The particles are lifted and heated quickly to the set temperature, then carried out of the top into the P04 cyclones. The temperature is controlled by trimming the fuel rate, and it sets LOI, BET and alpha content. The cone shape spreads the jet and gives back-mixing that evens out temperatures. Before ignition, a start-up burner and a BMS purge sequence (at least 4-5 volume changes) are required.
details_to_model: Tall vertical cylinder on the calciner tower's central bay; bottom cone with large vertical hot-air inlet duct from C01 (refractory-lined, ~2.5-3.5 m)
Material inlet chute(s) from P02 dip-legs entering the cone at 45-60 deg with splash plates

Burner ring: 6-12 gas lances (each with manual isolation valve, automatic shut-off valve pair, flexible hose, flame scanner sight tube, cooling/purge-air connection) arranged radially around the cone at a burner platform
Start-up burner (larger, with own combustion-air fan) at the bottom; ignitors
Top outlet: 1 or 2 large refractory-lined ducts curving to the P04 cyclones
Inspection/manway doors at 3-4 levels (refractory-plugged), observation ports with glass, 6-10 thermocouples (Type K/N in ceramic sheaths) at different heights, pressure taps
Support ring girder at about mid-height on tower steel; shell expansion allowance; metallic expansion joints at ducts
External shell painted with high-temperature paint; perimeter platforms with toe-boards at each burner and door level; heat shields where walkways pass
hazards_and_safety: Fuel explosion on light-off or after flame failure: BMS per NFPA 85/86 / EN 746-2 / AS 3814 with SIL-rated (IEC 61511) shut-off
Hot shell and radiant heat; CO and NOx near doors
Refractory work: respirable crystalline silica and refractory ceramic fibre dust; heat stress
Hot alumina flushes on furnace trips (inventory drains to HV/coolers)
common_problems: Refractory spalling at cone and burner ports
Flame instability at low load; burner tip erosion
Temperature excursions from feed surges (over-calcination raises alpha and lowers BET)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Control LOI with furnace temperature AND HV residence; check BET trend daily
Keep the O2 trim narrow: low O2 raises CO and the ESP trip risk; high O2 wastes fuel
Follow the refractory dry-out/heat-up curve (typically ~25-50 degC/h, engineering estimate) after relining
instrumentation_and_control: TIC furnace outlet -> fuel flow FIC cascade
Flame scanners per burner; BMS permissives
equipment.drive_and_power: No drive; burners supplied from 15-GS-001; combustion air drawn by ID fan 15-FN
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell 12-16 mm; high-alumina dense castable/brick working lining; insulating backup
equipment.alternatives: Outotec/Metso CFB furnace: fuel injected into a dense circulating bed fluidised by primary air from high-pressure blowers, with a recycle cyclone and seal pot; solids residence ~20-30 min in the loop, ~950-1000 degC.
sources: Raahauge B.E. & Williams F.S. (eds), Smelter Grade Alumina from the Bayer Process, Springer 2022
Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry (rotary kiln vs stationary calciner energy)
EU JRC BREF Non-Ferrous Metals Industries (2017), alumina chapter

equipment.name: Furnace separation cyclones (P04)
equipment.function: Separate calcined alumina from hot furnace gas at ~950-1050 degC; gas to P02 riser, solids to holding vessel.
equipment.type_selected: Heavily refractory-lined hot cyclones with cast heat-resistant vortex finders
equipment.why_this_type: These are the hottest cyclones in the system; recovering solids efficiently here is vital for product yield and heat economy.
key_dimensions: Cylinder ID inside lining ~6-7 m each, height ~18-24 m (engineering estimate)
Lining ~250-300 mm (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: This is the same centrifugal principle as the other cyclones, but at full calcination temperature. Gas volume is largest here, so these are the largest cyclones in the tower. Underflow passes through pendulum flaps into the holding vessel. Any carry-over to P02 is recycled back through the furnace.
details_to_model: Large cyclones high in the tower beside the furnace top; thick refractory, external shell with stiffening rings
Segmented cast vortex finder; roof manway
Dip-legs with refractory-lined pendulum flaps feeding HV inlet chutes
Air blasters on cone; TCs and pressure taps; expansion joints on inlet and outlet ducts
hazards_and_safety: Highest-temperature solids in the area (~1000 degC): blockage clearing only to written procedure with full thermal PPE
Shell hot spots signal refractory loss: barricade and inform
common_problems: Vortex finder segment failure causes efficiency loss (higher P02 load, higher fines)

equipment.name: Holding vessel (calcination retention vessel)
equipment.function: Holds calcined alumina in a fluidised bed at ~920-1000 degC for extra residence so dehydroxylation finishes at lower temperature (lower LOI at high BET and low alpha) with less fuel.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical refractory-lined bubbling fluidised-bed vessel with nozzle grid and overflow weir/outlet
equipment.why_this_type: A simple fluidised volume gives minutes of residence that the furnace (seconds) cannot. This is how the GSC-HV makes SGA with BET ~70 m2/g at lower temperature.
key_dimensions: ID ~4.5-6 m, bed height ~2-4 m, overall height ~8-12 m (engineering estimate)
Bed inventory ~25-70 t (engineering estimate for 10-30 min at 146 t/h)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (vendor literature cites 'several to ~30 min')

equipment.working_principle: Alumina from the P04 cyclones falls into a bed kept fluid by air blown up through nozzles in the grid plate. The fluidised bed behaves like a well-mixed liquid. Material flows over a weir or through an adjustable bottom outlet towards cooling cyclone C01, and bed level (from differential pressure) sets the residence time. The remaining hydroxyl groups leave slowly at near-furnace temperature, so LOI drops without the high peak temperature that would turn transition alumina into alpha-alumina and collapse BET. The small HV off-gas joins the furnace gas.
details_to_model: Squat refractory-lined cylinder below P04 cyclones; 2 inlet chutes from P04 flaps on the roof
Wind box/plenum below grid with fluidising air pipe from blower, isolation and control valve
Grid plate with many cap nozzles (visible in cutaway)
Overflow outlet chute with flow-control gate to C01 riser; emergency dump outlet
Off-gas vent duct to furnace; DP taps across bed; 3-4 TCs; inspection doors and manways; platform ring
hazards_and_safety: Large inventory of ~1000 degC fluid alumina: on trip it slumps; opening doors may release a flood of hot material
Confined space: entry only after fully cold and drained
common_problems: Nozzle plugging/erosion; bed defluidisation on blower failure
instrumentation_and_control: Bed DP level -> outlet gate control
equipment.materials: CS shell, dense refractory lining, heat-resistant steel nozzles
sources: FLSmidth GSC with holding vessel vendor literature
Raahauge B.E. & Williams F.S. (eds), Smelter Grade Alumina from the Bayer Process, Springer 2022

equipment.name: Cooling cyclones C01-C04 (suspension coolers)
equipment.function: Cool alumina from ~950 to ~250-320 degC in four counter-current stages while preheating combustion air to ~750-900 degC.
equipment.qty_operating: 4 stages per train; C01 typically 2 cyclones in parallel, C02-C04 1 each (~5 cyclones per train, ~10 total)
equipment.type_selected: Riser + tangential cyclone stages, refractory-lined (hot) to lightly lined (cold), pendulum flaps
equipment.why_this_type: Direct gas-solid contact recovers most of the product sensible heat into combustion air. This is the main reason suspension calciners use ~35-40 % less fuel than rotary kilns.
key_dimensions: C01 ID ~5-6 m (x2); C02-C04 ID ~4.5-6 m (engineering estimate)
Each stage riser ~2.5-3.5 m ID (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.parameter: Alumina temperature C01 in -> C04 out
Air temperature C04 in -> C01 out

equipment.working_principle: Each stage is a riser plus a cyclone. Hot alumina from the stage above is dropped into the air stream rising from the stage below. It gives up heat in a second or two and is separated again in that stage's cyclone. The alumina therefore moves down C01 -> C04 while the air moves up C04 -> C01, the way a counter-current exchanger works. Four stages recover most of the product's sensible heat. Cold ambient air is drawn in at the C04 riser inlet by the ID fan, through an inlet silencer/filter and control damper.
details_to_model: Cascade of cyclones on lower tower levels, interconnected by risers and dip-legs with pendulum flaps
C01/C02 refractory lined; C03/C04 thinner abrasion lining
Ambient air inlet at C04 riser: louvred inlet hood with bird screen, silencer and damper; FBC exhaust air duct joins here
Air blasters on each cone; TCs and pressure taps per stage
Platforms at each cyclone inlet/flap level
hazards_and_safety: Hot alumina and hot air ducts; burn hazards at doors
Noise at air inlet
common_problems: Flap leakage reduces heat recovery (C01 air temperature falls, fuel rises)
Erosion at riser elbows (alumina is very abrasive, Mohs ~9 for alpha fraction)

equipment.name: Fluid bed cooler (FBC)
equipment.function: Final cooling of alumina from ~250-320 to ~70-90 degC by indirect water cooling in a fluidised bed; heat recovered to hot wash water.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal rectangular multi-compartment bubbling fluid bed with immersed water-cooled tube bundles
equipment.why_this_type: Fluidised alumina has high bed-to-tube heat transfer (typically ~200-400 W/m2K, engineering estimate), and the compartments give near counter-current plug flow.
key_dimensions: ~20-35 m long x ~4-6 m wide x ~5-7 m high including plenums (engineering estimate)
4-6 compartments separated by weirs/baffles; ~8-20 removable tube bundles (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Alumina enters one end and flows through the compartments under weirs or baffles. Air from blowers below the nozzle grid keeps it fluidised. Bundles of tubes carrying cooling water hang in the bed, and the moving particles carry heat to the tube walls very effectively. Water flows counter-current, from the outlet end to the inlet end, to get the most heat recovery. The fluidising air is heated by the bed and leaves through an exhaust duct to the C04 air inlet, so its heat is recovered as combustion air. Cooled alumina overflows at the discharge end into the product airslide.
details_to_model: Long rectangular steel box at grade/low level near tower base, with roof hatches above each tube bundle for crane removal
Tube bundles: U-tube or hairpin bundles hung from roof flanges, each with its own inlet/outlet valves, flow indicator and vent/drain; inlet and outlet headers along the side on a pipe rack
Air plenums (wind boxes) under each compartment with air pipes, manual balancing dampers and pressure gauges; grid with cap nozzles
Inlet chute from C04 at one end; overflow outlet box at the other end with discharge gate to airslide; bottom drain gates per compartment
Exhaust air outlet nozzle on roof to duct; inspection doors and sight glasses; bed TCs and DP taps per compartment
Gantry/monorail crane above roof for bundle pulling; walkway platform along roof
hazards_and_safety: Hot fluidised alumina flows like water: lockout and drain before entry
Tube leak: steam/water in the hot bed causes lumps, pressure surges and wet product
Pinch/crush during bundle lifting
common_problems: Tube erosion near nozzles; tube leaks
Nozzle blockage; defluidisation and channelling
operating_tips_and_key_points: Bed humidity/exhaust dew-point or water make-up trend gives early warning of tube leaks; isolate the bundle and run on the remaining bundles
equipment.materials: CS casing; CS or low-alloy tubes with wear shields; stainless nozzles
sources: FLSmidth / Metso Outotec FBC vendor literature
Kunii D. & Levenspiel O., Fluidization Engineering, 2nd ed. (bed-to-tube heat transfer)

equipment.name: FBC and holding-vessel fluidising air blowers
equipment.function: Supply fluidising air to the FBC compartments and the holding vessel.
equipment.type_selected: Multistage centrifugal or rotary-lobe (Roots) blowers with inlet filter/silencer
equipment.why_this_type: They give the moderate pressure (25-50 kPa) at steady flow needed for fluidisation; a standby is essential because bed collapse means a stop.
key_dimensions: Packaged skid ~4 x 2 x 2.5 m each with acoustic enclosure (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Rotary-lobe blowers trap and push fixed pockets of air (positive displacement); multistage centrifugals raise pressure across several impellers in series. Either way, filtered ambient air is compressed and sent through a header to the plenums of each fluid bed compartment and the HV. Each branch has flow control and a non-return valve.
details_to_model: Blower on baseplate with motor, V-belt or direct coupling, guard
Inlet filter-silencer, discharge silencer, relief valve, non-return valve, isolation butterfly
Acoustic enclosure with ventilation fan; pressure and temperature gauges
hazards_and_safety: Noise >85 dB(A) outside enclosures
Rotating parts; hot discharge pipe (~80-120 degC)

equipment.name: Electrostatic precipitator (calciner off-gas)
equipment.function: Remove alumina/hydrate dust from calciner off-gas to meet emission limits and recover product.
equipment.type_selected: Dry horizontal-flow plate-type ESP, 3-4 fields in series, rigid discharge electrodes, tumbling-hammer rapping
equipment.why_this_type: Handles the large, humid, warm gas volume at low pressure drop (~0.2-0.4 kPa); calciner dust in humid gas has resistivity suitable for ESP. Fabric filters are an alternative but suffer from the dew-point and moisture (~85 degC) of the gas.
key_dimensions: Casing ~20-30 m long x ~18-25 m wide x ~15-18 m high plus hoppers ~6-8 m (engineering estimate)
Collecting area ~10,000-15,000 m2 (SCA ~80-110 m2 per m3/s) (engineering estimate)
Plate spacing ~400 mm; collecting plate height ~12-15 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: typical licence limits; EU BREF NFM 2017 BAT-AEL range for alumina calcination lower

equipment.working_principle: High negative DC voltage on the discharge electrodes creates a corona that charges the dust particles as gas passes slowly (about 0.8-1.2 m/s) between earthed collecting plates. The charged particles migrate to the plates and form a layer. Periodic hammer rapping knocks the layer into the hoppers below. Each field removes most of the remaining dust; three or four fields in series give over 99.9 % collection. Gas distribution screens at the inlet spread the flow evenly. CO in the gas is a key hazard, because sparking in a combustible mixture can cause an explosion. The T/R sets therefore trip automatically on high CO.
details_to_model: Large rectangular box casing on columns; inlet transition (funnel) with 2-3 perforated distribution screens; outlet transition
Roof: one transformer-rectifier set per field (oil-filled tank with HV bushing in bus duct), insulator housings with heaters and purge-air fans, rapping drive motors for discharge electrodes
Side: rapping gear motors driving tumbling hammer shafts for collecting plates
Pyramidal hoppers (e.g., 2 across x 3-4 along), each with level probe, heater pads, poke hole and outlet to screw conveyor/rotary valve
Access doors on each field with Castell key interlock and earthing switch; stairs to roof penthouse; full insulation and cladding (~100 mm mineral wool + profiled sheeting)
Cutaway internals: collecting plates (C-profile strips), discharge electrode frames with pipe-and-spike electrodes, gas flow baffles
hazards_and_safety: High voltage (~70-100 kV DC): access only via key-interlock sequence (T/R off, earth switch closed, key released), plus earthing sticks
CO explosion risk: CO analyser at inlet; T/R trip at high CO (typical alarm ~0.3-0.5 %, trip ~0.5-1.0 % vol, site-specific engineering estimate)
Hot dust in hoppers (fluid, burns); confined space; heavy rapping hammers
common_problems: Hopper bridging from condensation when cold
Discharge electrode breakage short-circuiting a field
Emission spikes after rapping (rapping puffs)
instrumentation_and_control: Per-field kV/mA, spark rate; automatic voltage control
Inlet CO/O2; outlet opacity/dust monitor (in stack)
equipment.materials: CS casing, CS plates/electrodes, porcelain/alumina-ceramic insulators
sources: EU JRC BREF Non-Ferrous Metals Industries (2017)
White H.J., Industrial Electrostatic Precipitation; Parker K.R., Applied Electrostatic Precipitation

equipment.name: ESP dust collection and return system
equipment.function: Collect ESP hopper dust and return it to the calciner (P02 riser/furnace) for re-processing.
equipment.qty_operating: Per train: ~2 collecting screws, ~6-8 rotary feeders, 1 dust bin + 1 dense-phase/ airlift return
equipment.qty_standby: Return conveyor: 1 shared standby or bypass to product/off-spec (engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: Hopper rotary valves -> collecting screw conveyors -> dust bin -> dense-phase blow tank to P02 riser
equipment.why_this_type: ESP dust is partly calcined (high LOI), so it must be recalcined, not sent to product. Pneumatic return reaches the high return point in the tower.
key_dimensions: Collecting screws ~400-500 mm dia; dust bin ~30-60 m3; blow tank ~2-4 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Rotary airlock valves let dust out of the hoppers without letting air into the negative-pressure ESP. Screw conveyors gather the dust into a small bin. A blow tank fills, is closed and pressurised, and pushes the dust in batches through a pipeline to the injection point in the calciner tower.
details_to_model: Rotary valves under each hopper with gear motors; inclined collecting screws under hopper rows
Dust bin with vent filter; blow tank with dome inlet valve, vent valve, aeration pad, outlet valve, air control panel
DN 100-150 conveying line routed up tower with long-radius wear-resistant bends
hazards_and_safety: Hot fine dust inhalation; pressurised vessel (do not open under pressure)
sources: Mills D., Pneumatic Conveying Design Guide, 2nd ed.

equipment.name: Calciner induced-draft (ID) fan
equipment.function: Draws all gas through the coolers, furnace, preheaters, dryer and ESP, and discharges it to the stack; sets the system draft and throughput.
equipment.type_selected: Large single-inlet (or double-inlet) centrifugal fan, backward-curved/aerofoil impeller, MV motor with VFD
equipment.why_this_type: High volume at ~8-11 kPa with variable-speed control; placed after the ESP so it handles clean gas (low wear).
key_dimensions: Impeller diameter ~3.2-4.5 m; casing height ~7-9 m (engineering estimate)
Motor ~1.5-2.5 MW, 6.6-11 kV (engineering estimate: 125 m3/s x 9.5 kPa / 0.82 eff ~ 1.45 MW shaft)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (sum of cyclone stages + dryer + ESP + ducts)

equipment.working_principle: The rotating impeller flings gas outward, raising its pressure in the spiral (volute) casing. That creates suction throughout the calciner. Speed sets total gas flow, which with fuel rate sets furnace O2 and calciner capacity. Because every stage is under negative pressure, leaks draw air in rather than letting hot dust out.
details_to_model: Spiral volute casing on concrete plinth; inlet box with isolation damper (multi-louvre) and flexible joint; outlet evase to stack duct
Overhung or centre-hung impeller with two pedestal bearings (oil-lubricated, with lube oil unit), each with RTDs and vibration probes
Large MV motor with coupling and guard; VFD in e-house
Casing insulated and clad; drain; inspection door; maintenance monorail/crane over fan
hazards_and_safety: Rotating machinery; overspeed/imbalance; noise >85 dB(A)
Hot casing; positive-pressure stack side
common_problems: Imbalance from dust build-up when ESP efficiency falls; bearing temperature rise
instrumentation_and_control: Vibration (proximity probes/accelerometers) and bearing TT with trips
Speed control from furnace draft/O2 controller

equipment.name: Calciner stack with CEMS
equipment.function: Disperses cleaned off-gas; carries continuous emission monitoring.
equipment.qty_operating: 2 (1 per train), or 1 concrete windshield with 2 steel flues
equipment.type_selected: Self-supporting steel stack (insulated) with sampling platforms
equipment.why_this_type: Simple; insulation keeps the flue above dew point to avoid condensation and corrosion.
key_dimensions: Flue ID ~3.0-3.5 m (exit velocity ~15-20 m/s) (engineering estimate)
Height ~60-90 m, set by dispersion modelling/regulation (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Buoyant, high-velocity gas leaves well above ground so that pollutants are diluted before reaching ground level. The CEMS measures dust, O2, CO, NOx, (SO2 if oil-fired), flow, temperature and moisture continuously for compliance reporting.
details_to_model: Tapered base with breech inlet from ID fan duct; access door; condensate drain
Sampling platform at ~8 duct diameters downstream of the inlet with 4 sampling ports (ISO 9096 / AS 4323.1 / US EPA Method 1)
CEMS shelter at base; analyser probes; caged ladder or ladder with fall-arrest rail; rest platforms
Aircraft warning lights, lightning rod/earthing, insulated + clad shell
hazards_and_safety: Work at height; flue gas exposure at sampling ports (CO, low O2, heat)

equipment.name: Fuel gas pressure-reducing, metering and safety shut-off skid (with BMS)
equipment.function: Conditions, meters and safely isolates natural gas supply to the calciner burners.
equipment.type_selected: Outdoor skid: ESD valve, filter-separator, heater (if needed), PRV streams with slam-shut, metering, per-train safety shut-off valve trains
equipment.why_this_type: Codes (NFPA 85/86, EN 746-2, AS 3814) require proven-closure double block and vent valves, purge permissives and flame supervision.
key_dimensions: Skid ~15-20 m x 6-8 m in fenced area, set back from ignition sources per hazardous-area classification (engineering estimate)
Main pipe DN 250-300 (engineering estimate for ~25,000 Nm3/h)
equipment.working_principle: Gas passes through an emergency shutdown valve and a filter, then pressure-reducing runs with a monitor regulator and slam-shut valve in case of overpressure. It is metered (ultrasonic or turbine meter) and sent to each train. At each burner header the burner management system (BMS) holds two automatic shut-off valves with a vent between them (double block and bleed). They open only after a proven purge and ignition sequence, and they close in less than 1 s on flame failure, low air flow or ESD.
details_to_model: Yellow-painted gas pipework on low supports; filter-separator vessel; regulator runs with slam-shuts and relief valves venting via vent stack
Flow meter run with straight lengths; pressure/temperature gauges and transmitters
Per-train valve trains on the furnace burner platform: manual isolation, SSOV pair, vent valve, pressure switches, control valve
Gas detectors, hazardous-area signage, fence, emergency stop
hazards_and_safety: Gas explosion/fire; hazardous area Zone 2 per IEC 60079-10-1
Pressure; venting near personnel
instrumentation_and_control: BMS PLC (SIL-rated per IEC 61511), valve proving system, gas detection

equipment.name: FBC cooling-water circuit: circulation pumps, plate heat exchangers, cooling tower
equipment.function: Circulate closed-loop water through FBC bundles, transfer heat to process wash water (plate HX), and trim excess heat in a cooling tower.
equipment.qty_operating: Pumps 1 per train; HX 1 per train; cooling tower 1 multi-cell (2-3 cells) common
equipment.qty_standby: Pumps 1 per train; cooling tower 1 cell spare (engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal pumps (ISO 5199/ISO 2858); gasketed plate heat exchangers; induced-draft counterflow cooling tower
equipment.why_this_type: Standard clean-water service; plate exchangers give close approach for heat recovery to hydrate wash water.
key_dimensions: Pumps ~300-400 m3/h at ~35-50 m, 55-90 kW (engineering estimate)
Plate HX frames ~3 x 1 x 3 m (engineering estimate)
Cooling tower cells ~10 x 10 m plan, fans ~6-8 m dia (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Centrifugal pumps drive treated water through the FBC tube bundles, where it heats to about 55-70 degC. In the plate heat exchangers the water heats the hydrate filter wash water (counter-current, thin corrugated plates) and is then cooled further in the cooling tower if needed. An expansion tank with nitrogen or air cushion, side-stream filter and corrosion-inhibitor dosing protect the loop.
details_to_model: Pump sets on concrete plinths with suction strainers, isolation valves, check valves, pressure gauges, coupling guards
Plate HX frames with tie-bolts and nozzles on fixed plate
Cooling tower with fan stacks, motors/gearboxes, louvres, basin, make-up and blowdown; expansion tank and dosing skid
hazards_and_safety: Rotating equipment; hot water (scald) ~70 degC; Legionella control in cooling tower

equipment.name: Calciner plant and instrument air compressors (incl. air-blaster supply)
equipment.function: Provide dry compressed air for instruments, air blasters, purge air and pneumatic actuators.
equipment.type_selected: Oil-free rotary screw compressors with refrigerant/desiccant dryers and receivers
equipment.why_this_type: Oil-free air avoids contaminating the alumina; air blasters need a reliable 6-8 bar supply.
key_dimensions: Each ~2,000-4,000 Nm3/h, 250-450 kW; receivers ~10-20 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Two meshing screw rotors compress air without oil in the compression chamber. The air is cooled, dried and stored in receivers, then piped to the tower, where each air blaster has its own small receiver. Fired by a solenoid valve, an air blaster dumps that receiver through a nozzle into the cyclone cone to dislodge build-ups.
details_to_model: Compressor packages in compressor house; dryers; vertical receivers with safety valves
Air blaster tanks (~50-150 L) on cyclone cones with quick-dump valves and nozzle pipes (~20-40 per train)
hazards_and_safety: Air blaster discharge can cause injury and hot dust ejection: isolate and depressurise before cone/door work
sources: Martin Engineering / Global Manufacturing air cannon practice

equipment.name: Calciner product auto-sampler
equipment.function: Takes representative samples of each train's product for process control (LOI, BET, alpha, PSD, Na2O).
equipment.type_selected: Timed cross-stream/screw-type sampler in FBC discharge airslide, with pneumatic sample delivery to laboratory
equipment.why_this_type: Each train's product must be monitored separately to adjust its furnace temperature and HV.
key_dimensions: Compact enclosure ~1 x 1 x 1.5 m on airslide (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A cutter or screw probe periodically takes a slice of the flowing alumina. The increments are combined into a composite, and a pneumatic tube sends it to the lab. Results feed back to the furnace temperature set point.
details_to_model: Sampler body on airslide with motor/actuator, sample bottle carousel or pneumatic tube send station
hazards_and_safety: Hot alumina (up to ~90 degC); moving cutter
sources: ISO 2927 (alumina sampling), ISO 806 (LOI), ISO 8008 (BET), ISO 2926 (sieve analysis) - verify current editions

equipment.name: Calciner area sump pumps
equipment.function: Return wash-down water and spilled hydrate/alumina slurry from area bunds to process.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cantilever slurry sump pumps (no submerged bearings), rubber/hard-metal wetted parts
equipment.why_this_type: Robust for intermittent abrasive slurry; no submerged bearings or seals.
key_dimensions: ~30-80 m3/h at ~20-30 m; 15-30 kW; sump ~3 x 3 x 3 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The motor sits above the sump on a mounting plate and drives a long cantilevered shaft to an impeller near the bottom, which pumps slurry to the process. Start and stop are controlled by sump level.
details_to_model: Grated sump pit with pump mounting plate, motor on top, discharge pipe with check and isolation valves, level float/radar
hazards_and_safety: Open pit/grating removal; mildly caustic slurry
sources: Weir Warman / Metso slurry pump practice

equipment.name: Calciner tower structure, stair tower, goods/passenger lift and maintenance hoists
equipment.function: Supports cyclones, furnace, HV and ducts; provides access and maintenance lifting.
equipment.type_selected: Braced structural-steel tower (or concrete core + steel) with grated floors, external stair tower and rack-and-pinion/traction lift
equipment.why_this_type: Gives access to ~10-14 working levels; the lift moves refractory, flaps and vortex-finder segments.
key_dimensions: Footprint ~25-30 m x 25-35 m; height to top of P01/P02 cyclones ~60-80 m (engineering estimate)
Lift capacity ~1.5-2.5 t (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: wind/cyclonic and seismic per AS 1170 / IS 875 / IS 1893

equipment.working_principle: The steel frame carries the hot vessels on support rings and lugs and allows for their thermal growth. Monorails and davits over each cyclone roof lift internals down through hatches and onto the lift.
details_to_model: Column/beam grid with diagonal bracing; grating floors, handrails with kick-plates; stair tower with landings every floor
Lift shaft with cage; monorail beams with chain hoists above cyclone roofs and FBC; partial wall cladding; emergency lighting; safety showers at each level near caustic/hot work
hazards_and_safety: Work at height; dropped objects; heat stress on upper levels; escape routes (2 per level)
sources: AS 1170 / IS 875 / IS 1893; AS 1657 (platforms, stairs, ladders)

areas.layout_notes: Two calciner towers side by side, ~40-60 m centre-to-centre (engineering estimate), each with its ESP, ID fan and stack in line downstream (gas flow direction away from the control room and towards the prevailing downwind side). Tower footprint ~25-30 x 25-35 m, height ~60-80 m; cyclone order from top: P01 (dryer cyclones) and P02 at top levels, P04 cyclones and furnace top in the middle-upper levels, HV mid-level, C01-C04 descending, FBC at grade. Hydrate pan filters (A14) are on an adjacent structure or on top of the calciner feed building so cake discharges directly into the feed bins. ESP ~20-40 m from tower, ID fan at grade beside ESP outlet, stack ~10-20 m beyond. Fuel gas skid in a fenced area >=15-30 m from ignition sources (hazardous-area study). Cooling tower and pumps at grade near the FBC. Main pipe rack (NG, cooling water, compressed air, power and control cables) along the calciner row, ~6-8 m high, linking to A14 and A16. Product airslides discharge to dense-phase vessels at the tower base, with pipelines ~300-600 m to product silos (A16). Common calciner control room/e-house ~50-100 m from towers, outside the hazardous-area and hot-alumina spill zone. Heavy-vehicle access roads around each tower for cranes (refractory relines), with laydown area.
interfaces: A14 Hydrate filtration/washing: wet hydrate feed (moisture and soda set calciner fuel use and product Na2O); hot wash water supplied from FBC heat recovery
A16 Product storage & conveying: calcined alumina from FBC airslides; off-spec diversion
Utilities: natural gas supply (or fuel oil from A17 port tank farm), MV power (~8-12 MW connected for 2 trains, engineering estimate), cooling water make-up, demineralised water, compressed air
Laboratory: LOI, MOI, BET, alpha, PSD, chemistry (ISO methods)
Environmental: stack CEMS reporting; ESP dust return
A13 Precipitation: hydrate strength and PSD govern product fines (-45 um) and attrition index

areas.purpose: Gently move hot SGA from the calciner fluid bed coolers to refinery product silos, store ~7 days of production, segregate off-spec material, and reclaim product to the overland conveyor to the port (plus an optional road-tanker loadout). Main design constraints: low particle attrition (to protect the -45 um specification), no moisture pick-up or contamination (Fe, Si, organics), and dust-free enclosed handling.
areas.process_description: 1) Each FBC discharges into an enclosed airslide that feeds a twin-vessel dense-phase pneumatic conveying system (one line per calciner). 2) Dense-phase conveying moves alumina at low velocity (~3-10 m/s, engineering estimate) and high solids loading to minimise particle breakage. Lean-phase airlifts are avoided because they generate fines. 3) The pipelines discharge at the silo roofs into 2 x 20,000 t concrete product silos (40,000 t, ~7 days). A diverter can send start-up or off-spec alumina (e.g., high LOI after a trip) to a 3,000-5,000 t off-spec silo, from which it is reprocessed back to calcination or digestion in controlled amounts. 4) Silo vent air (conveying air) passes through pulse-jet bag filters, and the dust returns to the silo. 5) Silo bottoms have aerated sectors (sequential aeration) with flow-control gates discharging into airslides and onto an enclosed reclaim belt conveyor fitted with a belt scale, a self-cleaning magnet (protects the Fe spec) and a sampler. 6) The reclaim conveyor feeds the covered overland conveyor (~8 km assumed; site-specific) to the port (A17), at ~800 t/h design, running ~8-10 h/d. 7) An optional road/rail tanker loadout serves domestic smelters. SGA properties that matter: loose bulk density ~0.95-1.05 t/m3, angle of repose ~30-35 deg, very abrasive, fluidisable (Geldart A/B), hygroscopic (MOI rises in humid air), so all handling is enclosed.

streams.name: SGA from calciners
streams.flow: 146 t/h per line at nameplate (design ~160-175 t/h per line); plant average 241 t/h

equipment.name: FBC discharge airslides and airslide blowers
equipment.function: Convey cooled alumina by gravity-fluidisation from FBC outlets to dense-phase vessel feed hoppers.
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed air-gravity conveyor (airslide) with woven polyester or ceramic porous membrane
equipment.why_this_type: Low power, almost no attrition, fully enclosed; ideal for fluidisable alumina on a downward slope.
key_dimensions: Width ~400-600 mm; slope ~4-8 deg; lengths ~10-40 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.unit: Nm3/min per m2 of fabric at ~3-6 kPa

equipment.working_principle: A rectangular trough is split horizontally by a porous fabric. Low-pressure air blown into the lower chamber passes up through the fabric and fluidises the alumina above it. Fluidised alumina flows like a liquid down the gentle slope. The upper chamber vents to a dust filter.
details_to_model: Two-piece flanged rectangular steel trough, bolted flanges every ~2-3 m, fabric between
Air inlet stubs with butterfly valves under trough; vent nozzles on top
Flow control gates, inspection windows/sight glasses; supports on slope; small centrifugal fan/blower with filter
hazards_and_safety: Hot alumina at ~80 degC flows freely if a cover is opened; dust

equipment.name: Dense-phase pneumatic conveying vessels (twin blow tanks per line)
equipment.function: Transport SGA from each calciner to the product silos with low attrition.
equipment.qty_standby: Cross-connection to allow one line to deliver to either silo; no idle spare line (engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: Twin pressure-vessel (blow tank) dense-phase system, alternating fill/convey for quasi-continuous flow
equipment.why_this_type: Low conveying velocity reduces particle breakage and pipe wear compared with lean-phase or airlifts; flexible pipe routing up ~50-60 m to silo roofs.
key_dimensions: Each vessel ~8-15 m3, ~2.5-3 m dia, ~4-5 m tall with conical bottom (engineering estimate)
Design pressure ~6 bar(g); ASME VIII Div 1 / AS 1210
Conveying distance ~300-600 m, lift ~50-60 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: While one vessel conveys, the other fills by gravity from the feed hopper through its inlet valve, with the vent valve open. When full (load cells or level probe), the inlet and vent close and the vessel is pressurised with air. The outlet valve then opens and a dense plug-like stream of alumina is pushed through the pipeline. When the vessel pressure drops (empty), the outlet closes and the vessel vents. The two vessels alternate, so delivery to the silo is nearly continuous.
details_to_model: Vertical pressure vessels in a steel frame below the airslide feed hopper; top dome/ball inlet valve with pneumatic actuator
Vent valve and vent line back to hopper; aeration cone/pad at bottom; outlet valve to pipeline; pressure-vessel nameplate, safety valve
Load cells or level probes; air control panel (pressure regulators, flow orifices, solenoids) in cabinet
Pipeline DN 250-350 (stepped), ceramic-lined or hardened long-radius bends, pipe supports with sliding shoes, routed on rack and up silo stair tower
hazards_and_safety: Pressure vessel: never open hatches under pressure; PSV testing
Pipeline blockage clearing under pressure is dangerous: depressurise first
Noise from venting
common_problems: Line blockage after feed surge or air loss
Bend wear
instrumentation_and_control: PLC sequence; pressure transmitters on vessel and line; line-blockage detection (pressure high/time)
equipment.materials: CS vessel; ceramic/alloy wear bends; abrasion-resistant valve seats
equipment.alternatives: Bucket elevator + enclosed belt conveyor + airslides (lower power, higher maintenance); airlift (lean phase, more attrition).
sources: Mills D., Pneumatic Conveying Design Guide, 2nd ed.
Klinzing G.E. et al., Pneumatic Conveying of Solids

equipment.name: Conveying air compressors with dryers and receivers
equipment.function: Supply dry, oil-free air for dense-phase conveying and silo aeration boost.
equipment.type_selected: Oil-free rotary screw compressors (VFD on one), refrigerated dryers, vertical receivers
equipment.why_this_type: Oil-free, dry air keeps the alumina clean and prevents moisture pick-up (MOI).
key_dimensions: Each ~60-90 Nm3/min, ~350-500 kW; receivers ~20-30 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Screw compressors supply a ring main and receivers. Each conveying line draws air through pressure regulators. The receivers buffer the fast pressurisation demand of the blow tanks.
details_to_model: Compressor house with packages, aftercoolers, dryers, receivers with PSVs and drains, ring-main headers
hazards_and_safety: Noise; stored pressure energy; hot surfaces

equipment.name: Refinery product alumina silos
equipment.function: Store SGA (~2 x 20,000 t) to buffer between calcination and port despatch.
equipment.type_selected: Slip-formed reinforced-concrete silos with central inverted cone and aerated annular floor (multi-sector sequential aeration)
equipment.why_this_type: Concrete silos hold large volumes on a small footprint; aerated floors with central cones give near-complete discharge of fluidisable alumina and first-in-first-out flow.
key_dimensions: ID ~26-28 m; wall height ~40-50 m; overall height including roof house ~50-60 m (engineering estimate: 20,000 t / ~1.0 t/m3 ~ 20,000 m3 + freeboard)
8-12 aeration sectors (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Alumina enters at the roof. To discharge, compressed air is blown sequentially into floor sectors through porous aeration panels or airslides sloping towards outlets in a central inverted cone. This fluidises the alumina above those sectors and it flows to the outlets. Flow control gates meter it into discharge airslides. Rotating the active sector draws the silo down evenly and avoids dead zones. The roof vent filter handles the displaced air plus the conveying air.
details_to_model: Tall concrete cylinder with smooth slipform finish; flat or conical steel/concrete roof with roof house (filters, inlet piping, diverters)
External stair tower with landings (or internal stairs in an annex) plus personnel/goods lift; roof handrails
Radar level gauges, pressure/vacuum relief valve, roof manholes, lightning protection
Base: discharge tunnel or ring with outlet gates (manual slide gate + pneumatic flow-control gate), aeration piping manifold with solenoid valves per sector, inspection doors into cone
Silo-top bag filter (pulse-jet) with fan and discharge rotary valve back to silo
hazards_and_safety: Silo entry: engulfment and fluidised-alumina drowning risk, never enter while aeration is possible (isolate blowers), confined space permit
Work at height on roof; structural overpressure if vent filter blinds
common_problems: Dead zones/caking from moisture ingress; sector valve failure
Segregation of fines near walls and filter return
operating_tips_and_key_points: Rotate silos (fill/reclaim) to keep stock fresh; keep roof hatches closed in rain (hygroscopic product)
instrumentation_and_control: Radar LT; vent filter DP; sector aeration sequencer; flow-gate position
equipment.materials: Reinforced concrete; steel roof; polyester/ceramic aeration panels
sources: Claudius Peters / IBAU silo technology literature

equipment.name: Off-spec alumina silo
equipment.function: Receive start-up/upset or contaminated alumina for controlled reprocessing.
equipment.type_selected: Steel silo with aerated cone bottom and rotary feeder
equipment.why_this_type: Keeps off-spec material out of product silos while still recovering it.
key_dimensions: ~3,000-5,000 t; ~14-16 m dia x ~25-30 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A diverter valve on the dense-phase line sends off-spec alumina here. It is later fed slowly back into the calciner (P02 riser) or to digestion so that it does not disturb product quality.
details_to_model: Steel shell on skirt or columns, conical aerated bottom, rotary feeder and small dense-phase return vessel; vent filter; ladder/stairs
hazards_and_safety: As for product silos

equipment.name: Silo vent and transfer-point dust collectors
equipment.function: Clean displaced/conveying air from silos and transfer points; return dust to process.
equipment.type_selected: Pulse-jet bag filters (polyester or PTFE-membrane bags) with exhaust fans
equipment.why_this_type: High efficiency (<10-20 mg/Nm3) on fine alumina dust; product recovery.
key_dimensions: Silo vent filters ~300-600 m2 cloth each; transfer collectors ~100-300 m2 (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; typical BAT for fabric filters

equipment.working_principle: Dusty air passes through filter bags from outside to inside, and dust collects on the bag surface. Short pulses of compressed air shaken through the bags from inside in sequence knock the dust off into the hopper. It is returned by rotary valve.
details_to_model: Rectangular housing with hopper, clean-air plenum with walk-in or top-access doors, pulse valves and header tank, rotary valve, fan with stack, DP gauge
hazards_and_safety: Confined space; compressed air; falling from roof access

equipment.name: Silo reclaim conveyor with belt scale, tramp-iron magnet and sampler
equipment.function: Collect alumina from silo discharges and deliver it to the overland conveyor at a measured rate.
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed troughed belt conveyor (1,050 mm), covered gallery, belt scale, self-cleaning overband magnet, cross-belt sampler
equipment.why_this_type: High-rate, gentle transport; magnet protects the Fe2O3 product spec; scale for inventory control.
key_dimensions: Belt 1,050 mm, ~3-3.5 m/s, length ~150-400 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (CEMA capacity for 1,050 mm, 35 deg trough, low surcharge ~0.08-0.09 m2)
engineering estimate: fluidisable alumina runs back on steep belts

equipment.working_principle: A rubber belt on troughed idlers carries alumina from silo outlets to the transfer tower. A belt scale (load cells under weigh idlers plus speed sensor) integrates the tonnage. An overband magnet lifts any tramp iron. A cross-belt sampler periodically sweeps a full cross-section of the stream.
details_to_model: Conveyor stringers, 3-roll troughing idlers at ~1.2 m pitch, return idlers ~3 m, hood covers/enclosed gallery with walkway
Head pulley drive (motor, fluid coupling/VFD, gearbox), tail pulley, gravity take-up, belt cleaners (primary/secondary), skirt boards
Pull-wire emergency stops along both sides, belt drift and speed switches, guards on all pulleys
Belt scale weigh frame; magnet with cross-belt and reject chute; sampler hammer-cutter
hazards_and_safety: Conveyor nip points (guarding per AS 4024 / ISO 14120); pull-wire stops; lockout
Dust
sources: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials, 7th ed.

equipment.name: Overland covered belt conveyor to port (with transfer towers)
equipment.function: Transport SGA from refinery silos to port silos.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (silo buffers at both ends cover outages)
equipment.type_selected: Covered troughed steel-cord belt conveyor on ground-level and elevated trestles, hooded with walkway (pipe conveyor alternative)
equipment.why_this_type: Lowest-cost, low-attrition, enclosed bulk transport for ~2 Mt/yr over a few km. Rail (covered hopper wagons) is the alternative for longer distances (e.g., Damanjodi -> Visakhapatnam).
key_dimensions: Length ~8 km assumed (site-specific; engineering estimate)
Belt 1,050 mm ST1000-ST1600 steel cord, ~3.5-4 m/s (engineering estimate)
Head drives ~2 x 315-450 kW (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate: 5,500 t/d / 800 t/h ~7 h + margin

equipment.working_principle: This is the same principle as the reclaim conveyor, over a long distance. Low-friction idlers and a steel-cord belt carry high tension. VFD drives give a controlled, soft start, and a gravity take-up keeps belt tension. Steel hoods keep rain off the hygroscopic product and stop wind blowing dust.
details_to_model: Continuous arched steel hoods on carry side, one-side walkway with handrail, crossover stairs every ~300-500 m
Elevated trusses at road/rail crossings; transfer towers with chutes, dust collectors, enclosed walls
Drive station with 2 motors, gearboxes, brakes, holdback; gravity take-up tower with counterweight
Pull-wire switches every ~50 m both sides, drift switches, rip detection, fire detection (linear heat), lighting
hazards_and_safety: Entrapment at idlers/pulleys; long isolation distances (radio + local isolators)
Heavy vehicles at crossings
sources: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials, 7th ed.

equipment.name: Road/rail tanker alumina loadout (optional, domestic market)
equipment.function: Load SGA into pressure-discharge bulk tankers for local smelters.
equipment.type_selected: Telescopic loading spout with integrated dust extraction over a weighbridge
equipment.why_this_type: Dust-free loading of enclosed bulk tankers.
key_dimensions: Loading rate ~150-300 t/h; weighbridge 18-25 m (engineering estimate)
