equipment.working_principle: The spout lowers onto the tanker hatch, alumina flows from an airslide through the inner cone, and displaced air is drawn back through the outer annulus to a filter. Level sensing stops flow when the tanker is full.
details_to_model: Small feed bin, flow gate, telescopic bellows spout with winch, hatch-seal cone, extraction fan/filter, weighbridge, traffic lights, fall-protection gantry
hazards_and_safety: Work at height on tanker roofs (fall-arrest gantry); vehicle movements

areas.layout_notes: Product silos located ~300-600 m from calciner towers, at the refinery boundary on the port side to shorten the overland route. Silos in a row ~10-15 m apart with shared stair/lift tower and a roof-level bridge carrying pipelines and a walkway; off-spec silo adjacent. Compressor house near dense-phase vessels at calciner base. Reclaim conveyor in a tunnel or ground-level gallery under the silo outlets, running to transfer tower TT-001, then the overland conveyor follows a dedicated corridor (with caustic/fuel pipelines and power/fibre) to the port. Road access for loadout away from main conveyor crossing points.
interfaces: A15 Calcination: product from FBC; off-spec return to P02
A17 Port: overland conveyor delivery to port silos; pipelines (caustic, fuel) share corridor
Utilities: compressed air, MV power, control system (despatch inventory)
Laboratory: product certificates from composite samples

areas.area_name: Port & export (alumina export; caustic, fuel and lime import)
areas.purpose: Receive SGA by overland conveyor, store ~100,000 t at the port, and load bulk carriers (Handysize-Panamax) at ~2,000 t/h with enclosed, dust-controlled handling and trade-certified weighing and sampling. Also receive bulk liquid caustic soda (50 % NaOH) and fuel oil from chemical/product tankers, and quicklime from bulk carriers or by road, for transfer to the refinery.
areas.process_description: EXPORT: 1) The overland conveyor discharges at the port receiving tower onto a silo-top conveyor with diverter gates into 4 x 25,000 t concrete silos (100,000 t ~ 1.5-2 cargoes). 2) For ship loading, two silos are reclaimed at the same time through aerated bottoms and flow-control gates onto a reclaim conveyor, then onto the jetty conveyor (enclosed gallery on trestle) and a wharf conveyor with a tripper feeding the travelling shiploader. 3) A trade-certified belt weigher (OIML R50) and a primary cross-stream sampler (ISO 2927 principles) on the jetty conveyor provide shipping weight and quality certificate; draft survey confirms. 4) The rail-mounted, luffing and telescopic (shuttle) shiploader moves between hatches; a telescopic cascade chute with dust extraction places alumina low in the hold to reduce dust and aeration. Holds must be clean and dry; alumina (IMSBC Code group C) is free-flowing when aerated and must be trimmed. No water sprays are used on product (moisture spec); dust control is by enclosure and bag filters. 5) Typical vessels: Handysize/Supramax 25,000-60,000 DWT (cargo ~30,000-55,000 t), occasionally Panamax 65,000-80,000 DWT; ~40-60 shipments/yr. Loading ~2,000 t/h rated (~1,400-1,700 t/h effective incl. hatch changes) gives a 50,000 t cargo in ~30-40 h. IMPORT: 6) Caustic soda 50 % w/w (UN 1824, class 8) arrives in chemical tankers (10,000-30,000 DWT parcels) at a common-user liquid berth. Ship pumps discharge through marine loading arms/hoses to 2 x ~15,000 m3 carbon-steel tanks (API 650) at <~50 degC (caustic SCC limit, NACE SP0403). Transfer pumps send caustic by pipeline (in the conveyor corridor) to refinery storage (A-liquor/utilities areas). 7) Fuel oil (HFO, backup/alternative calciner and boiler fuel) and diesel (mine fleet) are received the same way into heated, bunded tanks. 8) Quicklime (IMSBC 'LIME (UNSLAKED)', group B: reacts with water and releases heat) is a small-tonnage import (~30,000-80,000 t/yr, if not supplied by road). A mobile harbour crane grabs it into a dust-controlled eco-hopper and loads covered trucks or a conveyor to lime silos.

streams.name: Ship loading
streams.basis: engineering estimate; typical alumina terminals 1,500-2,500 t/h

streams.name: Caustic soda import
streams.flow: ~120,000-200,000 t/yr NaOH (100 %) = ~240,000-400,000 t/yr 50 % solution (depends on reactive silica; to be confirmed by digestion/DSP area); ship discharge ~500-1,000 m3/h; transfer to refinery ~100-200 m3/h

streams.name: Fuel oil import (backup/alternative)
streams.flow: Backup only if NG-fired; if HFO is primary fuel ~150,000 t/yr (3.0 GJ/t x 2.0 Mt / ~40 GJ/t)

equipment.name: Port receiving tower and silo-top distribution conveyor
equipment.function: Receive the overland conveyor and distribute alumina into any port silo.
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed troughed belt conveyor across silo roofs with pneumatic plough/diverter-gate discharge points
equipment.why_this_type: Simple, enclosed and selectable feed to each silo.
key_dimensions: Belt 1,050 mm; length ~150-200 m across 4 silos at ~60-70 m elevation (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: An inclined gallery lifts the belt to the silo roofs. Plough or diverter gates over each silo inlet divert the stream into the selected silo. A dust collector serves each discharge point.
details_to_model: Inclined truss gallery with cladding, walkway both sides; receiving tower with chutes and dust collector; plough diverters with actuators above each silo inlet
hazards_and_safety: Work at height; conveyor guarding; wind exposure

equipment.name: Port alumina storage silos
equipment.function: Store ~100,000 t SGA to assemble ship cargoes and buffer shipping delays.
equipment.type_selected: Slip-formed concrete silos with aerated multi-sector floors and central cones (same technology as 16-SI)
equipment.why_this_type: Silos give contamination-free, weather-proof storage and gravity/aeration reclaim at high rate without mobile equipment. Large enclosed sheds with portal reclaimers (used at some alumina ports) are the alternative but need mobile equipment and generate more dust.
key_dimensions: ID ~28-30 m; wall ~45-50 m; overall ~55-65 m (engineering estimate: 25,000 t at ~1.0 t/m3)
Silo spacing ~5-10 m; common stair/lift tower

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (~1.5-2 x largest typical cargo)

equipment.working_principle: Same as the refinery silos: sequential sector aeration fluidises alumina above the active sectors, and it flows through central-cone outlets and flow-control gates into airslides onto the reclaim conveyor. Gate positions are adjusted to hold the shiploader rate steady.
details_to_model: Four tall concrete cylinders in a row; roof house with distribution conveyor, vent filters and inlets
Base outlet chambers with gates, airslides and blower house (rotary-lobe blowers ~0.5-0.8 bar(g)); reclaim tunnel below
Radar level, P/V relief, lightning protection, aircraft lighting if required, cyclone-rated design for coastal sites
hazards_and_safety: Engulfment / fluidised-material drowning; confined space; work at height
Coastal wind loads; corrosion protection

equipment.name: Reclaim, jetty and wharf conveyors with trade belt weigher and shipment sampler
equipment.function: Convey alumina from port silos along the jetty to the shiploader; measure the cargo weight for trade and take the quality-certificate sample.
equipment.qty_operating: 3 conveyors in series (reclaim, jetty, wharf with tripper)
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed troughed belt conveyors 1,400 mm; jetty conveyor in closed gallery on piled trestle; OIML R50 class 0.5 belt scale; cross-stream primary sampler with sample preparation
equipment.why_this_type: High rate with full enclosure over water (no spillage to sea).
key_dimensions: Belt 1,400 mm at ~4 m/s (engineering estimate; CEMA area ~0.15-0.17 m2 for low-surcharge alumina)
Jetty length site-specific, ~0.5-2 km (engineering estimate)
Drives ~250-600 kW each (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Belt conveyors move the alumina from the silos to the wharf. On the wharf conveyor, a travelling tripper (part of the shiploader) lifts the belt over a pulley pair and discharges the material onto the shiploader boom belt wherever the loader is positioned. The trade belt weigher integrates mass. It is calibrated with test chains or a material test against a weighbridge. The sampler cuts the full stream at fixed intervals to build a composite for ISO testing.
details_to_model: Fully clad jetty gallery with walkway, windows, lighting, fire detection; trestle on steel piles with cross-bracing
Wharf conveyor along the berth in an open-top or covered trench with belt-lifting tripper carriage rails
Trade weigher in a wind-shielded section; sampler house with cutter, secondary divider, sample bottles
Transfer towers with dust collectors; pull-wires, drift switches
hazards_and_safety: Conveyor entrapment; falls over water (life rings, rescue boat access)
Lightning/wind on exposed galleries
sources: OIML R50 continuous totalising automatic weighing instruments

equipment.name: Travelling shiploader (rail-mounted, luffing and telescopic boom)
equipment.function: Loads alumina into bulk carriers at ~2,000 t/h, reaching all hatches and across the ship's beam.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (port silo buffer; maintenance windows between ships)
equipment.type_selected: Rail-mounted travelling shiploader with luffing boom, telescopic (shuttle) boom conveyor, tripper, and telescopic cascade loading chute with dust extraction
equipment.why_this_type: A linear wharf with one loader covering Handysize-Panamax vessels; luffing clears ship air draft and the shuttle reaches the far side of the hold without warping the ship.
key_dimensions: Rail gauge ~12-16 m; travel length ~200-260 m (engineering estimate)
Outreach from fender line ~22-30 m; boom shuttle stroke ~10-15 m; luff angle ~-10 to +15 deg (engineering estimate for Panamax beam 32.3 m)
Boom belt 1,400 mm; loader mass ~600-1,200 t (engineering estimate)
Air draft clearance under boom ~18-22 m above wharf (site/tide dependent, engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; per AS 4324.1 / ISO 5049-1 design

equipment.working_principle: The loader travels on two rails along the wharf. The wharf conveyor belt passes through the tripper carriage, which raises the belt and discharges onto the loader's boom conveyor. The boom luffs (raised or lowered by hydraulic cylinders or wire-rope winch) to clear hatch coamings and cranes. The boom conveyor shuttles in and out to place the chute anywhere across the hatch. The telescopic cascade chute drops alumina through a series of cones so that it stays a dense stream and does not spread as a plume. Its lower end sits close to the cargo pile, and an extraction ring draws dust back to the loader's bag filter. The operator in the boom cab follows a hatch sequence (load plan) to keep the ship's stresses and trim within limits.
details_to_model: Portal gantry (2 legs seaside, 2 landside) with equalised bogies (~16-32 wheels total), rail clamps, storm tie-down pins and pits, buffers
Tripper car coupled to landside with inclined belt, discharge chute and dust seal
Slewing not required; luffing boom (box girder or truss) pivoted on the portal, with luffing cylinders/rope reeving and counterweight
Shuttle (telescopic) boom with conveyor 1,400 mm, belt covers, walkway and handrails both sides
Operator cab under/on boom with tilted glazing, A/C; electrical house on portal; MV cable reel and cable trench; anemometer at boom tip
Telescopic cascade chute (~10-20 m extension) with hoist winch, dust extraction hood/skirt; trimming spoon optional
Anti-collision (laser/radar) boom-to-ship and loader-to-loader sensors, travel warning horns/beacons, emergency stops, lighting masts
Onboard pulse-jet dust collector at boom tail transfer
hazards_and_safety: Boom/ship collision; crushing at rails (travel alarms, wheel guards)
Wind and cyclone: auto storm-brake engagement, tie-downs, anemometer interlocks
Work at height and over water; hatch access (falls into holds), oxygen-depleted holds (entry permits)
Dust exposure at hatch; noise
common_problems: Chute wear and liner replacement; dust emissions at hatch openings when chute is lifted high
Cable reel faults
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep chute discharge low in the pile; reduce rate when topping off to avoid alumina flushing
Coordinate the load plan with ship's officer for trim and ballast; draft surveys at start and finish
instrumentation_and_control: PLC with position encoders (travel, luff, shuttle), load-plan display, rate control to silo gates
Wind speed interlocks, overload/slack rope, end limits
equipment.materials: Structural steel (marine coating system ISO 12944 C5-M/CX)
sources: AS 4324.1 / ISO 5049-1 mobile equipment for continuous handling of bulk materials

equipment.name: Alumina export berth (wharf, fenders, mooring)
equipment.function: Safely berth and moor Handysize-Panamax bulk carriers alongside the shiploader.
equipment.type_selected: Open piled wharf (steel/concrete piles, concrete deck) or jetty head with mooring/breasting dolphins
equipment.why_this_type: Open piled structures suit deep-water, sea-exposed sites and minimise dredging.
key_dimensions: Berth length ~250-280 m (engineering estimate; Panamax LOA ~225-230 m)
Dredged depth ~-13.5 to -15 m CD (engineering estimate for Panamax draft ~12-14 m plus under-keel clearance)
Deck level ~+4 to +6 m CD (site tide dependent)
equipment.working_principle: Fenders absorb berthing energy. Mooring lines from the ship go to quick-release hooks (QRH) or bollards. Tension and environmental loads are checked against OCIMF MEG4 practice and BS 6349 / PIANC design rules.
details_to_model: Cone or cell fenders with steel frontal panels at ~15-25 m spacing
Quick-release mooring hooks (100-150 t SWL) on mooring dolphins with access walkways
Shiploader rails with cable trench, wharf conveyor, crane rail stops
Gangway tower; bollards; ladders and life-rings at ~30 m; navigation lights; fire monitors and hydrants
Spill containment kerbs and drainage to collection sumps
hazards_and_safety: Mooring line snap-back zones (painted marking)
Falls into water; ship movement
Heavy vehicles on wharf deck

equipment.name: Port dust collection system (transfer towers, silo roofs, shiploader)
equipment.function: Capture alumina dust at all transfer points and the loading chute.
equipment.type_selected: Pulse-jet bag filters with fans
equipment.why_this_type: Water sprays are not acceptable on SGA (moisture/MOI spec); dry filtration recovers product.
key_dimensions: ~100-800 m2 cloth each (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: As for 16-DC. Each enclosure is held at slight negative pressure so dust is drawn into the filter instead of escaping.
details_to_model: Filter casings with hoppers, rotary valves returning dust to belt, fans and short stacks, extraction hoods at chutes
hazards_and_safety: Confined space, compressed air, work at height
sources: EU JRC BREF NFM 2017 / BREF on Emissions from Storage

equipment.name: Marine loading arms / hose system for caustic and fuel import
equipment.function: Connect tanker manifolds to shore pipelines for caustic soda and fuel oil discharge.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 caustic arm, 1 fuel arm (common-user liquid berth)
equipment.type_selected: Counterbalanced marine loading arms DN 200-250 with powered emergency release couplers (PERC)
equipment.why_this_type: Safe, repeatable connections for hazardous liquids; ERC prevents rupture if the ship drifts.
key_dimensions: Arm reach envelope ~15-20 m; riser ~10-15 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Swivel-jointed articulated pipe arms, balanced by counterweights, connect to the ship manifold through a quick-connect coupler. If the ship moves beyond the operating envelope, the PERC closes valves on both sides and separates, limiting spillage.
details_to_model: Riser, inner arm, outer arm, counterweight, swivels, quick-connect/disconnect coupler, PERC with double ball valves, hydraulic power pack, drip tray, separate caustic-resistant arm (stainless/CS) colour-coded
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spray (severe burns/blindness): face shield, chemical suit, safety showers on berth
Fuel fire; spill to sea (spill kits, booms)
sources: OCIMF Design and Construction Specification for Marine Loading Arms

equipment.name: Caustic soda (50 % NaOH) import storage tanks
equipment.function: Store imported caustic soda for transfer to the refinery.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical fixed cone-roof carbon-steel tanks (API 650) in a concrete bund, insulated (and heated only where ambient falls below ~15 degC)
equipment.why_this_type: Carbon steel is acceptable for 50 % NaOH below the caustic stress-corrosion-cracking limit (keep <~50 degC per NACE SP0403 chart, without PWHT).
key_dimensions: ~15,000 m3 each: ~32-34 m dia x ~18-20 m high (engineering estimate)
Bund capacity >=110 % of largest tank (AS 3780 / local codes)

operating_parameters.basis: NACE SP0403 limits; crystallisation ~12 degC for 50 %

equipment.working_principle: These are atmospheric storage tanks filled by ship discharge and emptied by transfer pumps. A breather vent with a CO2 scrubber (optional) limits carbonation. High-level alarms and an independent high-high trip on the ship-discharge valve prevent overfill.
details_to_model: Cylindrical tank with external spiral stair, roof handrail, roof manhole, breather vent
Shell manways (2), inlet nozzle with internal downcomer, outlet nozzle with ROSOV, drain, sample point
Radar level gauge + independent high-high level switch; temperature element
Insulation (where used) with metal cladding; steam/electric heating coil (where required)
Concrete bund wall with sump and pump; safety showers/eyewash at bund access and pump area; corrosive signage
hazards_and_safety: Caustic burns and eye damage; slippery spills; never mix with acids or aluminium (H2 generation)
Confined-space entry only after neutralisation and gas test (H2 possible if aluminium was present)
sources: AS 3780 Storage and handling of corrosive substances

equipment.name: Caustic transfer pumps and pipeline to refinery
equipment.function: Pump caustic from port tanks to refinery caustic storage.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal pumps (ISO 5199 / API 610 OH2) with double mechanical seals; carbon-steel welded pipeline DN 150-200 with pigging and leak detection
equipment.why_this_type: Reliable continuous transfer; double seals prevent caustic leakage.
key_dimensions: Pump ~150-250 m3/h at ~80-150 m head, 75-160 kW (engineering estimate for ~8 km line)
Pipeline ~8 km DN 150-200 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Centrifugal pumps raise pressure to overcome pipeline friction and static head. Flow is controlled by a control valve or VFD against refinery tank level. A mass-balance leak detection system (in/out meters) alarms on loss.
details_to_model: Pump sets in bunded pump bay with seal pots (barrier fluid), suction/discharge valves, strainers, gauges, splash guards over flanges
Pipeline on sleepers or buried with marker posts, pig launcher/receiver, block valves, flow meters each end
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spray from flanges/seals (flange guards), burns; safety showers

equipment.name: Fuel oil (HFO) and diesel import tanks and transfer pumps
equipment.function: Store HFO (backup/alternative calciner and boiler fuel) and diesel (mine fleet), and transfer to the refinery/mine.
equipment.type_selected: API 650 cone-roof (HFO, heated and insulated) and cone-roof/internal floating-roof (diesel) tanks in bunds; positive-displacement screw pumps for HFO
equipment.why_this_type: HFO must be heated to stay pumpable; screw pumps handle viscous oil.
key_dimensions: HFO ~10,000-15,000 m3 each; diesel ~3,000-5,000 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Tanks receive oil from tankers through the loading arm. Heating coils (steam or thermal oil) keep the HFO viscosity low enough to pump. Screw pumps send fuel by pipeline or truck loading to the refinery.
details_to_model: Insulated HFO tanks with heater coil nozzles, suction heaters, foam pourers, fixed fire-water cooling rings
Bunds, oily-water separator, truck loading bay
Screw pump sets with strainers and relief valves
hazards_and_safety: Fire/explosion (NFPA 30 / AS 1940), H2S in HFO tank headspace, hot oil burns, spill to sea

equipment.name: Mobile harbour crane with grab and dust-controlled eco-hopper (quicklime import)
equipment.function: Unload bulk quicklime (and general cargo/spares) from vessels at a multipurpose berth.
equipment.type_selected: Rubber-tyred mobile harbour crane (~100-150 t class) with electro-hydraulic clamshell grab; mobile eco-hopper with bag filter and flap-sealed grid
equipment.why_this_type: Flexible for small, irregular import parcels; the eco-hopper limits highly irritant lime dust.
key_dimensions: Grab ~10-20 m3; hopper ~40-60 m3 on legs high enough for truck under-loading (~5 m clearance) (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The crane grabs lime from the hold and opens the grab over the hopper grid. Self-closing flaps and an extraction filter keep dust inside the hopper. Lime discharges into covered tippers or pneumatic tankers below, which haul it to refinery lime silos.
details_to_model: Crane on outriggers with tower, boom, cab, grab; eco-hopper with filter house, fan, discharge gate, truck lane, wheel-wash
hazards_and_safety: Quicklime reacts exothermically with water: keep dry, no water fire-fighting on bulk lime, burns to eyes/skin/lungs (full PPE and RPE)
Suspended loads; vehicle movements

equipment.name: Port fire water pumps (electric, diesel, jockey)
equipment.function: Provide fire water and foam for the berth, tank farm and conveyors.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal split-case fire pumps per NFPA 20, with diesel-driven standby
equipment.why_this_type: Code-listed, reliable fire supply independent of grid power.
key_dimensions: ~500-1,000 m3/h at ~100-120 m head (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The jockey pump keeps the ring main pressurised. When a hydrant or monitor opens and pressure falls, the duty pump starts automatically, and the diesel pump starts if the duty pump fails or power is lost.
details_to_model: Pump house with split-case pumps, diesel engine with fuel tank and exhaust, controllers, test header, fire water tank
hazards_and_safety: Rotating equipment; diesel fuel

areas.layout_notes: The port terminal sits on reclaimed or natural land behind the berth. Four alumina silos are in a row ~200-500 m from the wharf, with the receiving tower at the overland conveyor end. The reclaim tunnel under the silos leads to a transfer tower, then the enclosed jetty gallery on a piled trestle (length site-specific) to a single alumina berth ~250-280 m long. Shiploader rails run the full berth length with storm tie-down points at a parking position at one end. The caustic and fuel tank farm is in a separate bunded compound ≥ ~50-100 m from the alumina silos and conveyors (spill and fire separation). It is connected by pipelines on a pipe track to the common-user liquid berth, and caustic and fuel lines to the refinery follow the overland conveyor corridor. A multipurpose berth with a mobile harbour crane and eco-hopper handles quicklime. Also on site: a substation/e-house, control room with view of the berth, workshop, laboratory sample room, and gatehouse with truck weighbridge. All structures use marine corrosion protection (ISO 12944 C5-M/CX) and are designed for cyclonic wind where applicable (e.g., Indian East Coast, northern Australia).
interfaces: A16: overland conveyor delivery (~800 t/h); despatch inventory/quality certificates
Refinery caustic storage and liquor make-up (caustic pipeline); utilities/boilers and calciners (fuel oil); causticisation/lime slaking (quicklime)
Mine (diesel supply for fleet)
Port authority: pilotage, tugs, navigation channel depth, berth scheduling
Customs/trade: belt-weigher and draft-survey reconciliation; ISO certificate sampling

open_questions: LIVE SOURCE VERIFICATION: WebSearch was disabled for this session and the vendor and journal sites could not be fetched. All references are cited from the author's engineering knowledge (standards, books, vendor literature) and must be checked by SMEs before release. In particular: current FLSmidth GSC/GSC-HV and Metso Outotec CFB maximum unit capacities and guaranteed heat consumption; current ISO alumina test-method numbers and editions (ISO 806, 8008, 2926, 2927); NACE SP0403 temperature limits for 50 % NaOH in carbon steel.

Calciner technology: confirm the choice of FLSmidth-type GSC with holding vessel over Metso Outotec CFB. If CFB is preferred, the stage list changes (venturi pre-dryer, 2 venturi preheaters, CFB furnace with recycle cyclone and seal pot, 3 suspension coolers, FBC with air- and water-cooled stages, high-pressure primary-air blowers).

Calciner count: 2 x 3,500 t/d (chosen) vs 3 x 2,300-2,500 t/d. Two units give a lower capital cost, but during a single-unit outage (~2-3 weeks/yr each for refractory) the plant must store ~2,000-2,500 t/d of hydrate (hydrate storage tanks/shed in A14) or cut back production.

Fuel: is pipeline natural gas available at the site? If not, the calciners fire HFO (~150,000 t/yr imported through A17, SO2 controls needed) or producer gas from coal gasifiers (as at some Indian refineries). This changes the burner design, fuel skid, stack CEMS and the port tank farm size.

Refinery-to-port distance and mode: an ~8 km covered overland conveyor is assumed. Longer distances (e.g., Indian East Coast inland refineries ~ hundreds of km) need rail with covered hopper/pressure-discharge wagons and rail loadout/unloading stations instead.
Port storage form: silos chosen (4 x 25,000 t). Some alumina ports use large enclosed sheds with portal/bridge reclaimers; confirm SME preference and port land availability.
Port location and vessel mix: confirm channel depth, tidal range and maximum vessel (Supramax vs Panamax). These set berth length, shiploader outreach, air draft and storage.
Emission limits: confirm the jurisdiction (e.g., India CPCB/SPCB vs Western Australia DWER licence) for particulate (30 vs 50 mg/Nm3), NOx and stack height.
FBC heat recovery: confirm whether recovered heat goes to hydrate wash water (assumed), spent liquor heating, or a cooling tower only.
Caustic consumption and lime demand must be reconciled with the digestion/desilication and causticisation area owners (reactive silica 1.5-3 % gives a wide caustic range).

Provisional Bayer liquor numbers outside this scope (caustic 230-280 g/L as Na2CO3, A/C ratios) suit Australian-style low-temperature practice. Indian East Coast plants have historically run lower concentrations. The digestion/precipitation owners should confirm them.

areas.area_name: A18 Evaporation (spent liquor concentration - multiple-effect falling-film evaporators with product flash)
areas.purpose: Remove the water that enters the liquor circuit (bauxite moisture, residue and hydrate wash water, lime slurry water, direct-steam condensate, gland/flush water) so the circuit stays in water balance. Concentrate part of the spent liquor from ~240 to ~300-320 g/L caustic (as Na2CO3), then blend it back to make digestion liquor at C ~270-290 g/L. Recover clean steam condensate for boiler feed and hot process condensate for washing. Design duty: ~420 t/h water evaporated (~1.75 t per t Al2O3) in 2 parallel trains of ~210 t/h, using ~100 t/h LP steam (steam economy ~4.0-4.5).
areas.process_description: 1) Spent liquor from precipitation/classification overflow (A12/A13) collects at ~55-65 degC in two evaporator feed tanks (18-TK-001/002). About 55% of it (~1,700 m3/h) goes to evaporation. The balance (~1,350 m3/h) bypasses evaporation and goes to the digestion liquor blend tanks (18-TK-021/022). Fine hydrate carried in the spent liquor is a nucleation source for gibbsite scale, so the feed is taken from well-clarified overflow and the tanks are not agitated hard. 2) Backward feed: each train's feed pumps (18-PP-001..004) deliver liquor to effect 6, the coldest effect (~0.15-0.2 bar(a), liquor ~60-65 degC). A bleed from each effect's recirculation pump discharge moves the liquor forward to the next hotter effect (6->5->4->3->2->1). 3) Each effect is a vertical falling-film calandria (18-EV-1x1..1x6). The recirculation pump lifts liquor to the top tube-sheet distributor. The liquor runs down the inside of 10-12 m tubes as a thin film, heated by vapour condensing on the shell side. The water vapour released travels down the tube with the film, separates in the effect's vapour separator (18-VS), passes a chevron/mesh demister, and heats the shell of the next colder effect. Effect 1 is heated by LP steam (4-5 barg, desuperheated to ~5-10 K superheat). Typical temperature cascade: steam ~155 degC; liquor in effect 1 ~135-145 degC; ~10-11 K effective driving force per effect; boiling-point rise of Bayer liquor ~5-10 K per effect; last-effect vapour ~50-55 degC. 4) Product liquor leaves effect 1 at ~135-145 degC and C ~300-320 g/L. It flashes through 4 product flash tanks (18-FT) down to ~100-105 degC. Each tank's flash vapour joins the vapour side of the matching effect, which adds roughly 0.3-0.5 to the steam economy. 5) The strong liquor goes to the blend tanks (18-TK-021/022). There it mixes with bypass spent liquor, 50% caustic make-up (A19) and causticised/purified returns to give digestion liquor (C ~270-290 g/L, A/C 0.36-0.38). The blend is pumped to the A06 digestion liquor tank and the A04 mill liquor tank. 6) Last-effect vapour condenses in a shell-and-tube surface condenser (18-CD-101/201) on cooling-tower water. Liquid-ring vacuum pumps (18-VP) remove non-condensables (air, CO2, light organics/VOCs). 7) Condensates: effect-1 steam condensate is clean. It is checked by conductivity and sodium analysers and returned to the power house (A20); it dumps automatically to the process condensate system on contamination. Vapour condensates from effects 2-6, the flash tanks and the condenser contain trace caustic (pH ~9-11) and volatile organics. They are flashed in a cascade of condensate pots and collected as process condensate (~50-95 degC) for residue washing (A08), hydrate/seed washing (A13/A14), lime slaking and cloth washing. 8) Chemistry and scaling: evaporation is a physical concentration step, but it raises supersaturation. (a) Dissolved silica forms desilication product (sodalite) scale, mainly in the hottest effects: 6 Na2SiO3 + 6 NaAl(OH)4 + Na2X -> Na6[Al6Si6O24].Na2X + 12 NaOH + 6 H2O (X = CO3, SO4, 2Cl, 2OH). (b) Gibbsite scale, Al(OH)4- -> Al(OH)3 + OH-, forms in the cooler effects when A/C is high or fine hydrate seeds are present. (c) At very high C, sodium carbonate, sulfate and oxalate 'salt out'. Each effect is descaled in rotation (caustic boil-out with hot spent liquor for gibbsite; inhibited dilute sulfuric acid for DSP; UHP water jetting). 9) High-temperature (boehmitic, ~240-260 degC) plants differ: they recover more heat regeneratively. Where they use direct live-steam injection, all that condensate dilutes the liquor and raises the evaporation load. Some still use older multi-stage flash/forced-circulation evaporators. This low-temperature design uses indirect live-steam heaters in digestion (A06), which keeps the evaporation duty moderate.

equipment.name: Evaporator feed (spent liquor) tanks
equipment.function: Buffer spent liquor from precipitation ahead of evaporation and digestion; split flow between evaporation and bypass.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each sized so one can be taken out for cleaning at reduced throughput)
equipment.type_selected: Vertical flat-bottom cone-roof atmospheric storage tank, API 650, with low-speed mixer
equipment.why_this_type: Large cheap surge volume (~2-3 h) decouples precipitation from the evaporators; standard for Bayer liquor.
key_dimensions: ~4,000 m3 working each; ~20 m dia x ~14-15 m shell height (engineering estimate)
Roof ~1:16 cone; bund wall ~1.5-2 m high around both tanks (>=110% of largest tank)
equipment.working_principle: Simple atmospheric surge tank. Spent liquor overflows into the tank from the precipitation/classification launder header. Two suction nozzles near the bottom feed the evaporator feed pumps and the bypass pumps. A slow side-entry or top-entry mixer keeps fine hydrate in suspension so it does not build up as a bottom layer, without the high shear that creates more fines. Level measurement balances in-flow against evaporator rate. Vents go to a common vent header because the liquor gives off steam and odour.
details_to_model: Cylindrical CS shell with visible horizontal weld seams (~8 courses of 1.8-2 m), insulation cladding (aluminium-zinc sheeting, ~50 mm) on shell and roof
Cone roof with handrail ring, roof manway (DN600) x2, radar level gauge nozzle, vent nozzle (DN300) to vent header, emergency vent hatch
Spiral stair on shell exterior with 2 intermediate landings; roof platform
Shell manways DN900 x2 at base (diametrically opposite) for cleanout; cleanout door optional
Inlet nozzle DN600 near top with internal down-comer; outlet nozzles DN500 x2 at ~0.5 m above floor with vortex breakers; drain/sump nozzle DN150
1 side-entry mixer (~30-45 kW) with motor and gearbox on bracket near base, OR top-entry agitator bridge
Ring-wall concrete foundation, anchor chairs, earthing bosses, bund floor sloped to sump pit with sump pump
Tank nameplate, contents label 'SPENT LIQUOR - CAUSTIC', safety shower within 10 m of bund access
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic liquor (~14% NaOH equivalent): severe chemical and thermal burns, permanent eye damage; full PPE (face shield, goggles, PVC/rubber gloves, caustic suit) for sampling and opening
Confined-space entry: isolate, drain, wash, ventilate, gas test; scale on floor; positive isolation (spades) of all nozzles
Hydrogen: never use aluminium tools/scaffold inside caustic tanks (Al + NaOH releases H2)
Overflow/overfill: independent high-high level trip on inlet; bund sized 110%
instrumentation_and_control: Radar level (LT) + independent HH level switch
Density meter on outlet (nuclear or Coriolis) for liquor control
Flow controllers on evaporator feed and bypass
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A36/A283/A516-70); spent liquor ~60 degC lies near the NACE SP0403 caustic-SCC threshold - PWHT of nozzle reinforcements/attachments as per owner philosophy
common_problems: Hydrate settles on the floor and reduces volume
Gibbsite scale on walls when liquor is cooled
Corrosion under insulation at the bund-wall splash zone
operating_tips_and_key_points: Do not let the level run low: the feed pumps cavitate and lose suction
Check density and C/A/C with the lab every shift; spent A/C above 0.40 means poor precipitation and a high evaporator scaling risk
sources: Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry (Bayer flowsheet) - verify
API 650 Welded Tanks for Oil Storage (design code used for Bayer liquor tanks)
NACE SP0403-2015 Avoiding Caustic Stress Corrosion Cracking of Refinery Equipment and Piping

equipment.name: Evaporator feed pumps
equipment.function: Pump spent liquor from the feed tanks to effect 6 of each train under flow control.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal process pump (ISO 5199 / ASME B73.1-style heavy duty, OH1/OH2), VSD-driven
equipment.why_this_type: Clean, low-solids liquor at moderate head; a VSD gives energy-efficient flow control.
key_dimensions: ~850-950 m3/h, ~35-45 m head each; motor ~160-200 kW, 4-pole (engineering estimate)
Suction DN400-450, discharge DN300-350
equipment.working_principle: A rotating closed impeller adds velocity energy to the liquor, and the volute turns it into pressure. The VSD sets the speed to hold the evaporator feed flow at its setpoint, which ties evaporation rate to plant water balance. The installed spare is on auto-start with suction and discharge valves open, and a check valve isolates it from reverse flow.
details_to_model: Baseplate on concrete plinth with grout, drip rim and drain to bund
Volute casing (CS or CD4MCuN duplex), back pull-out design, coupling guard (yellow), TEFC motor
Double cartridge mechanical seal with seal-support pot (API Plan 53A/53B) on stand
Suction: eccentric reducer (flat on top), strainer (temporary cone), isolation knife-gate or butterfly valve DN450
Discharge: concentric reducer, swing check valve, isolation valve, pressure gauge with diaphragm seal
Magnetic flowmeter on common discharge to each train
Drain/flush connections with quick couplings for condensate flush
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spray from seal failure: seal guard/splash shield; safety shower nearby
Rotating coupling: guard; LOTO before maintenance
Hot surfaces ~60 degC
instrumentation_and_control: VSD speed control from evaporator feed FIC
equipment.materials: Casing CS or duplex SS; impeller CD4MCuN duplex; shaft sleeve duplex; seal faces SiC/SiC
common_problems: Seal leaks from crystallisation of caustic on the faces
Impeller scaling with gibbsite
operating_tips_and_key_points: Flush with condensate before shutdown so liquor does not crystallise in the casing
Run the standby pumps weekly
sources: ISO 5199 Technical specifications for centrifugal pumps Class II

equipment.name: Falling-film evaporator effects (calandrias)
equipment.function: Heat transfer bodies of the 6-effect evaporator trains: condense steam or vapour on the shell side to boil water out of the liquor flowing as a film inside vertical tubes.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 installed; one train can run at increased steam rate during the other train's descale (~60-70% total capacity), or effects are descaled one at a time with bypass
equipment.type_selected: Vertical shell-and-tube falling-film evaporator with top liquor distribution box, backward feed
equipment.why_this_type: Falling film works at low temperature difference with short residence and high heat-transfer coefficients. It needs no hydrostatic head (no boiling-point elevation from liquid depth), so it suits a 6-effect cascade with good steam economy. This is the dominant modern Bayer evaporation technology. Alternatives: older multi-stage flash/forced-circulation shell-and-tube 'Kestner' units, and mechanical vapour recompression (MVR) falling film where cheap power favours electrification.
key_dimensions: Heat transfer area ~1,300-3,000 m2 per effect (effect 1 smallest, cold effects largest) (engineering estimate)
Tubes ~50 mm OD x 2.6-3 mm wall, 10-12 m long, ~700-1,600 tubes per effect, triangular pitch ~64 mm
Calandria shell ID ~2.4-3.4 m; overall body height ~18-22 m including top distribution chamber (~2 m) and bottom vapour/liquor chamber with sump (~3-4 m)
Expansion bellows on shell (single or double convolution) ~1/3 down from the top tube sheet

operating_parameters.parameter: Wetting rate (film flow per tube perimeter)
operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate - typical falling-film design rule

equipment.working_principle: Liquor recirculated by the effect's pump enters the top chamber and passes through a distribution plate (perforated plate or individual tube ferrules/swirl inserts) that puts an even film on the inside wall of every tube. On the shell side, steam (effect 1) or vapour from the previous effect condenses on the tube outside and gives up latent heat through the wall to the film. The film boils at a temperature set by the effect's pressure plus the liquor's boiling-point rise. The vapour and film travel down together (co-current), which thins the film and keeps the heat-transfer coefficient high. At the bottom the liquor collects in the sump and the vapour turns into the side duct to the separator. Shell-side condensate drains from the lower tube sheet to a condensate pot, and non-condensables are bled from vent nozzles at the coldest shell zone. A dry tube (film breakdown) scales very quickly, so a minimum wetting rate is always kept by recirculation, independent of the forward flow.
details_to_model: Tall slender vertical cylinder on a structural steel support ring at ~1/3 height (lugs on the shell) carried by the evaporator structure
Top: domed or flat bolted cover with davit arm for removal; liquor inlet nozzle DN300-400 entering the distribution box; inspection manway DN600; sight glass with wiper and lamp
Distribution plate with ferrules visible when the cover is open (training cutaway: tube sheet with 1,000+ tube ends)

Shell: steam/vapour inlet nozzle DN800-1,400 (effect 1 smaller DN500-700) with impingement plate inside; NCG vent nozzles DN50-80 at 2-3 levels; condensate outlet DN150-250 at lower tube sheet; shell expansion bellows; pressure gauge and PSV on shell (effect 1)

Bottom: conical/torispherical lower chamber with large side vapour outlet DN1,200-1,800 to the separator and liquor outlet DN400 to the recirculation pump suction; bottom manway DN600 for descaling access; drain DN100
Insulation (mineral wool ~75-100 mm + Al cladding) on shell, top and bottom; uninsulated personnel-protection cages are not acceptable - all hot surfaces clad
Platforms at top-cover level (with davit and hoist beam), at bellows/vent level and at bottom manway level; caged ladders/stair tower shared by the train
Training cutaway: falling film inside tubes, vapour core, shell-side condensate droplets, scale layer (DSP) on hot effects
hazards_and_safety: Steam at 4-5 barg / 155 degC and hot caustic liquor up to 145 degC: risk of flashing and scalding if opened under pressure - verify zero pressure, temperature < 50 degC and drain before breaking flanges
Vacuum effects: implosion risk if vacuum breakers fail; design for full vacuum
Confined space for descaling (tube-sheet and bottom chamber entry); acid cleaning gives off H2S? (not expected) but CO2, and hydrogen if acid contacts aluminium/zinc; gas test
UHP water jetting of tubes (1,000-2,500 bar): trained crews, deadman controls, exclusion zone
Working at height on platforms ~20-25 m
instrumentation_and_control: Liquor level in bottom sump (DP or radar)
Recirculation flow (magflow) with low-flow alarm (dry-tube protection)
Forward-flow control valve to next effect on level control
Density meter on product (controls final C)
Steam flow (vortex/orifice) to effect 1 with pressure control
Conductivity on each condensate stream (tube-leak detection)
equipment.materials: Shell and liquor-side heads: carbon steel SA-516-70 with PWHT (caustic SCC per NACE SP0403); tubes seamless carbon steel (SA-179/SA-214) - some vendors use stainless steel in cold effects; tube sheets CS; gaskets compressed graphite/caustic-resistant
common_problems: DSP scale in effects 1-2 reduces U by 30-50% over 2-6 weeks
Gibbsite scale in cold effects when spent A/C is high or fines carry over
Uneven distribution leading to dry tubes and rapid local scale
Tube leaks contaminating condensate
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch the overall delta-T and steam rate trend: a rising steam pressure at a constant rate means scale
Never cut recirculation below the minimum wetting flow
Descale in a planned rotation, and do the caustic boil-out before the acid clean
Keep the spent A/C low and the feed free of fines, which is the best scaling prevention
sources: Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia (evaporation in Bayer process) - verify
Smith P. (2009) The processing of high silica bauxites - review of existing and potential processes, Hydrometallurgy 98:162-176 (DSP chemistry)
TEMA Standards; ASME BPVC Section VIII Div.1 (shell and tube pressure design)

equipment.name: Vapour-liquid separators (one per effect)
equipment.function: Separate the water vapour leaving the bottom of each calandria from entrained liquor droplets before the vapour goes to the next effect's shell, which protects condensate purity.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical separator with tangential/side vapour inlet, chevron (vane) or wire-mesh demister and wash sprays
equipment.why_this_type: Caustic carry-over contaminates condensate, which then cannot be sent to the boilers or used as wash water. Two-stage separation (gravity/centrifugal, then demister) is standard.
key_dimensions: ~4-6 m dia x 8-12 m tall; cold effects largest because vapour density is low under vacuum (engineering estimate)
Vapour inlet DN1,200-1,800 at mid-height; vapour outlet DN1,200-2,000 on top
equipment.working_principle: The vapour-liquor mixture enters through a large side nozzle and loses velocity in the large cross-section. Droplets fall by gravity and centrifugal action to the bottom, which drains back to the calandria sump or recirculation suction. The vapour rises through a demister pad, where fine mist impinges on vanes or wires, coalesces and drains. Intermittent condensate sprays wash the demister to dissolve salt build-up. The cleaned vapour goes to the next effect's shell.
details_to_model: Large-bore vapour duct (DN1,200-1,800) from calandria bottom to separator, with expansion joint
Separator body with top elliptical head, top vapour outlet with large-radius elbow to next effect
Demister pad support ring and wash spray header (visible in cutaway)
Liquor return leg DN300-400 from separator bottom to the recirculation pump suction, with level bridle
Manway DN600 at demister level and DN600 near bottom; platforms at both
Insulation + cladding; sight glass at liquor level
hazards_and_safety: As effects: vacuum/pressure, hot caustic
Demister replacement is a confined-space entry with work at height inside the vessel
instrumentation_and_control: Condensate conductivity downstream as carry-over indication
equipment.materials: Carbon steel PWHT; demister SS 316L or duplex
common_problems: Demister blinding with salts
Carry-over during surges or foaming (organics)
operating_tips_and_key_points: A conductivity rise in the next effect's condensate often means demister damage or flooding
Use the demister sprays at each change of shift
sources: GPSA/ vendor demister design practice (Souders-Brown sizing)

equipment.name: Effect recirculation pumps (with forward-transfer bleed)
equipment.function: Keep the tube film wetted by circulating liquor from each effect sump to its top distributor. A bleed from the discharge, on level control, transfers liquor to the next hotter effect.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 installed (warehouse spare rotating assemblies; effect bypass allows change-out)
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal process pump, large-capacity low head (OH1/OH2)
equipment.why_this_type: High flow and low head; liquor is near saturation, so low NPSH required. The pump sits well below the sump, giving ~6-10 m static suction head.
key_dimensions: ~800-1,500 m3/h at ~20-30 m head; ~90-200 kW motor; 6-pole (~990 rpm) for low NPSHr (engineering estimate)
Suction DN450-600, discharge DN350-450
equipment.working_principle: The liquor in each effect sump is at its boiling point, so the pump depends on static head (sump elevation above the pump) to avoid flashing at the impeller eye. The pump lifts liquor ~20 m to the top of the calandria. A control valve on a side branch passes a forward flow to the next effect, set by the sump level. The recirculation rate stays essentially constant to protect the wetting rate.
details_to_model: Pumps at grade under the structure, in a row along the train, each below its effect
Long vertical suction leg from sump with large-radius bends, isolation valve and expansion joint
Discharge riser up the structure to the calandria top with check valve, isolation valve, magflow meter and forward-transfer control valve branch
Seal pot/ seal-water panel beside each pump; drip trays; coupling guards
Pump maintenance monorail or mobile crane access lane
hazards_and_safety: Liquor up to 145 degC can flash to steam if released: never open a casing under pressure
Seal failure sprays hot caustic: splash guards, safety showers along the pump row
instrumentation_and_control: Recirculation flow FT with low-flow alarm/trip of steam
equipment.materials: Casing CS/ductile or duplex; impeller CD4MCuN or high-chrome iron; double mechanical seal (Plan 53/54) with condensate barrier
common_problems: Cavitation when sump level drops or pressure dips
Impeller and casing scaling
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the sump levels steady; a level swing upsets both the wetting and the NPSH
sources: API 610 / ISO 13709 (centrifugal pumps for petroleum and heavy-duty chemical service) - reference for robust design
Hydraulic Institute ANSI/HI 9.6.1 NPSH margin guideline

equipment.name: Product liquor flash tanks
equipment.function: Flash-cool the hot product liquor from effect 1 (~140 degC) in 4 stages to ~100-105 degC. The flash vapour is sent to the shells of matching effects to raise the steam economy.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical flash vessel with tangential inlet, internal impingement baffle and demister
equipment.why_this_type: Recovers the sensible heat of the product liquor without extra heat-transfer surface, and gives atmospheric-pressure strong liquor for storage.
key_dimensions: ~3-4 m dia x ~7-10 m tall each (engineering estimate)
Liquor inlet DN350; vapour outlet DN600-900; liquor outlet DN350
equipment.working_principle: Liquor entering a vessel at lower pressure than its saturation pressure partly boils (flashes) until it reaches the boiling point at that pressure. The vapour formed is taken off the top through a demister to the shell side of the effect operating at about the same pressure. The cooler liquor flows by pressure difference, on level control, to the next flash tank.
details_to_model: Row of 4 progressively larger vessels stepped down in elevation beside the train
Inlet nozzle with level-control valve upstream; vapour line to effect shell sloped without pockets
Level gauge (guided-wave radar) and gauge glass; PSV/ vacuum breaker on each
Manway, platform at top, insulation
hazards_and_safety: Hot flashing caustic liquor: line breaks can create a scalding steam/liquor cloud
Erosion at inlet nozzles from flashing two-phase flow - inspect wall thickness
equipment.materials: Carbon steel PWHT; inlet impingement plate wear-resistant (SS or hard-faced)
common_problems: Scale in let-down valves
Erosion of outlet piping
operating_tips_and_key_points: A product temperature well above design after the last flash means a flash-vapour line is blocked or a valve is closed
sources: Engineering estimate; standard flash-train practice (see also A07 flash cooling)

equipment.name: Final (surface) condensers
equipment.function: Condense the vapour from effect 6 (and the last flash) under vacuum using cooling-tower water; this sets the vacuum and the total temperature span of the train.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal shell-and-tube surface condenser (vapour shell side, cooling water tube side, 2-pass), TEMA AES/BEM type
equipment.why_this_type: Keeps caustic-containing condensate out of the cooling water circuit. Alternative: direct-contact barometric condenser with barometric leg and hot well - cheaper and common in older plants, but it contaminates the cooling water with caustic and organics.
key_dimensions: ~2,500-4,000 m2 per unit; shell ~3.5-4.0 m dia x ~10-12 m long (engineering estimate)
Vapour inlet DN1,800-2,200 top; CW nozzles DN700-900; condensate outlet DN200 to hot-well/ condensate pot

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate for tropical site (wet bulb ~27-28 degC)

equipment.working_principle: Low-pressure vapour enters the shell over a tube bundle and condenses on the cold tubes. Condensation shrinks the volume about 10,000-fold, which creates and holds the vacuum. Non-condensable gases accumulate in a baffled air-cooling zone and are drawn off by the vacuum pumps. Condensate drains to a hot-well and is pumped to the process condensate tank. A warmer cooling-water supply or a fouled tube raises the vacuum pressure, which reduces evaporation capacity.
details_to_model: Large horizontal cylinder on two saddles (one fixed, one sliding) at high level (~+18-22 m) so condensate drains by gravity
Bolted channel heads at each end with CW inlet/outlet nozzles and removable covers (tube cleaning access), lifting lugs
Large top vapour inlet with expansion joint from the effect-6 separator
Air-offtake nozzle to vacuum pumps; condensate drain to hot-well/ condensate pot with loop seal
Rupture disc/ vacuum breaker; thermometers on CW lines; platforms at both channel ends
hazards_and_safety: Vacuum: implosion design, vacuum breaker
Tube leak lets caustic into cooling water: pH/conductivity monitoring of CW return
Channel cover removal requires lifting plan
equipment.materials: Shell CS; tubes SS 316L or titanium (chloride CW); tube sheets CS clad or duplex
common_problems: CW-side fouling/ scaling raises back-pressure
Air leaks into the vacuum system
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check the vacuum against the CW temperature: a rising approach means fouling or air in-leakage
sources: HEI Standards for Steam Surface Condensers (reference)

equipment.name: Vacuum pumps (non-condensable gas removal)
equipment.function: Remove air and non-condensable gases from the final condensers and the effect shells' vent manifolds to keep the vacuum.
equipment.type_selected: Liquid-ring vacuum pump package with separator and seal-liquid cooler
equipment.why_this_type: Handles saturated, wet gas and condensable slugs robustly. Alternative: multi-stage steam ejectors (no moving parts but use steam).
key_dimensions: ~1,500-3,000 m3/h suction volume at ~0.12 bar(a); ~55-110 kW motor (engineering estimate)
Skid ~4 m x 2 m with separator tank ~1 m dia
equipment.working_principle: An eccentric impeller turns in a casing partly filled with seal liquid. The liquid forms a rotating ring, and the spaces between the vanes expand (suction) and contract (compression) as the impeller turns. Gas is drawn in through the port plate, compressed and discharged with some seal liquid to a separator. The liquid is cooled and recirculated, and the gas goes to the vent/ odour-control system.
details_to_model: Skid with pump, motor, belt or direct coupling, gas-liquid separator vessel, plate cooler, seal-liquid pipework
Suction line with isolation valve, check valve, vacuum gauge; discharge to vent header
hazards_and_safety: Odorous/VOC-bearing vent gas: route to treatment
Rotating equipment guards; noise ~85 dB(A)
equipment.materials: Ductile iron/ SS casing; SS impeller
common_problems: Hot seal liquid lowers capacity
Scale in the port plate
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the seal liquid cool; capacity falls quickly as it warms
sources: Vendor practice for liquid-ring vacuum pumps (e.g., Gardner Denver Nash) - generic

equipment.name: Condensate pots, condensate cascade, clean and process condensate tanks and pumps
equipment.function: Collect shell-side condensate from each effect, flash it down in cascade to recover heat, segregate clean effect-1 steam condensate (to the boilers) from process condensate (to washing), and pump both onward.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical condensate pots with level control; atmospheric/vented condensate tanks; horizontal centrifugal pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Simple, standard practice; segregation protects the boilers from caustic contamination.
key_dimensions: Pots ~1.0-1.5 m dia x 2.5-3.5 m
18-TK-011 clean condensate ~150 m3 (~6 m dia x 6 m); 18-TK-012 process condensate ~600-800 m3 (~10 m dia x 9 m) (engineering estimate)
Pumps: clean ~120 m3/h x 60 m; process ~450 m3/h x 60 m

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate - set by boiler water chemistry

equipment.working_principle: Condensate drains from each effect shell into a pot that seals the vapour while letting liquid pass on level control. Each pot's condensate flows to the next colder pot, where part of it flashes to steam that rejoins the vapour system. Effect-1 steam condensate is kept separate and checked online by conductivity and sodium analysers. If caustic is detected (tube leak), three-way dump valves divert it to process condensate automatically.
details_to_model: Row of small vertical pots under the effects, each with gauge glass, level transmitter and control valve
Two conductivity analyser cabinets with sample coolers near the clean condensate line
Three-way automatic dump valve (actuated, yellow position indicator)
Tanks with vent stacks, ladders, insulation; pump set at grade with guards
hazards_and_safety: Hot condensate/flash steam: burns
Caustic contamination of boiler feed causes caustic gouging/embrittlement in boilers: a key interlock
instrumentation_and_control: Conductivity (and Na analyser on clean line)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel; analysers SS
common_problems: Analyser drift leading to false dumps or missed contamination
operating_tips_and_key_points: Calibrate conductivity analysers weekly; never bypass the dump interlock
sources: ASME 'Consensus on operating practices for the control of feedwater and boiler water chemistry in modern industrial boilers' (CRTD-34)

equipment.name: Strong liquor / digestion liquor blend tanks and transfer pumps
equipment.function: Receive strong evaporated liquor, bypass spent liquor and caustic make-up, blend to digestion liquor strength, and pump to digestion (A06) and mill liquor (A04).
equipment.type_selected: API 650 atmospheric insulated tanks with top-entry agitator; horizontal centrifugal pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Surge between evaporation and digestion (~1.5-2 h); the blending point for controlling digestion caustic.
key_dimensions: ~3,000-3,500 m3 working each; ~18 m dia x ~14 m (engineering estimate)
Pumps ~1,000 m3/h x 50-60 m head, ~250 kW each
equipment.working_principle: Strong liquor at ~100 degC and cooler bypass spent liquor are mixed by the agitator. Caustic make-up is added to the inlet to reach the target C, measured by an online density/conductivity correlation and checked by the lab (titration). The transfer pumps send liquor on flow control to the digestion liquor tank and mill liquor tank.
details_to_model: Two insulated tanks in a common bund, agitator bridge on roof with gearbox and motor
Caustic make-up injection quill nozzle on inlet (labelled), sample point with cooler and safety shower
Pump row with discharge header, flowmeters, isolation valves
hazards_and_safety: ~100 degC strong caustic (~18% NaOH equivalent): severe burns; the hottest storage in the plant
Caustic make-up addition point: local concentration and heat of dilution
equipment.materials: Carbon steel fully stress-relieved (PWHT) - above the NACE SP0403 threshold at this temperature/concentration
common_problems: Salt crystallisation (carbonate/oxalate) on cooler walls and roof
Caustic SCC at non-PWHT attachments
operating_tips_and_key_points: Add caustic gradually and keep the agitator running

equipment.name: Effect-1 steam control and desuperheating stations
equipment.function: Control the LP steam flow and pressure to effect 1 and remove superheat (heat transfer is better with near-saturated steam).
equipment.type_selected: Steam pressure/flow control valve with spray-water desuperheater (condensate injection)
equipment.why_this_type: Standard; condensing steam close to saturation gives the best shell-side coefficient and limits scale-promoting hot spots.
key_dimensions: Steam line DN500-600; control valve DN300-400; desuperheater spool ~6-8 m straight run (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A control valve throttles the LP steam to the pressure needed for the required evaporation rate. Downstream, atomised condensate is sprayed into the steam and evaporates, cooling the steam close to saturation. A downstream temperature controller sets the spray rate.
details_to_model: Steam header take-off with isolation gate valve, strainer, control valve with actuator and positioner, manual bypass globe valve
Desuperheater probe/nozzle with spray-water line, control valve, temperature element ~10 diameters downstream
Steam traps and drip legs; insulation; PSV on effect-1 shell
hazards_and_safety: Steam at 155-170 degC: burns; water hammer if drains are not cleared at start-up
instrumentation_and_control: Evaporation rate control: steam flow setpoint from density/ water-balance controller
equipment.materials: Carbon steel A106B piping; valve trim stellite
common_problems: Water hammer at start-up
Spray nozzle erosion
operating_tips_and_key_points: Warm up and drain the lines slowly; open steam gradually after vacuum is established in the train

equipment.name: Evaporator descaling system (caustic boil-out, acid cleaning, UHP water jetting)
equipment.function: Remove DSP, gibbsite and salt scale from the evaporator tubes, separators, flash tanks and piping on a planned rotation.
equipment.type_selected: Fixed acid storage/ make-up tank with circulation pumps and hoses; mobile UHP jetting units
equipment.why_this_type: Bayer evaporator scale is unavoidable. Inhibited dilute H2SO4 dissolves DSP (sodalite/cancrinite), hot spent liquor or caustic dissolves gibbsite, and UHP jetting removes hard deposits.
key_dimensions: Acid make-up tank ~50-80 m3 (HDPE/FRP or rubber-lined CS); circulation pumps ~150-250 m3/h; neutralisation pit (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; confirm with chemical cleaning vendor

equipment.working_principle: The effect to be cleaned is isolated, drained of liquor and flushed with condensate. Hot spent liquor or caustic is circulated first to dissolve gibbsite. After flushing, inhibited dilute sulfuric acid is circulated to dissolve aluminosilicate scale, with the iron in solution and the acid strength monitored. Spent acid is neutralised (with spent caustic) before return to the process or to the residue system. Remaining hard scale is jetted out at 1,000-2,500 bar.
details_to_model: Acid tank with bund, acid unloading point, eyewash/ safety shower, pumps on skid
Flexible hose connections (hammer unions), temporary spools, blinds/ spades
Mobile UHP jetting trailer with lances, foot-pedal dump valve, hose whip restraints
hazards_and_safety: Sulfuric acid AND caustic in the same area: violent heat on mixing; strict segregation and flushing
Hydrogen evolution if acid contacts zinc/galvanised parts or Al tools
UHP water injection injuries; noise
Confined space
instrumentation_and_control: Acid strength (conductivity/ titration), temperature, iron content
Interlocks preventing liquor valves opening to acid circuit
equipment.materials: Acid tank FRP/ rubber-lined CS; pumps alloy 20 or lined
common_problems: Incomplete cleaning leading to shorter run times
Corrosion when the inhibitor is under-dosed
operating_tips_and_key_points: Always complete positive isolation, and flush with condensate between caustic and acid steps
sources: Industry practice for Bayer heater/ evaporator descaling (see A06/A07 draft: inhibited H2SO4)

areas.layout_notes: Two evaporator trains stand side by side in one open steel structure, about 75-90 m long x 30-35 m wide x 28-32 m high (engineering estimate). The 6 calandrias of each train are in a straight row, ~10-12 m centres, supported at ~+8-10 m. Each separator is beside its calandria. The product flash tanks (4 per train) are stepped down at the hot end of the train. The surface condensers are at high level (~+18-22 m) at the cold end so condensate drains by gravity, with the vacuum pumps below at grade. Recirculation and transfer pumps are at grade beneath their effects, in two rows with a central maintenance aisle (truck access for pump change-out). Platform levels: grade, ~+10 m (bellows/ lower vents), ~+22 m (top covers, davits), with stair towers at each end and a lift (optional). The feed tanks (18-TK-001/002) and the strong liquor blend tanks (18-TK-021/022) are in an adjacent bunded tank farm ~20-40 m from the structure. Area location: between the precipitation/ spent-liquor tank farm (A12/A13; ~100-200 m) and digestion (A06; ~100-250 m). LP steam comes from the power house (A20, ~150-300 m), and the cooling towers are ~100-200 m away. The pipe rack (3 tiers, +6/+9/+12 m) runs along one long side carrying spent liquor, strong liquor, steam, condensate, CW and the vent header. Clear lay-down areas at each end allow tube jetting and crane access (mobile crane ~100-200 t for cover/ bellows work).
interfaces: A12/A13 Precipitation/ Classification: spent liquor ~3,050 m3/h to 18-TK-001/002 (evaporation ~1,700 m3/h + bypass ~1,350 m3/h)
A06 Digestion: digestion liquor (blend, C 270-290 g/L) ~2,100-2,200 m3/h to 06-TK-101
A04 Grinding: mill liquor ~600 m3/h to 04-TK-020

A19 Liquor purification: 50% caustic make-up into 18-TK-021/022; strong liquor side-streams to the oxalate crystallisation (~150-250 m3/h) and to the liquor burning facility (~15-25 m3/h); return of purified/ leached liquor
A20 Utilities: LP steam ~100 t/h at 4-5 barg; clean condensate return ~100 t/h; cooling water ~5,000 m3/h; instrument air; 6.6/0.415 kV power
A08 Residue washing / A13-A14 hydrate washing: process condensate ~420 t/h as hot wash water
Vent/ odour control: NCG from vacuum pumps (optionally to the A19 RTO)
Laboratory: C, A, S, density, TOC, oxalate, condensate conductivity

areas.area_name: A19 Liquor purification (causticisation, oxalate removal, organics removal by liquor burning, caustic make-up)
areas.purpose: Hold the liquor impurities at steady, acceptable levels and keep the caustic inventory up. 1) Causticisation: convert sodium carbonate (from bauxite carbonates, CO2 uptake and organic degradation) back to caustic with slaked lime, holding C/S ~0.86-0.90. 2) Oxalate removal: crystallise and remove sodium oxalate before it co-precipitates with gibbsite and causes fines, poor hydrate quality and high soda in the product. 3) Organics (TOC) removal: destroy humic and other organics that raise viscosity, reduce precipitation yield, discolour hydrate and stabilise oxalate. A side-stream liquor burning facility (LBF) is used, and it also destroys the oxalate cake. 4) Caustic make-up: receive, store and dose 50% NaOH to replace soda losses (~75 kg NaOH/t Al2O3).
areas.process_description: 1) Causticisation (side-stream on dilute liquor, 'improved' two-stage scheme). A side-stream (~500 m3/h) of first/second residue washer overflow (C ~100-130 g/L, carbonate ~20-30 g/L as Na2CO3, ~85-100 degC) goes to the causticisation feed tank. Dilute liquor is used because the carbonate-hydroxide equilibrium favours conversion at low caustic concentration. Reactor 1 (19-TK-111) receives slaked lime slurry from the A20 lime system. At moderate temperature (~70-90 degC, short residence ~10-30 min) the lime reacts with aluminate and carbonate to form hydrocalumite: 4 Ca(OH)2 + 2 NaAl(OH)4 + Na2CO3 -> Ca4Al2(OH)12.CO3 (+ water of crystallisation) + 4 NaOH. The slurry is then heated (direct steam injection, 19-SI-101) to ~100-105 degC in Reactors 2-3 (19-TK-112/113, ~1-2 h), where the hydrocalumite reacts with more carbonate to give calcium carbonate and release aluminate: Ca4Al2(OH)12.CO3 + 3 Na2CO3 -> 4 CaCO3 + 2 NaAl(OH)4 + 4 NaOH. The net reaction is Ca(OH)2 + Na2CO3 -> CaCO3 + 2 NaOH. The competing reaction to avoid is 3 Ca(OH)2 + 2 NaAl(OH)4 -> Ca3Al2(OH)12 (tricalcium aluminate, TCA) + 2 NaOH. It wastes lime and alumina, and TCA forms if hydrocalumite is held too long or too hot in high-aluminate liquor. Lime efficiency is ~50-65% for conventional single-stage causticisation and ~80-95% for the improved scheme (licensor data - verify). The causticised slurry (CaCO3 ~8-12 t/h solids) returns to the residue washer train (A08, washer 3 feed), so the CaCO3 leaves with the residue and the regenerated caustic is recovered up the washer train. 2) Oxalate removal. Sodium oxalate forms when humic organics degrade (in bauxite and in digestion). It accumulates to its critical stability limit (~3-5 g/L in spent liquor, depending on C, temperature and organics). Above that it co-precipitates on the hydrate as fine needles. At this plant, (a) controlled co-precipitation onto the fine/tertiary seed is washed off with hot condensate in A13 seed washing, giving an oxalate-rich seed-wash liquor (~150 m3/h). (b) This is mixed with a side-stream of strong evaporated liquor (~150-250 m3/h; high caustic lowers oxalate solubility, the 'salting-out' effect), cooled to ~45-50 degC in a wide-gap plate cooler and crystallised in seeded, agitated crystallisers (19-CR-201/202, ~4-8 h, oxalate seed ~20-50 g/L). (c) A thickener separates the crystals. Most of the underflow is recycled as seed; a bleed is filtered on a horizontal vacuum belt filter. The overflow (oxalate-depleted liquor) returns to the evaporator feed. (d) The oxalate cake (~0.4-0.8 t/h Na2C2O4 plus adhering liquor) goes to the liquor burner, where 2 Na2C2O4 + O2 -> 2 Na2CO3 + 2 CO2 (sodium oxalate also decomposes above ~290 degC to Na2CO3 + CO). Alternatives used in industry: lime destruction (Na2C2O4 + Ca(OH)2 -> CaC2O4 + 2 NaOH, calcium oxalate disposed with residue) and biological oxalate destruction (reported at Worsley, WA - verify). 3) Organics removal - liquor burning facility (LBF). A strong-liquor side-stream (~15-25 m3/h, TOC ~20-25 g/L) is concentrated in a forced-circulation evaporator (19-EV-301) to ~50-60% total solids. It is mixed in a pug mill with recycled burnt product (and the oxalate cake) into agglomerates and burned in a rotary kiln (19-KL-301) at ~900-1,050 degC (engineering estimate). The sodium organic salts oxidise (R-COONa + O2 -> Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O), and in the hot zone sodium carbonate reacts with the alumina from dehydrated aluminate: Na2CO3 + Al2O3 -> 2 NaAlO2 + CO2. Carbonate soda is therefore returned as 'caustic-equivalent' aluminate. The burnt product is cooled, dissolved in lean liquor (19-TK-311) and returned to the circuit. Kiln off-gas passes dust collection (ESP/ baghouse), then a regenerative thermal oxidiser (RTO) to destroy VOCs and odour (cf. the RTO fitted to the Alcoa Wagerup liquor burning facility - verify), then the stack. Alternatives: fluidised-bed liquor burners (cf. Alcoa Kwinana liquor burning - verify) and wet oxidation (~250-280 degC, ~80-110 bar, O2) - not selected (high pressure, corrosion, cost). East Coast India bauxite is low in organics, so the LBF can be smaller or deferred. Darling Range bauxite is organic-rich, which makes the LBF essential. 4) Caustic make-up. 50% NaOH is imported through the port (A17), railed or trucked to the refinery, unloaded into 2 storage tanks and dosed on ratio control to the strong liquor blend tanks (A18). Design rate ~18 t/h NaOH (100% basis) = ~36 t/h of 50% solution (~24 m3/h); range 55-110 kg NaOH/t Al2O3 depending on reactive silica. Soda losses: DSP (~0.69 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2), soluble soda in residue, soda in product (~0.3-0.4% Na2O), oxalate/LBF, spills. Note for high-temperature plants: boehmitic plants run lower caustic/higher temperature and add lime in digestion (to form cancrinite/ hydrogarnet that lowers soda loss and improves boehmite extraction), so their lime use is often higher and their causticisation arrangement differs.

equipment.name: Causticisation feed tank and feed pumps
equipment.function: Buffer the dilute washer-overflow side-stream and feed it at a controlled rate to Reactor 1.
equipment.type_selected: API 650 insulated atmospheric tank; horizontal centrifugal pumps (VSD)
equipment.why_this_type: Steady feed rate and composition are essential for lime efficiency.
key_dimensions: ~500 m3 (~9 m dia x 8.5 m) (engineering estimate)
Pumps ~550 m3/h x 30-40 m, ~90 kW
equipment.working_principle: A surge tank fed from the washer overflow launder via a flow-controlled branch. Feed pumps on flow control, with the lime dose ratioed to the feed carbonate (online analyser or lab).
details_to_model: Small insulated tank with roof manway, radar level, vent to vent header
Pump pair with guards, magflow on discharge, sample point with cooler, safety shower
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic liquor (~10% NaOH eq.), burns
Confined space
instrumentation_and_control: Level, flow, temperature; carbonate/ conductivity analyser (optional)
equipment.materials: CS, PWHT per NACE SP0403
common_problems: Scale (TCA, hydrate) in feed line
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hold the feed steady; carbonate swings upset the lime ratio

equipment.name: Causticisation Reactor 1 (hydrocalumite formation)
equipment.function: Contact slaked lime with the dilute aluminate liquor under controlled, moderate-temperature, short-residence conditions to form hydrocalumite (the intermediate that makes the improved process efficient).
equipment.type_selected: Agitated, baffled, cylindrical atmospheric reactor tank with top-entry agitator
equipment.why_this_type: Well-mixed short-residence contact disperses the lime rapidly, so hydrocalumite rather than TCA forms.
key_dimensions: ~200 m3 working; ~7 m dia x 7.5 m (engineering estimate)
Agitator ~30-55 kW, hydrofoil/pitched-blade impeller ~2.5 m dia, 4 wall baffles
equipment.working_principle: Lime slurry and liquor enter together near the impeller. Calcium hydroxide dissolves and reacts with aluminate and carbonate ions, precipitating a layered double hydroxide (hydrocalumite, Ca4Al2(OH)12.CO3.xH2O). In this compound, carbonate is held between positively charged calcium-aluminium hydroxide layers. Residence time and temperature are limited so the hydrocalumite does not convert to stable tricalcium aluminate. The slurry overflows to Reactor 2.
details_to_model: Tank with bridge-mounted agitator drive (motor + right-angle gearbox) on roof, 4 vertical baffles
Lime slurry inlet nozzle with pinch/ knife-gate valve and magflow; liquor inlet; overflow box/ launder to Reactor 2
Roof manway, vent, platform with handrails, stair access; drain DN200 with knife-gate
Insulation and cladding
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry; lime is an irritant/ corrosive
Agitator: LOTO before entry; confined space
equipment.materials: CS, PWHT; agitator shaft/impeller CS with wear protection
common_problems: Lime grit settling
Scale on impeller
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check the lime efficiency daily (carbonate removed vs CaO added)
sources: Rosenberg S.P., Wilson D.J., Heath C.A. (2001) 'Some aspects of calcium chemistry in the Bayer process', Light Metals 2001, TMS - verify
Rosenberg S.P., Healy S.J. et al., Alcoa patent WO 99/58450 'Improved causticisation of Bayer liquors' - verify
Whittington B.I. (1996) 'The chemistry of CaO and Ca(OH)2 relating to the Bayer process', Hydrometallurgy 43:13-35

equipment.name: Causticisation slurry heater (direct steam injection)
equipment.function: Raise the slurry from Reactor 1 to ~100-105 degC before Reactors 2-3.
equipment.type_selected: In-line direct steam-injection (sparger/ jet) heater
equipment.why_this_type: No heat-transfer surface to scale with lime/ TCA; small temperature rise.
key_dimensions: DN300-350 body ~1.5-2 m long; LP steam ~3-6 t/h (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Steam is injected through nozzles into the flowing slurry and condenses instantly, giving up its latent heat. The condensate adds to the liquor (a small water load for evaporation). A temperature controller trims a steam valve.
details_to_model: Inline cylindrical body with steam nozzle, control valve, check valve, isolation; temperature element downstream
hazards_and_safety: Steam hammer if slurry stops: low-flow interlock closes steam
equipment.materials: CS/ hard-faced nozzle
common_problems: Nozzle blockage by scale
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never inject steam into stagnant slurry

equipment.name: Causticisation Reactors 2-3 (carbonate conversion) and discharge pumps
equipment.function: Hold the hydrocalumite slurry at ~100-105 degC long enough to convert it to calcium carbonate with release of aluminate and caustic, then pump the slurry to the washer train.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated atmospheric reactor tanks; rubber-lined/ high-chrome horizontal slurry pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Series reactors approach plug flow, which gives higher conversion.
key_dimensions: ~550-600 m3 each; ~9.5 m dia x 9 m (engineering estimate)
Agitators ~45-75 kW each
Pumps ~600 m3/h x 30-40 m, ~110 kW

operating_parameters.basis: Rosenberg et al. (Alcoa) - verify; engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: Hydrocalumite is unstable at higher temperature in carbonate-bearing liquor and reacts to calcium carbonate (calcite), releasing aluminate and hydroxide back to the liquor. Agitation keeps solids suspended. Overflow passes from R2 to R3, and the R3 product is pumped to washer 3, where the CaCO3 leaves with residue.

Pump pair at grade with knife-gate valves, flushing connections, drain to bund sump
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry at boiling point - vents release steam
Confined space; agitator isolation
instrumentation_and_control: Level, temperature, agitator power, discharge flow/ density
equipment.materials: CS PWHT; pumps rubber-lined or high-chrome
common_problems: Overlong residence converts Hc to TCA (lime loss)
Scale build-up on walls
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the temperature and residence within the window; sample carbonate in and out each shift
