Rosenberg et al. Light Metals 2001 - verify

equipment.name: Oxalate crystalliser feed tank, pumps and feed cooler
equipment.function: Combine oxalate-rich seed-wash liquor with a strong-liquor side-stream and cool the mixture to ~45-50 degC to create oxalate supersaturation.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated feed tank; wide-gap plate heat exchanger (cooling water)
equipment.why_this_type: Wide-gap plates tolerate fine solids and are easy to clean; cooling drives oxalate supersaturation.
key_dimensions: Tank ~300 m3 (~7.5 m dia x 7 m)
Cooler duty ~8-14 MW; ~400-600 m2 plate area, frame ~3.5 m tall x ~1.2 m wide x ~4-5 m long (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Sodium oxalate solubility falls as temperature falls and as caustic concentration rises (common-ion/ salting-out effect). Mixing the low-caustic, high-oxalate wash liquor with strong liquor, then cooling it, makes the mixture supersaturated with oxalate without nucleating gibbsite (the A/C of the mix is kept low).
details_to_model: Plate pack between fixed and movable frame plates, tie bolts, carrying/guide bars, 4 corner nozzles
Tank with agitator, pumps with guards, CW connections with isolation valves
hazards_and_safety: Caustic leaks at plate gaskets: spray shield fitted over the plate pack
equipment.materials: Plates SS 316L or titanium? (CW side chlorides) - SS 316L typical for caustic at <50 degC; EPDM gaskets
common_problems: Oxalate/ hydrate scale on plates
operating_tips_and_key_points: Switch to the spare cooler and caustic-wash the fouled one when the DP doubles
sources: Power G., Loh J. (2010) 'Organic compounds in the processing of lateritic bauxites to alumina Part 1', Hydrometallurgy 105:1-29

equipment.name: Oxalate crystallisers
equipment.function: Grow sodium oxalate crystals on recycled oxalate seed so oxalate is removed as a filterable solid.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated, baffled, flat or shallow-cone-bottom crystalliser tanks with draft-tube or hydrofoil agitator
equipment.why_this_type: Seeded, well-mixed growth avoids fine nucleation; long residence completes desupersaturation.
key_dimensions: ~1,000-1,200 m3 each; ~11 m dia x 12 m (engineering estimate)
Agitators ~55-90 kW each
equipment.working_principle: Supersaturated liquor contacts a large surface of existing sodium oxalate crystals (needle-shaped). Oxalate deposits on these seeds instead of forming new fines. Recycling thickened seed keeps the surface area high, and the liquor desupersaturates towards solubility as it passes through the two tanks.
details_to_model: Two large tanks with roof agitators, overflow launders between, platforms
Seed recycle inlet; sample points; drain valves
hazards_and_safety: Caustic liquor (~45 degC, still corrosive)
Confined space with scaled internals
instrumentation_and_control: Temperature, level, solids density, oxalate (lab, IC/ titration)
equipment.materials: CS (temperature below caustic-SCC threshold)
common_problems: Oxalate scale on walls and impellers
Poisoning of crystal growth by organics (humates)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the seed charge up; low seed causes fine oxalate that does not settle
sources: Power, Loh & Vernon (2012) 'Organic compounds in the processing of lateritic bauxites to alumina Part 2: Effects of organics in the Bayer process', Hydrometallurgy 127-128:125-149

equipment.name: Oxalate thickener
equipment.function: Settle oxalate crystals, return most as seed, bleed product solids to the filter and overflow clear liquor to evaporator feed.
equipment.type_selected: High-rate bridge-supported thickener with centre drive and rakes, flocculant optional
equipment.why_this_type: Compact; oxalate crystals settle readily when well grown.
key_dimensions: ~15-18 m dia, ~4-5 m side wall, ~10 deg floor cone (engineering estimate)
Drive torque ~100-200 kNm class
equipment.working_principle: Feed enters a central feedwell where it is slowed down and spread. Crystals settle to the floor, and the slowly turning rakes move them to the central cone for underflow pumping. Clear liquor rises to a peripheral overflow launder.
details_to_model: Circular tank on ring wall, full-diameter bridge with walkway, centre drive with motor/gearbox, rake arms with blades, feedwell, peripheral launder with outlet box
Underflow pumps (2, one standby) with recycle and bleed lines
hazards_and_safety: Falls into thickener: bridge handrails
Rake bogging: torque alarm
instrumentation_and_control: Rake torque, bed level, underflow density
equipment.materials: CS
common_problems: Rake overload from oxalate scale build-up
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch rake torque trends

equipment.name: Oxalate filter, vacuum system and cake handling
equipment.function: Dewater the oxalate bleed and deliver the cake to the liquor burner (or to lime destruction).
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal vacuum belt filter with cake wash (alternative: pressure filter or pusher centrifuge)
equipment.why_this_type: Allows displacement washing of entrained caustic; simple maintenance.
key_dimensions: ~8-12 m2 filtration area; belt ~1.5-2 m wide x ~8-10 m long (engineering estimate)
Cake bin ~50 m3 with screw feeder
equipment.working_principle: Slurry is fed onto a moving rubber drainage belt that carries a filter cloth over vacuum boxes. Filtrate is sucked through the cloth into a receiver, and the cake is washed with a little condensate, dewatered and discharged over the head roller to a screw conveyor.
details_to_model: Long low frame with rubber belt, filter cloth, vacuum box, feed box, wash sprays, cloth tracking rollers, discharge chute
Filtrate receiver vessel, liquid-ring vacuum pump, filtrate pump
Screw conveyor to cake bin, bin vent
hazards_and_safety: Caustic-wet cake
Pinch points at rollers; guarding
equipment.materials: SS frame/ rubber belt, polypropylene cloth
common_problems: Cloth blinding
operating_tips_and_key_points: Wash the cloth every shift

equipment.name: LBF feed concentrator (forced-circulation evaporator)
equipment.function: Concentrate the strong-liquor side-stream to ~50-60% total solids before liquor burning, to cut kiln fuel.
equipment.type_selected: Single- or double-effect forced-circulation evaporator with external shell-and-tube heater and axial recirculation pump
equipment.why_this_type: High concentration and near-saturated salts mean scaling. Forced circulation suppresses boiling in the tubes, which falling film cannot handle at these solids levels.
key_dimensions: Heater ~300-500 m2; separator ~3 m dia x 8 m; axial circulation pump ~2,000-3,000 m3/h, ~150-250 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A large axial pump drives the liquor at high velocity (2-3 m/s) through the heater tubes, under enough static head that it does not boil in the tubes. It then flashes in the separator, which keeps salt deposition out of the tubes.
details_to_model: Vertical separator, external heater (inclined or vertical), large elbow loop with axial pump at bottom, steam inlet, condensate pot, vapour line to condenser
hazards_and_safety: Very concentrated hot caustic (~25-35% NaOH eq.): severe burns
Salt blockages
instrumentation_and_control: Density of product, level, steam flow
equipment.materials: Nickel-alloy or duplex in hot zones (high caustic concentration and temperature) - engineering estimate; verify per NACE SP0403
common_problems: Salting/ blockages
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the density within range; overconcentration plugs lines

equipment.name: Liquor burner rotary kiln with feed pug mill and burner
equipment.function: Oxidise sodium organic salts and oxalate to sodium carbonate and convert carbonate to sodium aluminate, destroying TOC and recovering soda.
equipment.type_selected: Direct-fired counter-current rotary kiln with twin-shaft pug mill feed and natural-gas burner
equipment.why_this_type: Handles sticky sodium salt agglomerates. Recycling burnt product dilutes the liquor so the bed does not melt. Alternatives: fluidised-bed liquor burner; wet oxidation.
key_dimensions: Kiln ~3.0-3.6 m shell dia x ~45-60 m long, slope ~2-3%, 2-3 tyres, girth gear drive ~200-350 kW (engineering estimate)
Pug mill ~1.2 m x 6 m twin shaft
Burner ~10-20 MW firing
equipment.working_principle: Concentrated liquor, oxalate cake and hot recycled product are mixed into damp granules and fed into the upper (cold) end of the inclined, slowly rotating kiln (~1-3 rpm). As the bed tumbles towards the burner end, it dries, then the organics burn (releasing heat), and finally sodium carbonate reacts with alumina to form sodium aluminate. Hot gases flow counter-current to the bed and leave at the feed end.
details_to_model: Long refractory-lined steel shell on 2-3 tyre/ roller stations with thrust roller, girth gear and pinion, main drive motor + gearbox, auxiliary (barring) drive
Feed end housing with seal, feed chute from pug mill; discharge (firing) hood with burner pipe, flame scanner, peep holes
Shell scanner (IR) gantry, kiln shell cooling fans
Platforms at each tyre station, lubrication systems on rollers
hazards_and_safety: Hot surfaces/ flame; burner management system per NFPA 85/86 (purge, flame failure trips)
Caustic dust; CO in confined zones; rotating machinery
Refractory relining = confined space, heat stress
instrumentation_and_control: Kiln inlet/outlet temperatures, O2/CO analyser, shell scanner, drive current, BMS
equipment.materials: Shell CS; refractory alkali-resistant alumina brick/castable
common_problems: Ring formation from molten salts
Refractory attack by soda
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the recycle ratio up to prevent melting and rings
sources: Power, Loh & Vernon (2012) Hydrometallurgy 127-128:125-149 (organics removal options including liquor burning and wet oxidation)
Alcoa Kwinana and Wagerup liquor burning references (public environmental reports) - verify
NFPA 86 Standard for Ovens and Furnaces

equipment.name: LBF product cooler, leach (dissolution) tank and pumps
equipment.function: Cool the burnt product, dissolve its soluble sodium aluminate/carbonate in lean liquor and return the solution to the circuit.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary drum cooler (or fluid-bed cooler); agitated leach tank; slurry pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Robust handling of hot granular product.
key_dimensions: Cooler ~2.5 m dia x 20 m (engineering estimate)
Leach tank ~150 m3
equipment.working_principle: Hot product is cooled by air/ water-jacket, part is recycled to the pug mill, and the net product is dissolved; Na aluminate re-enters the liquor as caustic + alumina.
details_to_model: Drum with tyres and drive, product recycle elevator/ screw, leach tank with agitator, pumps
hazards_and_safety: Hot solids; caustic dust; exothermic dissolution
equipment.materials: CS
common_problems: Dust emissions; lumps
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the leach tank agitated, because lumps cause blockages

equipment.name: LBF off-gas cleaning: dust collector, regenerative thermal oxidiser, ID fan and stack
equipment.function: Remove sodium salt dust and destroy VOCs/ odour in the kiln off-gas before discharge.
equipment.type_selected: ESP or pulse-jet baghouse; 2- or 3-can regenerative thermal oxidiser (ceramic media beds); centrifugal ID fan; steel stack
equipment.why_this_type: VOC/odour emissions from Bayer liquor burning have been a documented community issue. An RTO destroys >95-98% of VOC with low fuel use.
key_dimensions: RTO ~3 canisters each ~5 m x 5 m x 8 m; stack ~40-60 m tall, ~2 m dia; ID fan ~400-800 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Dust is removed first to protect the RTO beds. In the RTO, gas passes up through a hot ceramic bed, reaches the burner chamber where the VOCs oxidise, and then exits down through a second bed that absorbs the heat. Valves switch the flow direction every 1-3 minutes, so ~95% of the heat is recovered.
details_to_model: Box-shaped ESP with hoppers and rappers OR baghouse with compartments and pulse valves
RTO canisters with poppet/ butterfly switching valves on manifolds, burner in top chamber
ID fan with VFD, silencer, stack with sampling platform and ports (CEMS)
hazards_and_safety: Explosion risk if LEL exceeded at RTO inlet: LEL monitor and dilution
Hot surfaces; ESP high voltage (interlocked access)
equipment.materials: CS; ceramic media; refractory
common_problems: Salt plugging of RTO media
operating_tips_and_key_points: Bake out the RTO media periodically to clear salt plugging
sources: Alcoa Wagerup refinery liquor burning facility RTO (public reports c.2006-2007) - verify
US EPA Air Pollution Control Technology Fact Sheet: Regenerative Thermal Oxidizer

equipment.name: Caustic soda (50% NaOH) unloading, storage and dosing
equipment.function: Receive 50% caustic by rail/road, store ~2 weeks of supply, and dose to the liquor blend tanks (and to minor users: resin regeneration, scrubbers).
equipment.type_selected: API 650 vertical cone-roof CS tanks, insulated, with external/coil heating; horizontal centrifugal pumps (sealless mag-drive or double mechanical seal)
equipment.why_this_type: Standard caustic storage practice. Carbon steel is suitable for 50% NaOH below ~50-60 degC (NACE SP0403 / Euro Chlor guidance); heating prevents crystallisation (freezing point ~12 degC).
key_dimensions: Tanks 2 x ~6,000 m3 (~22 m dia x 16 m); ~14 days at 24 m3/h (engineering estimate; bulk import tanks at port in A17)
Bund >=110% of largest tank, acid/alkali-resistant coating
Unloading: 2 rail/road bays with canopy, air or pump unloading, ~60-80 t per tank wagon
equipment.working_principle: Wagons or trucks are coupled with dry-break couplings and emptied by transfer pump (or low-pressure air) into the storage tanks through a filter. Dosing pumps deliver caustic on flow-ratio control to the blend tanks, where it mixes into hot liquor. The heat of dilution is small at the blend tank because caustic enters a large hot stream.
details_to_model: Two large insulated tanks with external heating coil/ steam-traced bottom, spiral stair, roof handrail, level radar and HH switch, vent with breather/ CO2 guard (carbonate pick-up)
Unloading bays with canopy, loading arms/ hoses, dry-break couplings, drip trays, wheel chocks, earthing clamp
Safety showers/ eyewash stations (tempered water, alarmed) at each bay and pump set
Pump set with splash guards, discharge filters, magflows; DN100-150 transfer lines with flanges guarded by spray shields
Signage: CORROSIVE 8 (UN1824), PPE board
hazards_and_safety: 50% NaOH: severe skin burns and blindness within seconds; flush at least 15-60 min
Large heat of dilution: never add water to concentrated caustic
Spray from flange leaks: flange spray guards
Heavy vehicle/ rail movements at the unloading bays
Hydrogen from aluminium contact
instrumentation_and_control: Level, temperature, flow; HH level trip on unloading pump
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (no PWHT needed at <~50 degC for 50% NaOH per NACE SP0403), EPDM/ PTFE gaskets, SS 316 small-bore
common_problems: Crystallisation in lines at low temperature
Leaks at hose couplings
operating_tips_and_key_points: Wear full PPE when coupling and uncoupling; check that the safety shower works before each unloading
sources: OxyChem Caustic Soda Handbook (handling and storage)
Euro Chlor GEST guidance on caustic soda storage - verify
NACE SP0403-2015 caustic soda service chart
ANSI/ISEA Z358.1 Emergency eyewash and shower equipment

areas.layout_notes: Causticisation (19-TK-101, 19-TK-111..113, pumps) is a compact bunded block (~40 m x 25 m) next to the residue washer train (A08), ~50-100 m from washers 1-3, so feed and return lines stay short. Lime slurry comes from the A20 lime system ring main (~100-300 m). The oxalate plant (feed tank, coolers, 2 crystallisers, thickener, belt filter house) is ~60 m x 40 m, located between the evaporation area (A18, strong liquor) and the seed washing/ classification area (A13), ~100-200 m from each. The liquor burning facility (concentrator, pug mill, kiln ~60 m long, cooler, leach tank, ESP/RTO and 40-60 m stack) takes ~120 m x 40 m. It is placed on the downwind side of the refinery, >=300 m from offices, control room and laboratory, near A18 (strong liquor feed) and with road access for refractory works. The caustic tank farm (2 x 6,000 m3) and unloading bays sit next to the refinery rail siding/ road gate, ~200-400 m from the liquor blend tanks (A18), with a dedicated caustic pipeline on the main rack. Every area has bunds sloped to sumps with sump pumps returning spills to the process, and safety showers within ~10 s travel (~15 m) of every caustic hazard point.
interfaces: A08 Settling & washing: dilute washer overflow side-stream ~500 m3/h to causticisation; causticised slurry returned to washer 3
A20 Utilities: slaked lime slurry ~45-60 m3/h (~6-7 t/h CaO); LP steam (~20-30 t/h total incl. LBF concentrator); cooling water to oxalate coolers; natural gas to the kiln/ RTO; compressed air; power
A13 Classification & seed: oxalate-rich seed-wash liquor ~150 m3/h
A18 Evaporation: strong liquor side-streams (oxalate ~150-250 m3/h; LBF ~15-25 m3/h); oxalate-depleted liquor returned to evaporator feed; caustic make-up dosed into 18-TK-021/022
A17 Port: imported 50% caustic soda (bulk storage at port) by rail/ road
A09 Residue: CaCO3/ calcium solids leave with residue
Laboratory: carbonate (S-C), oxalate, TOC, lime availability, lime efficiency calculation
Environment: LBF stack CEMS, odour monitoring

areas.area_name: A20 Utilities (steam and power cogeneration, boiler feed and condensate, raw and demineralised water, cooling water, compressed air, lime storage and slaking, fuel gas)
areas.purpose: Supply the refinery's steam (~410 t/h process steam at MP 10-12 barg and LP 4-5 barg), electricity (~55-60 MW refinery plus ~6-10 MW for mine, overland conveyor and port), raw and demineralised water (~550 m3/h raw), cooling water (~10,000 m3/h circulating), compressed and instrument air (~10,000-12,000 Nm3/h), slaked lime (~40 kg CaO/t Al2O3) and natural gas (~2,200-2,400 GJ/h for the calciners, boilers, gas turbines and kiln). The design is N+1 for reliability, so that agitation and steam continue on loss of a unit. Settling of solids in precipitators and thickeners after a total power loss is one of the most costly refinery upsets.
areas.process_description: 1) Steam and power (cogeneration). Two gas-turbine generators (~25-35 MW ISO class) exhaust at ~500-550 degC into two heat-recovery steam generators (HRSG) with duct burners, each making up to ~150 t/h at ~63-65 bar(a)/ 470-480 degC. Two gas-fired water-tube auxiliary boilers (~150 t/h each, same steam conditions) make up the balance and give N+1 cover. HP steam passes through a back-pressure/ extraction steam turbine generator (~35-40 MW), with MP extraction at 10-12 barg (digestion live-steam heaters) and LP exhaust at 4-5 barg (evaporators, pre-desilication, causticisation, deaerators, tank heating). Pressure-reducing and desuperheating stations (PRDS) back up each level when the turbine is off. Total generation (~95-100 MW) exceeds site demand (~65 MW), so ~30 MW is exported to the grid (as at gas cogeneration plants supplying Australian refineries, e.g., the Alinta Pinjarra cogeneration plant - verify). The site can also island on grid failure. Alternative (common at Indian refineries such as Lanjigarh, Utkal and Damanjodi): coal-fired CFBC boilers with back-pressure turbines (higher CO2, ~0.8-1.0 t CO2/t alumina). 2) Boiler feedwater and condensate. Clean condensate returns from the digestion live-steam heaters (~150 t/h) and evaporator effect 1 (~100 t/h). It is checked by conductivity and sodium analysers with automatic dump, then filtered (cartridge/ precoat condensate polishing) into condensate tanks. Together with demineralised make-up (~100-150 t/h: direct-injection steam to pre-desilication, causticisation and losses is not returned) it is deaerated at ~1.5 barg/ ~127 degC. Chemicals: oxygen scavenger, amine or ammonia for pH, phosphate or caustic-free all-volatile treatment as the boiler supplier specifies. Caustic ingress from a heater tube leak is the main boiler-chemistry risk: caustic gouging and caustic embrittlement. 3) Raw water. Water is pumped from a dam/ river (~10-30 km pipeline) into a lined raw-water storage pond (~7 days) and distributed to: cooling-tower make-up, the water treatment plant (clarifier, multimedia filters, RO, mixed-bed polishers -> demin), firewater, potable, dust suppression, gland/ seal water and residue washing top-up. Most process wash water comes from process condensate (A07/A18) and recycled residue-area (RSA) decant/ stormwater, which keeps fresh water at ~2-2.5 m3/t. 4) Cooling water. A 5-cell (4+1) induced-draft counterflow cooling tower (~10,000 m3/h, range ~10 K) serves the evaporator surface condensers (~50-60 MW), precipitation interstage coolers (~30-40 MW), oxalate coolers, compressor and turbine lube/ generator coolers, and the calciner/ hydrate areas (as required). The water is treated against scale, corrosion and biofouling, with pH and conductivity monitored to catch caustic ingress from process exchangers. 5) Compressed air. Four oil-free centrifugal compressors (3 duty, 1 standby, ~4,000 Nm3/h each at 8 barg) feed plant air (filter cake blowing, air-lances, tools, pneumatic conveying top-ups) and, through desiccant dryers, instrument air at a -40 degC pressure dew point (ISO 8573-1 class 2 for water). Instrument air has priority on a receiver with a non-return valve. 6) Lime. Quicklime (CaO ~88-92% available) arrives by road/ rail bulk tanker and is pneumatically blown to 2 silos (~1,500 t each, ~12 days). It is slaked in 2 x 100% slakers with hot process condensate (CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2, about -1.14 MJ/kg CaO exothermic, slurry ~75-85 degC). Grit is removed, and the 15-20% slurry is stored and circulated around a ring main to causticisation (A19), the security-filter TCA/ filter-aid preparation (A10), digestion/ pre-desilication (A05/A06, optional) and residue neutralisation. 7) Fuel. Natural gas arrives by pipeline at a receiving station (filtration, heating, metering, pressure reduction to ~25-30 barg for gas turbines and ~4-8 barg for calciners, boilers and kiln). Diesel is stored for the emergency generators, firewater diesel pumps and the mobile fleet. 8) Electrical. A 132 kV grid connection and main substation, with 11 kV generation and distribution, 6.6 kV/ 3.3 kV for large motors (mills, compressors, CW pumps), and 415 V MCCs. Two emergency diesel generators support essential loads (control systems, lube oil, thickener rakes, selected agitators, lighting). Note for high-temperature (boehmitic) plants: digestion needs steam at ~30-60 bar or molten salt/ hot oil heating, so the steam cycle has a high-pressure process header and less back-pressure power per tonne of steam.

equipment.name: Gas turbine generators (cogeneration)
equipment.function: Generate electricity and supply hot exhaust gas to the HRSGs.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (aux boilers and grid cover loss of one)
equipment.type_selected: Industrial or aeroderivative gas turbine, ~25-35 MW ISO, dry low-NOx combustor, 11 kV air-cooled generator
equipment.why_this_type: High combined heat-and-power efficiency (~75-80% fuel utilisation) with natural gas; widely used for steam/power supply to refineries in Western Australia.
key_dimensions: Package enclosure ~20 m L x 5 m W x 6 m H; elevated inlet filter house ~8 m x 6 m x 6 m; exhaust ~3-3.5 m dia transition to HRSG (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: An axial compressor draws filtered air and compresses it ~15-25 times. Fuel burns in the combustor at constant pressure, and the hot gas expands through the turbine stages, driving both the compressor and the generator. The exhaust (~500 degC) still carries most of the fuel energy and is recovered in the HRSG to make steam.
details_to_model: Acoustic enclosure with doors, ventilation fans, fire suppression (CO2/ water mist) cylinders
Inlet air filter house with weather hoods, multi-stage filters, inlet duct and silencer
Generator with terminal box, neutral earthing cubicle, bus duct to step-up transformer
Lube oil skid with coolers (fin-fan), fuel gas skid (filter, heater, stop/control valves)
Exhaust diffuser to HRSG with expansion joint; bypass stack with diverter damper (optional)
hazards_and_safety: Fuel gas leak/ explosion: gas detection in enclosure, ventilation, ESD
Hot surfaces, noise >100 dB(A) inside enclosure
Rotating machinery; CO2 fire suppression asphyxiation - lockout before entry
instrumentation_and_control: Turbine control system (speed, load, exhaust temperature spread)
Vibration (proximity probes), flame detection, gas detection
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Inlet filter clogging from bauxite/alumina dust
Compressor fouling
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep inlet filters changed (refinery dust); offline/online compressor washes
sources: API 616 Gas Turbines for Petroleum, Chemical and Gas Industry Services
Alinta Pinjarra cogeneration plant supplying Alcoa Pinjarra refinery - verify

equipment.name: Heat recovery steam generators with duct burners
equipment.function: Recover GT exhaust heat (plus supplementary firing) to raise HP steam for the process and turbine.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal-gas-flow, natural-circulation, single-pressure HRSG with duct burner, superheater, evaporator, economiser
equipment.why_this_type: Single pressure matches a process steam plant; supplementary firing gives flexibility to follow the steam load.
key_dimensions: Casing ~8-10 m W x ~22-25 m H x ~25-30 m L; steam drum ~1.8 m dia x 12 m on top; stack ~45-50 m x 4-4.5 m dia (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Exhaust gas flows horizontally through banks of finned tubes: superheater (hottest), evaporator (riser tubes connected to the steam drum, where steam separates from water by natural circulation), then economiser (preheats feedwater). Duct burners in the inlet duct raise the gas temperature when more steam is needed.
details_to_model: Large rectangular insulated casing with external stiffeners, access doors, inlet transition duct
Steam drum on top with safety valves, water level gauges (2 direct + transmitters), main steam stop valve, non-return valve
Downcomers and riser pipes, headers, blowdown lines to blowdown tank
Duct burner runners with flame scanners and gas train
Stack with CEMS platform, ladders, aviation lights; platforms at drum and header levels
hazards_and_safety: High-pressure steam: drum safety valves to ASME I / IBR/ AS 1228; boiler explosion risk from low water
Furnace explosion: purge before firing (NFPA 85)
Hot surfaces; confined space in casing
instrumentation_and_control: Three-element drum level control, low-low level trip
equipment.materials: Superheater alloy steel (T22/T91); evaporator/economiser CS finned tubes
common_problems: Economiser corrosion at low feedwater temperature
Caustic contamination of feedwater causing under-deposit gouging
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never bypass low drum-level trips; blow down as the chemistry requires
sources: ASME BPVC Section I (Power Boilers) / Indian Boiler Regulations / AS 1228
NFPA 85 Boiler and Combustion Systems Hazards Code

equipment.name: Auxiliary gas-fired water-tube boilers
equipment.function: Provide the balance of HP steam and N+1 back-up when a GT/HRSG is offline.
equipment.type_selected: Shop-assembled D-type package water-tube boiler with low-NOx burners, FD fan and economiser
equipment.why_this_type: Fast start, high availability, compact; 150 t/h is near the upper limit for shop assembly.
key_dimensions: ~150 t/h each; package ~20-22 m L x ~6 m W x ~9-10 m H; stack ~40 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Gas burns in a water-cooled furnace. Radiant heat boils water in the membrane walls, and convection banks complete evaporation between the steam drum and the mud drum. A superheater raises the steam temperature, and an economiser recovers flue-gas heat into the feedwater.
details_to_model: Long boxy casing with burner front (windbox, burner, gas train, flame scanners), FD fan and silencer at front
Steam drum on top with safety valves and gauge glasses; economiser on top/rear; flue duct to stack
Platforms on burner front and drum level; ladders
hazards_and_safety: As HRSG: furnace explosion, low water, high-pressure steam
Gas train leaks: gas detection
instrumentation_and_control: Burner management system (purge, flame safeguard, trips)
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Refractory damage at burner throat
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep one aux boiler on hot standby (minimum fire) so it can take load quickly if a GT trips

equipment.name: Back-pressure / extraction steam turbine generator
equipment.function: Expand HP steam to the process pressures while generating electricity.
equipment.type_selected: Multi-stage back-pressure turbine with controlled MP extraction, gearbox, 11 kV generator
equipment.why_this_type: All exhaust steam is used by the process (no condenser loss), giving ~80%+ thermal utilisation of the steam-raising fuel.
key_dimensions: Turbine-gearbox-generator train ~15-18 m long on ~8 m high concrete table-top; turbine hall with ~50-80 t EOT crane (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Steam expands through nozzle and blade rows, converting pressure energy to velocity and then to shaft torque. Part of the steam is extracted at the MP pressure through a controlled extraction valve, and the remainder exhausts at LP header pressure. The turbine is governed on header pressure (back-pressure control) while the generator supplies the grid/island.
details_to_model: Turbine casing with HP inlet stop and control valves (actuator rack), extraction and exhaust nozzles to large-bore headers, lagging
Reduction gearbox (if high-speed), generator with exciter, lube oil console, steam seal system
Table-top foundation with stair, turbine hall crane, PRDS stations beside
hazards_and_safety: Overspeed (trip valves tested), high-pressure steam, hot surfaces, noise
Lube-oil fire: fire detection/ deluge
instrumentation_and_control: Governor, overspeed protection, vibration/ axial position monitoring (API 670)
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Valve stem deposits; seal wear
operating_tips_and_key_points: Test the trip valves on schedule; the process headers must not lose pressure on a turbine trip, so the PRDS must take over automatically
sources: API 612 Special-purpose steam turbines; API 670 machinery protection

equipment.name: Pressure-reducing and desuperheating stations (PRDS) and steam headers
equipment.function: Back up the turbine (HP->MP, HP->LP, MP->LP) and keep header pressures constant.
equipment.type_selected: Combined pressure-reducing / desuperheating valve with spray water from BFW
equipment.why_this_type: Fast-acting header pressure control on turbine trip.
key_dimensions: Valves DN300-500 inlet, DN600-900 outlet; headers DN600-1,000 on main rack (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A control valve drops the steam pressure; feedwater sprayed in after the valve removes the superheat. Pressure and temperature loops trim each.
details_to_model: Angle-body control valve with large actuator, spray nozzle assembly, silencer/ diffuser, long straight run, drain pots and traps, PSVs on downstream headers
hazards_and_safety: High noise; steam hammer
equipment.materials: Alloy/ CS piping per pressure class
common_problems: Trim erosion
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the PRDS warm (small bleed) for instant response

equipment.name: Deaerators and boiler feedwater pumps
equipment.function: Remove dissolved O2/CO2 from feedwater and pump it at boiler pressure to the HRSGs/ boilers.
equipment.type_selected: Spray-tray deaerator on horizontal storage tank; horizontal multistage barrel/ ring-section pumps (BB4/BB5) with VSD or hydrodynamic coupling
equipment.why_this_type: Standard; multistage pumps reach ~75-80 barg.
key_dimensions: Deaerator head ~2.5 m dia x 5 m; storage ~3.5 m dia x 14 m (~100 m3), elevated ~15-20 m above pump suction (engineering estimate)
BFW pumps ~330 m3/h x ~850-900 m, ~1.0-1.3 MW each
equipment.working_principle: Feedwater is sprayed into a steam-filled head and heated to saturation, which drives out dissolved gases; these vent with a little steam. The tank stores deaerated water, and its elevation gives the BFW pumps NPSH. Multistage pumps raise the pressure in series impellers.
details_to_model: Elevated structure with horizontal tank and vertical head, vent condenser, safety valves, level gauges
Pumps at grade with suction strainers, minimum-flow recirculation valves (ARC), large motors, lube units
hazards_and_safety: Hot pressurised water flashing if lines break
Pump minimum-flow protection to prevent overheating
instrumentation_and_control: Deaerator pressure/level, dissolved O2 analyser, pump auto-start on low header pressure
equipment.materials: CS; pumps 13Cr internals
common_problems: Vent valve throttled too far (poor O2 removal)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch the dissolved O2 and pH every shift

equipment.name: Condensate return tanks, condensate polishing and pumps
equipment.function: Collect returned process condensate, verify purity, polish and pump to deaerators.
equipment.type_selected: Atmospheric CS (internally coated) tanks; cartridge/ precoat filter + mixed-bed polishers; centrifugal pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Bayer condensate can carry caustic and alumina from leaks; polishing and dump protection are essential.
key_dimensions: Tanks 2 x ~1,500 m3 (~13 m dia x 12 m); polishers 2 x ~150 m3/h (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Online conductivity and sodium analysers on each return line divert contaminated condensate to the process. Accepted condensate is filtered and polished by ion exchange before deaeration.
details_to_model: Analyser shelter with sample coolers, three-way dump valves, filter vessels, resin vessels, regeneration chemical skid
Tanks with vents/ overflow, pump set
hazards_and_safety: Hot water; regeneration acid/caustic
instrumentation_and_control: Conductivity, Na, silica analysers; tank levels
equipment.materials: Coated CS / SS
common_problems: Resin exhaustion by caustic slugs
operating_tips_and_key_points: Treat every analyser alarm as real until proven otherwise

equipment.name: Main substation, transformers and emergency diesel generators
equipment.function: Connect to the grid, distribute power at 11 kV and lower, and provide emergency power to essential loads.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 substation; 2 grid transformers; generator step-up/ unit transformers; 2 EDGs
equipment.type_selected: 132 kV GIS or AIS switchyard, 2 x ~80 MVA 132/11 kV ONAN/ONAF transformers, 11 kV metal-clad switchgear, 2 x ~3 MVA diesel generators
equipment.why_this_type: Firm supply with export capability; islanding capability protects the precipitation and thickener inventories.
key_dimensions: Switchyard ~80 m x 60 m; transformers ~8 m x 5 m x 6 m each with fire walls and oil bunds; EDG containers ~12 m x 3 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Power from the generators and grid is collected on 11 kV switchboards and distributed by feeders to area substations. Protection relays isolate faults selectively. On total power loss, load-shedding and EDG auto-start restore essential loads within seconds, and the refinery restarts in sequence (agitators before settled solids harden).
details_to_model: Fenced switchyard with gantries, circuit breakers, disconnectors, CTs/VTs, surge arresters, overhead line entry
Large oil transformers with radiators, conservator, Buchholz relay, firewalls and oil containment
Switchroom building with cable trenches, battery room; EDG containers with exhaust stacks and day tanks
hazards_and_safety: Electrocution/ arc flash: permits, switching procedures, arc-rated PPE
Transformer fire: deluge, firewalls
Diesel fuel
instrumentation_and_control: SCADA/ power management system with load shedding
common_problems: Dust and caustic mist on outdoor insulators (flashover) - insulator washing
operating_tips_and_key_points: Practise the black-start sequence; prioritise precipitator and thickener agitation/ rakes
sources: IEC 61936-1 Power installations exceeding 1 kV AC

equipment.name: Natural gas receiving station and diesel storage
equipment.function: Receive, filter, heat, meter and reduce pipeline gas for all burners and GTs; store diesel for emergency and mobile use.
equipment.type_selected: Skid-mounted gas station: inlet ESD valve, filter-separators, water-bath or electric heaters, pressure-reduction runs (active/monitor regulators + slam-shut), ultrasonic fiscal meters; API 650 diesel tanks
equipment.why_this_type: Standard pipeline custody transfer and pressure reduction.
key_dimensions: Gas station compound ~60 m x 30 m, vent stack ~10-15 m; diesel tanks 2 x ~500 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Gas is cleaned of liquids/ dust and heated so that the Joule-Thomson cooling across the regulators does not cause hydrates or ice. It is then reduced in pressure in two stages and metered for custody transfer. Slam-shut valves protect downstream piping from overpressure.
details_to_model: Fenced compound, yellow-painted piping with flow arrows, filter-separator vessels, heater, regulator runs, meter runs with flow conditioners, vent stack, ESD valve with actuator, gas detectors
hazards_and_safety: Flammable gas/ explosion; hazardous area zoning; hot work permits
Diesel fire
instrumentation_and_control: Fiscal metering, gas chromatograph (calorific value), pressure/ temperature, gas detection, ESD
equipment.materials: CS API 5L
common_problems: Regulator instability; filter DP
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check the filter DP and the heater outlet temperature daily

equipment.name: Raw water intake pumps, pipeline and raw water storage pond
equipment.function: Supply fresh water to the refinery and store ~7 days of demand.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical turbine pumps (VS1) at river/ dam intake or horizontal split-case pumps (BB1); HDPE-lined earth-embankment pond
equipment.why_this_type: Reliable bulk water transfer; the pond buffers dry-season or pipeline outages.
key_dimensions: Pumps ~240 m3/h each at ~60-120 m head (route dependent); pipeline DN500-600, ~10-30 km (engineering estimate)
Pond ~100,000 m3 (~150 m x 120 m x 6 m deep) (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Pumps lift water from the source and push it through the pipeline to the refinery pond. Distribution pumps (on the pond) supply the treatment plant, cooling tower make-up, firewater tanks and process users.
details_to_model: Intake structure with screens, VS1 pumps with motors on deck, surge vessel, pipeline with air valves and scour valves
Pond with HDPE liner, crest road, inlet/outlet structures, fence, life rings
hazards_and_safety: Drowning (pond): fencing, life rings, no-entry
Water hammer in long pipeline: surge protection
equipment.materials: Ductile iron/ steel pipeline with cathodic protection
common_problems: Algae in pond
Intake screen blockage
operating_tips_and_key_points: Track the water balance: rising raw-water demand often signals process condensate being lost to drain
sources: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe; Hydraulic Institute standards

equipment.name: Water treatment and demineralisation plant
equipment.function: Produce clarified/ filtered service water and demineralised boiler make-up.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 clarifier, filters, 1 RO train, 1 mixed bed
equipment.type_selected: Lamella or solids-contact clarifier; multimedia pressure filters; RO (2-pass or 1-pass + mixed bed); mixed-bed ion exchange polishers
equipment.why_this_type: Low chemical consumption, reliable high-purity water for 63-65 bar boilers.
key_dimensions: Clarifier ~12-15 m dia; filters 4 x ~3 m dia; RO 2 x ~100 m3/h permeate on skids ~12 m x 3 m; mixed beds 2 x ~2.5 m dia; demin tanks 2 x ~1,500 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Coagulant and flocculant agglomerate the suspended solids, which settle in the clarifier. The water is then filtered. High-pressure membranes (RO) reject ~98-99% of dissolved salts, and mixed-bed resins remove the remaining ions by exchange for H+ and OH-.
details_to_model: Clarifier with rake bridge, filter vessels with face piping, RO skids with pressure vessels (white FRP tubes) and HP pumps, mixed-bed vessels with sight glasses, chemical day tanks (HCl/ NaOH for regeneration), neutralisation pit
hazards_and_safety: Regeneration acid and caustic: segregation, showers
Chlorine/ biocide handling
instrumentation_and_control: Conductivity, silica analyser, pH, turbidity, SDI
equipment.materials: FRP/ SS/ rubber-lined CS
common_problems: Membrane fouling
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch the RO differential pressure and normalised permeate flow
sources: Engineering estimate; standard industrial water treatment practice

equipment.name: Firewater storage and fire pumps
equipment.function: Provide dedicated firewater for the refinery hydrant/ deluge network.
equipment.qty_operating: 2 tanks, 1 electric + 1 diesel main pump, 1 jockey
equipment.type_selected: API 650 tanks with reserved volume; horizontal split-case (BB1) fire pumps listed to NFPA 20; jockey pump
equipment.why_this_type: Code compliance; diesel independence from power loss.
key_dimensions: Tanks 2 x ~2,500 m3; pumps ~500-700 m3/h at ~10-12 bar (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A jockey pump keeps the ring main pressurised. A pressure drop (hydrant opened) automatically starts the electric pump, then the diesel pump.
details_to_model: Fire pump house with red-painted pumps, diesel engine with day tank and exhaust, controllers, test header outside, tanks with level gauges
hazards_and_safety: Diesel exhaust in pump house - ventilation
instrumentation_and_control: Pump controllers, ring pressure, tank level
equipment.materials: CS/ ductile iron
common_problems: Failed weekly run tests
operating_tips_and_key_points: Run the weekly churn test and the annual flow test
sources: NFPA 20 Installation of Stationary Pumps for Fire Protection

equipment.name: Cooling tower, cooling water pumps, side-stream filter and chemical dosing
equipment.function: Reject ~100-110 MW of low-grade heat from evaporator condensers, precipitation interstage coolers and machinery coolers.
equipment.type_selected: Multi-cell induced-draft counterflow cooling tower (FRP or concrete structure, film fill), horizontal split-case CW pumps (BB1) or vertical (VS1) in a pump pit
equipment.why_this_type: Counterflow film fill gives a compact plan for a given duty; the N+1 cell allows maintenance.
key_dimensions: 5 cells, each ~15 m x 15 m plan, fan deck ~12-14 m above basin, fan ~9-10 m dia with ~4 m velocity-recovery stack, ~150-200 kW per fan (engineering estimate)
Basin ~2 m deep with sump; CW pumps ~3,400 m3/h x 35-40 m, ~450 kW each; headers DN1,200-1,400
equipment.working_principle: Warm water is sprayed over fill packs and runs down as a thin film while fans draw air upwards. A small part of the water (~1.5% per 10 K) evaporates, which cools the rest. Drift eliminators catch droplets. The cooled water collects in the basin and is pumped back to users. Blowdown limits the dissolved-solids build-up, and chemicals control scale, corrosion and Legionella.
details_to_model: Row of 5 cells with fan stacks on top, gearboxes and drive shafts, motors outside the stacks, access stairs to fan deck, handrails
Hot-water distribution headers with spray nozzles, fill packs, drift eliminators (visible in cutaway), louvres at air inlets
Concrete basin with sump screens, CW pump pit or pump house, large-bore headers, side-stream sand filter, dosing skid with chemical totes and bund
Vibration switches on each fan; lightning protection
hazards_and_safety: Legionella aerosol: biocide programme, drift eliminators, testing
Fan rotating parts: LOTO; working at height on fan deck
Chemical handling (biocides, acid)
Caustic ingress from a leaking exchanger raises pH: detect and isolate
instrumentation_and_control: Basin level, supply/return temperature, pH, conductivity (blowdown control), ORP/ free chlorine, fan vibration trips, fan VSDs for temperature control
equipment.materials: FRP structure or concrete; PVC fill; SS 316 hardware
common_problems: Fill fouling (dust from bauxite/alumina)
Scaling at high cycles
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch the CW return pH; a jump above ~9 points to a caustic leak at a process exchanger
sources: CTI ATC-105 Acceptance Test Code for Water Cooling Towers

equipment.name: Air compressors, dryers and receivers
equipment.function: Supply oil-free plant air and dry instrument air.
equipment.type_selected: Oil-free integrally-geared 3-stage centrifugal compressors with intercoolers; heat-of-compression or blower-purge desiccant dryers; vertical receivers
equipment.why_this_type: Large steady demand, high efficiency, oil-free air for filter/ pneumatic conveying service.
key_dimensions: ~4,000 Nm3/h each at 8 barg; ~450-500 kW; package ~6 m x 3 m x 3 m (engineering estimate)
Receivers: plant 2 x ~50 m3; instrument 1 x ~30 m3
equipment.working_principle: Air is compressed in three high-speed impeller stages with water intercooling between them. Desiccant towers adsorb the moisture, and one tower regenerates while the other is on line. Receivers smooth demand peaks and give ride-through for instrument air on compressor trips.
details_to_model: Compressor packages with inlet filters/ silencers, blow-off valves, intercooler shells, control panels
Twin-tower dryers with switching valves, pre/after-filters
Large vertical receivers with PSV, drain traps, manway
Header piping painted blue, priority valve to instrument air
hazards_and_safety: Stored pressure energy: PSVs, pressure-vessel inspection
Noise; hot surfaces
instrumentation_and_control: Master sequencer; header pressure; dew point analyser
equipment.materials: Vendor standard; receivers CS
common_problems: Inlet filter clogging from dust
Dryer valve failures
operating_tips_and_key_points: Find and fix leaks; they typically waste 10-20% of compressed air

equipment.name: Quicklime unloading and storage silos
equipment.function: Receive bulk quicklime by pneumatic tanker and store ~12 days.
equipment.type_selected: Steel silos on skirt/ concrete base with conical hopper, bin-vent filters, aeration, rotary valves and screw/ weigh feeders
equipment.why_this_type: Standard dry-bulk storage that keeps the quicklime dry and controls dust.
key_dimensions: ~1,500 t each; ~12 m dia x ~16-18 m cylinder + 60 deg cone; top ~28-32 m above grade (engineering estimate; bulk density ~0.9-1.1 t/m3)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate: 40 kg CaO/t at ~90% available CaO

equipment.working_principle: Tankers blow lime through a fill pipe to the silo roof. The conveying air leaves through a pulse-jet bin-vent filter. Aeration pads help the lime flow from the cone to a rotary valve and screw feeder, and the screw feeds the slaker by weight.
details_to_model: Tall silos with roof railing, bin-vent filter, pressure-vacuum relief valve, radar level, high-level switch, fill pipes down the side to a tanker connection with hose coupling and earthing
Skirt with access door, discharge gate, rotary valve, screw feeder, weigh feeder
Stair tower to roof, tanker bay with wheel stops
hazards_and_safety: Quicklime is corrosive to eyes/skin and reacts exothermically with water: dust masks, goggles, eyewash
Silo overpressure during filling (relief valve, high-level trip)
Entry into silo strictly prohibited without engulfment controls
instrumentation_and_control: Level radar, HH switch, filter DP, weigh feeder
equipment.materials: CS
common_problems: Bridging/ rat-holing; moisture ingress causes hardening
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the lime dry; never hose down near the silo bases
sources: National Lime Association - 'Lime: Handling, Application and Storage' (bulletin) - verify

equipment.name: Lime slakers with grit removal and vapour scrubber
equipment.function: Hydrate quicklime with hot water to a reactive Ca(OH)2 slurry and remove grit.
equipment.type_selected: Detention (slurry) slaker with agitated slaking chamber and grit screw (alternative: paste slaker, or vertical ball-mill slaking for higher reactivity)
equipment.why_this_type: Robust and gives a consistent 15-20% slurry. Slaking temperature control (~75-85 degC) gives fine, reactive hydrate particles, which matters for causticisation efficiency.
key_dimensions: ~12-15 t/h CaO each; slaking chamber ~25-35 m3 (~3.5 m dia x 3 m) with ~30-45 kW agitator; grit classifier screw ~6 m long; overall ~10 m x 4 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 releases ~1.14 MJ/kg CaO. Water flow is controlled to hold the slaking temperature: too cold gives coarse, low-reactivity hydrate, and too hot (boiling) 'drowns' the particles. Agitation breaks agglomerates. Overflow slurry passes a screen and the grit (unburnt stone, silica) is screwed out to a bin.
details_to_model: Box-shaped slaking tank with top agitator, lime inlet chute from feeder, water inlet with flowmeter/ control valve, thermowell
Inclined grit screw with motor, grit discharge chute to skip
Vapour hood and duct to wet scrubber with fan and stack
Discharge to slurry tank via screen box
hazards_and_safety: Exothermic reaction: steam/ hot slurry eruptions if water is added too fast; burns
Lime dust and slurry (pH ~12.5): eye injuries; eyewash essential
instrumentation_and_control: Slaking temperature control (water flow), lime feed rate, agitator current
equipment.materials: CS, wear liners
common_problems: Scaling in the water inlet; grit screw wear
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hold the slaking temperature steady; lime reactivity affects causticisation efficiency and filter-aid quality
sources: Lime supplier slaking guides (e.g., Lhoist/ Carmeuse technical bulletins) - verify
Whittington (1996) Hydrometallurgy 43:13-35 (lime reactivity in Bayer process)

equipment.name: Slaked lime slurry storage tank and lime ring main pumps
equipment.function: Store slaked lime slurry and circulate it continuously around a ring main to the users.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated CS tank; horizontal rubber-lined centrifugal slurry pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Continuous circulation at ~1.5-2.5 m/s prevents settling and scaling; users take off through control valves.
key_dimensions: ~600 m3 (~10 m dia x 8 m), agitator ~45-75 kW; pumps ~150-250 m3/h x 40-50 m; ring main DN125-200, ~1-2 km loop (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The agitator keeps the slurry suspended. Pumps circulate it through the ring and back to the tank; each user draws its dose through a magflow meter and control/pinch valve, and a back-pressure valve at the ring end keeps the ring full.
details_to_model: Tank with agitator bridge, level radar, ring main return nozzle
Pump set with knife-gate valves, flushing connections
Ring main on rack with flushing points, drain points at low spots, user take-off stations (magflow + pinch valve + flush)
hazards_and_safety: Alkaline slurry: eye protection
Line scale and blockages: flushing protocol
instrumentation_and_control: Ring pressure/flow, density meter, tank level
equipment.materials: CS; rubber-lined pumps
common_problems: Calcium carbonate scale in ring main
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never stop the ring; flush dead legs with water when a user is offline

areas.layout_notes: The power house (GTs, HRSGs, aux boilers, STG hall, deaerator bay, BFW pumps, condensate polishing) is in a block ~150 m x 100 m beside the steam load centre. It is ~150-300 m from digestion (A06) and evaporation (A18), so the large-bore MP/LP headers stay short on the main pipe rack. HRSG and boiler stacks (~40-50 m) are on the downwind side of the block. The main 132 kV substation sits next to the power house on the side away from the cooling towers, at least 100-150 m from the towers to avoid drift/ mist on insulators. The cooling tower (5 cells in a row, ~80 m x 18 m plus pump pit) lies between precipitation (A12) and evaporation (A18) to minimise CW header length, with the long axis perpendicular to the prevailing wind and >=30-50 m from buildings and air intakes. The compressor house is near the power house or centre of air demand (hydrate filtration A14, calcination/ pneumatic conveying A15/A16). The lime area (silos ~30 m tall, slakers, slurry tank) is in a ~50 m x 40 m compound beside the refinery access road and near causticisation (A19) and clarification (A08/A10), with a tanker turning circle. The raw water pond and water treatment plant are at a site high point or edge, with firewater tanks and the fire pump house nearby. The gas receiving station is at the site boundary near the pipeline entry and >=50-100 m from ignition sources, with a gas pipeline to the power house and calciners on the rack. Diesel storage is next to the EDGs and the mobile-equipment refuelling bay. A main E-W pipe rack spine (~1.2-1.5 km) and N-S branches (2-4 tiers, +6 to +15 m) carry steam, condensate, CW, air, lime and gas to all areas.
interfaces: A06 Digestion: MP steam ~150 t/h at 10-12 barg; clean condensate return; BFW for desuperheating
A05 Pre-desilication: LP steam ~25-40 t/h (direct injection, not returned)
A18 Evaporation: LP steam ~100 t/h; clean condensate return ~100 t/h; CW ~5,000 m3/h
A19 Liquor purification: lime slurry ~45-60 m3/h; LP steam ~20-30 t/h; natural gas to LBF kiln/RTO; CW to oxalate coolers
A12 Precipitation: CW to interstage coolers (~30-40 MW); essential power for agitators
A15 Calcination: natural gas ~720-780 GJ/h (~2.9-3.2 GJ/t); compressed air; power
A10 Security filtration: lime for TCA filter aid
A08/A09 Residue: lime for neutralisation (if required); cooling tower blowdown; RSA return water to raw/ process water
A01/A02/A17 Mine, overland conveyor and port: 33 kV power feeders (~6-10 MW); conveyor regenerative power returned
A17 Port: imported quicklime/ caustic logistics (with A19)
All areas: instrument air, plant air, potable and firewater, 11/6.6/0.415 kV power, DCS/ SCADA

Mine (A01) on a bauxite plateau ~20 km from the refinery, linked by a 2-flight overland conveyor (A02). Refinery core ~1.6 km x 1.0 km (~150-180 ha) laid out along the process flow. Upwind/entry end: administration, central control room, laboratory, workshops, stores. Stockyard (A03, ~550 m x 130 m) at one end -> grinding (A04) -> pre-desilication (A05) -> digestion (A06) and flash (A07), the central 'hot' block -> settling and washing (A08, thickeners ~40-50 m dia) -> residue filtration (A09) at the edge facing the residue storage area (RSA). From A08 the liquor goes to security filtration (A10) -> heat interchange (A11) -> precipitation tank farm (A12, the tallest tanks, ~300-400 m long) -> classification and seed (A13) -> hydrate filtration (A14) -> calcination (A15, downwind end) -> product silos and rail/ conveyor load-out (A16) -> port (A17). Evaporation (A18) lies between A12 and A06. Liquor purification (A19): causticisation next to A08, the oxalate plant between A18 and A13, the LBF downwind. Utilities (A20): power house next to A06/A18, cooling towers between A12 and A18, lime compound near A08/A19, substation upwind of the cooling towers, raw-water pond and gas station at the boundary. Main E-W pipe rack spine ~1.2-1.5 km with N-S branches.

open_questions: SOURCING LIMITATION: WebSearch was blocked in this run (HTTP 403 'feature not enabled for your organization') and direct downloads were refused by the proxy (e.g., EU NFM BREF PDF). Only a few Wikipedia pages and a US DOE PDF could be fetched. All other citations (Light Metals, Hydrometallurgy, NACE, ASME, NFPA, ISO, licensor patents) are from domain knowledge and are marked 'verify' where uncertain. SME review must check them before use.

Residue mass conflict: my balance gives ~1.1-1.3 t dry residue/t Al2O3 (~280-300 t/h), but the A04-A07 draft states ~400-430 t/h (1.65-1.8 t/t). The difference is probably the ~136 t/h of gibbsite combined water released in digestion. The A08/A09 authors need one reconciled figure for thickener and filter sizing.

Steam intensity: I set ~1.7 t/t (410 t/h) using the A06 draft's comparatively low live-steam demand (~0.55-0.7 t/t with double-stream slurry plus liquor heaters). If the SME prefers direct live-steam slurry heating, digestion steam rises (and its condensate is lost to the liquor). Total steam would then be ~2.0-2.5 t/t, with a larger evaporation duty and larger boilers.

Steam/power plant concept: natural-gas cogeneration (2 GT + HRSG + aux boilers + back-pressure STG) was chosen as the generic design. Indian East Coast refineries typically use coal-fired CFBC captive power plants. The owner should confirm the fuel because it changes the A20 3-D model substantially (coal yard, ash handling, ESPs, tall stack).

Causticisation: the improved two-stage (hydrocalumite) scheme is based on Alcoa-published concepts. Reactor temperatures and residences are engineering estimates and must be checked against licensor or literature data. Also confirm whether the causticised slurry returns to the washer train (selected) or goes to a dedicated thickener/ filter.

Organics removal technology: a rotary-kiln liquor burner with RTO was selected as the generic option. Confirm against SME knowledge of real practice (fluid-bed versus kiln liquor burners at Kwinana/ Wagerup, wet oxidation, biological oxalate destruction at Worsley). For low-organic East Coast India bauxite the LBF may be omitted, using oxalate removal plus lime destruction only.

Evaporator configuration: 2 trains x 6-effect falling film with backward feed and 4 product flash stages, ~210 t/h water each. Confirm against a vendor reference (e.g., GEA/ Andritz/ HRS-type Bayer FFE). Also confirm the number of effects (5-7), feed sequence (backward versus mixed), surface versus barometric condensers, and whether a salting evaporator (carbonate/sulfate removal) is needed.
Caustic consumption (75 kg NaOH/t) and lime (40 kg CaO/t) are estimates for 2% reactive silica. Both scale with the project bauxite assays and the desilication/ causticisation efficiency.
Port distance and alumina transport mode (rail versus conveyor) are assumed (~30-60 km rail). A16/A17 authors to confirm. This also sets caustic and quicklime logistics.
Climate basis (design wet bulb ~27-28 degC, monsoon) affects cooling tower size, evaporator vacuum and condenser area. Confirm the site meteorology basis for the generic plant.
Electricity intensity (~230 kWh/t) is above the ~150 kWh/t average cited on Wikipedia. Verify with SME/ benchmark data (it depends on grinding, filtration type and calciner fans).

findings.tag: plantwide 'Residue (dry) leaving digestion'; A06/A07 digested-slurry streams
findings.issue: The residue tonnage contradicts itself across areas. A04-A07 give ~400-430 t/h dry residue (1.65-1.8 t/t) and '~140 t/h residue solids per unit'. A08/A09 size on 265 t/h (1.1 t/t), and A20 gives ~290 t/h. The A04-A07 figure was worked out as 640 - 256 + DSP, which never subtracts the ~136 t/h of gibbsite combined water (Al2O3·3H2O) that leaves in solution or as vapour. Thickeners, washers, filter presses, the RSA and the settler feed solids load all depend on this number.
findings.correction: Use one residue basis everywhere: ~265-290 t/h dry (1.10-1.20 t/t Al2O3) at 640 t/h dry bauxite, with design ~290 t/h (equipment margin to ~320 t/h). Per digestion unit this is ~90-100 t/h, not ~140 t/h. Delete '400-430 t/h (1.65-1.8 t/t)' from the A04-A07 plantwide table and from the A06/A07 stream compositions.
findings.evidence: Component balance on 640 t/h dry: Fe2O3 ~20% = 128; TiO2 ~2% = 13; total SiO2 ~3.5% = 22; unextracted Al2O3 (total 46.5% minus 40% available) = 42; non-gibbsite LOI (goethite and kaolinite water) ~4% = 26; other ~6. Inert residue is ~237 t/h. Adding DSP Na2O plus anion (~12), causticisation CaCO3 (~8) and TCA/lime solids and minor gibbsite losses (~5-10) gives ~265-290 t/h. The A01 LOI cross-check (24-26%) agrees: 40% x 54/102 = 21.2% gibbsite water. The world average is ~1.0-1.5 t/t, ~1.2 typical (IAI 2015; Evans 2016), and high-grade gibbsitic ore sits at the low end.

findings.issue: There are two inconsistent spent-liquor systems. A11 collects ALL spent liquor (~3,100-3,400 m3/h) in 11-TK-001, heats it in the PL/spent PHEs to 82-90 degC and sends it to evaporation and digestion. A18 then receives spent liquor 'from A12/A13 at 55-65 degC' (~3,050 m3/h) in its own feed tanks 18-TK-001/002, and splits it 1,700 m3/h to evaporation and 1,350 m3/h to bypass. The same liquor is counted twice, the temperatures disagree by ~25 K, and the regenerative heat A11 recovers (~95-110 MW) has nowhere to go if A18 takes cold liquor. Feeding 82-90 degC liquor to effect 6 of a backward-feed evaporator running at ~60-65 degC would flash it on entry and waste most of that heat.
findings.correction: Fix the routing. Precipitation/classification overflow and filtrates go to 11-TK-001 (55-62 degC), then through the A11 interchangers to ~82-90 degC, then to an A18 evaporator feed/bypass split tank. Do NOT draw cold spent from A12/A13 into A18 as well. Then either (a) change the evaporator to mixed feed (hot spent liquor enters a mid-temperature effect, e.g. effect 3 or 4, at ~85 degC) or (b) take the evaporator feed upstream of A11 and accept that only the bypass stream (~1,350 m3/h) recovers PL heat, recomputing the A11 duty (~45-55 MW, or the PL cannot be cooled to 76-82 degC without a much larger trim cooler). Both drafts need one stated choice.
findings.evidence: Liquor and heat balance: 3,000 m3/h PL x 1.30 t/m3 x 3.25 kJ/kg.K x 26 K = ~92 MW, which needs ~3,200 m3/h of spent liquor on the cold side. A18 shows only 1,350 m3/h bypassing to digestion and a 55-65 degC evaporator feed, which is incompatible with the A11 duty.

findings.issue: The cooling-water system is undersized relative to the loads the other areas declare. A20 sets ~10,000 m3/h circulation and ~100-110 MW rejection, with only 30-40 MW for precipitation interstage cooling. The individual areas declare: A12 interstage 45-70 MW and 5,000-7,000 m3/h; A18 surface condensers 50-60 MW and ~5,000 m3/h; A11 trim coolers 5-25 MW and 500-1,500 m3/h; A19 oxalate coolers 8-14 MW; plus compressor, turbine and generator coolers and calciner FBC trim. That sums to ~120-180 MW and ~12,000-16,000 m3/h.
findings.correction: Size the cooling tower for ~150-180 MW at a 10 K range, i.e. ~13,000-16,000 m3/h circulating (e.g. 6+1 cells instead of 4+1). Raise make-up to ~250-350 m3/h, which moves the fresh-water figure toward ~2.5-3 m3/t. Correct the A20 precipitation interstage duty to 45-70 MW so it matches A12.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic sum of the duties stated in the A11, A12, A18 and A19 drafts. Precipitation exotherm check: ~240 t/h Al2O3 precipitated x ~0.55-0.6 GJ/t heat of crystallisation is ~37-40 MW on its own, before the ~17 K sensible cooling of ~3,000 m3/h liquor plus seed (~55-60 MW) and before the heat lost from 30 uninsulated tanks.

findings.issue: The digestion heat balance leaves out the endothermic heat of gibbsite dissolution. Al(OH)3 + OH- -> Al(OH)4- absorbs roughly 25-30 kJ/mol Al(OH)3, ~0.5-0.6 GJ/t Al2O3 extracted. For 256 t/h extracted that is ~35-40 MW for the plant (~12-14 MW per unit). It shows up as a temperature drop of ~8-10 K across the digester train unless the mixed feed is heated above the holding temperature. The live-steam estimate (~23-28 MW per unit, 0.55-0.7 t/t) appears to cover only sensible heating to 145 degC. A12, by contrast, correctly treats the reverse reaction (precipitation) as exothermic.
findings.correction: Add the dissolution endotherm to the A06 heat balance. Either heat the combined feed to ~150-155 degC so the digester exit is ~143-145 degC, or add live-steam trim at digester 1-2. Raise live steam to ~0.75-0.9 t/t Al2O3 (~180-215 t/h MP steam for the plant, ~60-70 t/h per unit) and carry this into the A20 MP header and boiler sizing (total process steam ~1.85-2.0 t/t). Confirm against a licensed heat and mass balance model.
findings.evidence: Heat of gibbsite precipitation/dissolution in Bayer liquor is ~-25 to -30 kJ/mol Al(OH)3 (Misra & White kinetic work; Wefers & Misra, Alcoa TP-19; Rosenberg & Healy 1996 thermodynamic model). The value should be verified, because web verification was not available in this review. Mass basis: 256 t/h Al2O3 = 5,020 kmol/h Al(OH)3 x ~27 kJ/mol = ~136 GJ/h = ~38 MW.

findings.issue: The DSP alumina loss is misleading and double counted. A05 says each tonne of reactive SiO2 'locks up ~0.85 t Al2O3' and puts the loss at ~11 t/h Al2O3. Kaolinite (Al2O3·2SiO2·2H2O) and sodalite DSP (Na2O·Al2O3·2SiO2 basis) have the same Al:Si ratio of 1:1. The alumina that ends up in DSP is therefore essentially the kaolinite's own alumina, which is already excluded from available alumina. The real penalty of reactive silica is soda loss (~0.6-0.7 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2), plus a small alumina loss only if DSP Al:Si exceeds the kaolinite ratio. Counting 11 t/h as an extra loss against the 256 t/h available extraction distorts the recovery and bauxite-factor reasoning.
findings.correction: Rewrite as: 'Reactive silica is precipitated as DSP, removing ~0.6-0.7 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2 (~37 kg Na2O/t Al2O3 at 2% reactive SiO2). Because kaolinite and DSP have the same Al:Si ratio, the alumina in DSP is the kaolinite's own alumina and is not part of available alumina (the laboratory available-alumina assay is net of DSP). Net alumina loss to DSP relative to available alumina is therefore small.' State explicitly that the 40% available Al2O3 basis is the NET low-temperature extractable figure.
findings.evidence: Stoichiometry: kaolinite Al2Si2O5(OH)4 gives Al2O3:SiO2 = 1:2 molar. Sodalite Na8[Al6Si6O24]X2 also gives Al2O3:SiO2 = 1:2 molar (0.85 t Al2O3 per t SiO2 in both). Standard available alumina / reactive silica assay practice (Authier-Martin et al. 2001, JOM) and Smith 2009 (Hydrometallurgy 98:162-176) both treat reactive silica primarily as a caustic-loss driver.

findings.issue: The dilution and caustic numbers do not close. Digester exit C is 250-265 g/L (A06). Diluting ~2,900 m3/h of it with 550-750 m3/h of W1 overflow at 80-140 g/L (A08) gives a PL C of ~225-240 g/L, but A08, A11 and A12 all state 240-255 g/L. A19 also states the W1 overflow is 130-170 g/L, which contradicts A08's 80-140 g/L. Precipitation yield and A/C targets depend on C.
findings.correction: Adopt one consistent set, for example: digestion liquor C 280-290 g/L; digester exit ~265-270 g/L (after bauxite moisture and direct-steam dilution); W1 overflow ~400-500 m3/h at ~130-160 g/L as Na2CO3; PL ~240-250 g/L. Alternatively keep 550-750 m3/h of W1 overflow and lower the PL design C to ~230-240 g/L, which gives a yield of ~76-79 g/L at dA/C 0.33. Make A08 and A19 state the same W1 overflow concentration.
findings.evidence: Mixing balance: (2,900 x 258 + 650 x 110)/3,550 = ~231 g/L. Caustic conservation from digestion liquor (2,750 m3/h x 280 g/L) to PL (3,100 m3/h) gives ~248 g/L only if dilution volume plus water added is ~350 m3/h.

findings.issue: The grinding slurry volumes are inconsistent. A04 adds 440-470 m3/h of mill liquor plus 160-250 m3/h of dilution liquor (600-720 m3/h total), yet claims a 44-48% solids product at ~830 m3/h. At 640 t/h dry bauxite plus 71 t/h moisture, 44-48% solids allows only ~480-560 m3/h of spent liquor. A06 and A18 carry '~600 m3/h liquor with slurry'. 600-720 m3/h of liquor would give ~40-42% solids and ~920-1,000 m3/h of slurry.
findings.correction: Set the total spent liquor to grinding at ~500-550 m3/h (mill ~380-420 m3/h plus pump-box/spray dilution ~120-150 m3/h), giving ~46% solids, SG ~1.70 and ~820-840 m3/h of slurry. Reduce the digestion liquor via the liquor heaters correspondingly (or raise it) so total digestion liquor stays at ~2,700-2,750 m3/h, and update the A18 interface figure (mill liquor ~520 m3/h, not ~600).
findings.evidence: Liquid mass at 46% solids = 640 x 0.54/0.46 = 751 t/h. Minus 71 t/h moisture = 680 t/h spent liquor / 1.31 t/m3 = ~520 m3/h. Slurry volume = 640/2.8 + 71 + 520 = ~820 m3/h.

findings.issue: The lime figure for TCA filter aid differs threefold. A10 states 0.5-2 kg CaO/t Al2O3 (0.1-0.5 t/h), while A20 allocates ~6 kg CaO/t (~1.45 t/h) to TCA in its 40 kg/t total. The A17 (15-40 kg/t, 30-80 kt/yr) and A20 (40 kg/t, ~89 kt/yr quicklime) totals also differ.
findings.correction: Adopt TCA filter-aid lime of ~2-5 kg CaO/t Al2O3 (~0.5-1.2 t/h CaO) in both A10 and A20, causticisation ~25-30 kg/t (A19: 6-7 t/h CaO), and a plant total of ~30-40 kg CaO/t (~65-90 kt/yr quicklime). Make A17 quote the same figure.
findings.evidence: Internal consistency check. Precoat 0.3-0.8 kg/m2 on ~4,000 m2 of filter area every 4-12 h plus 50-150 mg/L body feed on 3,200 m3/h is ~0.2-0.5 t/h TCA, i.e. ~0.15-0.35 t/h CaO equivalent, which supports A10's lower range. A20's 6 kg/t should then be reduced or justified.

findings.issue: The PL temperature chain is not consistent. A11 takes PL in at 100-106 degC, but A08 settler overflow is 98-104 degC and A10 filtered liquor is 95-102 degC (after a 20-40 min tank and Kelly filters). PL cannot gain temperature through clarification and filtration.
findings.correction: Set the A11 PL inlet to ~95-100 degC (design 98). The A11 PHE outlet then reaches 76-82 degC with a smaller duty (~80-95 MW). Re-check the trim cooler duty for a 72-78 degC fill.
findings.evidence: Heat losses only from blow-off (103-108) through dilution with 95-100 degC W1 overflow, settlers, tank and filters.

findings.issue: The stated residence time ignores the seed slurry volume. Growth slurry flow is the PL (~3,000-3,300 m3/h) plus coarse seed slurry (~1,500-2,200 m3/h) plus fine seed (~150-300 m3/h), about 4,000-4,800 m3/h. Through 22 operating growth tanks of ~4,500 m3 (~99,000 m3) that gives ~21-25 h, not 25-30 h. The total is ~28-32 h, not 32-38 h.
findings.correction: Either state growth residence as ~21-25 h and total as ~28-32 h, or add ~4-6 growth tanks (or enlarge tanks to ~5,500-6,000 m3) to achieve the claimed 25-30 h. Confirm that spent A/C 0.36-0.38 is achievable at the chosen residence time and end temperature with a precipitation model.

findings.tag: plantwide bauxite factor and feed rate
findings.issue: The areas use different bauxite factors and feed rates: A01 2.7 t/t (650 t/h dry, 720 wet in A03); A04/A20 2.65 (640/711); A10 2.5-2.6 (600-630 t/h dry). The Darling Range comparison also varies: 3.2-3.8 (A01), 3-3.5 (A14), 3.5-4+ (A17), 3-4 (A10). Grinding is also inconsistent: A03 crushes to -40 mm with 3 bins (3 lines), while A04 assumes -25 mm with 4 bins (3+1 lines).
findings.correction: Freeze one plant basis: 2.65 t dry bauxite/t SGA (net available Al2O3 40%, ~94-95% overall recovery), 640 t/h dry and 711 t/h wet (10% moisture). Quote Darling Range as roughly 3.5-4 t dry/t, marked 'verify, ore and recovery dependent'. Align the A03 crushed top size and bin count with the A04 mill selection (-25 mm, 3+1 bins, or revise A04).
findings.evidence: Check: 1/(0.40 x 0.945) = 2.65. For comparison, NALCO Damanjodi mines ~6.3 Mt/yr for ~2.1 Mt/yr alumina, ~3.0 t/t as-mined (wet), which is consistent with ~2.65-2.7 dry.

findings.issue: The reference configuration is not representative of low-temperature practice. Slurry heaters with PD feed pumps are mainly high-temperature (boehmitic) practice. Low-temperature gibbsitic refineries typically use 'double-stream' digestion in which only the spent liquor is regeneratively heated in shell-and-tube heaters, while the slurry (after pre-desilication) is heated by direct live-steam injection or mixing, using centrifugal pumps only. This avoids kaolinite/DSP fouling of slurry heater tubes (1-4 week descaling cycles in the draft). The draft flags this as an open question but presents slurry heaters as the base case.
findings.correction: For a representative low-temperature reference plant, make the base case liquor-only regenerative heating (6 flash stages to 6 liquor heaters plus live-steam liquor heaters), with slurry pumped by centrifugal pumps and heated by live-steam injection or by mixing with the superheated liquor in digester 1. Keep slurry heaters and PD pumps as an option. Redo the flash-vapour/heater duty split, because the liquor heaters must then absorb all ~45-48 MW of flash vapour per unit, and the live-steam demand rises.
findings.evidence: Published flowsheets of low-temperature Darling Range-type refineries (e.g. Adamson, Bloore & Carr 1963; Hudson et al., Ullmann's) versus high-temperature tube/slurry-heater plants (QAL, European plants). Heat check: flash vapour available is ~78 t/h per unit (~47 MW), and liquor heating from 95 to 128 degC needs ~28 MW.

findings.issue: The sand design basis does not match either reference ore. 10-15% of residue as sand is high for India East Coast khondalite bauxite (low quartz, typically a few % sand) and far too low for Darling Range ore (~40-50% sand). The design ore is the India East Coast type.
findings.correction: For the India East Coast design ore, set sand at ~3-8% of residue (~10-25 t/h) with a 45 t/h design maximum, and state that Darling Range ore would need a sand circuit roughly 5-10 times larger.
findings.evidence: Ore mineralogy: Darling Range residue is reported as roughly half sand (quartz-rich), while East Coast khondalite bauxite has low total SiO2 (2-5%).

findings.issue: The A11 wording 'Cooling below the dew point of the regenerative exchangers' is technically wrong; this is not a dew point.
findings.correction: Replace with: 'Cooling below the temperature achievable against spent liquor (approach limit of the regenerative PHEs) is done in a cooling-water trim cooler.'
findings.evidence: Terminology; dew point refers to vapour condensation, which does not occur in liquor/liquor exchange.

findings.issue: The draft does not mention the boehmite content of gibbsitic ores (typically ~1-5% in Darling Range and some East Coast ores). At 145 degC this boehmite is largely not extracted, and undissolved boehmite can seed boehmite reversion in the flash train and settlers when the liquor is supersaturated, causing alumina loss. Neither A06 nor A08 mentions it.
findings.correction: Add: 'Boehmite present in gibbsitic ore (~1-5%) is largely unextracted at 145 degC and reports to residue (counted in total but not in available Al2O3). Undissolved boehmite can seed boehmite reversion between digestion and the settlers, so residence time from blow-off to settler overflow is kept short.' Include the boehmite figure in the ore specification.
findings.evidence: Standard low-temperature Bayer practice and known boehmite reversion losses at gibbsitic refineries (Light Metals literature).

findings.issue: The digester design temperature (~175 degC) is lower than the temperature the contents can reach at relief conditions. Digester 1 takes direct MP steam at 10-12 barg (saturation ~184-192 degC) through 06-SI. The 06-HX-301..306 live-steam heaters can also push liquor toward ~185 degC. With a blocked outlet and steam still on, the vessel heats until the PSV lifts at 9 barg plus accumulation. Liquor at ~10-11 bar(a), with BPE of ~6 K, boils at ~186-190 degC. That exceeds the design temperature, which sets the allowable stress (UG-23 / ASME II-D) and the PWHT/SCC envelope.
findings.correction: Set digester design conditions to about 9-10 barg at 200 degC, or at least 195 degC (MDMT to site minimum), and confirm wall thickness at that temperature. SA-516-70 allowable stress is essentially unchanged to about 200 degC, so thickness stays about 24-26 mm including 6 mm CA. Size the PSVs per API 521 for the blocked-outlet case with full steam to 06-SI plus heater steam. Interlock 06-SI and the live-steam heater steam valves on high digester pressure and temperature as a SIL-rated SIS function.
findings.evidence: ASME BPVC VIII-1 UG-20: design temperature must not be less than the mean metal temperature expected at the coincident pressure. The steam saturation temperature at 11 barg is ~187 degC (IAPWS-IF97). The draft gives MP steam at 10-12 barg (A06/A20).

findings.issue: Flash tank 1 has a design pressure of ~6 barg, but the digesters upstream operate at up to 6.5 barg (design 9 barg). If the digester let-down valve fails open or is bypassed, FT1 sees digester pressure plus a two-phase flashing flow. The draft lists a PSV on each flash tank but sets no relief case. Gas/vapour blow-by through a wide-open valve with the digester inventory flashing is normally the governing case, and it is large.
findings.correction: Either (a) rate FT1 for the same design pressure as the digesters (~9-10 barg and FV), or (b) keep 6 barg and size the FT1 PSV per API 520/521 for the 'control valve failed open' two-phase case (DIERS/HEM method), discharging to 06-TK-201. Option (a) is usually cheaper. Also state the hydrotest at 1.3 x MAWP (UG-99) and include PSV inlet/outlet lines and the relief header in the 3-D model.
findings.evidence: API 521 Section 4.4.8 (control valve failure) and 4.4.14 (gas blow-by). Draft values: digester operating 4.5-6.5 barg (A06) vs FT1 design ~6 barg (A07).

findings.issue: Residue tonnage is inconsistent across areas. A06 gives ~140 t/h per unit (400-430 t/h, 1.65-1.8 t/t). A08/A09 give 265 t/h (1.1 t/t). A20 gives 280-300 t/h. The A06 figure does not remove the ~136 t/h of gibbsite combined water that leaves as liquor water: 256 t/h Al2O3 x 54/102. Thickeners, washer pumps, filter presses, the RSA fleet and RSA volume all scale on this number.
findings.correction: Use a single design residue of ~1.15-1.2 t dry residue per t Al2O3, i.e. ~280-290 t/h at 241 t/h Al2O3. Basis: 640 t/h dry bauxite - 256 Al2O3 extracted - ~140 combined water + ~9 Na2O to DSP + ~10-15 lime-derived solids. Size A08-A09 for ~300-320 t/h design (110%). Correct the A06 stream to '~93-97 t/h residue per unit'.
findings.evidence: Stoichiometry of Al2O3.3H2O (156/102). The draft A20 note already identifies this error. World residue average ~1-1.5 t/t (Evans 2016, cited in the A09 draft).

findings.issue: The HRSG steam rating is not achievable with the stated firing. With GT exhaust of 80-100 kg/s and duct firing to ~800-850 degC, a single-pressure HRSG at 64 bar(a)/475 degC with ~140 degC stack temperature can raise only ~85-100 t/h. Example: 90 kg/s x 1.15 kJ/kgK x (850-140) K = ~73 MW, divided by ~2,850 kJ/kg = ~92 t/h. Reaching 150 t/h would need an HRSG inlet of ~1,250-1,300 degC, which requires a fully fired, water-wall furnace HRSG, not duct burners. Installed capacity is therefore about 2 x 95 + 2 x 150 = ~490 t/h. With N+1 (loss of one 150 t/h boiler) only ~340 t/h is available, against a demand of 410-440 t/h.
findings.correction: Rate the HRSGs at ~90-100 t/h each with supplementary firing to ≤850-900 degC. Then (a) add a third auxiliary boiler, or (b) uprate the auxiliary boilers to ~2 x 200 t/h (field-erected), so the N-1 steam capacity is ≥ ~440-460 t/h. Remove the '150 t/h fired' figure.
findings.evidence: HRSG heat balance (cp exhaust ~1.1-1.15 kJ/kgK). Unlined duct burners are typically limited to ~870-950 degC liner/duct temperature (vendor practice for Coen/John Zink duct burners). Steam enthalpy rise feedwater→64 bar/475 degC is ~2,850 kJ/kg (IAPWS-IF97).

findings.issue: The mill feed bins and weigh feeders are specified twice, and the two versions conflict.
