Present the truck at the best swing angle (~45-70 degrees) and double-side load where possible.

equipment.name: Large wheel loaders
equipment.function: Flexible loading at small faces, rehandle and blending from ROM-pad fingers into the dump hopper, cleanup, stockpile management, excavator cover.
equipment.type_selected: ~95-100 t class wheel loader (Caterpillar 992 class / Komatsu WA900 class), rock bucket ~10-12 m3
equipment.why_this_type: Highly mobile between faces and the ROM pad, and able to blend grade-bin fingers directly into the hopper.
equipment.alternatives: Additional excavator (less mobile); integrated tool carriers for small tasks.

Tyres: 50/65R51 for the 992 class (~3.4 m diameter) or 45/65R45 for the WA900/990 class (~3.0 m); model the tyre to the chosen machine (OEM spec sheets, verify)

The machine charges the pile, crowds, reverses and turns to load the truck or hopper. On the ROM pad it takes bucket loads from different grade-bin fingers in a set ratio to make a blended feed.
details_to_model: Articulated frame with centre hinge; large rock bucket with segment edges
Cab with front access stairs, platform handrails, rear-view cameras
Rock tyres (optional tyre chains), mud guards
Payload weighing display, beacon, lights, fire suppression

Reversing: cameras, radar, proximity detection
Tyre explosion and tyre handling: exclusion zones, nitrogen inflation

equipment.name: Rear-dump haul trucks (~90-t class)
equipment.function: Haul ore to the primary sizer dump hopper or the ROM pad, and cap and waste to backfill or dumps.
equipment.type_selected: Mechanical-drive rigid rear-dump truck, ~90-98 t payload (Caterpillar 777 / Komatsu HD785 class)
equipment.why_this_type: Selective mining on several faces with moderate hauls (2-6 km) suits 90-t trucks, which match the 200-t excavators, keep haul-road width and cost moderate, and give fleet granularity. FLEET SIZING (revised): cycle ~27 min (load 3.5, haul 5 km loaded ~12, dump 1.5, return ~8.5, spot/queue 1.5) gives ~200 t/h nominal and ~165 t/h effective. At ~5,000-5,500 operating h/yr each truck moves ~0.85-0.9 Mt/yr. Ore 5.9 Mt/yr needs ~7 trucks; waste ~1.5 Mt/yr on shorter backfill hauls needs ~2. Total 9-10 operating, so 10 operating + 2 spare (engineering estimate).
equipment.alternatives: 136-t (CAT 785 class) trucks (fewer operators, wider roads, less selective); road trains on long public-standard haul roads; trolley-assist or battery-electric trucks for decarbonisation; autonomous haulage.
key_dimensions: Length ~10.5 m, width ~6.1-6.5 m, height (body down) ~5.0-5.2 m, height with body raised ~10 m (OEM class, approximate)
Tyres 27.00R49 (diameter ~2.7 m), so windrow/berm height >= ~1.4 m
Body heaped capacity ~60-65 m3 (liner plates, optional tailgate)

operating_parameters.basis: OEM rimpull curves (approximate); site speed limits apply
Engineering estimate: 2 x 12 h, 7 d/wk roster after availability, utilisation and monsoon losses (corrected from 6,000)

equipment.working_principle: A V-12 diesel drives the rear axle through a torque converter, an automatic planetary powershift transmission, a differential and planetary final drives. Oil-cooled multi-disc brakes and engine/retarder braking control speed on downgrades, which is critical on in-pit ramps and plateau haul roads. At the dump the body is raised by two multi-stage hoist cylinders and the load slides out over the tail. Payload monitoring (from strut pressures) and the FMS log every load (source, destination, tonnage) so ore quality can be reconciled with the refinery.
details_to_model: Rigid frame, 2 axles, 6 tyres (dual rear), front suspension struts
Dual-slope or flat-floor dump body with canopy (cab protector), body liner plates, rock ejectors between the rear duals
Two body hoist cylinders; body pivot pins at the rear of the frame
Left-side cab with diagonal stairway across the radiator front, platform handrails, ROPS/FOPS
Large front radiator grille; exhaust through the body (body heating) or a vertical stack
Fire-suppression bottles, auto-lube, mud flaps, large fleet numbers on body and cab, beacons, buggy-whip flag, rear cameras, proximity radar, GNSS/FMS antenna
Model loaded and empty states, and body-raised position at the hopper
hazards_and_safety: Collisions with light vehicles (blind spots up to ~10 m or more): segregation, buggy whips, CAS/proximity detection, positive radio communication
Runaway on grade: brake testing, retarder use, escape lanes and berms
Dump edges: windrows >= half wheel height; wheel stops at the hopper
Tyre fires and explosions: 300 m exclusion for heated tyres (OEM guidance); tyre handler only
Fatigue: fatigue monitoring systems, shift design
Dust: water carts, cab pressurisation

Thompson R.J. (2011/2015) Mine haul road design, construction & maintenance management (Univ. Pretoria course notes)
EMESRT Design Philosophies; ISO 3471 (ROPS), ISO 3449 (FOPS), ISO 3450 (braking)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Payload target 100% +-10%; avoid overloads (10/10/20 rule).
Maintain haul roads with graders and water carts; rolling resistance strongly affects cycle time and tyre life.
FMS assignment of ore sources is the first stage of blending.

equipment.name: Haul-road support: motor graders and water carts
equipment.function: Graders maintain haul-road profile, crossfall and windrows; water carts suppress haul-road dust and provide first-response fire water.
equipment.type_selected: ~16-ft blade motor grader (CAT 16M class, ~4.9 m blade); ~70-76 kL water cart on a 90-t truck chassis (CAT 777 class) with spray bars and water cannon
key_dimensions: Grader length ~11 m, blade 4.9 m (OEM class)
Water cart tank ~70-76 kL on a 777-class chassis (OEM class)
equipment.working_principle: The grader's mouldboard is set at an angle to cut out ruts and potholes and windrow loose material, restoring the crown or crossfall that drains water off the road. The water cart's engine-driven centrifugal pump discharges through rear spray heads (each controlled by the operator) and a front monitor cannon that also serves for fire fighting. Water binds the fines so wheel traffic does not raise dust. Over-watering makes roads slippery, so water is applied intermittently.
details_to_model: Grader: articulated frame, front axle and rear tandem axles, mouldboard with circle and drawbar, rear ripper, ROPS cab
Water cart: elliptical tank with baffles, top fill hatch with ladder and handrails, rear spray bar with 4-6 heads, front water cannon, side hose reel, pump housing
hazards_and_safety: Slippery roads from over-watering: intermittent sprays, never water ramps or intersections heavily
Grader working on an active haul road: radio calls, beacons

equipment.type_selected: Purpose-built mining support vehicles (engineering estimate of fleet)

Fuel truck: ~20-30 kL tank with hose reels and lube modules (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: Tracks (walks) between pits on haul roads at ~2-3 km/h; part-dismantled for long moves
operating_parameters.basis: 200-t excavator mass exceeds the low-loader rating (OEM class)

Fuel and lube trucks use fast-fill dry-break couplings. The tyre handler grips and rotates the ~3-t tyres. The low loader moves dozers and drill rigs between pits; the 200-t excavators walk.

MMU with product bins and hose reel, explosives placards
Fuel truck with hose reels, fast-fill nozzle, spill kit
Low loader carrying a dozer
hazards_and_safety: Interaction between light and heavy vehicles (highest fatality risk): segregation, CAS
Explosives transport and handling: licensed, placarded vehicles
Tyre handling: tyre handler only, exclusion zones

equipment.name: Bulk explosives precursor depot (MMU depot) and explosives magazine
equipment.function: Store bulk AN prill and emulsion precursor and garage, fill and wash the MMUs (01-ED-001). Store packaged explosives, boosters and electronic detonators separately (01-MZ-001).
equipment.type_selected: Licensed bulk depot with AN prill silos, emulsion (ANE) storage tanks, MMU loading gantry, wash bay with sump; separate earth-mounded magazines for high explosives and for detonators
equipment.why_this_type: About 0.8-1.5 kt/yr of bulk explosives for ~3.0-3.5 Mbcm/yr of blasting needs on-site bulk storage and MMU servicing. Separation distances are set by regulation.
key_dimensions: AN prill silos 2 x ~60-100 t (~6-8 m tall, cone bottom, on legs over the MMU loading lane) (engineering estimate)
Emulsion precursor tanks 2 x ~30-50 kL in a bund (engineering estimate)
MMU shed ~25 x 12 m; wash bay ~20 x 8 m with sediment/oil sump (engineering estimate)
Magazines: earth-mounded or bunded steel-container type; separation distances per the licence (site-specific)
equipment.working_principle: AN prill and emulsion precursor arrive by road tanker and bulk truck and are stored in silos and tanks. Precursor emulsion is not an explosive until it is sensitised (gassed) in the hole by the MMU. MMUs load at the gantry under gravity (prill) and by pump (emulsion), then drive to the pit. The magazine stores detonators and boosters apart from bulk products and from each other.
details_to_model: Silos on steel legs with loading spouts over the drive-through lane, top access ladder and handrails
Bunded emulsion tanks with pumps and hose to the gantry
MMU shed and wash bay; fence with placards, gatehouse, lightning protection masts
Magazine compound: separate earth-mounded magazines, security fence, CCTV, access road
hazards_and_safety: Explosion and fire: separation distances, no ignition sources, lightning protection, fire breaks
AN contamination with fuel or organics: housekeeping, segregated storage
Security: licensed access control

equipment.name: ROM pad with grade-bin stockpiles
equipment.function: Buffer between mining and sizing. Holds ore in grade bins (e.g. high/low reactive silica, high/low available alumina) for controlled blending by wheel loader into the dump hopper when trucks are not tipping directly. Also holds pre-monsoon buffer stock.
equipment.type_selected: Compacted laterite pad with 4-6 finger stockpiles beside the dump hopper ramp
key_dimensions: Pad area ~4-6 ha (engineering estimate)
Finger piles ~10-30 kt each, ~6-8 m high, end-tipped and dozer-trimmed (engineering estimate)
Total ROM buffer ~50-100 kt (~3-6 days of refinery feed) (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Trucks either tip directly into the hopper or end-tip on a designated finger according to the FMS-assigned grade bin. Each finger has a sign board showing its bin code and running grade. The loader blends from the fingers in a ratio set by the mine geologist so the sizer feed meets the reactive silica and available alumina targets.
details_to_model: Finger piles with coloured grade-bin signboards on posts
Bunded perimeter; drains to the sediment pond
Mobile lighting towers (4 x LED) for night work
Windrows along tipping edges
hazards_and_safety: Truck tipping at the pile edge: windrows, tip-and-push (no spotters)
Loader-truck interaction: traffic management plan, one-way loop

equipment.name: Truck dump station (2-sided dump hopper) with pedestal rock breaker
equipment.function: Receives ROM ore from 90-t trucks and presents it to the apron feeder. The rock breaker clears oversize and bridged boulders.
equipment.type_selected: Semi-mobile station: reinforced-concrete or MSE-wall ramps and tipping deck with a steel-lined, modular steel hopper; hydraulic pedestal-boom rock breaker
equipment.why_this_type: Two-sided tipping halves truck queueing. Relocatable (semi-mobile) steel modules allow the station to move as mining progresses across the plateau, every ~5-10 years.
equipment.alternatives: Fully mobile track-mounted in-pit sizer; fixed concrete station for long-life central locations.

Hopper top opening ~12 m long x 8-9 m wide; tipping-deck height above apron feeder ~8-10 m (engineering estimate)
Wheel stop (concrete kerb/bumper block) ~1.2-1.4 m high (>= ~half the 2.7 m tyre diameter) (engineering estimate per OEM guidance)
Rock breaker boom reach ~8-10 m, hammer ~1.5-2.5 t class (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: 400-500 HB abrasion-resistant steel, 25-40 mm (or rock-box ledges)

equipment.working_principle: Trucks reverse to the wheel stop and raise the body. The load slides into the hopper, whose sloping walls (>= ~50-60 degrees) direct ore onto the apron feeder. A level radar on the hopper switches green/red traffic lights for the drivers. If a large boulder bridges the feeder throat, the rock-breaker operator (in a cabin or by remote) lowers the hydraulic hammer to break it.
details_to_model: Concrete ramp and tipping deck with wheel stops on both sides; traffic lights and signage on the tipping deck
Hopper with AR-plate liners on bolted segments and rock-box ledges at the impact zone; no grizzly (the sizer accepts ROM)
Fog/spray dust-suppression ring around the hopper rim (~10-16 nozzles)
Rock breaker on a concrete pedestal at one corner: slew base, boom, stick, hydraulic hammer, power pack, operator cabin with a window over the hopper
Structural steel frame over the apron feeder; MCC/e-house, transformer, local control room
Handrails at all edges, stair towers, lighting masts, CCTV
hazards_and_safety: Truck reversing over the hopper edge: wheel stops, lighting, traffic lights
Engulfment or falls into the hopper: fixed grating barriers, no entry while live, confined-space and isolation permits for liner changes
Flying fragments from the rock breaker: exclusion zone, cabin guarding
Dust plumes on tipping: fogging sprays

equipment.name: Apron feeder (sizer feeder)
equipment.function: Withdraws ROM ore from the dump hopper at a controlled rate and delivers it into the primary sizer.
equipment.type_selected: Heavy-duty apron (pan) feeder with cast manganese-steel pans and VFD electric drive (or hydraulic drive)
equipment.why_this_type: Withstands the direct impact of 90-t truck loads and handles sticky, clay-rich bauxite by positive displacement, where vibrating feeders would blind.
equipment.alternatives: Belt feeder (only with smaller lump size); feeder-breaker (combined feeder and sizer for lower capacities).
key_dimensions: Pan width ~2.0-2.4 m, head-tail centres ~12-16 m, inclination 0-15 degrees (engineering estimate)
Overall height including skirts ~3 m
equipment.working_principle: Overlapping cast pans are bolted to two strands of heavy tractor-type chain running over sprockets. The head sprocket shaft is driven by a shaft-mounted planetary gearbox and VFD motor. The ore bed is carried forward at slow speed and drops off the head into the sizer; speed control sets the throughput. Impact rails and rollers under the loaded section carry the dump impact, and skirt plates along the hopper hold the bed. Spillage under the feeder is collected by a dribble conveyor.
details_to_model: Pans (~2.4 m wide) with flared side flights, two chain strands, ~10-14 carry rollers and impact rails
Head shaft with drive sprockets, torque arm, shaft-mounted gearbox and motor
Tail shaft with idler wheels and screw take-ups
Side skirts with replaceable liners; adjustable gate at the discharge
Dribble/spill conveyor beneath (small belt ~800 mm) with its own drive
Access platforms on both sides with removable guard panels
hazards_and_safety: Nip points at sprockets and rollers: fixed guarding, LOTO
Hang-ups and sudden release of material: never enter the hopper with material above
Heavy lifting of pans and chains: lifting beams and monorail
instrumentation_and_control: VFD speed control from the sizer power / hopper level loop
Zero-speed switch on the tail shaft
Hopper level radar driving the traffic lights
sources: FLSmidth / Metso apron feeder literature (class data)

equipment.name: Primary twin-shaft mineral sizer
equipment.function: Reduces blasted ROM bauxite (up to ~1.0-1.5 m, sticky, clay-bearing) to -200 mm for the 1,200 mm overland.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (ROM pad buffer; spare shaft assembly held)
equipment.type_selected: Twin-shaft toothed roll sizer, primary duty (MMD 1000-1300 series class, shaft centres ~1.0-1.3 m)
equipment.why_this_type: Gibbsitic bauxite is soft to medium strength, with sticky clays and high moisture. Sizers break by tension and shear, produce few fines and tolerate wet sticky feed because the teeth self-clean. They are low-profile, which suits relocatable stations, and handle high capacity. Gyratory and jaw crushers blind with clay and make the station larger.
equipment.alternatives: Feeder-breaker (lower capacity); double-roll toothed crusher; mobile jaw crusher for cap-rich feed.
key_dimensions: Overall length ~6-8 m, width ~3-4 m, height ~2-2.5 m excluding drives (engineering estimate)
Two shafts ~3-4 m long with tooth rings (~3 horn-type teeth per ring) (engineering estimate)
Drive trains on each side: motor + fluid coupling + right-angle gearbox, ~5-7 m long in total

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (consistent with the mine roster)

equipment.working_principle: Two parallel shafts carrying large teeth rotate slowly towards each other. Lumps are gripped by the teeth and broken in tension and shear (three-point loading) rather than compression. Material already smaller than the gap between the teeth and shafts falls straight through, so few fines are made. Product size is set by the shaft centre distance and the tooth profile. The scroll arrangement of the teeth moves oversize along the shafts, and counter-rotation self-cleans sticky clay. Each shaft has its own motor and fluid coupling, which slips under overload; tramp metal triggers a reverse-and-clear sequence.
details_to_model: Heavy fabricated box housing with removable top covers and side liner plates; feed opening matched to the apron feeder discharge
Two toothed shafts visible from the top: rings of replaceable, hardfaced tooth tips in a helical/scroll layout
Drive trains on each side: TEFC motor (~400 kW) on a base frame, guarded fluid coupling, right-angle helical-bevel gearbox, gear coupling to the shaft
Breaker comb and side combs; discharge chute below to sacrificial conveyor 01-CV-001
Overhead crane or monorail (~20-30 t) for shaft removal; lay-down area
Lubrication unit (grease/oil); RTDs on bearings
Dust extraction hood at the discharge
hazards_and_safety: Nip and crush at the shafts: full guarding, no entry without isolation and shaft locking
Ejected fragments: covers closed
Heavy lifts (shaft ~15-25 t): certified lifting plan
Noise and dust
instrumentation_and_control: Motor power/current, coupling temperature, bearing temperatures, vibration
Shaft speed sensors; overload trip with auto-reverse
Interlocks: sizer running before the apron feeder starts; downstream conveyors running before the sizer starts
common_problems: Tooth wear in abrasive ferricrete: hardfacing rebuild every few months
Clay packing in monsoon: shaft scrapers, reduced feed rate
sources: MMD Group sizer technical literature (twin-shaft sizer principle)

equipment.name: Sizer discharge (sacrificial) conveyor with self-cleaning tramp magnet and metal detector
equipment.function: Receives sized ore under the sizer, removes tramp steel and transfers ore to the field conveyor (A02).
equipment.type_selected: Heavy-duty troughed belt conveyor 1,400 mm with impact cradles under the loading zone; overband self-cleaning electromagnet; metal detector coil
key_dimensions: Length ~40-80 m, belt 1,400 mm, inclined ~10-15 degrees (engineering estimate)
Overband magnet frame ~2 m x 1.5 m, suspended ~400-600 mm above the burden (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (slow for the impact zone)

operating_parameters.value: Fabric EP 1000/4-5 ply, 10 mm top cover

equipment.working_principle: The short, slow 'sacrificial' belt absorbs the impact of sized ore and protects the expensive overland belt. An overband electromagnet with its own cross-belt lifts ferrous tramp (bucket teeth, drill steel, DTH bits) and discharges it into a tramp bin. A downstream metal detector catches non-magnetic and manganese-steel tramp and stops the belt or triggers a flop gate.

Overband magnet with self-cleaning belt and tramp chute to a skip bin

areas.layout_notes: Plateau-top deposit of ~10-20 km2 (life-of-mine reserves for ~30 years at ~5.9 Mt/yr). Mining proceeds in blocks of ~10-50 ha, irregular in plan, 10-30 m deep, on 5-8 m benches with 8% ramps. About 3 faces are active at any time for blending. Haul roads (22-25 m wide) radiate 2-6 km from a central semi-mobile primary sizing station at the plateau edge or centroid of ~5-10 years of reserves; the station is relocated about every 5-10 years. The ROM pad (4-6 ha) sits beside the dump-station ramp. Dump station: ramps rise ~8-10 m to the tipping deck on two sides (MSE walls); the sizer sits below with drives on both sides; MCC/e-house and transformer are ~20-30 m away. The mine infrastructure area (workshop, fuel farm, offices with mine control room, laboratory) is within ~1-3 km of the station on stable ground. The bulk explosives depot and magazines are isolated at their licensed separation distances. Sediment ponds are at low points down-gradient of the pits and pad. Communications towers are on high points. The field conveyor (A02) starts at the sizer and runs to the overland tail.

A03: quality data (grade-control block model, FMS source tonnages) to the stockyard for blending reconciliation
Utilities: diesel supply (~10-15 ML/yr), 33 kV power to the sizer station, raw water for dust suppression, fibre link to the refinery CCR
Refinery laboratory: grade-control assays and reconciliation of mined tonnage with refinery feed (tonnage mined = refinery feed +- stock change)
Environment/closure: rehabilitation programme, water discharge licences, explosives licences

areas.area_name: Ore transport (mine to refinery overland conveyor system)
areas.purpose: Transport an average of ~5.9 Mt/yr of sized wet bauxite from the mine sizing station to the refinery stockyard over a generic ~20 km route (plateau to valley, assumed net fall ~150 m, i.e. ~0.75% average decline). The system must be reliable, low in operating cost and dust, and have a small land footprint. It is designed for 1,800 t/h so that it can catch up and build pre-monsoon stock.
areas.process_description: SELECTION: overland belt conveyor vs rail for 10-50 km. (a) Conveyor: continuous and electrically driven, so operating cost is low. Labour is low because it is operated remotely from the refinery CCR. It follows terrain with horizontal curves and grades up to ~15-18% (rail ~1-2%). Single loading and discharge points match a single mine and a single refinery. It is proven at this scale: ~50 km overland from the Boddington-area bauxite mine to the Worsley refinery (Wikipedia, 'Worsley Alumina'); ~14.6 km single-flight cable-belt conveyor from Panchpatmali mine to the Damanjodi refinery (verify); Alcoa's Huntly-Pinjarra and Willowdale-Wagerup overlands (lengths to verify); Channar 20 km iron-ore overland (Nordell 1991). (b) Rail: favoured above ~50-100 km, for multiple sources or customers, or where rail already exists. It needs a loop and loadout, a car dumper, rolling stock and crews, and flat gradients (heavy earthworks on plateau escarpments). (c) Slurry pipeline (e.g. Paragominas-Alunorte ~244 km): only for very long distances; requires wet grinding at the mine. DECISION: overland belt conveyor in 2 flights of ~10 km each. The intermediate transfer allows a lower belt rating and splits the risk. It is fed by a relocatable field conveyor (~2-5 km) from the semi-mobile sizer. Sequence: sized ore from 01-CV-001 -> 02-CV-001 field conveyor -> 02-CV-002 overland flight 1 -> intermediate transfer station 02-TS-001 -> 02-CV-003 overland flight 2 -> refinery junction tower -> 03-CV-001. POWER (corrected): the conveyor is NET MOTORING at all normal load cases. Artificial-friction resistance (ISO 5048 / DIN 22101, f ~0.012-0.016, moving mass ~220 kg/m) is ~1.2-1.6 MW per 10 km flight at design load. The gravity credit for a 75 m fall per flight is only ~0.37 MW, so absorbed power is ~0.9-1.4 MW per flight. Regeneration occurs only on local steep descending sections, transiently during stopping, or when only the downhill parts are loaded. Steady-state regeneration would require an average decline above ~2.8% (f x m_moving / m_load ~ 0.014 x 220/111). Active-front-end (AFE) VFDs are still specified for torque control, load sharing and absorbing that local or transient regenerative power. Controlled caliper brakes are required for safe stopping. A full dynamic (transient) analysis sets the start and stop ramps, take-up travel and brake sizing. It must include the loaded-downhill/empty-uphill and loaded-uphill/empty-downhill cases.

equipment.working_principle: An endless rubber belt with embedded longitudinal steel cords runs over pulleys at each end and is supported by thousands of idler rolls in between. Drive pulleys at the head and tail transmit torque by friction (Euler-Eytelwein: T1/T2 <= e^(mu*theta)) from motors through gearboxes. A winch take-up keeps enough slack-side tension that the belt does not slip on the pulley or sag excessively between idlers. Over long distances the main resistance is the indentation of the belt's bottom cover as it rolls over the idlers, so a low-rolling-resistance cover compound substantially reduces power. On this route the small average decline only partly offsets the friction, so the drives normally motor. Where a local section descends steeply or only the downhill part of the belt is loaded, the load can drive the belt; the AFE drives then act as generators and the controlled caliper brakes ensure safe stopping. VFDs ramp starts and stops so the stress waves travelling along the elastic belt do not cause slip, belt lift-off in concave curves or excessive tension. Horizontal curves are achieved by tilting (banking) the idlers and holding belt tension within a band so the belt stays centred.

equipment.working_principle: Each VFD converts the fixed-frequency supply to variable frequency so the motor accelerates the belt along a programmed S-curve. Torque is shared between the head drives by master-slave control, and the tail drive tensions the return strand. During stops and on locally steep downhill sections the active front end can return braking energy to the grid. The disc brakes are applied in a controlled way during emergency stops or a power failure, bringing the loaded belt to rest without overstressing it. An oil conditioning unit cools and filters the gearbox oil.

equipment.name: Overland belt weigh scales and belt-condition monitoring
equipment.function: Measure delivered tonnage (mine production reconciliation) and detect belt rips and cord damage.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 scale per flight; rip detection on both flights; 1 steel-cord scanner

Rip loops embedded in the belt are sensed by detectors; a missing loop signal means a rip and stops the belt. The magnetic scanner maps cord breaks and splice elongation.

equipment.working_principle: Old belt is pulled out and new belt pulled in by winches while belt clamps hold tension. Steel-cord ends are stepped and laid into a multi-step overlap with uncured rubber, and the electrically heated press vulcanises the splice. For idler changes, the belt-lifting trolley raises the belt off the idler set with the conveyor isolated, and the service truck crane swaps the frame or rolls. areas.layout_notes: Route ~20 km on a cleared corridor ~20-40 m wide containing the conveyor, a gravel patrol/maintenance road on one side, a 33 kV overhead power line and a fibre-optic cable. The belt line runs ~1-1.5 m above ground on sleepers, rising onto trusses over roads and creeks. Horizontal curves (R ~2-4 km) follow ridgelines and avoid sensitive areas. Vertical alignment follows the terrain; concave and convex curve radii are set by dynamic analysis (concave R typically several hundred to more than 1,000 m). Average decline ~0.75%; local steeper sections are identified for braking design. Flight 1 tail is at the mine (drive station + loading chute from the field conveyor). The intermediate transfer station at ~10 km has its drives and substation. Flight 2 head is at the refinery junction tower. Each drive station has a fenced route substation (02-SS). Fauna and stock crossings are provided every ~1-2 km where required; dust/rain hoods run throughout.
interfaces: A01: receives -200 mm ore from 01-CV-001 at up to 1,800 t/h; sequence interlocks with the sizer and feeder
A03: delivers to 03-CV-001 (stockyard incoming conveyor) at the junction tower
Electrical: 33 kV supply; net consumer (~1.8-2.8 MW for both flights at design load); transient regenerative power only
Control: fibre-optic link; controlled from the refinery CCR, monitored from the mine control room 01-CR-001
Maintenance: shared heavy workshop and stores at the refinery

areas.area_name: Bauxite receiving, stockpiling, blending and secondary/tertiary sizing at the refinery
areas.purpose: Receive overland ore at up to 1,800 t/h. Homogenise its quality in chevron blending beds to stabilise the available alumina and reactive silica fed to digestion. Provide strategic storage for mine, overland and monsoon outages. Remove tramp metal, reduce ore to the agreed mill-feed size of -25 mm nominal (P80 ~15-20 mm), sample it for metallurgical accounting, and deliver it to the A04 mill feed bins at ~711 t/h wet average (640 t/h dry). A03 ENDS at the shuttle conveyor 03-CV-005 above the A04 bins. The mill feed bins and weigh feeders (04-BN-001..004 / 04-WF-001..004) belong to A04.
areas.process_description: 1) Ore arrives on 03-CV-001 at the junction tower. An on-line PGNAA analyser and belt scale record tonnage and elemental composition (Al2O3, SiO2, Fe2O3, TiO2) plus microwave moisture, for stacking control. A diverter gate in the junction tower routes ore either to the blending yard or to the emergency stockpile feed conveyor 03-CV-006. 2) A travelling tripper on the yard conveyor feeds a rail-mounted side-boom stacker. The stacker builds two in-line blending beds (A and B) by CHEVRON stacking: it travels the full bed length at constant speed, laying ~300-500 thin layers on top of one another, so each cross-section contains material from the whole build period. 3) While one bed is being built, the other is reclaimed full-face by a bridge-type bucket-wheel reclaimer whose harrow rakes the whole cross-section. This cuts all layers at once and gives a variance reduction (blending effect) of typically ~5-10:1 for chevron beds with this layer count. 4) A strategic/emergency stockpile of ~300-350 kt (~18-20 days) is built by a radial luffing stacker 03-RS-001, with dozer push to extend the pile. Area is reserved for extension to ~45 days at monsoon-climate sites. It is reclaimed by a 992-class wheel loader (988-class backup) into a two-sided ground hopper and belt feeder at >= 750-800 t/h, which covers mill demand when the bridge reclaimer is down. 5) Reclaimed ore passes an overband magnet and a metal detector. 6) Two-stage sizing in the crusher house. There are two parallel lines (1 duty + 1 standby); each line is a secondary twin-shaft sizer (-200 -> -75 mm) feeding a tertiary twin-shaft sizer (-75 -> -25 mm nominal, P80 ~15-20 mm), as agreed with A04 for single-stage ball milling. 7) The mill-feed conveyor 03-CV-004 carries crushed ore to the A04 bin building. The mechanical cross-belt sampler 03-SA-001 on 03-CV-004 takes the metallurgical-accounting sample of refinery feed (ISO 8685); the cutter aperture is practical here because top size is -25 mm. 8) A reversible shuttle conveyor 03-CV-005 at the A04 bin-top elevation distributes ore to the 4 mill feed bins (04-BN-001..004) by bin-level priority. Lime and spent liquor are added in A04. 9) Dust control: water sprays and fog at transfers, fog cannons on the stockpiles, and a pulse-jet baghouse on the crusher house and transfer points. Stockyard runoff drains to a lined settlement pond and is recycled. A mobile-fleet wash bay serves the loaders and dozers. No caustic is handled in A03; first caustic contact is in A04 grinding.

Where the stacker is positioned, the belt is diverted up and over a pair of pulleys on the tripper, which moves with the stacker, so material discharges through a chute onto the stacker boom conveyor. In the junction tower a flop gate selects either 03-CV-001 (blending beds) or 03-CV-006 (emergency stockpile).

equipment.name: On-line cross-belt elemental analyser (PGNAA) and moisture meter with belt scale
equipment.function: Real-time measurement of Al2O3, SiO2, Fe2O3, TiO2, CaO and moisture in incoming ore, for stacking control and quality reporting.
equipment.type_selected: Prompt Gamma Neutron Activation Analyser (Cf-252 source or electronic neutron generator) straddling the belt, plus a microwave transmission moisture analyser
equipment.why_this_type: Measures the full belt cross-section continuously; used in bauxite and cement operations for feed-forward blending.
equipment.alternatives: Laboratory analysis of increments only (slow); on-belt XRF (surface only).
key_dimensions: Analyser 'C-frame' tunnel ~2-2.5 m long, ~3 m wide, ~2 m high around the belt; mass ~5-10 t because of shielding (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: Not measured directly; inferred by correlation with grade-control data

equipment.working_principle: Neutrons from the source pass through the ore. Nuclei capture neutrons and emit gamma rays of element-specific energies, which detectors above and below the belt count and deconvolve into element concentrations. Microwaves passing through the burden are attenuated and phase-shifted in proportion to its water content.
details_to_model: Shielded enclosure straddling the belt with radiation trefoil signs; belt-profile plough to level the burden
Air-conditioned electronics cabinet with local display
hazards_and_safety: Ionising radiation source: licensed, interlocked shutter, controlled area, radiation safety officer; listed in the plant-wide radiation-source register and radiation management plan
Do not remove covers; source handling by licensed personnel only
sources: Vendor literature (Thermo Scientific CB Omni, Scantech GEOSCAN class) - verify

equipment.name: Rail-mounted luffing side-boom stacker (chevron stacking)
equipment.function: Builds the two in-line chevron blending beds.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (when the stacker is down, incoming ore is diverted to the emergency stockpile via 03-CV-006 / 03-RS-001)
equipment.type_selected: Travelling side stacker with luffing (non-slewing or limited-slew) boom fed by an integral tripper
equipment.why_this_type: Chevron stacking along the bed centreline from a boom at the side of the yard is the standard linear blending-bed arrangement. Luffing keeps the drop height low, reducing dust and segregation.
equipment.alternatives: Circular blending store with slewing stacker and bridge scraper/bucket-wheel reclaimer (compact footprint, covered); slewing/luffing stacker-reclaimer (no blending).
key_dimensions: Boom length ~28-35 m (reaches the bed centreline ~25 m from the rail) (engineering estimate)
Rail gauge ~6-8 m; travel ~500-600 m (engineering estimate)
Machine mass ~200-350 t (engineering estimate)
Luffing range ~-12 to +18 degrees; discharge height up to ~19-20 m

operating_parameters.basis: Calculated: ~110 kt bed / (~250-400 t per pass)

equipment.working_principle: The stacker travels continuously back and forth along the bed while discharging at the bed centreline, so each pass lays a thin roof-shaped (chevron) layer. Over a few days, hundreds of layers accumulate, each representing a short period of mine production. Because the reclaimer later cuts across all layers at once, short-term quality fluctuations are averaged out. A boom-tip level sensor luffs the boom up or down to keep a small, constant drop height, which minimises dust and size segregation. Reversal at the end of the bed is automatic, controlled by position encoders.
details_to_model: Portal/gantry undercarriage with bogie sets (~16-24 wheels) on crane rails (A100/A120 class) on concrete beams
Integrated tripper car coupled to the stacker
Boom: lattice or box girder with 1,200 mm conveyor, walkways on both sides, handrails, boom-tip chute with telescopic or cascade spout and spray nozzles
Counterweight on the opposite side; luffing hydraulic cylinders or rope luffing winch
Operator cab (or remote/automatic operation) with a clear view of the pile; machinery house with MCC
Motorised MV trailing-cable reel and cable trench along the yard; anemometer on top (high-wind park mode); rail clamps and storm anchors
Anti-collision radar/laser sensors on the boom, emergency stops, travel siren and beacons, stair access to all levels
hazards_and_safety: Boom collision with the pile or reclaimer: anti-collision system, zone interlocks
Working at height on the boom: handrails, fall protection
High wind: storm pins and rail clamps; operating limit ~20 m/s (engineering estimate)
Travel crush zone near the rails: exclusion fencing, travel warning
sources: thyssenkrupp / FLSmidth / TAKRAF stockyard machine literature (class data)

Cross-section ~470 m2 -> ~630-650 t per metre at ~1.35 t/m3 (calculated)

CEMA material data for bauxite (~35 degrees); engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: See the stacker and reclaimer. The conical ends of a chevron bed are poorly blended because they contain only some of the layers. End-cone effects are reduced by using long beds and by reclaiming the start cone separately or mixing it in gradually.

Concrete pad with drainage slope and perimeter drains; yard lighting towers; fog cannons on masts

Mobile plant only with a permit

equipment.name: Blending-yard portal roof shed (monsoon-climate variant)
equipment.function: Keeps rain off the blending beds to limit ore moisture swings, bin hang-ups and mill-feed variability at high-rainfall (monsoon) sites.
equipment.type_selected: Longitudinal steel portal-frame (or space-frame arch) shed spanning both beds and the reclaimer rails, open or partly clad at the sides for ventilation

Length ~450-500 m covering both beds (engineering estimate)
Portal frames at ~10-12 m centres on concrete pad footings; ridge ventilator; translucent roof sheeting strips (engineering estimate)

Work at height for roof maintenance: roof walkways, anchor lines

equipment.name: Bridge-type bucket-wheel blending reclaimer (full-face)
equipment.function: Reclaims a blending bed across its full cross-section to deliver blended ore at a controlled rate.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (emergency stockpile reclaim at >= 750-800 t/h is the backup route)
equipment.type_selected: Bridge reclaimer spanning the bed, with a traversing bucket wheel (or drum) and oscillating harrow
equipment.why_this_type: Full-face reclaiming is needed to realise the chevron blending. Bucket-wheel and drum types handle sticky ore better than scrapers and allow the required capacity.
equipment.alternatives: Drum reclaimer (full-width drum with buckets, ~3-4 m diameter); bridge scraper reclaimer (lower capacity, more wear with abrasive ore).
key_dimensions: Bridge span (rail centres) ~52-55 m (engineering estimate)
Bucket wheel ~4-5 m diameter with 8-12 buckets of ~0.4-0.6 m3 each (engineering estimate; corrected from 6-7 m / 1.0-1.5 m3, which would give ~3,000-4,000 t/h)
Harrow: triangular frame matching the pile cross-section (~50 m base x ~19 m high) with rows of tines (engineering estimate)
Machine mass ~300-450 t (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The bridge advances slowly into the pile face. The harrow, a rake shaped like the pile cross-section, oscillates across the face and loosens a thin slice from all layers, which slides down to the toe. The bucket wheel travels back and forth along the bridge at the bottom of the face, scoops this material and discharges it onto the bridge conveyor, which feeds the yard reclaim conveyor 03-CV-002 through a chute. The reclaim rate is controlled by bridge advance and wheel traverse speed, based on wheel motor power and the downstream belt scale.
details_to_model: Box-girder bridge on two end carriages (bogies on rails each side); one fixed and one pendulum (hinged) support
Bucket wheel (~4-5 m) with buckets having replaceable lips/teeth; wheel carriage running on bridge rails; wheel drive (motor + gearbox)
Harrow frame with tine rows (~0.5-1 m spacing); hydraulic oscillation cylinders
Bridge conveyor (~1,200-1,400 mm) with discharge chute down to the yard conveyor
Operator cab, electrical house, cable reel, walkways and handrails, access stairs at each end, anemometer, storm anchors
Anti-collision with the stacker; travel siren and beacons
hazards_and_safety: Face collapse near the pile: no access
Moving harrow and wheel: interlocked access gates
Working at height; high-wind limits

equipment.function: Builds the strategic/emergency stockpile independently of the blending-bed stacker, including during stacker outages.

equipment.why_this_type: The rail side-stacker reaches only ~25-35 m from its rail and cannot build a ~120 m wide, 300-350 kt pile. A radial stacker builds a kidney-shaped pile of ~100-120 kt live directly; dozers push the pile out a further ~30-60 m to reach full capacity.

Once the kidney pile reaches its geometric limit, a D10-class dozer pushes material outward to extend the pile to full capacity.

Kidney-shaped pile with dozer-pushed extension; dozer working on the pile
Anemometer, beacon, cable reel, guards

Head drive with backstop, belt scale, cleaners, transfer chutes, pull-wire switches

Detector coil frame with non-metallic zone

equipment.name: Secondary and tertiary twin-shaft sizers (two parallel lines, 1 duty + 1 standby)
equipment.function: Reduce reclaimed ore from -200 mm to -25 mm nominal (P80 ~15-20 mm) for single-stage ball milling in A04. Secondary: -200 -> -75 mm. Tertiary: -75 -> -25 mm.
equipment.type_selected: Secondary twin-shaft sizer with breaker bar (MMD 625/750 series class) feeding a tertiary twin-shaft sizer with breaker bar (MMD 500 series class), stacked in series in each line
equipment.why_this_type: Wet, sticky gibbsitic ore: sizers give a controlled top size with few fines and do not blind, unlike screens plus cone crushers. A reduction from -200 to -25 mm (ratio ~8) is too large for one sizer stage (typically ~3-5:1), so two stages are used (~2.7:1 and ~3:1). Hammer and impact crushers give a finer product but wear quickly in ferruginous ore and clog when wet.
equipment.alternatives: Hammer/impact crushers to -25 mm (finer, higher wear); toothed double-roll crushers; single stage to -40 mm with the A04 Bond calculation using F80 ~20-25 mm (mill power ~10-20% higher), which was not adopted.
key_dimensions: Secondary sizer ~5-6 m long including drives, ~2.5-3.5 m wide, ~1.5-2 m high; shaft centres ~625-750 mm (engineering estimate)
Tertiary sizer ~4.5-5.5 m long including drives, ~2.5-3 m wide, ~1.5 m high; shaft centres ~500 mm (engineering estimate)
Crusher house: 5-level steel-framed, clad building, ~25 x 22 m plan, ~40-45 m high (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate; confirm with vendor testwork on wet ore

equipment.working_principle: As for the primary sizer, but with closer shaft centres and a breaker bar under the shafts. The breaker bar holds oversize against the teeth so it is broken a second time, giving a tighter top size. A hydraulic flop gate at the top of the crusher house selects the duty line. In each line, ore falls from the secondary sizer through a short chute directly into the tertiary sizer below, which discharges onto the collecting conveyor 03-CV-004.
details_to_model: Diverter flop gate at the top level splitting to two line feed chutes
Two lines side by side; on each, the secondary sizer on an upper floor above the tertiary sizer, drives on the outer sides
Maintenance crane (~20-25 t) over both lines; hatch openings through floors; lay-down bay at ground level
Discharge chutes onto collecting conveyor 03-CV-004
Dust extraction hoods on feed and discharge points, ducts to 03-DC-001
Grating floors with kick plates; stair tower and hoist bay
hazards_and_safety: Nip/crush at the shafts; heavy lifts; dust; noise above 90 dB(A)
Clearing blocked chutes: isolation, confined-space rules
instrumentation_and_control: Motor power, bearing temperatures, vibration; blocked-chute probes; diverter position switches
Interlock: tertiary sizer and 03-CV-004 running before the secondary sizer starts
common_problems: Tooth wear in abrasive ferricrete: hardfacing rebuilds
Packing of the tertiary sizer with wet clay in monsoon: scrapers, reduced feed rate

equipment.name: Mill-feed conveyor with metallurgical cross-belt sampler
equipment.function: Carry crushed ore from the crusher house to the A04 mill feed bin building, and take the refinery-feed accounting sample on the -25 mm stream.
equipment.type_selected: Troughed belt conveyor 1,200 mm in an enclosed gallery; hammer-type cross-belt primary sampler with secondary divider, sample crusher and reject return (ISO 8685 principles)
key_dimensions: 03-CV-004 ~150-300 m, inclined ~12-15 degrees, rising to the A04 bin-top/shuttle elevation (~+25 m per A04) (engineering estimate)
Sampler cutter aperture >= ~100 mm (>= 3 x 25 mm top size with margin) across the 1,200 mm belt; sample station module ~6 x 4 x 6 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The conveyor lifts crushed ore to the bin building. At timed intervals the sampler's rotating cutter sweeps across the belt and takes a complete cross-section of the stream (correct delimitation and extraction per Gy sampling theory). The increment is crushed and divided to a laboratory sample, and rejects return to the belt. Locating the sampler after sizing makes the ISO cutter-aperture rule practical; PGNAA on incoming ore remains for stacking control.
details_to_model: Enclosed gallery with windows and ventilation, walkways on both sides
Cutter housing over the belt with curved belt-matching idler frame, motor and brake
Sample chute to secondary divider and crusher, sample collector canisters; enclosed module with access door and stair
hazards_and_safety: Fast-moving cutter: interlocked access
Sample-handling dust
sources: ISO 6140 Aluminium ores - Preparation of samples

equipment.name: Reversible travelling shuttle conveyor over the A04 mill feed bins (A03 battery limit)
equipment.function: Distribute crushed ore to the four A04 mill feed bins (04-BN-001..004) by bin-level priority. This is the A03/A04 battery limit.
equipment.type_selected: Reversible shuttle belt conveyor on a rail-mounted carriage at the A04 bin-top elevation
key_dimensions: Shuttle ~40-50 m long travelling on rails over 4 bin inlets; elevation per A04 (~+25 m) (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The shuttle conveyor is a short reversible belt on a carriage. By moving and reversing, it discharges into whichever bin needs filling, controlled by the A04 bin level radars.
details_to_model: Shuttle carriage with rails, reversible drive, end chutes, cable festoon
Bin-top floor openings with dust seals (floor and bins in A04 scope)
hazards_and_safety: Travelling shuttle crush zone; openings over bins: gratings and interlocks
instrumentation_and_control: Shuttle position encoder; bin selection by level priority from the A04 radars; high-level interlock

equipment.name: Pulse-jet baghouse dust collector with exhaust fan (crusher house and transfer points)
equipment.function: Capture dust from sizer feed and discharge points, transfer chutes and the shuttle/bin-top inlets.
equipment.type_selected: Pulse-jet fabric filter (polyester needle-felt bags), centrifugal ID fan, rotary valve returning dust to the mill-feed conveyor
key_dimensions: Housing ~12 x 5 m plan, ~12-15 m high including hopper (engineering estimate)
~600-1,000 bags, ~150 mm diameter x 4-6 m long (engineering estimate)
Stack ~25-30 m high with sampling ports
equipment.working_principle: Dusty air drawn through the hoods enters the housing. Dust is captured on the outside of the filter bags while clean air passes through and leaves via the fan to the stack. Short pulses of compressed air from blow pipes above each row of bags flex the bags and knock the dust cake into the hopper, and a rotary valve returns it to the process.
details_to_model: Rectangular housing with walk-in clean-air plenum doors, blow-pipe header and solenoid valves on top, compressed-air receiver
Pyramidal hopper, rotary valve, screw conveyor
Ductwork with blast gates, ID fan with silencer, stack with platform and sampling ports
Differential pressure gauge and broken-bag detector
hazards_and_safety: Confined space inside the housing; rotating fan; dust exposure during bag changes

equipment.name: Dust suppression (sprays, fog cannons), water supply pumps, stockyard drainage, settlement pond and mobile-fleet wash bay
equipment.function: Control fugitive dust from stockpiles and transfers, manage stockyard stormwater, and clean yard mobile plant.
equipment.qty_operating: Spray pump skid 1+1; fog cannons ~4-8 around the yard and emergency pile; drainage pumps 1+1; 1 wash bay
equipment.type_selected: Multistage centrifugal spray pump skid with filtration; mast-mounted oscillating fog cannons (~50-80 m throw); submersible sump pumps; HDPE-lined settlement pond; concrete wash pad with high-pressure monitors and sediment/oil separator
key_dimensions: Fog cannon barrel ~2-3 m long on an ~8-12 m mast (engineering estimate)
Settlement pond ~1-2 ha, 3 m deep, HDPE-lined (engineering estimate)
Wash bay ~25 x 10 m with ramp, sediment trap and oil-water separator (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: Engineering estimate (avoids sticky ore and extra water in the refinery balance)

equipment.working_principle: Fine water droplets either wet the ore (sprays at transfers) or agglomerate airborne particles so they fall out (fog cannons). Sprays are interlocked to run only when material is flowing. Stockyard runoff carries fines to the pond, where they settle; clear water is pumped back to the spray system or to process water. The wash bay removes bauxite mud from loaders and dozers before workshop entry.
details_to_model: Spray bars with flat-fan nozzles at each transfer chute, solenoid valves
Fog cannons on masts with fan housing and nozzle ring
Pump skid in a small shed, filters, pressure gauges
Concrete-lined drains and sumps around the beds; pond with clean-out ramp, fencing and life rings
Wash bay with monitors on posts, sediment trap and separator
hazards_and_safety: Slippery surfaces; electrical equipment in wet areas; drowning in the pond
High-pressure water jets at the wash bay

areas.layout_notes: Stockyard at grade on the refinery's upwind side (relative to prevailing wind towards the offices), adjacent to the grinding area (A04). The junction tower (with analyser, scale and diverter) is where the overland enters. From it, an in-line yard ~500-550 m long x ~110-130 m wide runs: incoming conveyor and stacker rails on one side, two beds (each ~50 m wide, ~200-220 m overall) end to end, bridge reclaimer rails straddling the beds (~52-55 m span), and the reclaim conveyor on the opposite side. The optional roof shed (03-RF-001, ~60-65 m span, ~28-32 m high) covers the beds. The emergency stockpile (~300-350 kt; ~250 x 120 m footprint, 15-18 m high, with reserved extension area) lies beside the yard, fed by 03-CV-006 and radial stacker 03-RS-001, with its two-sided ground hopper discharging to 03-CV-002. An inclined covered gallery (~12-15 degrees) rises from the yard to the top of the crusher house (~40-45 m high, two lines of secondary over tertiary sizers). The mill-feed gallery 03-CV-004 (with the sample station) rises to the A04 bin building, where shuttle 03-CV-005 runs at the A04 bin-top elevation (~+25 m) over the four A04 bins. A ~6 m perimeter road surrounds the yard for maintenance, fire access and loader cleanup. Electrical substation and MCC rooms are near the crusher house; the wash bay is at the yard access road; the settlement pond is at the yard's low corner.
interfaces: A02: receives up to 1,800 t/h from 02-CV-003

A04 Grinding: A03 ends at shuttle 03-CV-005 discharging into A04 mill feed bins 04-BN-001..004 (A04 owns bins and weigh feeders 04-WF-001..004); crushed product -25 mm nominal, P80 ~15-20 mm, ~711 t/h wet average, bin filling up to 1,100 t/h; shuttle elevation set by A04 (~+25 m)
Laboratory/QA: accounting samples from 03-SA-001 (after sizing), PGNAA data, reconciliation of refinery feed with mine (A01) FMS tonnages
Utilities: process/raw water for dust suppression, compressed air for the baghouse, power
Control: CCR (stockyard machines in automatic mode, interlocked conveyor sequences)
HSE: PGNAA source included in the plant-wide radiation-source register
