equipment.name: Agglomeration precipitators (AG-1..3; Line A = 001-003, Line B = 004-006)
equipment.function: Provide ~7-11 h of hot, agitated contact between fresh supersaturated PL and a low charge of fine seed, so that fines cement into strong agglomerates that become the cores of the product particles.
equipment.qty_operating: 5-6 (one may be bypassed for descaling in rotation)
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical, flat-bottomed (with grout/concrete fillet) carbon-steel tank, 14 m ID x ~31 m shell, fixed cone roof with agitator bridge; top-entry mechanical agitator (12-AG); bottom-draw airlift transfer
equipment.why_this_type: Large (~4,500 m3) tanks keep the tank count and piping manageable. Mechanical hydrofoil agitation keeps the high solids suspended at ~15-30 W/m3 and needs less energy than full air agitation. Flat bottoms with fillets suit large mechanically agitated tanks; conical bottoms suit air-agitated designs (alternative).
equipment.alternatives: Pachuca or air-agitated precipitators with a central draft tube and airlift (older practice; no rotating parts in the slurry but high air consumption and a conical bottom). Draft-tube mechanical agitation (impeller in a central draft tube) gives strong axial circulation at lower power, but the draft tube scales. A gravity-overflow series (no airlifts) can short-circuit and accumulate coarse particles.
key_dimensions: ID ~14.0 m; shell height ~31 m; working level ~29-29.5 m; working volume ~4,400-4,600 m3 (engineering estimate)
Roof cone ~1:12 rising to an agitator bridge at ~32-33 m above grade

Shell thickness ~22-26 mm bottom strake (incl. 3 mm CA) tapering to ~8-10 mm top strake (API 650 one-foot method: td = 4.9D(H-0.3)G/Sd + CA = 4.9 x 14 x 30.7 x 1.55 / 173 + 3 ≈ 22 mm for A516-70, Sd 173 MPa; hydrotest tt ≈ 11 mm; API 650 minimum nominal for D <15 m is 5 mm, raised for stiffness and agitator loads; engineering estimate)
Bottom fillet: 45 deg grout or concrete ring ~1.0-1.5 m high at the shell/floor junction to prevent dead zones
Tank centres ~18 m (4 m clear between tanks for stair towers and launders)

operating_parameters.value: 72-78 (may drop ~1-3 K through the stage: heat loss vs heat of crystallisation)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (5-6 x 4,500 m3 / ~2,200-2,900 m3/h total slurry)

equipment.working_principle: PL arriving at 72-78 degC is strongly supersaturated, and only a small surface area of fine seed is offered. Gibbsite deposits quickly on the fines. Because the particle number and the supersaturation are both high, colliding particles are bridged by new gibbsite and 'cemented' into agglomerates. A higher temperature favours this cementing over new nucleation. The agitator keeps everything suspended with enough shear to make particles collide but not so much that the young agglomerates break apart. Slurry leaves each tank through a bottom-draw airlift into the launder feeding the next tank, so coarse particles cannot accumulate on the bottom. After the third tank the slurry passes to growth tank G-1, where the coarse seed charge is added.
details_to_model: Shell with horizontal strakes ~2.4-2.5 m high (12-13 strakes); wind girder near the top

Cone roof with a central steel agitator bridge (two box girders spanning the full 14 m, supported on the shell or on independent columns) carrying the gearbox and motor; bridge has grating deck, handrails and toe-boards (AS 1657 / ISO 14122)

Roof: 2-3 DN900 roof hatches (descaling access and inspection), slurry inlet box/chute from the launder (~1.5 x 1.5 m) entering through the roof, DN600 PL and seed inlet nozzles on AG-1, radar level nozzle with a large-diameter stilling well or non-contact radar, 2 DN400 vents with goosenecks

Shell: 2 large access doors at grade (~1.2 x 1.8 m oval or 1,500 mm round, hinged, bolted) for descaling and excavator entry, 180 deg apart; 1-2 DN900 manholes at ~15 m reachable from the stair tower; DN300 drain/emptying nozzle at the floor with knife-gate valve; 3-4 thermowells at heights ~3, 12, 20, 27 m; DN50 ball-valve sample points at mid-height inside a splash box
Nozzle and attachment welds on prefabricated, stress-relieved insert plates (visible thicker plate panels around large nozzles)

Airlift riser (12-AL) pipe DN600-900 running inside the tank against the wall from ~0.5-1 m above the floor to above the liquid level, then discharging through the shell into the launder box; DN50-100 air injection pipe down the outside with a flanged connection and valve station
Bypass launder connection (gate or flap) for taking the tank out of series
DN600 emergency overflow nozzle at ~29.8 m to a closed overflow pipe running to the bund
4 full-height wall baffles ~1.0-1.2 m wide (~T/12) offset ~0.15 m from the wall, at 90 deg spacing, braced to the shell
Spiral stair or shared stair tower between tank pairs, with landings; roof perimeter handrail; earthing bosses; nameplate
External surface: uninsulated (aids cooling; site-dependent)
Concrete ringwall foundation with oiled-sand or bitumen bedding, under-floor leak detection telltales; bunded tank farm with sumps
Visual wear and scale: buff/white hydrate crust on the inside walls, launders and roof hatches when modelling the 'cleaning' state
hazards_and_safety: Descaling entry is a confined space with falling scale slabs: permit, positive isolation (spades on all inlets, airlift air isolated and vented, agitator LOTO with the shaft mechanically locked), forced ventilation, continuous gas test (mainly O2), standby person, rescue tripod at the roof hatch
Hot caustic slurry at 70-78 degC: chemical and thermal burns; full caustic PPE at sample points and roof hatches
Working at height (>30 m) on roofs and bridges: handrails, no climbing outside guards, permits for roof-hatch work
Tank overflow or launder spill of thousands of m3 of caustic slurry: bund to 110% of the largest tank, high-high level trip on the feed
Hydrate splash makes walkways slippery; housekeeping
Never open the bottom access doors until the tank is empty and washed (~30 m of slurry head otherwise)
Radiometric density gauges (where fitted): managed under the plant radiation-safety plan and source register
instrumentation_and_control: Radar level LIT plus high-high level switch
Slurry density or solids: nuclear density gauge on the airlift discharge or periodic manual sampling
Agitator power and torque monitoring (scale build-up and sanding indicator)
Lab samples every 2-4 h for A/C, solids, PSD (laser diffraction), seed surface area
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A516-70 / AS 1548 PT460 / IS 2062 E350). At 72-78 degC in ~14 wt% NaOH-equivalent liquor the service is at or just above the NACE SP0403 PWHT line: PWHT the nozzle and attachment welds (stress-relieved insert-plate assemblies) on AG-1..3 and G-1..G-4 (>~68 degC); full shell PWHT is not practical or normally required. Cooler tanks (G-5..G-13) do not need PWHT. Corrosion allowance 3 mm. Agitator wetted parts CS with 3-6 mm corrosion/erosion allowance.
common_problems: Gibbsite scale on walls, baffles, roof underside, launders and agitator shafts/blades. It builds ~100-300 mm/yr (engineering estimate), cuts working volume and unbalances agitators. Tanks are descaled every ~12-36 months (engineering estimate) by ultra-high-pressure water jetting (UHP ~1,000-2,500 bar), mechanical breaking (excavator with hammer) or caustic dissolution
Sanding: solids settle if the agitator trips and can 'bog' the impeller, so restarting needs a high-torque drive or air lancing
Short-circuiting if baffles or airlifts fail
Fines nucleation events from too-low temperature or a high-A/C PL spike
Oxalate co-precipitation (destabilised oxalate) gives fine, high-soda hydrate
operating_tips_and_key_points: Agglomeration needs high temperature AND low seed surface. Adding too much fine seed or running too cold gives growth or nucleation instead of agglomeration
Never stop agitation on a tank holding slurry unless it is planned: if the agitator trips, start emptying or air-lancing within minutes to hours
PSD (particle size distribution) moves in slow cycles of weeks. Respond to trends with small changes to fine seed charge and fill temperature
sources: Misra C., White E.T., 'Kinetics of crystallization of aluminium trihydroxide from seeded caustic aluminate solutions', Chem. Eng. Prog. Symp. Ser. 67(110), 1971
Ilievski D., White E.T., 'Agglomeration during precipitation: agglomeration mechanism identification for Al(OH)3 crystals in stirred caustic aluminate solutions', Chem. Eng. Sci. 49 (1994)
Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry
Donaldson D., Raahauge B.E. (eds), Essential Readings in Light Metals Vol. 1 Alumina and Bauxite, TMS/Wiley 2013
API 650 (5.6.3.2 one-foot method; Table 5-2 allowable stresses)
Engineering estimate for all sizes and counts

equipment.name: Growth precipitators (G-1..G-13; Line A = 007-019, Line B = 020-032)
equipment.function: Grow hydrate on a large coarse-seed surface over ~23-29 h with falling temperature, to reach the target yield (A/C to ~0.36-0.39) and build product particle size.
equipment.type_selected: Same as agglomeration tanks: 14 m ID x ~31 m, ~4,500 m3 working, flat bottom with fillet, cone roof, top-entry mechanical agitator, bottom-draw airlift transfer
equipment.why_this_type: Standardising on one tank size and one agitator size minimises spares and lets tanks be repurposed. CHANGED: 13 tanks per line (12 operating) instead of 12 (11 operating), because the growth flow includes ~0.6-1.1 kt/h of seed solids and cake liquor on top of the PL. 24 x 4,500 m3 / 3,700-4,400 m3/h gives ~24-29 h.
equipment.alternatives: Fewer, larger tanks (~6,000-8,000 m3) reduce the count but need larger agitators and footprints. A single-stage 'European' layout instead of two-stage.
key_dimensions: As 12-TK-001..006: ID ~14 m, shell ~31 m, working ~4,500 m3 (engineering estimate)
Total precipitation installed working volume ~144,000 m3 (32 tanks); ~135,000 m3 normally online (30 tanks) (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (108,000 m3 online / 3,700-4,400 m3/h, less ~5% for scale)
design basis (confirmed across areas); to be verified with a precipitation model
yield = C x (A/C_PL - A/C_spent), e.g. 245 x (0.70-0.37) = 81 g/L

equipment.working_principle: In growth the seed surface is large, so the supersaturation is spent mainly on deposition onto existing particles rather than on new nuclei or agglomeration. The growth rate falls as A approaches A*, so the slurry is cooled in steps (interstage cooling). This lowers A* and restores the driving force, so the tail of the train still precipitates. The rate also falls with temperature (activation energy ~60 kJ/mol), so there is an economic optimum: too cold and growth is slow while nucleation and soda pick-up increase; too hot and yield is lost. Slurry moves tank to tank by airlifts drawing from near the floor, so coarse particles move forward and a plug-flow-like residence-time distribution builds up over 12-13 tanks in series.
details_to_model: Identical tank model to agglomeration (reuse asset) with different inlet arrangements: G-1 has a DN500 coarse seed inlet and the slurry inlet box; G-4 and G-8 have a DN500-600 interstage cooler suction nozzle on the shell ~1.5-2.5 m above the floor with knife-gate valve; G-5 and G-9 have the cooler return nozzle on the roof or upper shell
G-13 has the outlet airlift and launder box to the classification feed launder
Each line arranged as 2 rows of 8 (serpentine): row 1 = AG-1..3 + G-1..5, row 2 = G-6..13 returning; Line B mirror image
Common elevated launder gallery at roof level (~31-32 m) between rows, steel-trestle supported, with a walkway along it
Stair towers every 2-3 tanks connecting grade, mid-landing (~15 m) and roof level
Pipe and cable racks along the outside of each row at ~6 m
hazards_and_safety: As agglomeration tanks: confined space, falling scale, working at height, hot caustic slurry (55-74 degC), large spill potential
Descaling with UHP water jetting (>1,000 bar): injection injuries, exclusion zones, dead-man controls
instrumentation_and_control: Line temperature profile display; A/C profile from lab or online analyser (thermometric titration) on selected tanks
equipment.materials: As 12-TK-001..006 (PWHT of nozzle/attachment welds on G-1..G-4 only)
common_problems: Scale (less than agglomeration in G-1..4, more in the cold tail tanks where fines nucleate)
Loss of yield if interstage coolers are fouled
Fines build-up, then excess fine seed, then a PSD cycle
operating_tips_and_key_points: Yield control: PL A/C (from digestion), fill temperature, end temperature (interstage coolers), seed charge and residence (number of tanks online)

Take a tank out of series only via the launder bypass gates. Keep the agitator running until the tank has been pumped down below the lower impeller. Never stop agitation on a tank holding slurry, and never open bottom access doors until the tank is empty and washed
sources: Rosenberg S.P., Healy S.J., 'A thermodynamic model for gibbsite solubility in Bayer liquors', 4th International Alumina Quality Workshop, Darwin, 1996
Hudson L.K. et al., Ullmann's 'Aluminum Oxide'
Wefers K., Misra C., 'Oxides and Hydroxides of Aluminum', Alcoa Technical Paper No. 19 (Revised), 1987
Engineering estimate for sizes and counts

equipment.name: Precipitator agitators
equipment.function: Keep the hydrate slurry (up to ~700 g/L) fully suspended and the tank well mixed, with enough shear for particle collision but a low enough tip speed to limit attrition and breakage of agglomerates.
equipment.qty_operating: 30-32 (one per tank; the agitator of an emptied tank is stopped)
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (spare gearbox, motor and impeller set held in store)
equipment.type_selected: Top-entry, centre-mounted, long-overhung shaft (no bottom steady bearing) with 2 axial-flow hydrofoil impellers (e.g. Metso OKTOP, SPX Lightnin A310/A510 family, EKATO, Philadelphia Mixing Solutions types), driven by a bevel-helical or planetary gearbox with integral thrust bearing (drywell) and a TEFC motor; VSD or soft-starter
equipment.why_this_type: Hydrofoils give high axial pumping per kW at low tip speed (~3-5 m/s), so attrition is low. Having no steady bearing avoids failures in scaling slurry. Two impellers cover the ~29 m liquid height (H/T ~2.1).
equipment.alternatives: Airlift (draft-tube) agitation: no moving parts in the slurry but high air consumption, a conical bottom and draft-tube scaling. Mechanical draft-tube circulators.
key_dimensions: Impeller diameter ~5.0-6.0 m (D/T ~0.36-0.43), 3 or 4 blades (engineering estimate)
Lower impeller ~1/3 D above the floor (~1.8-2.5 m), upper impeller at ~45-60% of liquid height (engineering estimate)
Hollow shaft ~350-600 mm OD, ~28-30 m long, in 2-3 flanged sections (engineering estimate)
Gearbox ~2.5 x 2.0 x 2.0 m, ~15-25 t (engineering estimate); motor 90-160 kW, 4-pole
Overall drive height above bridge ~4-5 m

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (15-30 W/m3 x 4,500 m3; check P = Np·ρ·N³·D⁵ with Np ~0.3, 15 rpm, D 5.5 m ≈ 35-40 kW per impeller)

equipment.working_principle: Each hydrofoil impeller works like a slow ship's propeller, pushing slurry down the tank axis. The flow turns at the floor, sweeps outward and up along the walls (the baffles stop the bulk from swirling), and returns to the impeller. This 'down-pumping' loop lifts settled particles off the floor (the just-suspended condition, Zwietering criterion) and circulates the whole volume several times per hour. Power draw is roughly ρ·Np·N³·D⁵, so small speed changes cause large power changes. The gearbox reduces the motor speed of ~1,480 rpm to ~10-18 rpm, and its output bearings carry the large downward thrust and bending moment of the long overhung shaft. Scale on the blades adds mass, unbalance and power, so torque and vibration trends show when a shaft needs cleaning.
details_to_model: Drive on the bridge: motor (horizontal or vertical, with fan cowl and terminal box) coupled to a right-angle bevel-helical gearbox; output flange; drywell lantern with mesh-guarded access windows; lifting lugs
Rigid shaft coupling flange under the gearbox; shaft seal: simple roof-penetration dust/vapour shroud (no pressure seal) with flexible boot
Shaft visible inside the tank: 2-3 bolted flanged sections; two hydrofoil impellers, each with 3-4 twisted, tapered blades bolted to a hub; replaceable wear tips optional
VSD cabinet in the MCC (if fitted); local control station on the bridge (start/stop/E-stop, ammeter)
Lubrication: gearbox oil cooler (small fan- or water-cooled exchanger), oil level sight glass, grease points
Lifting: removable bridge hatch and davit points so a mobile crane (~200-300 t class at ~35 m radius) can lift the drive; shaft sections lifted through a roof hatch
Vibration sensors on gearbox housing (accelerometer cable to junction box)
Guarding: mesh guard around couplings and drywell (ISO 14120)
hazards_and_safety: Rotating shaft in the tank: an entrant could be struck. Isolate and lock the motor AND mechanically lock the shaft (pin or brake), because flowing slurry can turn the impeller (windmilling)
Heavy lifts at height (gearboxes ~20 t): lift plans, exclusion zones
Hot gearbox oil; noise ~80-85 dB(A) near the drive
Never start an agitator buried in settled solids at full speed: shaft or gearbox overload
instrumentation_and_control: Motor current/kW to DCS; torque calculation
Gearbox oil temperature and level switch; bearing vibration (online for critical units)
Run/trip status; a trip alarm triggers the sanding-response procedure
equipment.materials: Shaft and impellers carbon steel (or high-strength low-alloy) with 3-6 mm erosion allowance; blade tips may be rubber- or polyurethane-coated; gearbox cast iron/steel
common_problems: Scale build-up on blades and shaft causes unbalance, vibration and gearbox bearing failure
Gearbox output bearing wear
Fatigue cracks at blade roots
Sanded impeller after a power failure
operating_tips_and_key_points: Restart after a trip within the allowed time or use the sanded-start procedure (low speed with high torque, or air lancing)
Trend kW per tank: rising kW means scale is building on the blades
equipment.drive_and_power: 90-160 kW TEFC motor, 6.6 kV or 690 V, VSD optional (engineering estimate); 32 agitators ~3-4 MW absorbed
sources: Paul E.L., Atiemo-Obeng V.A., Kresta S.M. (eds), Handbook of Industrial Mixing, Wiley 2004 (hydrofoil design, solids suspension, Zwietering)
Vendor product literature (Metso OKTOP, SPX Lightnin, EKATO) - general ranges only

equipment.name: Transfer airlifts and inter-tank launders (incl. bypass launders and gates)
equipment.function: Move slurry from the bottom of each precipitator to the top of the next one in series without pumps, and allow any tank to be bypassed.
equipment.qty_operating: ~28-30 airlifts in use (one installed per tank; G-4 and G-8 airlifts are on standby while their interstage cooler pumps run); ~2 x 16 launder sections plus bypass launders
equipment.qty_standby: G-4/G-8 airlifts act as cooler-station bypass; redundant air injection points per airlift recommended
equipment.type_selected: Airlift riser DN600-900 (one per tank) inside the tank against the wall; open rectangular steel launders with removable covers sloping ~0.5-1% between tanks; slide gates or flap gates for bypass
equipment.why_this_type: Airlifts have no moving parts in slurry, tolerate scale, and draw from the bottom so coarse particles cannot accumulate. Launders allow visual inspection and easy cleaning.
key_dimensions: Riser DN600-900, length ~30 m (engineering estimate)
Air injection at ~6-12 m submergence via a DN80-100 air line and annular or spider injector (engineering estimate)
Launder ~0.8-1.2 m wide x 0.8-1.0 m deep, slope ~1:100, on roof-level steel trestles (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Compressed air injected into the riser forms bubbles, so the mixture inside the riser is lighter than the slurry outside. The heavier slurry outside pushes the mixture up and out of the top into the launder. Flow rises with air rate until slugging sets in. The launder then carries the slurry by gravity to the next tank's inlet box. Each tank's launder has an inlet gate and a bypass gate: closing the inlet and opening the bypass routes slurry straight past the tank so it can be pumped down and descaled while the line keeps running.
details_to_model: Riser emerging through the shell or roof edge into a launder head box (~1.5 x 1.5 x 1.5 m) with a splash cover and vent

Air supply station on the shell exterior at grade or mid-landing: isolation ball valve, globe throttle valve, rotameter or flow transmitter, pressure gauge, non-return valve, quick-connect for an air lance

Launders: U or rectangular channel with stiffener ribs, bolted removable grating or plate covers, on steel trestles between tank roofs; slide gates with rising-stem handwheels at each tank junction; bypass launder parallel to the main launder
Walkway along launders with handrails
Scale visible as buff crust inside launders
hazards_and_safety: Compressed air: never disconnect a pressurised hose
Open launder of hot caustic slurry at height: keep covers on, splash guards, handrails
Gate operation in a hot caustic splash zone: PPE
instrumentation_and_control: FT on air to each airlift (or manual rotameter)
Launder level switches at critical points (overflow alarm)
equipment.materials: Riser carbon steel, sometimes rubber-lined at the bottom inlet; launders carbon steel 8-10 mm
common_problems: Riser scale-up reduces capacity
Air injector blockage
Launder overflows when a gate is mis-set
sources: Engineering estimate; common Bayer practice (see Donaldson and Raahauge 2013 compilation)

equipment.name: Precipitation airlift air compressors
equipment.function: Supply oil-free low-pressure air to all transfer airlifts and to air lances for sanded-tank recovery.
equipment.type_selected: Oil-free rotary screw compressors (or multistage centrifugal blowers) with inlet filter-silencer, aftercooler and air receiver
equipment.why_this_type: Delivers 2.5-4 barg air reliably in the required flow range. Oil-free air avoids oil reaching the liquor, where it would act as an organic contaminant.
key_dimensions: Package ~5 x 2.5 x 2.5 m each in an acoustic enclosure; receiver ~10-20 m3 vertical vessel (engineering estimate)
Motor ~200-400 kW each (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Twin helical rotors trap and compress air without oil in the compression chamber (timing gears keep the rotors apart). The air is cooled, collected in a receiver to steady the pressure, and distributed via a ring main along the precipitator rows.
details_to_model: Compressor house (steel portal frame, cladding, roll-up door, louvres) with 4 packages; receiver outside; DN300 ring main on the pipe rack with drops to each tank
Inlet filters and silencers on the roof or wall
hazards_and_safety: Noise >85 dB(A) inside the enclosure; hearing-protection zone
Pressure vessel (receiver) to ASME VIII / AS 1210 with safety valve
Hot surfaces
instrumentation_and_control: Header pressure control (load/unload, VSD lead unit)

equipment.name: Interstage cooler slurry pumps (4 stations x 1 operating + 1 standby)
equipment.function: Draw the full line flow from G-4 and G-8 of each line, pump it through the interstage coolers and return it to the next tank (G-5 / G-9).
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal heavy-duty centrifugal slurry pump, rubber- or high-chrome-lined (e.g. Weir Warman AH, Metso MDM/HM, KSB GIW type), with VSD, gland water or expeller seal
equipment.why_this_type: Hydrate slurry is abrasive (~35-40% w/w solids), so replaceable wear liners and slow speed are needed. A VSD sets the loop flow and holds the channel velocity in the coolers.
key_dimensions: Discharge DN450-500, suction DN500-600 (engineering estimate)
Motor ~250-450 kW (engineering estimate)
Pump plus motor ~6 x 2 m on a common baseplate, or an overhead V-belt drive

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (return to tank top ~31 m from a suction at ~2 m; wide-gap PHE dP ~0.7-1.2 bar at 0.6-1.0 m/s)

equipment.working_principle: Same centrifugal principle as the liquor pumps, but with a large, thick, slow impeller and replaceable liners. The low speed limits wear and hydrate attrition. Gland seal water (condensate) or an expeller keeps abrasive solids out of the shaft packing. If the pump stops, the cooler must be flushed with liquor quickly, or settling solids will block the wide-gap channels. The tank's own airlift is then reopened to keep the line moving.
details_to_model: Pumps at grade beside G-4/G-8 in a bunded area; large DN600 knife-gate suction valve at the tank nozzle, flexible rubber spool/expansion joint, suction drain and flush connections
Slurry pump: split casing with bolts, liner, impeller adjustment mechanism at the bearing housing, gland water line with rotameter, coupling or V-belt drive with guard
Discharge knife-gate or pinch valve, pressure gauge with diaphragm seal, flushing connection
Cooler return line rising up the tank side to the roof with pipe supports and rubber-lined bends
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry: a worn casing or liner can burst; inspect for wear
Flushing and draining procedures before opening
Rotating equipment guarding, LOTO
instrumentation_and_control: Magflow on loop flow, PT discharge, VSD speed, motor current
Low-flow trip with automatic liquor flush of the cooler (protects coolers from settling)
equipment.materials: Natural rubber or high-chrome (27% Cr white iron) liners and impeller; CS casing
common_problems: Wear of liners and impeller
Scale in the suction nozzle
Gland water dilution of liquor (use minimal flow or expeller seals)
sources: Weir Minerals Warman / KSB GIW slurry pump literature (general)
Wills' Mineral Processing Technology, 8th ed. 2016 (slurry pumping)

equipment.name: Interstage coolers (4 stations x 3 units: 2 operating + 1 cleaning)
equipment.function: Remove the heat of crystallisation plus the required sensible heat from the precipitation slurry so the growth train follows the target temperature profile (~72 to ~57 degC).
equipment.type_selected: Wide-gap (free-flow) plate heat exchangers: slurry side with ~8-16 mm free-flow channels and no contact points, cooling-water side with standard narrow-gap plates; 316L plates, EPDM gaskets
equipment.why_this_type: Wide-gap channels pass ~450-700 g/L hydrate slurry without plugging and are much more compact than shell-and-tube. Cooling water allows control independent of liquor-heat recovery.
equipment.alternatives: (a) Vacuum flash interstage coolers: slurry flashes in a vessel under vacuum, and the vapour condenses in a barometric or surface condenser. There is no heat-transfer surface in slurry and a small concentrating effect, but it needs vacuum equipment and large vessels. (b) Spiral heat exchangers, which are very tolerant of solids. (c) Older plants used vertical shell-and-tube coolers or cooling elements inside the precipitators. All engineering judgement.
key_dimensions: ~150-250 m2 per unit (engineering estimate: station duty ~11-17 MW, LMTD ~28-32 K, U ~1,000-1,500 W/m2.K; 2 operating units per station)
~60-100 plates per unit (~30-50 slurry channels of ~1 m width x ~11 mm gap), sized for 0.6-1.0 m/s slurry velocity
Frame ~3.5 m high x 1.5 m x 4-6 m; ports DN400-500 slurry, DN400 CW (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (~2,000 m3/h x SG 1.55 x cp ~2.5-2.6 kJ/kg.K ≈ 2.2 MW/K x dT 5-7 K)

equipment.working_principle: Same plate-and-frame principle as the A11 PHEs. On the slurry side the plates are pressed with deep corrugations and no contact points, leaving a wide open channel that hydrate particles pass through without bridging. Cooling water flows counter-current in narrow channels on the other side. The channel count is chosen to keep slurry velocity at ~0.6-1.0 m/s, so particles stay suspended in the port and distribution zones. Cooling the supersaturated slurry deposits gibbsite scale on the slurry side, so one unit per station is always offline for hot-caustic or high-pressure water cleaning. Slurry outlet temperature is controlled by the cooling-water flow.
details_to_model: Same visual vocabulary as the A11 PHEs (frame, carrying bar, tie bolts, spray shield) but with fewer, thicker plates and visibly larger slurry ports
Knife-gate isolation valves on slurry nozzles (not butterflies), butterfly valves on CW nozzles
Liquor flush and condensate connections with automatic flush valves; drain valves to a bunded trench
Thermowells on all nozzles; CW control valve; dP gauge on the slurry side
Shelter roof over each station; mobile-crane access for plate handling
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry spray from gasket failure: spray shields
Abrasion of plates near ports can lead to leaks into the cooling water: CW-return pH/conductivity monitoring
Thermal relief on blocked-in sides
instrumentation_and_control: TIC on slurry outlet (cascade to CW valve)
AIT pH or conductivity on CW return
Interlocks: CW and slurry flows confirmed before opening valves; low-slurry-flow trip starts an automatic liquor flush
equipment.materials: 316L plates (thicker gauge on the slurry side), EPDM gaskets, CS frame
common_problems: Gibbsite scale and blockage in the port distribution areas
Gasket erosion
Loss of cooling in summer (cooling-tower approach) limits yield
operating_tips_and_key_points: Interstage cooling is the main summer bottleneck. Watch cooling-water supply temperature against end-of-train temperature
Flush the slurry side with liquor before any stop longer than a few minutes
sources: Alfa Laval WideGap PHE product literature (general; alumina-specific page not accessible)

equipment.name: Precipitator emptying (drain-down) pumps
equipment.function: Empty a bypassed precipitator to a running tank downstream before descaling, and return slurry after maintenance.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal slurry pump, rubber-lined, on a fixed plinth connected to a drain header (or a skid-mounted, diesel-driven mobile unit)
equipment.why_this_type: Robust for settled, coarse hydrate, and allows a tank to be fully emptied below the airlift's minimum level.
key_dimensions: ~300-600 m3/h, 30-40 m head, 110-200 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Takes slurry from the floor drain nozzle of the tank being emptied and pumps it to a running tank downstream, while the tank's agitator keeps running until the level is below the lower impeller. Flushing liquor is used to clear the line after each use.
details_to_model: DN300 drain header along the base of each row with knife-gate branch valves to each tank
Pump at the line end with flexible-hose suction connection points

equipment.name: Precipitation scale handling: scale pad, crusher and scale return
equipment.function: Receive gibbsite scale broken out of precipitators, launders and coolers, drain and wash entrained liquor from it, crush it, and return it to A04 grinding / A06 digestion, where it dissolves as high-grade, silica-free alumina.
equipment.type_selected: Bunded, sloped concrete scale pad with drainage to a sump; track-mounted mobile jaw or impact crusher with grizzly feeder; front-end loader and trucks to the A03/A04 mill-feed reclaim (crushed to -25 mm to suit A04 mill feed)
equipment.why_this_type: Scale is produced in campaigns (one tank every few weeks), so mobile equipment is cheaper than a fixed plant. Low-temperature digestion dissolves gibbsite scale readily, so recycling it recovers alumina and caustic instead of creating waste.

Mobile crusher ~15 x 3 x 4 m, 100-300 t/h (engineering estimate)

equipment.working_principle: Scale slabs removed through the tank access doors by excavator or loader are tipped on the pad. areas.layout_notes: Precipitation is the largest tank farm in the refinery after residue. It has 32 tanks of ~14 m dia x ~31 m: 2 lines x (3 agglomeration + 13 growth). Each line is laid out as a 2-row serpentine (8 + 8 tanks) at ~18 m centres, so a row is ~145 m long, with a ~10-12 m aisle between rows carrying the roof-level launder gallery, pipe rack and stair towers. Lines A and B sit side by side, separated by a ~20-25 m access road for mobile cranes (~200-300 t class) and descaling equipment. The approximate block footprint is ~165 m x 130 m (engineering estimate). The interstage cooler stations sit at grade near G-4/G-5 and G-8/G-9 of each line. The compressor house is at one end, and the scale pad is at the block edge with truck access. The PL distribution box is on a steel tower or on the AG-1 roofs, fed from the A11 rack. Precipitation is upstream of (higher than) A13 so G-13 slurry gravitates to classification. Tank roofs are at ~31-33 m, and drives and bridges peak at ~36-38 m. Bunds (110% of the largest tank) have sumps at low corners. The precipitation cooling-tower block (A20) is placed nearby but downwind, to avoid drift onto the walkways.
interfaces: A11: cooled PL (72-78 degC) and fill-temperature control
A13: fine seed and coarse seed returns; G-13 slurry out to classification

A20 utilities: precipitation cooling water (A12 ~5,000-7,000 m3/h, 45-70 MW; the A20 tower must be sized for the combined A11 + A12 + A18 + A19 demand, ~14,000-15,000 m3/h), compressed air for airlifts (own compressors), instrument air, power (32 agitators x 90-160 kW plus pumps and compressors; area load ~6-10 MW, engineering estimate), condensate for seal and flush
A04/A06: crushed gibbsite scale returned to mill feed
A19 oxalate plant: oxalate behaviour depends on fine-seed washing in A13
Maintenance: descaling contractors, UHP water-jetting units, mobile cranes; plant radiation-safety plan for radiometric gauges

areas.purpose: Separate the end-of-precipitation hydrate by size into (1) coarse product hydrate (to A14 filtration and A15 calcination), (2) coarse (growth) seed recycled to G-1, and (3) fine seed recycled to agglomeration after washing to remove co-precipitated sodium oxalate. A13 also recovers clear spent liquor (thickener overflow) for A11. Classification sets the product PSD and the seed balance.
areas.process_description: 1) G-13 slurry from each line (~1,850-2,200 m3/h, 450-700 g/L solids, 55-60 degC) flows by gravity launder into a primary cyclone feed tank (one per line). 2) Primary classification: slurry pumps feed a primary cyclone cluster. The cut size d50c is ~80-110 µm (engineering estimate), set so that the underflow solids rate equals the product rate (~370-420 t/h total). Underflow (coarsest particles, ~55-65% w/w solids) goes to the A14 product slurry tanks. Overflow goes to a secondary cyclone feed tank. 3) Secondary classification: secondary cyclones (finer cut, d50c ~40-60 µm, engineering estimate) produce an underflow of coarse seed (~1,050-1,800 t/h) and an overflow carrying fines (<~45 µm) and most of the liquor. 4) Coarse seed is dewatered on vacuum disc filters to remove spent liquor, which would otherwise dilute the supersaturation in growth. The cake is repulped with a cooled-PL side-stream (~500-900 m3/h from A11) in coarse seed repulp tanks and pumped to G-1. Because these tanks hold supersaturated PL in contact with a large seed area, they act as small precipitators and scale, so they are descaled on the same cycle as the precipitators. 5) Secondary overflow (~1,900-2,600 m3/h) goes to two tertiary (fine seed) thickeners. Clear overflow (spent liquor) gravitates to 11-TK-001. Thickened underflow (fine seed, ~400-700 g/L) is pumped to the fine seed drum filters. 6) Fine seed washing: on the drum filters the cake is washed with hot condensate (~85-95 degC). Sodium oxalate that co-precipitated on the fine seed during the cool end of precipitation dissolves, and the oxalate-rich wash filtrate goes to the A19 oxalate plant. This is critical in high-organic Darling-Range-type liquors and smaller for India East Coast bauxite. The washed fine seed is repulped with PL and pumped to AG-1. 7) Seed balance: if fines accumulate (nucleation event), excess fine seed can be sent to the product stream, returned to A06 digestion, or held in the fine seed tank. Classification therefore 'tunes' the PSD cycle. Alternative older design: three-stage gravity classifiers (primary, secondary and tertiary thickener/classifier vessels with rakes), still widely used.

equipment.name: Primary cyclone feed tanks (one per line)
equipment.function: Receive G-13 slurry by gravity and provide pump suction head and a little surge for the cyclone feed pumps.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical agitated carbon-steel tank with conical or sloped bottom, open or vented roof, top-entry agitator
equipment.why_this_type: Keeps coarse hydrate suspended at the pump suction; a small surge volume (~8-15 min) absorbs flow fluctuations.
key_dimensions: ~300-500 m3 working each; ~8-9 m ID x 8-9 m (engineering estimate)
Agitator ~30-55 kW
equipment.working_principle: A buffer pump-box: level control varies the speed of the duty cyclone feed pumps to keep the tank between limits and give a stable cyclone inlet pressure.
details_to_model: Launder inlet box with splash plate, top-entry agitator on a bridge, 2-3 DN500 suction nozzles near the bottom with knife-gate valves, radar level, overflow to bund, drain nozzle, access stair and roof platform, manway

key_dimensions: DN400-450 discharge; motor ~250-400 kW (engineering estimate)

DN450 riser pipes up the cyclone structure, rubber-lined long-radius bends

FIT magflow, DIT nuclear density (radiation-safety plan applies)

equipment.name: Primary hydrocyclone clusters (product classification)
equipment.function: Separate the coarsest hydrate (product, ~370-420 t/h total) from the circulating seed and liquor.
equipment.qty_operating: 2 clusters (one per line), each ~6 of 8 cyclones operating
equipment.type_selected: Radial manifold cyclone cluster of large hydrocyclones ~650-760 mm (26-30 in) dia, polyurethane- or rubber-lined (e.g. FLSmidth Krebs gMAX, Weir Cavex type), each with an inlet knife-gate valve
equipment.why_this_type: Compact, no moving parts, a sharp enough cut for hydrate, and easy to adjust (number of cyclones online, apex size, pressure). A modern alternative to gravity classifiers.
equipment.alternatives: Gravity primary classifier (large conical tank with rake and upward liquor flow, e.g. 15-25 m dia), as used in many older Bayer plants: gentler on particles (less attrition) but large and slow to respond.
key_dimensions: Cyclone ~660-760 mm ID, overall height ~3.5-4.5 m each; inlet ~250 x 150 mm rectangular; vortex finder ~250-300 mm; apex (spigot) ~120-180 mm (engineering estimate)
Cluster manifold ~3.5-4.5 m dia, overall cluster ~7-8 m dia x ~6 m high (engineering estimate)
Mounted on a steel structure with the cyclone deck at ~18-22 m

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (vendor range for 650-760 mm units)

equipment.working_principle: Slurry enters tangentially at high velocity and spins in the cylindrical section, creating a strong centrifugal field (hundreds of g). Coarse, heavy particles are thrown to the wall and spiral down the cone to the apex (underflow). Finer particles and most of the liquid move to the central upward vortex and leave through the vortex finder (overflow). The cut size is the particle size with a 50% chance of reaching either outlet. It depends on cyclone diameter, inlet pressure, slurry density and viscosity, and the vortex-finder and apex sizes. A 'roping' underflow means the apex is overloaded and coarse particles are being lost to the overflow; a 'spray' discharge is normal.
details_to_model: Circular steel manifold (distributor) with a central bottom DN450 feed inlet and radial branches; each branch has a knife-gate or pinch valve with actuator to a cyclone inlet head

Cyclones arranged radially, inclined slightly or vertical; each has an inlet head, cylinder section, 1-2 cone sections and an apex housing with replaceable spigot (bolted flanges and clamp rings visible)
Overflow pipes from each cyclone top (vortex-finder outlet, gooseneck) into a circular overflow launder or collection box above the manifold, with a vent/siphon breaker
Annular, open-top underflow collection launder with splash cover beneath the apexes, discharging to a chute to the A14 product tank
Manifold pressure gauge (diaphragm seal), PT, sampling point
Steel support structure with grating deck, handrails, stair access, monorail and 2-5 t hoist for cyclone change-out
Wear indicators, labels 'C1-C8'
hazards_and_safety: Pressurised hot caustic slurry at height: liner wear-through causes jets; inspect liners
Spray from the apex: splash enclosure
Working at height and manual handling of heavy cyclone sections (~200-500 kg): use the hoist
instrumentation_and_control: Overflow and underflow sampling for PSD
equipment.materials: Steel casing with gum rubber or polyurethane liner; ceramic (alumina) apex liners optional
common_problems: Apex blockage by scale chunks
Liner wear at inlet and apex
Roping at high solids loads
operating_tips_and_key_points: Product rate is set by the number of cyclones in use and the apex size. Change one variable at a time and check the product PSD
sources: Wills' Mineral Processing Technology, 8th ed., Wills and Finch 2016 (hydrocyclone theory)
FLSmidth Krebs gMAX and Weir Cavex product literature (general size ranges)

equipment.why_this_type: As for the primary feed

details_to_model: Same visual set as the primary feed tanks and pumps; the tanks sit under the primary cyclone structure so overflow gravitates in
hazards_and_safety: As primary

equipment.name: Secondary hydrocyclone clusters (seed classification)
equipment.function: Split primary overflow into coarse seed (underflow) and fines plus liquor (overflow).
equipment.type_selected: Radial cyclone cluster with ~500-660 mm (20-26 in) lined hydrocyclones

Overflow pipe to the tertiary thickener feed launder
hazards_and_safety: As primary

equipment.name: Coarse seed filters
equipment.function: Dewater coarse seed (secondary cyclone underflow) to a cake of ~8-15% moisture, removing spent liquor before the seed returns to growth.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary vacuum disc filter (8-10 discs, ~3.9-4.5 m dia), polypropylene sector bags, snap-blow cake discharge, bottom-feed agitated trough
equipment.why_this_type: Disc filters give the largest filter area per floor area for very fast-filtering coarse hydrate. Snap-blow discharge is reliable. No washing is needed for coarse seed.
equipment.alternatives: Horizontal belt or table filters (larger footprint); vacuum drum filters; or no seed filtration (cyclone underflow direct to G-1: simpler, but it dilutes supersaturation and lowers yield).
key_dimensions: ~120-180 m2 filter area per unit (engineering estimate)
Disc dia ~3.9-4.5 m, 8-10 discs on a central hollow shaft; trough ~6-8 m long x 4.5 m wide x 3 m deep; unit ~9 x 5 x 5 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Each disc is made of ~20-30 sectors covered with filter-cloth bags, connected through the hollow central shaft to a control valve (filter head). As a sector dips into the agitated slurry trough, vacuum pulls liquor through the cloth and a cake forms on both faces. Above the slurry the sector stays under vacuum and air drawn through the cake dewaters it. Just before the scraper the control valve switches the sector to a brief compressed-air 'snap blow' that inflates the cloth and drops the cake into chutes between the discs. Filtrate and air go to a receiver (separator), where liquor drains to a filtrate pump and air goes to the vacuum pump.
details_to_model: Steel trough with paddle or rocker agitator underneath (geared motor at the side); slurry feed distributor along the trough; overflow weir box
Central shaft with discs, each sector visible as a wedge-shaped bag with clamping strips; filter head (control valve) at one or both ends with large DN300-400 vacuum pipes
Cake scrapers or deflectors between discs; discharge chutes down to the repulp tank below
Drive: geared motor with VSD at the shaft end; guards
Hood or covers with vapour extraction; inspection doors
Low-pressure cloth-wash spray headers above the discs
Filter floor ~10-12 m above grade (gravity discharge to the repulp tanks below); 5-10 t maintenance hoist over each filter
hazards_and_safety: Rotating discs and scrapers: guards and LOTO before cloth changes
Hot caustic vapour and splash inside the hood
Vacuum system: implosion of receivers; snap-blow compressed air
Slippery floors
equipment.materials: Carbon steel trough and frame; PP sectors; PP monofilament cloth; 316 SS control-valve wear plates
common_problems: Cloth blinding with fines or scale
Sector bag tears
Cake not discharging (low snap-blow pressure)

equipment.name: Coarse seed repulp tanks and coarse seed charge pumps
equipment.function: Repulp coarse seed cake with a cooled-PL side-stream and pump it to G-1 of each line.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated CS tanks (~200-400 m3) with high-power agitators for dense slurry; horizontal slurry pumps with VSD
equipment.why_this_type: Dense, coarse seed slurry (~1,000-1,200 g/L) needs vigorous agitation and robust pumps
key_dimensions: Tank ~7-8 m dia x 7-8 m; agitator ~55-90 kW; pump ~500-900 m3/h, 40-50 m head, 250-400 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Filter cake falls from the disc filters into the tank, where agitation and a metered PL addition form a pumpable slurry. Flow control on the seed pump, cascaded from the seed-charge setpoint (ratio to PL flow), sets the growth-stage seed charge. The tank holds supersaturated PL with a very large seed area, so precipitation starts here and the tank walls and agitator scale like a precipitator.
details_to_model: Tank under the disc filter discharge chutes; top-entry agitator; PL inlet; suction nozzles; DN400-500 seed line rising to the precipitation launder gallery; magflow and nuclear density gauge on the seed line
Large shell access door for descaling, as on the precipitators
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry; confined space; rotating equipment; scale fall during descaling
instrumentation_and_control: Seed mass flow = magflow x density (DCS)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel; nozzle/attachment welds PWHT'd (72-78 degC PL service, as AG tanks)

equipment.name: Tertiary (fine seed) thickeners
equipment.function: Settle fine hydrate from the secondary cyclone overflow, producing a clear spent-liquor overflow and a thickened fine seed underflow.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each sized for ~60-70% of flow to allow short outages)
equipment.type_selected: Conventional or high-rate bridge-supported / centre-column thickener, flat or shallow-cone floor, with feedwell, rake drive and flocculant dosing
equipment.why_this_type: Fine hydrate settles slowly. Thickening recovers fine seed and clarifies spent liquor in one unit.
equipment.alternatives: Tertiary gravity classifier (older design); cyclones plus clarifier; direct fine seed filtration (no thickener).
key_dimensions: ~35-45 m dia each, side wall ~4-6 m, centre depth ~6-8 m (engineering estimate: rise rate ~0.7-1.3 m/h on ~950-1,300 m3/h per thickener)
Centre column or bridge with rake drive ~2.5 m dia; feedwell ~6-8 m dia x 3-4 m deep
equipment.working_principle: Feed enters a central feedwell that dissipates energy and mixes in flocculant, so fine particles form flocs that settle quickly. Clear liquor rises to a peripheral overflow launder. Solids settle, compact into a bed and are raked slowly toward the central underflow cone, where pumps withdraw them. The rake drive measures torque: high torque warns of a heavy bed or scale, and the rakes are lifted automatically if torque keeps rising.
details_to_model: Large circular concrete or steel tank with peripheral overflow launder (V-notch weirs and scum baffle) and a launder outlet box
Access bridge from the edge to the centre (~20 m) with walkway, handrails, flocculant and feed pipes
Central drive unit: large slewing ring gear, hydraulic or electric motors, rake lift mechanism, torque indicator
Rake arms (2 long + 2 short) with angled blades and scraper; feedwell hanging below the drive
Underflow cone outlet with 2 underflow pumps in a tunnel or below-grade pit (or at grade beside a tank raised on steel legs)
Vapour visible over the warm liquor surface
hazards_and_safety: Large open surface of hot caustic liquor: drowning or immersion hazard; handrails on the bridge
Underflow tunnel: confined space, flooding risk
Rake drive pinch points
instrumentation_and_control: Underflow density (nuclear) controls the underflow pump VSD
equipment.materials: Carbon steel (or concrete with caustic-resistant coating), CS rakes
common_problems: Scale on rakes and walls; high torque
Fines carry-over to spent liquor (it then scales PHEs and evaporators)

equipment.name: Tertiary thickener underflow pumps
equipment.function: Withdraw fine seed underflow to the fine seed filters.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal slurry pumps with VSD (density control)
equipment.why_this_type: Dense fine slurry
key_dimensions: ~150-250 m3/h each, 25-35 m head, 45-90 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Speed control holds the underflow density setpoint, which in turn controls the thickener bed inventory.
details_to_model: Pumps in a tunnel or pit beside the cone; dilution/flush connection; knife-gate valves; density gauge
hazards_and_safety: Confined space in tunnels; flood alarm

equipment.name: Fine seed filters with oxalate wash
equipment.function: Dewater fine seed and wash it with hot condensate to dissolve co-precipitated sodium oxalate (sent to the A19 oxalate plant) before the seed returns to agglomeration.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary vacuum drum filter with cake-wash spray headers and scraper or belt discharge
equipment.why_this_type: Drum filters allow a well-defined wash zone on the cake, which a disc filter does not. Throughput is moderate.
equipment.alternatives: Horizontal belt filter (better counter-current washing, larger footprint); repulp-and-thicken washing.
key_dimensions: ~50-80 m2 each, drum ~3.5-4 m dia x 5-6.5 m face (engineering estimate)
Overall ~8 x 5 x 5 m
equipment.working_principle: The drum rotates partly submerged in the slurry trough. Vacuum through internal drainage pipes forms a cake on the cloth. As the cake rises, hot condensate sprays wash it. Sodium oxalate is far more soluble in water than in strong spent liquor, so it dissolves and is drawn through as a separate wash filtrate. The filter valve keeps mother and wash filtrate apart, so the oxalate-rich wash goes to the oxalate plant. The cake is then dewatered and scraped off at the discharge point.
details_to_model: Cylindrical drum with longitudinal filtrate-pipe ribs and cloth caulked into grooves (or wire-wound)
Trough with oscillating agitator; filter valve at one trunnion end with 2 outlet pipes (mother and wash filtrate)
2-3 wash spray headers with flat-fan nozzles above the drum; scraper blade and discharge chute
Drive gearmotor and girth gear; hood with vapour extraction
hazards_and_safety: Rotating drum nip points; hot water and caustic sprays; vapour
instrumentation_and_control: Wash flow ratio to solids; drum speed; vacuum; trough level
Wash filtrate conductivity or oxalate analysis (lab)
equipment.materials: CS drum and trough; 316 SS spray headers; PP cloth
common_problems: Cloth blinding by fines
Poor oxalate removal if the wash ratio is low; oxalate then destabilises in precipitation (fines, high soda)
sources: Hind A.R., Bhargava S.K., Grocott S.C., 'The surface chemistry of Bayer process solids: a review', Colloids and Surfaces A 146 (1999) 359-374

equipment.working_principle: Seed mass flow is calculated from magflow x density and ratioed to the agglomeration PL flow.
details_to_model: Tank with agitator, PL repulp inlet, suction nozzles, seed line to the AG-1 head boxes, density gauge, magflow
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry

equipment.name: Oxalate wash filtrate tank and pumps
equipment.function: Collect oxalate-rich wash filtrate from the fine seed filters and send it to the A19 oxalate plant.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical CS tank ~150-300 m3 with centrifugal process pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Simple surge

areas.layout_notes: A13 sits immediately downstream of (and at a lower grade than) the precipitation G-13 tanks, so slurry gravitates from G-13 via launders to the primary cyclone feed tanks. The classification building is a multi-level steel structure (~40 x 30 m, ~25-28 m high, engineering estimate). Grade holds the feed tanks, slurry pumps and repulp tanks. The seed filter floor (disc and drum filters) is at ~10-12 m, above the repulp tanks for gravity discharge. The primary and secondary cyclone decks are at ~18-22 m, above their feed tanks. Overhead cranes (10-20 t) serve the filter floor, and monorails serve the cyclones. The vacuum pump hall is at grade on one side. The two tertiary thickeners (~40 m dia) sit beside the building, higher than the spent-liquor tank (11-TK-001) so overflow gravitates to it. The A14 product filter building adjoins on the calcination side so primary underflow pipe runs are short. Floors are bunded and sloped to sumps, and safety showers are at every level.

A11: cooled-PL side-streams for repulping; tertiary overflow and filtrates to spent-liquor tank 11-TK-001

areas.purpose: Filter the product hydrate (primary cyclone underflow), wash out entrained spent liquor with hot condensate to minimise soluble soda carried to calcination and to recover caustic, and deliver a cake of ~6-10% free moisture to the A15 calciner hydrate storage at ~370-420 t/h dry. A14 also holds a product-hydrate slurry storage buffer so precipitation can keep running through a calciner outage.
areas.process_description: 1) Primary cyclone underflow (~55-65% w/w solids, ~185-210 t/h dry per line) enters the agitated product slurry tanks. 2) Filter feed pumps deliver slurry on a ring main to horizontal rotating table (pan) vacuum filters, 4 operating + 1 standby. 3) On each filter the cake forms in ~30-60 s, and the mother liquor (spent liquor) is drawn off to the mother-filtrate receiver and returned to 11-TK-001. 4) Two-stage counter-current displacement washing: hot condensate (85-95 degC) goes on the final wash zone, and that wash filtrate is recycled as the first wash. Weak wash filtrate returns to the liquor circuit (spent-liquor tank or residue washing, per the plant water balance). 5) The cake is dewatered by air drawn through it (dry zone), then discharged by a helical scroll to a collecting conveyor. A low-pressure air blow-back loosens the residual heel, and high-pressure sprays wash the cloth each revolution. 6) The cake (6-10% free moisture; soluble Na2O typically <0.05%, engineering estimate) travels by belt conveyor with a belt scale and automatic sampler to the A15 hydrate storage or calciner feed bins. 7) Buffer storage (added after review): when a calciner is down (each is 3,500 t/d nameplate against ~5,780 t/d plant rate) or the filters are down, surplus primary underflow is diverted to two large agitated product-hydrate storage tanks. These give ~3-5 days of buffer at the one-calciner deficit. The stored slurry is reclaimed to the filter feed tanks when calcining capacity returns. Total Na2O in the final SGA (~0.30-0.45%) is mostly occluded in the crystal lattice during precipitation and is not removed by washing; washing removes only surface liquor.

equipment.name: Product hydrate filters
equipment.function: Form, wash (2-stage counter-current, hot condensate) and dewater the product hydrate cake and discharge it to the product conveyor.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal rotating table (pan) vacuum filter: annular table of radial cells under a shared cloth, rotary valve, helical scroll cake discharge (Dorr-Oliver/FLSmidth, Gaudfrin type), ~70-100 m2 each
equipment.why_this_type: The horizontal cake allows excellent displacement washing with sharp separation of mother, wash and weak filtrates. It suits fast-draining, granular hydrate at high throughput, has a long industry record for product hydrate, and gives a clean continuous discharge.
equipment.alternatives: Horizontal vacuum belt filter (similar washing, longer footprint, more cloth tracking issues); rotary drum filter with washing (less effective on a curved cake); tilting-pan filter (very good washing, more complex mechanics).
key_dimensions: Effective area ~70-100 m2 per filter (engineering estimate: ~400-420 t/h / (4 x 1.0-1.5 t/m2.h))
Table outer dia ~10.5-12.5 m, inner dia ~3-4 m, cell depth ~150-250 mm, rim height ~200 mm (engineering estimate)
~24-36 radial cells
Overall with drive, valve and hood ~14 x 14 m footprint; table top at the filter floor (~6-8 m above grade)
equipment.working_principle: The table is a large horizontal ring divided into radial cells, each with a drainage grid and cloth and each piped to a central rotary valve beneath. As the table rotates, every cell passes through fixed zones set by the valve. (1) Feed: a feed box spreads slurry evenly and vacuum draws the mother liquor to the mother receiver. (2) First wash: recycled wash filtrate displaces the remaining mother liquor. (3) Final wash: hot condensate displaces the first-wash liquor; the wash filtrates are kept separate for counter-current reuse. (4) Dry zone: air pulled through drains the cake to 6-10% moisture. (5) Discharge: a slowly rotating helical scroll set a few mm above the cloth sweeps the cake radially outward over the rim into a chute, and a low-pressure blow-back through the valve lifts the heel. (6) Cloth wash: high-pressure sprays clean the cloth before the cell returns to the feed zone. Displacement washing works best with a level, crack-free cake, which is why the horizontal geometry is used.

Discharge hopper or chute at the outer rim to the collecting conveyor below
Cloth-wash spray bar and LP blow-back air header
Hood/canopy over the table with vapour extraction duct to an exhaust fan or scrubber; hinged inspection doors; lighting

areas.layout_notes: The product filter building (~60 x 30 m, ~20 m to eaves, engineering estimate) adjoins A13 and is as close as possible to the A15 hydrate storage and calciners, keeping conveyors short. Ground floor (0 m): product slurry tanks, feed pumps, filtrate receivers and pumps, the vacuum pump hall (acoustically separated) and the wash-water tank and heater. Filter floor (~6-8 m): 5 table filters in a row at ~16 m centres with hoods, and the feed and wash headers. Collecting conveyor 14-CV-001 runs under the filter discharge chutes at ~3-4 m, then turns onto an inclined transfer gallery to A15. A 20 t overhead crane covers the filter floor, with a ground-floor drop zone. The two product-hydrate storage tanks (~21 m dia x ~28 m) stand outside the building in their own bund between A13 and A14, with the reclaim pump bay beside them. The building is open-sided or louvred for ventilation, floors are bunded and sloped to sumps, and safety showers are at each floor and stair.

decisions.finding: A12 residence time ignores seed slurry volume (growth ~21-25 h, total ~28-32 h, not 25-30 / 32-38 h)
decisions.reason: The arithmetic criticism is correct: the growth flow must include seed solids and cake liquor. Recalculated, the growth flow is ~3,700-4,400 m3/h. The reviewer's 4,000-4,800 m3/h double-counts the coarse-seed repulp liquor, which is a PL side-stream already inside the 3,000-3,300 m3/h. Of the two options offered, I added one growth tank per line (G-13; 32 tanks total, 12 growth operating per line), which restores ~23-29 h growth and ~31-38 h total. Tags, flows, layout (2 rows of 8 per line) and the plant-wide numbers were updated. Agglomeration residence was also recalculated (~7-11 h), because ~600-1,100 m3/h of PL is now shown going to seed repulping. Verification of the spent A/C 0.36-0.38 with a precipitation model is carried as an open question.

decisions.finding: A11 'below the dew point of the regenerative exchangers' wording is wrong
decisions.reason: Terminology error. Replaced with 'below the temperature achievable against spent liquor (the approach limit of the regenerative PHEs)'.

decisions.finding: Cooling-water balance does not close (A20 tower 10,000 m3/h / 30-40 MW interstage vs A12 45-70 MW)
decisions.reason: The conclusion is accepted: the A12 interstage duty of 45-70 MW stands, and A20 should size the tower for ~14,000-15,000 m3/h. My area values were re-checked. The reviewer's evidence factor ('4.18 MW per 1,000 m3/h per 10 K') is wrong: 1,000 m3/h of water over a 10 K range removes ~11.6 MW. The A12 5,000-7,000 m3/h for 45-70 MW is therefore consistent. The A11 trim-cooler numbers were corrected to normal 7-15 MW / 600-1,300 m3/h and design 25-30 MW / ~2,600 m3/h. Tower sizing is owned by A20.

decisions.finding: Carbon steel PL piping is not below the NACE SP0403 PWHT line; PWHT is required
decisions.reason: PL at 98-104 degC and ~14 wt% NaOH-equivalent is in the PWHT region. Applied plant-wide philosophy to A11 (PL piping and strainers, heated spent-liquor piping at 82-90 degC, CIP system). Extended to nozzle/attachment welds (stress-relieved insert plates) on AG-1..3, G-1..G-4 and the coarse-seed repulp tanks (72-78 degC, at or near the line). Spent liquor <62 degC, cool growth tanks and hydrate storage are excluded. The chart check against the current NACE edition remains for the materials owner.

decisions.finding: Precipitator bottom strake 28-32 mm overstated; wide-gap PHE slurry velocity 0.3-0.6 m/s too low
decisions.reason: Shell: accepted in substance. Using API 650 Sd = 173 MPa for A516-70 (the reviewer used 160 MPa, which is the value for a lower grade), td = 4.9 x 14 x 30.7 x 1.55/173 + 3 ≈ 22 mm and tt ≈ 11 mm, so the bottom strake is now ~22-26 mm. The top strake is ~8-10 mm; the API 650 minimum for D <15 m is 5 mm, not 6 mm. Velocity: accepted that 0.3-0.6 m/s is too low. The design is set to 0.6-1.0 m/s (minimum ~0.5 with low-flow trip and automatic liquor flush) rather than 0.8-1.2 m/s. A check calculation (~35-50 slurry channels per unit, ~150-250 m2) shows 0.6-1.0 m/s fits the required area in single pass, whereas 0.8-1.2 m/s would force fewer channels or multi-pass with higher dP. Unit area and pump head were updated accordingly.

decisions.finding: Operating tip about not stopping flow with the agitator running points at the wrong risk
decisions.reason: Replaced with the reviewer's wording: bypass via launder gates, keep the agitator running until the level is below the lower impeller, never stop agitation on a tank holding slurry, and never open bottom doors until the tank is empty and washed. The same logic was applied to the emptying-pump description.

decisions.finding: Missing: A14 product hydrate slurry storage tanks with reclaim pumps
decisions.reason: Added 14-TK-004/005 (2 x ~8,000-10,000 m3, ~21 m x 28 m) with 14-AG-004/005 agitators and 14-PP-013..016 reclaim pumps (2+2). This holds ~13,000-22,000 t of hydrate, ~3-5 days of the one-calciner deficit (2 x 3,500 t/d against ~5,780 t/d). Wet-cake storage at A15 remains with the A15 owner.

decisions.finding: Missing: precipitation scale handling and return to digestion
decisions.reason: Added 12-SH-001 scale pad and 12-CR-001 mobile crusher with return of -25 mm scale to the A04 mill feed (~5,000-20,000 t/yr, engineering estimate).

decisions.finding: Consistency: PL temperature A10 95-102 vs A11 100-106 degC
decisions.reason: A11 inlet aligned to 98-104 degC; PHE duty recalculated to ~80-100 MW.

decisions.finding: Consistency: 'A?' references for evaporation/digestion/oxalate
decisions.reason: Replaced with A18 (evaporation and liquor blending), A06 (digestion), A19 (oxalate plant), A15 (calcination), A20 (utilities), A07/A18 (condensate).

decisions.finding: Consistency: seed repulp tanks act as small precipitators and will scale
decisions.reason: Noted in the A13 process description and the 13-TK-005/006 entry (descaling access door, kW trend, PWHT of nozzle welds).

decisions.finding: Consistency: spent-liquor routing between A11 and A18 must be decided
decisions.reason: Defined the A11 side: all heated spent liquor goes to A18, and A18 owns the split between evaporation (~1,700 m3/h) and the blend bypass. The final split remains an A18 decision.

decisions.finding: HSE: plant radiation-safety plan for radiometric gauges; eyewash flushing up to 60 min for alkali eye exposure
decisions.reason: Added to A11 pump hazards, A12 tank hazards and safety showers, and the A12/A13 interfaces.

open_questions: STATUS (in reply to the user's 'what is the current status?'): Heat interchange (A11), precipitation (A12), classification (A13) and hydrate filtration (A14) have now been reconciled with the expert review. All 6 findings were dispositioned (4 accepted, 2 partly accepted), 2 missing items were added (hydrate storage, scale handling), and the plant-wide PL temperature, area numbering and PWHT philosophy were aligned. Live web verification was again unavailable (WebSearch returned HTTP 403), so all changed numbers rest on mass and heat balances, API 650 and standard Bayer literature and are marked as engineering estimates.

Precipitation model check: confirm that spent A/C 0.36-0.38 is reachable with ~31-38 h total residence, 32 tanks (30 online), a 72-78 degC fill and a 55-60 degC end temperature, at the stated seed charges.

Heat of precipitation of gibbsite (~20-30 kJ/mol assumed) and ambient losses from uninsulated precipitators (~15-30 MW assumed) should be verified in the plant heat balance, because together they set the interstage cooling duty.
Precipitation flowsheet: confirm Australian-style two-stage (agglomeration + growth) as the reference, versus single-stage.
PL cooling technology: regenerative PHEs (selected) versus multi-stage vacuum flash cooling; SME to confirm which is more representative of the chosen reference plants.
Interstage cooling: wide-gap PHE (selected, 0.6-1.0 m/s) versus vacuum flash or spiral exchangers; the vendor should confirm the channel velocity, dP and plugging margin for 450-700 g/L hydrate.
Site climate for cooling water (India East Coast ~32-34 degC supply vs Western Australia) strongly affects end-of-train temperature and summer yield.
Precipitator standard size: 4,500 m3 (14 x 31 m) kept for asset reuse; newer plants use ~6,000-8,000 m3+ tanks, which would cut the count to ~20-24.
Classification route (hydrocyclones vs gravity classifiers) and inclusion of coarse-seed filtration should be confirmed for the reference plant.
Product hydrate filter type: horizontal table filter selected; confirm versus belt or tilting-pan filters.
Oxalate management: fine-seed washing assumes high-organic liquor; for India East Coast bauxite it may be smaller. The A19 owner should confirm the oxalate route and load.
Spent-liquor split at A18 (evaporation vs blend bypass) and the destination of weak hydrate wash filtrate (spent tank vs residue washing) belong to the plant water and caustic balance owners.
Cooling tower sizing (A20) must be raised to ~14,000-15,000 m3/h to cover A11 (design ~2,600), A12 (5,000-7,000), A18 and A19.
Materials owner to confirm the PWHT boundary on the current NACE SP0403 chart, especially for agglomeration tanks at 72-78 degC.
SGA specification for the reference smelter customer (Na2O, -45 µm, -20 µm, attrition index, BET), which sets precipitation and classification targets.

areas.purpose: Turn washed product hydrate (gibbsite, Al(OH)3) into smelter-grade alumina (SGA). Two identical gas suspension calciner trains with holding vessels (GSC-HV) dry, dehydrate (calcine) and cool it. The area also holds a product-hydrate slurry buffer so that a calciner outage does not force an immediate cut in refinery output. Calcination sets product LOI, BET surface area and alpha-alumina content. It cannot remove soda or fix weak particles: Na2O and particle size come from precipitation and hydrate washing (A13/A14). This is the refinery's largest single fuel user and CO2 source.
areas.process_description:
TECHNOLOGY CHOICE: The reference plant uses the FLSmidth-type Gas Suspension Calciner with Holding Vessel (GSC-HV), 2 trains x 3,500 t/d nameplate. The alternative is the Metso Outotec (ex-Lurgi) Circulating Fluid Bed (CFB) calciner. Both are proven at about 3,000-4,500 t/d per unit with similar fuel use (about 2.8-3.1 GJ/t). GSC was chosen for three reasons. (a) Its stages suit the training curriculum: venturi flash dryer, 2 preheater cyclone stages, stationary furnace, holding vessel, 4 cooling-cyclone stages, fluid bed cooler and ESP. (b) The whole gas path runs under suction from one ID fan, so there are no high-pressure primary-air blowers and dust cannot leak outward. (c) It holds little material, so it starts and stops quickly. CFB differences are noted under 'alternatives'.
STEP 0 - Hydrate buffer (15-TK-001/002): Normally, product hydrate slurry from the A13 product classification goes straight to the A14 product filters. When one calciner is down (refractory relines take about 2-3 weeks per unit per year, plus trips), the shortfall is about 3,500 t/d of dry hydrate. That slurry (about 40-50 wt% solids in spent liquor) is diverted to two agitated storage tanks, which hold about 4-5 days of the shortfall. Afterwards it is pumped back to the product filters at a controlled rate while both calciners run at up to about 110-121 % of average demand. Outages longer than the buffer need a planned cut in refinery rate.
STEP 1 - Feed: Washed hydrate filter cake from the A14 product hydrate filters falls by chute or short belt into each train's calciner feed bin. The cake is at 6-10 % free moisture and 50-80 degC, with about 0.20-0.30 % Na2O on a dry hydrate basis and d50 about 80-100 um. Twin variable-speed screw feeders meter it into the venturi flash dryer.
STEP 2 - Drying (stage A01/P01): Gas leaving preheater cyclone P02 at about 350-420 degC enters through a venturi throat at the bottom of the dryer riser. It lifts the hydrate and the free moisture flashes off in about 1-2 s. Two dryer cyclones (P01) separate the dried hydrate at about 140-170 degC. The gas (about 140-170 degC, about 45-55 vol% H2O) goes to the ESP, then the ID fan, then the stack.
STEP 3 - Preheating and partial dehydration (P02): P01 solids are injected into the riser duct that carries furnace gas (about 950-1050 degC) from the P04 cyclones. In about a second they reach about 320-400 degC and start to dehydrate: 2 Al(OH)3 -> Al2O3 + 3 H2O(g). The reaction absorbs about +205 kJ/mol, or about 2.0 GJ/t Al2O3 including vaporising the water (thermochemical calculation from standard heats of formation). The heat in the furnace gas limits how far it goes in P02. A heat balance gives roughly 35-60 % of the bound water released here, with solids LOI falling from 34.6 % to roughly 15-25 % (engineering estimate). Furnace and HV complete the rest. Fine particles heated fast go gibbsite -> chi-alumina, while coarse particles in humid gas partly go to boehmite (AlOOH) first.
STEP 4 - Calcination (P04 furnace): The partly dehydrated solids enter the lower cone of the refractory-lined stationary furnace. Combustion air from cooling cyclone C01 arrives at about 650-800 degC. Natural gas is injected through a ring of burners in the cone and burns with the solids in suspension. Gas and solids leave the top at about 950-1050 degC, a set point that controls LOI and BET, with 2-4 % excess O2. Gas residence time in the furnace is only about 1-3 s. The furnace separation cyclones (P04) split the solids from the gas, which goes on to P02 (step 3).
STEP 5 - Holding vessel (HV): Solids from P04 drop into an air-fluidised, refractory-lined holding vessel. They stay about 10-30 min (engineering estimate) at about 920-1000 degC, which finishes the last hydroxyl removal. With the HV the furnace can run about 50-100 degC cooler than a GSC without one for the same LOI (vendor claim). That gives higher BET, lower alpha-alumina and lower fuel use. HV off-air returns to the furnace.
STEP 6 - Suspension cooling (C01-C04): Hot alumina passes counter-current through 4 cooling-cyclone stages. The ID fan draws ambient air, plus the FBC exhaust air, in at the C04 riser. The air takes up heat stage by stage and becomes the furnace combustion air. Alumina cools from about 950-1000 degC to about 180-280 degC, and the air heats from about 30-60 degC to about 650-800 degC. In this service the air carries about 15-20 % more heat per degree than the alumina (about 125,000-145,000 Nm3/h of air vs 146 t/h of alumina per train). An ideal 4-stage balance therefore gives at most about 730 degC air and about 160 degC alumina, and real stages fall a little short of that (engineering estimate).
STEP 7 - Fluid bed cooler (FBC): Alumina from C04 enters a multi-compartment air-fluidised bed. Water-cooled tube bundles immersed in the bed bring it to about 70-90 degC (duty about 5-8 MW per train). The heat goes through plate heat exchangers to make hot wash water for the hydrate filters, with a cooling tower as trim. Warm FBC exhaust air goes into the C04 air inlet so its heat is recovered.
STEP 8 - Product: The FBC overflows into airslides feeding the dense-phase conveyors to the product silos (A16). An auto-sampler takes samples for LOI, MOI, BET, alpha, PSD, Na2O and impurities and makes hourly composites.
PHASE CHEMISTRY: Gibbsite goes to chi or boehmite, then gamma, delta and theta (the transition aluminas, BET 60-80 m2/g in SGA), and finally alpha (corundum). Alpha forms significantly only above about 1100-1200 degC and is held below about 10 % in SGA, because it dissolves slowly in cryolite and lowers HF scrubbing capacity at the smelter. Raising calcination temperature lowers LOI and BET and raises alpha. Holding solids longer at moderate temperature (the HV) lowers LOI and keeps BET high.
HIGH-TEMPERATURE (BOEHMITIC) PLANTS: they use the same calciner technology. The differences are upstream: digestion at 240-270 degC with flash/heat-recovery trains. Hydrate quality depends on precipitation practice, not on the digestion route.
GAS SIDE: the whole GSC gas path is under negative pressure, from about -0.5 kPa at the C04 air inlet to about -9 to -13 kPa at the ID fan inlet (engineering estimate). That covers 7 cyclone stages in series plus the venturi, furnace, ESP and ducts. The ESP outlet dust limit is 30-50 mg/Nm3 (typical licence, set by jurisdiction). The off-gas is very humid (dew point about 78-85 degC), so all ducts, the ESP and the stack must run well above about 120 degC.

streams.flow: ~240-250 t/h wet per train at nameplate (~223 t/h dry = 1.53 t dry hydrate/t Al2O3 x 146 t/h); plant ~395-410 t/h wet at 241 t/h Al2O3

equipment.name: Product hydrate slurry storage tanks (calciner-outage buffer) with agitators and reclaim pumps
equipment.function: Store product hydrate slurry while one calciner is down, then return it to the product filters, so that a calciner outage does not immediately cut refinery output.
equipment.qty_operating: 2 tanks (normally low level, filled during outages); 1 reclaim pump
equipment.type_selected: Vertical flat-bottom (or shallow-cone) carbon-steel tanks with top-entry hydrofoil agitators (precipitator-type), centrifugal slurry reclaim pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Many Bayer refineries keep hydrate storage ahead of calcination. Holding the hydrate as slurry in spent liquor uses the same tank and agitator design as precipitation, is easy to reclaim by pump, and needs no extra filtration step. A covered wet-cake shed with front-end loaders is the alternative, but it handles cake twice and makes dust and contamination risks worse.
key_dimensions: Working volume ~8,000-10,000 m3 each, e.g. ~22-24 m ID x ~24-26 m tall (engineering estimate)
Capacity ~15,000-17,000 t dry hydrate total (~1.18 m3 slurry per t hydrate at 50 wt%), ~4-5 days of the one-calciner shortfall (engineering estimate)
Agitator ~200-300 kW, 2-3 hydrofoil impellers on a ~25 m shaft (engineering estimate)
Reclaim pumps ~200-400 m3/h at ~30-40 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (limited by spare calciner and filter capacity)

equipment.working_principle: While one calciner is down, a diverter on the product hydrate slurry line sends the surplus slurry into these tanks. The agitators keep the coarse hydrate (d50 about 90 um) suspended, and the tank level rises over the outage. The liquor is spent liquor, so the hydrate is stable and grows only slightly. When both calciners are back, the reclaim pumps return slurry to the A14 product filters at a controlled rate. Both calciners then run above the average rate (up to 3,500 t/d each) until the tanks are drawn down. Agitators must never stop with solids in the tank, because coarse hydrate settles fast and sets into a hard bed.
details_to_model: Two large cylindrical tanks with fixed roof and bridge-mounted top-entry agitator drives (motor, gearbox and support beam), roof walkway and handrails
Inlet nozzle with downcomer; side-outlet suction nozzles near the bottom with knife-gate isolation valves; overflow and drain nozzles; flushing liquor connections
Slurry pumps in a bunded pump bay with suction and discharge knife-gate valves, pressure gauges and flush connections
Radar level transmitter, agitator power/torque monitoring, bottom scour/sparge connections; external spiral stair, roof manhole, shell manways (2)
Concrete bund with sump pump; safety showers at stair base and pump bay
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spent liquor (~240 g/L as Na2CO3 at ~60 degC): burns and eye damage; face shield, gauntlets, safety showers
Confined-space entry only after draining, washing, isolation of the agitator (LOTO) and gas test
Agitator failure with a full tank: risk of sanded tank and overloaded drive on restart
common_problems: Hydrate settling and scaling on walls and impellers if the tank stands half-full for long periods
Pump wear and line plugging on reclaim
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the tanks near empty in normal operation so the full buffer is available
Agree the outage plan with precipitation: past ~4-5 days the refinery rate must be cut
instrumentation_and_control: Tank LT with high/high-high alarms; agitator current and torque trip
Reclaim FIC to A14 filter feed; slurry density meter
equipment.materials: Carbon steel tanks (caustic service below the NACE SP0403 SCC limit at <70 degC with PWHT of nozzles per the owner's caustic materials philosophy); hard-metal or rubber-lined pumps
sources: Common Bayer practice (hydrate storage ahead of calcination); review finding (mechanical)

equipment.name: Calciner hydrate feed bin
equipment.function: Buffers wet hydrate from the product filter so that pulses in cake discharge do not upset the steady calciner feed.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical steel bin with steep conical (or wedge/transition) mass-flow hopper, load-cell mounted
equipment.why_this_type: Wet hydrate (6-10 % moisture) is cohesive and bridges. A steep, low-friction mass-flow hopper feeding twin screws gives first-in-first-out flow and a measurable inventory for feed control.
key_dimensions: Diameter ~6-8 m, cylinder ~6-8 m, cone ~5-7 m (engineering estimate)
Live capacity ~150-300 t (~0.6-1.2 h at 240 t/h) (engineering estimate)
Hopper half-angle ~15-25 deg from vertical, lined (engineering estimate, to be confirmed by Jenike flow-function testing)
equipment.working_principle: Filter cake falls into the bin from the filter discharge chute or belt. The bin sits on 3-4 load cells, so the control system always knows the inventory.
