streams.flow: ~15-25 m3/h liquor (~8-14 t/h water evaporated in 19-EV-301)
streams.composition: TOC ~20-30 g/L C in strong liquor; concentrated to ~50-60% total solids
streams.basis: Engineering estimate to remove ~1.0-1.5 kg TOC/t Al2O3 at ~80-90% destruction

streams.name: LBF off-gas
streams.composition: N2, CO2, H2O, O2, dust (Na salts), VOCs/odour before RTO

streams.name: 50% caustic soda make-up
streams.from_to: A17 port tanks -> ~8 km caustic pipeline (backup: road tankers via 19-UL-401) -> 19-TK-401/402 -> 19-PP-401..403 -> 18-TK-021/022
streams.flow: ~24 m3/h average (~36 t/h solution; ~18 t/h NaOH 100%)
streams.temperature: 20-40 degC (keep >15 degC; 50% NaOH freezes at ~12 degC; keep metal <45 degC)
streams.composition: NaOH 48-50% w/w, SG ~1.52, low NaCl/Na2CO3 (membrane grade preferred)
streams.basis: Engineering estimate: 75 kg NaOH/t Al2O3; agrees with A17 import 120-200 kt/yr

equipment.name: Causticisation feed tank and feed pumps
equipment.function: Buffer the dilute washer-overflow side-stream and feed it at a controlled rate to Reactor 1.
equipment.type_selected: API 650 insulated atmospheric tank; horizontal centrifugal pumps (VSD)
equipment.why_this_type: A steady feed rate and composition are essential for lime efficiency.
key_dimensions: ~600 m3 (~10 m dia x 8.5 m), ~1 h residence (engineering estimate)
Pumps ~650 m3/h x 30-40 m, ~110 kW
equipment.working_principle: A surge tank fed from the washer-overflow launder through a flow-controlled branch. The feed pumps run on flow control, and the lime dose is ratioed to the feed carbonate (online analyser or lab).
details_to_model: Small insulated tank with roof manway, radar level and vent to the vent header
Pump pair with guards, magflow on the discharge, sample point with cooler, safety shower
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic liquor (~7-9% NaOH equivalent, ~90 degC): burns
Confined space
equipment.materials: CS; PWHT of nozzle/attachment welds per owner rule (design temperature >=65 degC)
common_problems: Scale (TCA, hydrate) in the feed line
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hold the feed steady; carbonate swings upset the lime ratio

equipment.name: Causticisation Reactor 1 (hydrocalumite formation)
equipment.function: Contact slaked lime with the dilute aluminate liquor under controlled, moderate-temperature, short-residence conditions to form hydrocalumite, the intermediate that makes the improved process efficient.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated, baffled, cylindrical atmospheric reactor tank with top-entry agitator
equipment.why_this_type: Well-mixed, short-residence contact disperses the lime quickly, so hydrocalumite forms rather than TCA.
key_dimensions: ~200-250 m3 working; ~7.5 m dia x 7 m (engineering estimate)
Agitator ~30-55 kW, hydrofoil/pitched-blade impeller ~2.5 m dia, 4 wall baffles
equipment.working_principle: Lime slurry and liquor enter together near the impeller. Calcium hydroxide dissolves and reacts with aluminate and carbonate ions, precipitating hydrocalumite (Ca4Al2(OH)12.CO3.xH2O). This is a layered double hydroxide in which carbonate sits between positively charged calcium-aluminium hydroxide layers. Residence time and temperature are limited so the hydrocalumite does not convert to stable tricalcium aluminate. The slurry overflows to Reactor 2.
details_to_model: Tank with bridge-mounted agitator drive (motor + right-angle gearbox) on the roof; 4 vertical baffles
Lime slurry inlet nozzle with pinch/knife-gate valve and magflow; liquor inlet; overflow box/launder to Reactor 2
Roof manway, vent, platform with handrails, stair access; DN200 drain with knife-gate
Insulation and cladding
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry; lime is an irritant and corrosive
Agitator: LOTO before entry; confined space
equipment.materials: CS with PWHT of welds per owner rule; agitator shaft/impeller CS with wear protection
common_problems: Lime grit settling
Scale on the impeller
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check lime efficiency daily (carbonate removed vs CaO added)
sources: Rosenberg S.P., Wilson D.J., Heath C.A. (2001) 'Some aspects of calcium chemistry in the Bayer process', Light Metals 2001, TMS - verify
Rosenberg S.P., Healy S.J. et al., Alcoa patent WO 99/58450 'Improved causticisation of Bayer liquors' - verify
Whittington B.I. (1996) 'The chemistry of CaO and Ca(OH)2 relating to the Bayer process', Hydrometallurgy 43:13-35

equipment.name: Causticisation slurry heater (direct steam injection)
equipment.function: Raise the slurry from Reactor 1 to ~100-103 degC before Reactors 2-3.
equipment.type_selected: In-line direct steam-injection (sparger/jet) heater
equipment.why_this_type: Has no heat-transfer surface for lime/TCA to scale.
key_dimensions: DN350-400 body ~1.5-2 m long; LP steam ~8-15 t/h (engineering estimate; CHANGED from 3-6 t/h after heat balance)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (~630 m3/h slurry x ~10-20 K)

equipment.working_principle: Steam is injected through nozzles into the flowing slurry and condenses at once, giving up its latent heat. The condensate adds to the liquor, which is a small extra water load for evaporation. A temperature controller trims a steam valve.
details_to_model: In-line cylindrical body with steam nozzle; steam control valve, check valve and isolation valve; temperature element downstream
hazards_and_safety: Steam hammer if the slurry stops: a low-flow interlock closes the steam
instrumentation_and_control: TIC on the outlet; low-flow trip
equipment.materials: CS body with hard-faced nozzle
common_problems: Nozzle blockage by scale
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never inject steam into stagnant slurry

equipment.name: Causticisation Reactors 2-3 (carbonate conversion) and discharge pumps
equipment.function: Hold the hydrocalumite slurry at ~100-103 degC long enough to convert it to calcium carbonate, releasing aluminate and caustic, then pump the slurry to the washer train.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated atmospheric reactor tanks; rubber-lined or high-chrome horizontal slurry pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Reactors in series approach plug flow, which gives higher conversion.
key_dimensions: ~600 m3 each; ~9.5 m dia x 9 m (engineering estimate)
Agitators ~45-75 kW each
Pumps ~650 m3/h x 30-40 m, ~110 kW

operating_parameters.basis: Rosenberg et al. (Alcoa) - verify; engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: At higher temperature in carbonate-bearing liquor, hydrocalumite is unstable and reacts to calcium carbonate (calcite), releasing aluminate and hydroxide back into the liquor. Agitation keeps the solids suspended. Slurry overflows from R2 to R3, and the R3 product is pumped to washer 3, where the CaCO3 leaves with the residue.
details_to_model: Two identical agitated tanks in line with interconnecting overflow launders; roof platforms with agitator drives
Pump pair at grade with knife-gate valves, flushing connections, drain to the bund sump
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic slurry near its boiling point: vents release steam
Confined space; agitator isolation
instrumentation_and_control: Level, temperature, agitator power, discharge flow/density
equipment.materials: CS with PWHT of welds per owner rule; pumps rubber-lined or high-chrome
common_problems: Overlong residence converts hydrocalumite to TCA (lime loss)
Scale build-up on the walls
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep temperature and residence inside the window; sample carbonate in and out every shift
sources: Whittington B.I. & Cardile C.M. (1996) 'The chemistry of tricalcium aluminate hexahydrate relating to the Bayer industry', Int. J. Mineral Processing 48:21-38 - verify
Rosenberg et al. Light Metals 2001 - verify

equipment.name: Oxalate crystalliser feed tank, pumps and feed coolers
equipment.function: Combine oxalate-rich seed-wash liquor with a strong-liquor side-stream and cool the mix to ~45-50 degC to create oxalate supersaturation.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated feed tank; wide-gap plate heat exchangers (cooling water)
equipment.why_this_type: Wide-gap plates tolerate fine solids and are easy to clean; cooling drives oxalate supersaturation.
key_dimensions: Tank ~300 m3 (~7.5 m dia x 7 m)

Total cooler duty ~15-20 MW (CHANGED from 8-14 MW): ~350 m3/h x ~1.3 t/m3 x ~3.2 kJ/kgK x ~40-45 K; LMTD ~28-30 K; U ~1.2-1.5 kW/m2K -> ~450-500 m2 total, i.e. 2 x ~250-300 m2 operating + 1 spare; each frame ~3.5 m tall x ~1.2 m wide x ~4-5 m long (engineering estimate)
Cooling water ~1,500-1,800 m3/h
equipment.working_principle: Sodium oxalate solubility falls as temperature falls and as caustic concentration rises (common-ion/salting-out effect). Mixing the low-caustic, high-oxalate wash liquor with strong liquor and then cooling it makes the mix supersaturated in oxalate. Keeping the mix A/C low limits gibbsite nucleation.
details_to_model: Plate packs between fixed and movable frame plates, with tie bolts, carrying/guide bars and 4 corner nozzles; spray shield over each pack
Tank with agitator; pumps with guards; CW connections with isolation valves
hazards_and_safety: Hot caustic leaks at the plate gaskets: spray shield over each plate pack
equipment.materials: Plates SS 316L (suitable for this caustic at <~95 degC inlet, with CW chloride controlled). Titanium is NOT used because it is attacked by hot caustic. If CW chloride is high, use a closed tempered-water loop. EPDM gaskets.
common_problems: Oxalate and hydrate scale on the plates
operating_tips_and_key_points: When the DP doubles, switch to the spare cooler and caustic-wash the fouled one
sources: Power G., Loh J. (2010) 'Organic compounds in the processing of lateritic bauxites to alumina Part 1', Hydrometallurgy 105:1-29

equipment.name: Oxalate crystallisers
equipment.function: Grow sodium oxalate crystals on recycled oxalate seed so oxalate is removed as a filterable solid.
equipment.type_selected: Agitated, baffled crystalliser tanks (flat or shallow-cone bottom) with draft-tube or hydrofoil agitator
equipment.why_this_type: Seeded, well-mixed growth avoids fine nucleation, and the long residence completes desupersaturation.
key_dimensions: ~1,000-1,200 m3 each; ~11 m dia x 12 m (engineering estimate)
Agitators ~55-90 kW each
equipment.working_principle: Supersaturated liquor contacts a large surface of existing needle-shaped sodium oxalate crystals. Oxalate deposits on these seeds instead of forming new fines. Recycling thickened seed keeps the surface area high, and the liquor desupersaturates towards solubility as it passes through the two tanks.
details_to_model: Two large tanks with roof agitators, overflow launders between them, platforms
Seed recycle inlet; sample points; drain valves
hazards_and_safety: Caustic liquor (~45 degC, still corrosive)
Confined space with scaled internals
instrumentation_and_control: Temperature, level, solids density, oxalate (lab: IC or titration)
equipment.materials: CS (below the caustic-SCC threshold at 45-50 degC)
common_problems: Oxalate scale on walls and impellers
Crystal growth poisoned by organics (humates)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the seed charge up; low seed gives fine oxalate that does not settle
sources: Power, Loh & Vernon (2012) 'Organic compounds in the processing of lateritic bauxites to alumina Part 2: Effects of organics in the Bayer process', Hydrometallurgy 127-128:125-149

equipment.name: Oxalate thickener
equipment.function: Settle oxalate crystals, return most of them as seed, bleed product solids to the filter, and send clear overflow liquor to the evaporator feed.
equipment.type_selected: High-rate, bridge-supported thickener with centre drive and rakes; flocculant optional
equipment.why_this_type: Compact; well-grown oxalate crystals settle readily.
key_dimensions: ~15-18 m dia, ~4-5 m side wall, ~10 deg floor cone (engineering estimate)
Drive torque ~100-200 kNm class
equipment.working_principle: Feed enters a central feedwell, where it slows down and spreads out. Crystals settle to the floor, and slowly turning rakes move them to the central cone for underflow pumping. Clear liquor rises to a peripheral overflow launder.
details_to_model: Circular tank on ring wall; full-diameter bridge with walkway; centre drive with motor/gearbox; rake arms with blades; feedwell; peripheral launder with outlet box
2 underflow pumps (1 standby) with recycle and bleed lines
hazards_and_safety: Falls into the thickener: bridge handrails
Rake bogging: torque alarm
instrumentation_and_control: Rake torque, bed level, underflow density
equipment.materials: CS
common_problems: Rake overload from oxalate scale build-up
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch rake torque trends

equipment.name: Oxalate filter, vacuum system and cake handling
equipment.function: Dewater the oxalate bleed and deliver the cake to the liquor burner (or to lime destruction).
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal vacuum belt filter with cake wash (alternatives: pressure filter or pusher centrifuge)
equipment.why_this_type: Allows displacement washing of entrained caustic; simple to maintain.
key_dimensions: ~8-12 m2 filtration area; belt ~1.5-2 m wide x ~8-10 m long (engineering estimate)
Cake bin ~50 m3 with screw feeder
equipment.working_principle: Slurry is fed onto a moving rubber drainage belt that carries a filter cloth over vacuum boxes. Filtrate is drawn through the cloth into a receiver. The cake is washed with a little condensate, dewatered, and discharged over the head roller to a screw conveyor.
details_to_model: Long, low frame with rubber belt, filter cloth, vacuum box, feed box, wash sprays, cloth-tracking rollers, discharge chute
Filtrate receiver vessel, liquid-ring vacuum pump, filtrate pump
Screw conveyor to the cake bin; bin vent
hazards_and_safety: Caustic-wet cake
Pinch points at rollers: guarding
equipment.materials: SS frame, rubber belt, polypropylene cloth
common_problems: Cloth blinding
operating_tips_and_key_points: Wash the cloth every shift

equipment.name: LBF feed concentrator (forced-circulation evaporator)
equipment.function: Concentrate the strong-liquor side-stream to ~50-60% total solids before liquor burning, to cut kiln fuel.
equipment.type_selected: Single- or double-effect forced-circulation evaporator with external shell-and-tube heater and axial recirculation pump
equipment.why_this_type: High concentration and near-saturated salts mean heavy scaling. Forced circulation suppresses boiling in the tubes; falling film cannot handle these solids levels.
key_dimensions: Heater ~300-500 m2; separator ~3 m dia x 8 m; axial circulation pump ~2,000-3,000 m3/h, ~150-250 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A large axial pump drives the liquor at high velocity (2-3 m/s) through the heater tubes, under enough static head that it does not boil inside them. The liquor flashes in the separator instead, which keeps salt deposits out of the tubes.
details_to_model: Vertical separator, external heater (inclined or vertical), large elbow loop with the axial pump at the bottom, steam inlet, condensate pot, vapour line to the condenser
hazards_and_safety: Very concentrated hot caustic (~25-35% NaOH equivalent): severe burns
Salt blockages
equipment.materials: Nickel alloy (e.g., alloy 200/201) or duplex in hot, concentrated zones; this service is in NACE SP0403 Area B/C, so PWHT CS is not adequate (engineering estimate - verify)
common_problems: Salting and blockages
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep density in range; overconcentration plugs lines

equipment.name: Liquor burner rotary kiln with feed pug mill and burner
equipment.function: Oxidise sodium organic salts and oxalate to sodium carbonate and convert the carbonate to sodium aluminate, destroying TOC and recovering soda.
equipment.type_selected: Direct-fired counter-current rotary kiln with twin-shaft pug-mill feed and natural-gas burner
equipment.why_this_type: Handles sticky sodium-salt agglomerates. Recycling burnt product dilutes the liquor so the bed does not melt. Alternatives: fluidised-bed liquor burner; wet oxidation.
key_dimensions: Kiln ~3.0-3.6 m shell dia x ~45-60 m long, slope ~2-3%, 2-3 tyres, girth-gear drive ~200-350 kW (engineering estimate)
Pug mill ~1.2 m x 6 m, twin shaft
Burner ~10-20 MW firing
equipment.working_principle: Concentrated liquor, oxalate cake and hot recycled product are mixed into damp granules and fed into the upper (cold) end of the inclined kiln, which turns slowly (~1-3 rpm). As the bed tumbles towards the burner end it dries, then the organics burn (releasing heat), and finally sodium carbonate reacts with alumina to form sodium aluminate. Hot gases flow counter-current to the bed and leave at the feed end.
details_to_model: Long refractory-lined steel shell on 2-3 tyre/roller stations, with thrust roller, girth gear and pinion, main drive motor + gearbox, and auxiliary (barring) drive
Feed-end housing with seal and feed chute from the pug mill; discharge (firing) hood with burner pipe, flame scanner and peep holes
IR shell-scanner gantry; kiln shell cooling fans
Platforms at each tyre station; roller lubrication systems
hazards_and_safety: Hot surfaces and flame; burner management system per NFPA 85/86 (purge, flame-failure trips)
Caustic dust; CO in confined zones; rotating machinery
Refractory relining: confined space and heat stress
instrumentation_and_control: Kiln inlet/outlet temperatures, O2/CO analyser, shell scanner, drive current, BMS
equipment.materials: Shell CS; alkali-resistant alumina brick/castable refractory
common_problems: Ring formation from molten salts
Refractory attack by soda
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the recycle ratio up to prevent melting and rings
sources: Power, Loh & Vernon (2012) Hydrometallurgy 127-128:125-149 (organics removal options including liquor burning and wet oxidation)
Alcoa Kwinana and Wagerup liquor burning references (public environmental reports) - verify
NFPA 86 Standard for Ovens and Furnaces

equipment.name: LBF product cooler, leach (dissolution) tank and pumps
equipment.function: Cool the burnt product, dissolve its soluble sodium aluminate/carbonate in lean liquor, and return the solution to the circuit.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary drum cooler (or fluid-bed cooler); agitated leach tank; slurry pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Robust handling of hot granular product.
key_dimensions: Cooler ~2.5 m dia x 20 m (engineering estimate)
Leach tank ~150 m3
equipment.working_principle: The hot product is cooled by air or a water jacket. Part is recycled to the pug mill and the net product is dissolved. The sodium aluminate re-enters the liquor as caustic plus alumina.
details_to_model: Drum with tyres and drive; product-recycle elevator or screw; leach tank with agitator; pumps
hazards_and_safety: Hot solids; caustic dust; exothermic dissolution
equipment.materials: CS
common_problems: Dust emissions; lumps
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the leach tank agitated; lumps cause blockages

equipment.name: LBF off-gas cleaning: dust collector, regenerative thermal oxidiser, ID fan and stack
equipment.function: Remove sodium-salt dust and destroy VOCs/odour in the kiln off-gas before discharge.
equipment.type_selected: ESP or pulse-jet baghouse; 2- or 3-can regenerative thermal oxidiser (ceramic media beds); centrifugal ID fan; steel stack
equipment.why_this_type: VOC and odour emissions from Bayer liquor burning have been a documented community issue. An RTO destroys >95-98% of VOC with low fuel use.
key_dimensions: RTO ~3 canisters, each ~5 m x 5 m x 8 m; stack ~40-60 m tall, ~2 m dia; ID fan ~400-800 kW (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: US EPA RTO fact sheet range; engineering estimate

equipment.working_principle: Dust is removed first to protect the RTO beds. In the RTO, gas flows up through a hot ceramic bed into the burner chamber, where the VOCs oxidise, then down through a second bed that absorbs the heat. Valves reverse the flow every 1-3 minutes, so ~95% of the heat is recovered.
details_to_model: Box-shaped ESP with hoppers and rappers, OR baghouse with compartments and pulse valves
RTO canisters with poppet/butterfly switching valves on manifolds; burner in the top chamber
ID fan with VFD and silencer; stack with sampling platform and CEMS ports
hazards_and_safety: Explosion risk if the RTO inlet exceeds the LEL: LEL monitor and dilution
Hot surfaces; ESP high voltage (interlocked access)
equipment.materials: CS; ceramic media; refractory
common_problems: Salt plugging of the RTO media
operating_tips_and_key_points: Bake out the RTO media periodically to clear salt plugging
sources: Alcoa Wagerup refinery liquor burning facility RTO (public reports c.2006-2007) - verify
US EPA Air Pollution Control Technology Fact Sheet: Regenerative Thermal Oxidizer

equipment.name: Caustic soda (50% NaOH) pipeline receipt, back-up tanker unloading, storage and dosing
equipment.function: Receive 50% caustic by the ~8 km pipeline from the port tank farm (A17), with a road-tanker bay as back-up. Store ~20 days of supply and dose it to the liquor blend tanks and minor users (resin regeneration, scrubbers).
equipment.qty_operating: 1 pipeline receipt station; 1 back-up road-tanker bay; 2 tanks; 2 dosing pumps
equipment.type_selected: API 650 vertical cone-roof CS tanks, insulated, with low-temperature heating; horizontal centrifugal pumps (sealless mag-drive or double mechanical seal)
equipment.why_this_type: Standard caustic storage practice. Carbon steel without PWHT is suitable for 50% NaOH only below ~45-50 degC (NACE SP0403 Area A). Gentle heating prevents crystallisation (freezing point ~12 degC). Pipeline receipt follows the A17 decision and removes ~1,000 tanker movements a year.
key_dimensions: Tanks 2 x ~6,000 m3 (~22 m dia x 16 m); ~20 days at 24 m3/h (CORRECTED from '~14 days'); bulk import tanks are at the port (A17) (engineering estimate)
Bund >=110% of the largest tank, with alkali-resistant coating
Pipeline receipt: pig receiver, flow meter, filter, flush connection (condensate) for line displacement
Back-up bay: 1 road bay with canopy, ~25-30 t per tanker

operating_parameters.basis: Caustic handbooks (keep above ~15 degC); NACE SP0403 Area A limit for 50% NaOH ~45-50 degC

equipment.working_principle: Caustic arrives by pipeline from the port tanks in batches, through a filter and meter into the storage tanks. The pipeline is displaced with condensate and kept full or flushed during long stops so it does not freeze or crystallise. In a back-up delivery, the tanker is coupled with dry-break couplings and emptied by transfer pump into the tanks. Dosing pumps deliver caustic on flow-ratio control to the blend tanks, where it mixes into a large hot liquor stream, so the heat of dilution is small. Tank heating uses tempered water (~40 degC) or low-pressure steam coils with surface temperature limited, so there are no local hot spots above the no-PWHT limit.
details_to_model: Two large insulated tanks with tempered-water heating coil or bottom heating panel, spiral stair, roof handrail, radar level and HH switch, vent with breather and CO2 guard (prevents carbonate pick-up)
Pipeline receipt skid: pig receiver, meter, filter, isolation valves, flushing hose station
Back-up road bay with canopy, loading hoses, dry-break couplings, drip tray, wheel chocks, earthing clamp
Tempered-water safety showers and eyewash stations (alarmed) at the bay, the receipt skid and each pump set
Pump set with splash guards, discharge filters and magflows; DN100-150 transfer lines with flange spray guards
Signage: CORROSIVE class 8 (UN1824), PPE board
hazards_and_safety: 50% NaOH causes severe skin burns, and blindness within seconds. Flush for at least 15 min (eyes: up to 60 min) with urgent medical review.
Large heat of dilution: never add water to concentrated caustic
Spray from flange leaks: flange spray guards
Pipeline: overpressure/surge protection, leak detection, pig-receiver opening procedure
Heavy-vehicle movements at the back-up bay
Hydrogen from contact with aluminium
instrumentation_and_control: Level, temperature, flow; HH level trip closes the pipeline receipt valve
Pipeline leak detection (flow balance between port and refinery meters)
equipment.materials: Carbon steel without PWHT, acceptable only because metal temperature is kept <=45-50 degC (NACE SP0403 Area A). EPDM/PTFE gaskets; SS 316 small-bore.
common_problems: Crystallisation in lines at low temperature
Leaks at hose couplings
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never let the tank heating raise the metal temperature above ~45 degC
Wear full PPE when coupling and uncoupling; check the safety shower works before every transfer
sources: OxyChem Caustic Soda Handbook (handling and storage)
Euro Chlor GEST guidance on caustic soda storage - verify
NACE SP0403-2015 caustic soda service chart (Area A/B/C)
ANSI/ISEA Z358.1 Emergency eyewash and shower equipment

areas.layout_notes: Causticisation (19-TK-101, 19-TK-111..113, pumps) is a compact bunded block (~45 m x 25 m) next to the residue washer train (A08), ~50-100 m from washers 1-3, so the feed and return lines stay short. Lime slurry comes from the A20 lime ring main (~100-300 m). The oxalate plant (~60 m x 40 m: feed tank, 3 plate coolers, 2 crystallisers, thickener, belt-filter house) sits between evaporation (A18, strong liquor) and seed washing/classification (A13), ~100-200 m from each. The liquor burning facility takes ~120 m x 40 m (concentrator, pug mill, ~60 m kiln, cooler, leach tank, ESP/RTO and a 40-60 m stack). It is on the downwind side of the refinery, at least 300 m from offices, control room and laboratory, near A18 for the strong-liquor feed, with road access for refractory work. The caustic tank farm (2 x 6,000 m3), the pipeline receipt skid and the back-up road bay sit at the refinery boundary where the port caustic pipeline enters, ~200-400 m from the liquor blend tanks (A18), with a dedicated caustic line on the main rack. Every area has bunds sloped to sumps, with sump pumps returning spills to the process, and safety showers within ~10 s travel (~15 m) of every caustic hazard point.
interfaces: A08 Settling & washing: washer 1 (+2) overflow side-stream ~600 m3/h to causticisation; causticised slurry (~630 m3/h) returned to washer 3. A08 to confirm washer 1 OF C ~110-140 and washer 2 OF ~70-100 g/L

A20 Utilities: slaked lime slurry ~25-35 m3/h (~4.2 t/h CaO); LP steam ~15-30 t/h (causticisation heater 8-15, LBF concentrator 5-15); cooling water ~1,500-1,800 m3/h to the oxalate coolers; natural gas ~40-70 GJ/h to the kiln and RTO; compressed air; power
A13 Classification & seed: oxalate-rich seed-wash liquor ~150 m3/h
A18 Evaporation: strong liquor side-streams (oxalate ~150-250 m3/h; LBF ~15-25 m3/h); oxalate-depleted liquor back to the evaporator feed; caustic make-up dosed into 18-TK-021/022
A17 Port: 50% caustic soda by the ~8 km pipeline from the port tanks (~24 m3/h average, batch transfers)
A09 Residue: CaCO3 and calcium solids leave with the residue
Laboratory: carbonate (S-C), oxalate, TOC, lime availability, lime-efficiency calculation
Environment: LBF stack CEMS, odour monitoring

areas.area_name: A20 Utilities (steam and power cogeneration, boiler feed and condensate, raw and demineralised water, cooling water, compressed air, lime storage and slaking, fuel gas)
areas.purpose:
Supply the refinery's utilities:
- Steam: ~450 t/h normal, 470 t/h design (~1.9-1.95 t/t), at MP 10-12 barg and LP 4-5 barg.
- Electricity: ~57-62 MW for the refinery plus ~6-10 MW for mine, overland conveyor and port.
- Raw water (~650 m3/h) and demineralised water.
- Cooling water: ~16,000 m3/h circulating (design).
- Compressed and instrument air: ~10,000-12,000 Nm3/h.
- Slaked lime: ~32 kg CaO/t Al2O3.
- Natural gas: ~2,400-2,600 GJ/h.
CHANGED from the draft:
- Steam demand raised from 410 to 450-470 t/h (gibbsite dissolution endotherm in digestion; evaporator steam 112 t/h).
- HRSGs re-rated to ~95-100 t/h each and a third auxiliary boiler added, so steam capacity with the largest unit out (N-1) is ~500 t/h.
- Cooling water raised from 10,000 to ~16,000 m3/h (7-cell tower).
- Lime lowered from 40 to ~32 kg CaO/t.
The utilities are designed N+1 so that agitation and steam continue when a unit is lost. Settling of solids in precipitators and thickeners after a total power loss is one of the most costly refinery upsets.
areas.process_description:
1) Steam and power (cogeneration).
Two gas-turbine generators (~25-35 MW ISO class, ~80-100 kg/s exhaust at ~480-550 degC) exhaust into two single-pressure heat-recovery steam generators (HRSG) with duct burners. Each HRSG raises ~35-45 t/h unfired and ~90-100 t/h fired (duct-burner outlet <=850-900 degC) at ~63-65 bar(a) / 470-480 degC.
Check: 90 kg/s x ~1.15 kJ/kgK x (850 - ~140) K = ~73 MW; divided by ~2,800 kJ/kg = ~94 t/h. Reaching 150 t/h would need a fully fired water-wall HRSG, which is not selected.
Three gas-fired D-type package water-tube boilers (~150 t/h each, same steam conditions) make up the balance. Normally two fire at ~65-90% load and the third is on hot standby. Installed HP capacity is 2 x 100 + 3 x 150 = ~650 t/h. With the largest unit (one 150 t/h boiler) out, ~500 t/h remains, which covers the ~450-470 t/h demand.
HP steam passes through a back-pressure/extraction steam turbine generator (~40-50 MW), with MP extraction at 10-12 barg (~190 t/h to the digestion live-steam heaters) and LP exhaust at 4-5 barg (~260-280 t/h to evaporators, pre-desilication, causticisation, LBF concentrator, deaerators and tank heating). Pressure-reducing and desuperheating stations (PRDS) back up each level when the turbine is off.
Total generation (~100-110 MW) exceeds site demand (~65-72 MW), so ~35-40 MW is exported to the grid (gas cogeneration supplying Western Australian refineries, e.g. the Alinta Pinjarra cogeneration plant - verify). The site can island on grid failure.
Alternative, common at Indian refineries (Lanjigarh, Utkal, Damanjodi): coal-fired CFBC boilers with back-pressure turbines (higher CO2, ~0.8-1.0 t CO2/t alumina; needs a coal yard, ash handling and ESPs).

2) Boiler feedwater and condensate.
Clean condensate returns from the digestion live-steam heaters (~180-200 t/h), evaporator effect 1 (~112 t/h) and the LBF concentrator (~8-12 t/h), ~290-310 t/h in total. It is checked by conductivity and sodium analysers with automatic dump, then filtered and polished into the condensate tanks. Together with demineralised make-up (~120-180 t/h; direct-injection steam to pre-desilication, causticisation and hydrate wash heating is not returned), it is deaerated at ~1.5 barg / ~127 degC. The deaerators take ~45-50 t/h of LP steam.
Chemical treatment: oxygen scavenger, amine or ammonia for pH, and phosphate or all-volatile treatment as the boiler supplier specifies. Caustic ingress from a heater tube leak is the main boiler-chemistry risk (caustic gouging and caustic embrittlement).

3) Raw water.
Water is pumped from a dam or river (~10-30 km pipeline) into a lined raw-water storage pond (~7 days) and distributed to: cooling-tower make-up (~280-310 m3/h), the water treatment plant (clarifier, multimedia filters, RO, mixed-bed polishers -> demin; ~190 m3/h raw), firewater, potable, dust suppression, gland/seal water and residue-washing top-up. Most process wash water comes from process condensate (A07/A18, ~650 t/h) and recycled residue-area (RSA) decant/stormwater. Cooling-tower blowdown and RO reject go to residue washing. Fresh water is ~2.7 m3/t.

4) Cooling water.
A 7-cell (6+1) induced-draft counterflow cooling tower (~16,000 m3/h design, ~14,000 normal, range ~10 K) rejects ~165-185 MW. Users:
- Evaporator surface condensers ~50-60 MW
- Precipitation interstage coolers ~45-70 MW (design 60)
- A11 trim coolers ~15 MW
- Oxalate coolers ~15-20 MW
- A15 product fluid-bed coolers ~10-12 MW, if on CW
- Compressor, turbine lube and generator coolers ~10 MW
The water is treated against scale, corrosion and biofouling, with pH and conductivity monitored to catch caustic ingress from process exchangers.

5) Compressed air.
Four oil-free centrifugal compressors (3 duty, 1 standby, ~4,000 Nm3/h each at 8 barg) supply plant air (filter cake blowing, air lances, tools, pneumatic-conveying top-ups) and, through desiccant dryers, instrument air at -40 degC pressure dew point (ISO 8573-1 class 2 for water). Instrument air has priority, through a receiver with a non-return valve.

6) Lime.
Quicklime (CaO ~88-92% available) arrives by road bulk tanker (from the port or a regional kiln) and is blown pneumatically into 2 silos (~1,500 t each, ~14 days at ~8.6 t/h). It is slaked in 2 x 100% detention slakers with hot process condensate: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2, about -1.14 MJ/kg CaO (exothermic), slurry ~75-85 degC. The water:lime ratio is controlled to hold that temperature. Grit is removed, and the 15-20% slurry is stored and circulated round a ring main to causticisation (A19), TCA/filter-aid preparation (A10), digestion/pre-desilication (A05/A06, optional) and residue neutralisation.

7) Fuel.
Natural gas arrives by pipeline at a receiving station for filtration, heating, metering and pressure reduction: ~25-30 barg for the gas turbines and ~4-8 barg for the calciners, boilers, duct burners and kiln. Diesel is stored for the emergency generators, diesel firewater pumps and the mobile fleet.

8) Electrical.
A 132 kV grid connection and main substation, with 11 kV generation and distribution, 6.6/3.3 kV for large motors (mills, compressors, CW pumps, BFW pumps) and 415 V MCCs. Two emergency diesel generators support essential loads (control systems, lube oil, thickener rakes, selected agitators, lighting).

Note for high-temperature (boehmitic) plants: digestion needs steam at ~30-60 bar or molten-salt/hot-oil heating, so the steam cycle has a high-pressure process header and less back-pressure power per tonne of steam.

streams.name: Process steam total
streams.from_to: 20-HR/20-BL -> 20-TG-001 / PRDS -> MP and LP headers -> A05, A06, A13/A14, A18, A19, deaerators
streams.basis: Engineering estimate. Breakdown: digestion MP ~190 (incl. gibbsite dissolution endotherm, process review), pre-desil ~35, evaporation ~112 (A18), A19 ~15-30, hydrate wash/filter ~20-25, deaerators ~45-50, tracing/tank heating/losses ~15-20. CHANGED from 410 t/h

streams.name: HP steam generation
streams.from_to: 2 x HRSG + 3 x aux boilers -> HP header -> 20-TG-001 / PRDS
streams.flow: ~430-460 t/h normal (desuperheat spray adds ~3-5% mass downstream); installed ~650 t/h; N-1 (largest unit out) ~500 t/h
streams.basis: Engineering estimate; HRSG rating per review finding (~95-100 t/h each)

streams.from_to: A06 live-steam heaters, A18 effect 1, A19 LBF concentrator -> 20-TK-021/022

streams.name: Demineralised make-up
streams.basis: Engineering estimate: non-returned steam ~100-110 + blowdown ~8 + dumps/losses

streams.from_to: Dam/river pump station -> pipeline -> 20-PD-101 pond -> users
streams.flow: ~650 m3/h average (~2.7 m3/t Al2O3), ~850 m3/h peak; ~5.4-5.7 GL/yr
streams.basis: Engineering estimate. CHANGED from 550 m3/h (larger cooling tower)

streams.name: Cooling water circulation
streams.from_to: 20-CT-201 basin -> 20-PP-201..205 -> A18 condensers, A12 interstage coolers, A11 trim, A19 oxalate coolers, A15 product coolers, A20 machinery coolers -> tower
streams.temperature: supply ~32 degC, return ~42 degC (tropical design wet bulb ~27-28 degC)
streams.basis: Engineering estimate: ~165-185 MW heat rejection. CHANGED from 10,000 m3/h (review)

streams.name: Cooling tower make-up / blowdown
streams.from_to: Raw water -> basin; blowdown -> A08 wash water / RSA
streams.basis: Engineering estimate (evaporation ~1.5% of circulation per 10 K = ~220-240 m3/h)

streams.name: Natural gas
streams.from_to: Pipeline -> 20-GS-501 -> GTs (25-30 barg), HRSG duct burners, aux boilers, calciners (A15), LBF kiln/RTO (A19)
streams.temperature: heated to ~15-25 K above dew point
streams.basis: Engineering estimate: GTs ~650 GJ/h + duct burners ~250-270 + aux boilers ~800 + calciners ~720 + LBF ~50

streams.name: Compressed air
streams.from_to: 20-AC-301..304 -> receivers -> plant air / instrument air headers
streams.composition: Oil-free; instrument air dew point -40 degC

streams.name: Quicklime / slaked lime
streams.flow: ~8.6 t/h quicklime (~7.7 t/h CaO; ~71 kt/yr quicklime) -> ~45-55 m3/h slurry at 15-20% w/w
streams.basis: Engineering estimate: 32 kg CaO/t Al2O3 (causticisation ~18, TCA filter aid ~6, other ~8). CHANGED from 40 kg/t

streams.name: Electricity
streams.from_to: GT/STG generators + 132 kV grid -> 11 kV switchboards -> users
streams.flow: Generation ~100-110 MW; site demand ~65-72 MW; export ~35-40 MW

equipment.name: Gas turbine generators (cogeneration)
equipment.function: Generate electricity and supply hot exhaust gas to the HRSGs.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (aux boilers and the grid cover the loss of one)
equipment.type_selected: Industrial or aeroderivative gas turbine, ~25-35 MW ISO, dry low-NOx combustor, 11 kV air-cooled generator
equipment.why_this_type: High combined heat-and-power efficiency (~75-80% fuel utilisation) on natural gas; widely used for steam/power supply to refineries in Western Australia.
key_dimensions: Package enclosure ~20 m L x 5 m W x 6 m H; elevated inlet filter house ~8 m x 6 m x 6 m; exhaust transition ~3-3.5 m dia to the HRSG (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.unit: MW each (ISO); ~5-10% lower at tropical ambient

equipment.working_principle: An axial compressor draws in filtered air and compresses it ~15-25 times. Fuel burns in the combustor at constant pressure, and the hot gas expands through the turbine stages, driving both the compressor and the generator. The exhaust (~500 degC, ~14-15% O2) still carries most of the fuel energy and is recovered in the HRSG; its oxygen also supports duct firing.
details_to_model: Acoustic enclosure with doors, ventilation fans and fire suppression (CO2 or water-mist) cylinders
Inlet air filter house with weather hoods, multi-stage filters, inlet duct and silencer
Generator with terminal box, neutral earthing cubicle and bus duct to the step-up transformer
Lube oil skid with fin-fan coolers; fuel gas skid (filter, heater, stop/control valves)
Exhaust diffuser to the HRSG with expansion joint; optional bypass stack with diverter damper
hazards_and_safety: Fuel gas leak/explosion: gas detection in the enclosure, ventilation, ESD
Hot surfaces; noise >100 dB(A) inside the enclosure
Rotating machinery; CO2 fire suppression is an asphyxiation hazard, so lock it out before entry
instrumentation_and_control: Turbine control system (speed, load, exhaust temperature spread)
Vibration (proximity probes), flame detection, gas detection
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Inlet filter clogging from bauxite/alumina dust
Compressor fouling
operating_tips_and_key_points: Change inlet filters on time (refinery dust); run offline/online compressor washes
sources: API 616 Gas Turbines for Petroleum, Chemical and Gas Industry Services
Alinta Pinjarra cogeneration plant supplying the Alcoa Pinjarra refinery - verify

equipment.name: Heat recovery steam generators with duct burners
equipment.function: Recover GT exhaust heat, plus supplementary firing, to raise HP steam for the process and turbine.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal-gas-flow, natural-circulation, single-pressure HRSG with duct burner, superheater, evaporator and economiser; supplementary firing limited to <=850-900 degC (unlined-duct burner practice)
equipment.why_this_type: Single pressure matches a process steam plant, and supplementary firing gives flexibility to follow the steam load. Rating CORRECTED to ~95-100 t/h: the earlier '150 t/h fired' needs ~1,250-1,300 degC firing, i.e. a fully fired water-wall HRSG.
key_dimensions: Casing ~7-8 m W x ~18-22 m H x ~20-25 m L; steam drum ~1.5-1.7 m dia x ~10-12 m on top; stack ~40-45 m x ~3.5-4 m dia (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: heat balance: 90 kg/s x 1.15 kJ/kgK x (850-140) K / ~2,800 kJ/kg = ~94 t/h
vendor practice for duct burners (review finding)

equipment.working_principle: Exhaust gas flows horizontally through banks of finned tubes: the superheater (hottest), then the evaporator, whose riser tubes connect to the steam drum where steam separates from water by natural circulation, then the economiser, which preheats the feedwater. Duct burners in the inlet duct use the ~14-15% O2 left in the GT exhaust to raise the gas temperature when more steam is needed.
details_to_model: Large rectangular insulated casing with external stiffeners, access doors and inlet transition duct
Steam drum on top with safety valves, 2 direct water-level gauges + transmitters, main steam stop valve, non-return valve
Downcomers and riser pipes, headers, blowdown lines to the blowdown tank
Duct burner runners with flame scanners and gas train
Stack with CEMS platform, ladders, aviation lights; platforms at drum and header levels
hazards_and_safety: High-pressure steam: drum safety valves to ASME I / IBR / AS 1228; boiler explosion risk from low water
Furnace explosion: purge before firing (NFPA 85)
Hot surfaces; confined space in the casing
instrumentation_and_control: Three-element drum level control, low-low level trip
equipment.materials: Superheater alloy steel (T22/T91); evaporator and economiser CS finned tubes
common_problems: Economiser corrosion at low feedwater temperature
Caustic-contaminated feedwater causing under-deposit gouging
operating_tips_and_key_points: Never bypass the low drum-level trips; blow down as the chemistry requires
sources: ASME BPVC Section I (Power Boilers) / Indian Boiler Regulations / AS 1228
NFPA 85 Boiler and Combustion Systems Hazards Code

equipment.name: Auxiliary gas-fired water-tube boilers
equipment.function: Provide the balance of HP steam (~260 t/h normal) and N-1 back-up when a GT/HRSG or a boiler is offline.
equipment.qty_standby: 1 (hot standby at minimum fire); N-1 across 5 steam generators gives ~500 t/h
equipment.type_selected: Shop-assembled D-type package water-tube boiler with low-NOx burners, FD fan and economiser
equipment.why_this_type: Fast start, high availability, compact. 150 t/h is within the shop-assembled D-type range (up to ~200-270 t/h). Three x 150 t/h (option a) was chosen over two field-erected 200 t/h units because 2 x 200 + 2 x 100 loses 200 t/h on a single failure (N-1 = 400 t/h, short of demand).
key_dimensions: ~150 t/h each; package ~20-22 m L x ~6 m W x ~9-10 m H; individual or common stack ~40 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Gas burns in a water-cooled furnace. Radiant heat boils water in the membrane walls, and convection banks between the steam drum and the mud drum complete the evaporation. A superheater raises the steam temperature, and an economiser recovers flue-gas heat into the feedwater.
details_to_model: Long, boxy casing with burner front (windbox, burner, gas train, flame scanners) and FD fan with silencer at the front
Steam drum on top with safety valves and gauge glasses; economiser on top or rear; flue duct to the stack
Platforms at the burner front and drum level; ladders
Three identical units side by side with a common BFW header and steam header
hazards_and_safety: As for the HRSG: furnace explosion, low water, high-pressure steam
Gas-train leaks: gas detection
instrumentation_and_control: Burner management system (purge, flame safeguard, trips)
Plant master steam-pressure controller with fast load pick-up on GT/HRSG trip
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Refractory damage at the burner throat
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep one boiler on hot standby (minimum fire) so it can take load quickly if a GT trips

equipment.name: Back-pressure / extraction steam turbine generator
equipment.function: Expand HP steam to the process pressures while generating electricity.
equipment.type_selected: Multi-stage back-pressure turbine with controlled MP extraction, gearbox and 11 kV generator
equipment.why_this_type: All exhaust steam is used by the process (no condenser loss), giving ~80%+ thermal utilisation of the steam-raising fuel.
key_dimensions: Turbine-gearbox-generator train ~15-18 m long on an ~8 m high concrete table-top; turbine hall with ~50-80 t EOT crane (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (~310 kJ/kg to MP, ~445 kJ/kg to LP at ~75% isentropic efficiency). CHANGED from 35-40

equipment.working_principle: Steam expands through nozzle and blade rows, converting pressure energy to velocity and then to shaft torque. Part of the steam is extracted at MP pressure through a controlled extraction valve, and the rest exhausts at LP header pressure. The turbine is governed on header pressure (back-pressure control) while the generator supplies the grid or island.
details_to_model: Turbine casing with HP inlet stop and control valves (actuator rack), extraction and exhaust nozzles to large-bore headers, lagging
Reduction gearbox (if high-speed), generator with exciter, lube oil console, steam seal system
Table-top foundation with stair; turbine-hall crane; PRDS stations beside
hazards_and_safety: Overspeed (test the trip valves), high-pressure steam, hot surfaces, noise
Lube-oil fire: fire detection and deluge
instrumentation_and_control: Governor, overspeed protection, vibration/axial position monitoring (API 670)
equipment.materials: Vendor standard
common_problems: Valve stem deposits; seal wear
operating_tips_and_key_points: Test the trip valves on schedule. The process headers must not lose pressure on a turbine trip, so the PRDS must take over automatically.
sources: API 612 Special-purpose steam turbines; API 670 machinery protection

equipment.name: Pressure-reducing and desuperheating stations (PRDS) and steam headers
equipment.function: Back up the turbine (HP->MP, HP->LP, MP->LP) and keep header pressures constant.
equipment.type_selected: Combined pressure-reducing/desuperheating valve with BFW spray water
equipment.why_this_type: Fast-acting header pressure control on a turbine trip.
key_dimensions: Valves DN300-500 inlet, DN600-900 outlet; headers DN600-1,000 on the main rack (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A control valve drops the steam pressure, and feedwater sprayed in downstream removes the superheat. Pressure and temperature loops trim each station.
details_to_model: Angle-body control valve with large actuator, spray-nozzle assembly, silencer/diffuser, long straight run, drain pots and traps, PSVs on the downstream headers
hazards_and_safety: High noise; steam hammer
equipment.materials: Alloy/CS piping per pressure class
common_problems: Trim erosion
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the PRDS warm (small bleed) for instant response

equipment.name: Deaerators and boiler feedwater pumps
equipment.function: Remove dissolved O2/CO2 from feedwater and pump it at boiler pressure to the HRSGs and boilers.
equipment.type_selected: Spray-tray deaerator on a horizontal storage tank; horizontal multistage barrel/ring-section pumps (BB4/BB5) with VSD or hydrodynamic coupling
equipment.why_this_type: Standard; multistage pumps reach ~80 barg.
key_dimensions: Deaerators 2 x ~300 t/h: head ~2.5 m dia x 5 m; storage ~3.5 m dia x 14 m (~100 m3) each, elevated ~15-20 m above pump suction (engineering estimate)
BFW pumps ~330 m3/h x ~850-900 m, ~1.0-1.3 MW each (2 x 50% + 1 spare)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (heating ~150 t/h make-up and ~300 t/h return condensate)

equipment.working_principle: Feedwater is sprayed into a steam-filled head and heated to saturation, which drives out dissolved gases; these vent with a little steam. The tank stores the deaerated water, and its elevation gives the BFW pumps their NPSH. The multistage pumps raise the pressure through impellers in series.
details_to_model: Elevated structure with horizontal tanks and vertical heads, vent condensers, safety valves, level gauges
Pumps at grade with suction strainers, automatic recirculation (minimum-flow) valves, large motors and lube units
hazards_and_safety: Hot pressurised water flashes if a line breaks
Pump minimum-flow protection to prevent overheating
instrumentation_and_control: Deaerator pressure and level, dissolved-O2 analyser, pump auto-start on low header pressure
equipment.materials: CS; pumps with 13Cr internals
common_problems: Vent valve throttled too far (poor O2 removal)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check dissolved O2 and pH every shift

equipment.name: Condensate return tanks, condensate polishing and pumps
equipment.function: Collect returned clean condensate, verify its purity, polish it and pump it to the deaerators.
equipment.type_selected: Atmospheric CS tanks (internally coated); cartridge/precoat filters + mixed-bed polishers; centrifugal pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Bayer condensate can pick up caustic and alumina through leaks, so polishing and dump protection are essential.
key_dimensions: Tanks 2 x ~1,500 m3 (~13 m dia x 12 m); polishers 3 x ~160 m3/h; pumps ~330 m3/h x ~40 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Online conductivity and sodium analysers on each return line divert contaminated condensate to the process. Accepted condensate is filtered and polished by ion exchange before deaeration.
details_to_model: Analyser shelter with sample coolers, three-way dump valves, filter vessels, resin vessels, regeneration chemical skid
Tanks with vents and overflows; pump set
hazards_and_safety: Hot water; regeneration acid and caustic
instrumentation_and_control: Conductivity, Na and silica analysers; tank levels
equipment.materials: Coated CS / SS
common_problems: Resin exhausted by caustic slugs
operating_tips_and_key_points: Treat every analyser alarm as real until proven otherwise

equipment.name: Main substation, transformers and emergency diesel generators
equipment.function: Connect to the grid, distribute power at 11 kV and below, and supply emergency power to essential loads.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 substation; 2 grid transformers; generator step-up/unit transformers; 2 EDGs
equipment.type_selected: 132 kV GIS or AIS switchyard; 2 x ~80 MVA 132/11 kV ONAN/ONAF transformers; 11 kV metal-clad switchgear; 2 x ~3 MVA diesel generators
equipment.why_this_type: Firm supply with export capability. The ability to island protects the precipitation and thickener inventories.
key_dimensions: Switchyard ~80 m x 60 m; transformers ~8 m x 5 m x 6 m each with firewalls and oil bunds; EDG containers ~12 m x 3 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Power from the generators and the grid is collected on 11 kV switchboards and distributed by feeders to area substations. Protection relays isolate faults selectively. On total power loss, load shedding and EDG auto-start restore essential loads within seconds, and the refinery restarts in sequence, with agitators started before settled solids harden.
details_to_model: Fenced switchyard with gantries, circuit breakers, disconnectors, CTs/VTs, surge arresters and overhead-line entry
Large oil transformers with radiators, conservator, Buchholz relay, firewalls and oil containment
Switchroom building with cable trenches and battery room; EDG containers with exhaust stacks and day tanks
hazards_and_safety: Electrocution and arc flash: permits, switching procedures, arc-rated PPE
Transformer fire: deluge, firewalls
Diesel fuel
instrumentation_and_control: SCADA/power management system with load shedding
common_problems: Dust and caustic mist on outdoor insulators (flashover): insulator washing
operating_tips_and_key_points: Practise the black-start sequence; give priority to precipitator and thickener agitation/rakes
sources: IEC 61936-1 Power installations exceeding 1 kV AC

equipment.name: Natural gas receiving station and diesel storage
equipment.function: Receive, filter, heat, meter and reduce pipeline gas for all burners and GTs; store diesel for emergency and mobile use.
equipment.type_selected: Skid-mounted gas station: inlet ESD valve, filter-separators, water-bath or electric heaters, pressure-reduction runs (active/monitor regulators + slam-shut), ultrasonic fiscal meters; API 650 diesel tanks
equipment.why_this_type: Standard pipeline custody transfer and pressure reduction.
key_dimensions: Gas compound ~60 m x 30 m; vent stack ~10-15 m; diesel tanks 2 x ~500 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The gas is cleaned of liquids and dust and heated so that Joule-Thomson cooling across the regulators does not form hydrates or ice. It is then reduced in pressure in two stages and metered for custody transfer. Slam-shut valves protect downstream piping from overpressure.
details_to_model: Fenced compound; yellow piping with flow arrows; filter-separator vessels, heater, regulator runs, meter runs with flow conditioners, vent stack, actuated ESD valve, gas detectors
hazards_and_safety: Flammable gas and explosion: hazardous-area zoning, hot-work permits
Diesel fire
instrumentation_and_control: Fiscal metering, gas chromatograph (calorific value), pressure/temperature, gas detection, ESD
equipment.materials: CS API 5L
common_problems: Regulator instability; filter DP
operating_tips_and_key_points: Check the filter DP and heater outlet temperature daily

equipment.name: Raw water intake pumps, pipeline and raw water storage pond
equipment.function: Supply fresh water to the refinery and store ~7 days of demand.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical turbine pumps (VS1) at a river/dam intake, or horizontal split-case pumps (BB1); HDPE-lined earth-embankment pond
equipment.why_this_type: Reliable bulk water transfer; the pond buffers dry seasons and pipeline outages.
key_dimensions: Pumps ~290 m3/h each at ~60-120 m head (depends on route); pipeline DN600, ~10-30 km (engineering estimate)
Pond ~110,000-120,000 m3 (~160 m x 130 m x 6 m deep) (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Pumps lift water from the source and push it through the pipeline to the refinery pond. Distribution pumps at the pond supply the treatment plant, cooling-tower make-up, firewater tanks and process users.
details_to_model: Intake structure with screens, VS1 pumps with motors on deck, surge vessel, pipeline with air valves and scour valves
Pond with HDPE liner, crest road, inlet/outlet structures, fence, life rings
hazards_and_safety: Drowning at the pond: fencing, life rings, no entry
Water hammer in the long pipeline: surge protection
equipment.materials: Ductile iron or steel pipeline with cathodic protection
common_problems: Algae in the pond
Intake screen blockage
operating_tips_and_key_points: Track the water balance: rising raw-water demand often means process condensate is being lost to drain
sources: AWWA M11 Steel Pipe; Hydraulic Institute standards

equipment.name: Water treatment and demineralisation plant
equipment.function: Produce clarified/filtered service water and demineralised boiler make-up.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 clarifier, filters, 2 RO trains, 1 mixed bed
equipment.type_selected: Lamella or solids-contact clarifier; multimedia pressure filters; RO (1-pass) + mixed-bed ion-exchange polishers
equipment.why_this_type: Low chemical use and reliable high-purity water for 63-65 bar boilers.
key_dimensions: Clarifier ~12-15 m dia; filters 4 x ~3 m dia; RO 3 x ~100 m3/h permeate on skids ~12 m x 3 m; mixed beds 2 x ~2.5-3 m dia (~200 m3/h); demin tanks 2 x ~1,500 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Coagulant and flocculant agglomerate the suspended solids, which settle in the clarifier, and the water is then filtered. High-pressure RO membranes reject ~98-99% of dissolved salts. Mixed-bed resins remove the remaining ions by exchanging them for H+ and OH-. RO reject goes to residue washing.

equipment.working_principle: Warm water is sprayed over fill packs and runs down as a thin film while fans draw air upward. A small part of the water (~1.5% per 10 K) evaporates, cooling the rest. Blowdown limits the build-up of dissolved solids, and chemicals control scale, corrosion and Legionella.

equipment.name: Lime slakers with grit removal and vapour scrubber
equipment.function: Hydrate quicklime with hot water to a reactive Ca(OH)2 slurry and remove grit.
equipment.type_selected: Detention (slurry) slaker with agitated slaking chamber and grit screw (alternatives: paste slaker, or vertical ball-mill slaking for higher reactivity)
equipment.why_this_type: Robust and gives a consistent 15-20% slurry. Controlling the slaking temperature (~75-85 degC) gives fine, reactive hydrate particles, which matters for causticisation efficiency.
key_dimensions: ~10-12 t/h quicklime each; slaking chamber ~25-35 m3 (~3.5 m dia x 3 m) with ~30-45 kW agitator; grit classifier screw ~6 m long; overall ~10 m x 4 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 releases ~1.14 MJ/kg CaO. The water:lime ratio is controlled to hold the slaking temperature. Too much water keeps the temperature too low and DROWNS the lime, giving coarse, low-surface-area hydrate. Too little water lets the slaker overheat and BURN the lime, which also lowers reactivity and risks steam/slurry eruptions. So a falling slaking temperature calls for LESS water per tonne of lime, and a rising temperature towards boiling calls for MORE water. The agitator breaks up agglomerates. The overflow slurry passes a screen, and grit (unburnt stone, silica) is screwed out to a bin.
details_to_model: Box-shaped slaking tank with top agitator, lime inlet chute from the feeder, water inlet with flowmeter and control valve, thermowell
Inclined grit screw with motor; grit discharge chute to a skip
Vapour hood and duct to a wet scrubber with fan and stack
Discharge to the slurry tank via a screen box
hazards_and_safety: Exothermic reaction: steam and hot-slurry eruptions if the slaker is starved of water (burning) or water is added suddenly to a hot dry charge; burns
Lime dust and slurry (pH ~12.5): eye injuries, so eyewash is essential
instrumentation_and_control: Slaking temperature control (water:lime ratio, trimmed by water flow), lime feed rate, agitator current
equipment.materials: CS with wear liners
common_problems: Scaling in the water inlet; grit screw wear
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hold the slaking temperature steady with the water:lime ratio. Low temperature means drowning (cut the water); near-boiling means burning (add water). Lime reactivity drives causticisation efficiency and filter-aid quality.
sources: Lime supplier slaking guides (Carmeuse/Lhoist technical bulletins; National Lime Association) - drowning vs burning terminology - verify
Whittington (1996) Hydrometallurgy 43:13-35 (lime reactivity in the Bayer process)

areas.layout_notes: The power house is a block ~170 m x 110 m beside the steam load centre. It holds the GTs, HRSGs, 3 auxiliary boilers, the STG hall, the deaerator bay, BFW pumps and condensate polishing. It is ~150-300 m from digestion (A06) and evaporation (A18), so the large-bore MP/LP headers stay short on the main pipe rack. The HRSG and boiler stacks (~40-45 m) are on the downwind side of the block. The main 132 kV substation sits next to the power house on the side away from the cooling tower, at least 100-150 m from it to avoid drift and mist on insulators. The cooling tower (7 cells in a row, ~110 m x 18 m, plus the pump pit) lies between precipitation (A12) and evaporation (A18) to keep the CW headers short. Its long axis is perpendicular to the prevailing wind, and it is >=30-50 m from buildings and air intakes. The compressor house is near the power house or the centre of air demand (hydrate filtration A14, calcination/pneumatic conveying A15/A16). The lime area (silos ~30 m tall, slakers, slurry tank) is a ~50 m x 40 m compound beside the refinery access road, near causticisation (A19) and clarification (A08/A10), with a tanker turning circle. The raw water pond (~160 m x 130 m) and water treatment plant are at a site high point or edge, with the firewater tanks and fire pump house nearby. The gas receiving station is at the site boundary near the pipeline entry, >=50-100 m from ignition sources, with gas lines to the power house and calciners on the rack. Diesel storage is next to the EDGs and the mobile-equipment refuelling bay. A main E-W pipe rack spine (~1.2-1.5 km) with N-S branches (2-4 tiers, +6 to +15 m) carries steam, condensate, CW, air, lime and gas to all areas.
interfaces: A06 Digestion: MP steam ~190 t/h (range 150-220) at 10-12 barg; clean condensate return ~180-200 t/h; BFW for desuperheating

Mine (A01) on a bauxite plateau ~20 km from the refinery, linked by a 2-flight overland conveyor (A02). Refinery core ~1.6 km x 1.0 km laid out along the process flow. Upwind/entry end: administration, CCR, laboratory, workshops, stores. Flow: stockyard (A03) -> grinding (A04) -> pre-desilication (A05) -> digestion/flash (A06/A07, the central hot block) -> settling and washing (A08) -> residue filtration (A09, at the edge facing the RSA). Liquor: A08 -> security filtration (A10) -> heat interchange (A11) -> precipitation (A12) -> classification (A13) -> hydrate filtration (A14) -> calcination (A15, downwind end) -> product silos and load-out (A16) -> ~8 km covered conveyor to the port (A17). A18 lies between A11/A12 and A06, with its inventory tanks on the A06 side. A19: causticisation next to A08, oxalate plant between A18 and A13, LBF downwind. A20: power house next to A06/A18, 7-cell cooling tower between A12 and A18, lime compound near A08/A19, substation away from the cooling tower, raw-water pond and gas station at the boundary. Main E-W rack ~1.2-1.5 km

decisions.finding: A20 20-HR-001/002 (major, mechanical): HRSG rating of 150 t/h fired is not achievable with duct firing; N-1 steam capacity (~340 t/h) is below demand.
decisions.reason: Own heat balance confirms it: 90 kg/s x ~1.15 kJ/kgK x (850-140) K = ~73 MW, divided by ~2,800 kJ/kg = ~94 t/h; unfired ~35-45 t/h. HRSGs re-rated to 95-100 t/h with firing <=850-900 degC, and the 150 t/h figure removed. Option (a) adopted: a third 150 t/h package boiler (20-BL-003), giving ~650 t/h installed and ~500 t/h N-1. Option (b), 2 x 200 t/h field-erected, was rejected because loss of one 200 t/h unit leaves 400 t/h, below the corrected 450-470 t/h demand. STG output, gas use and energy intensity were recalculated.

decisions.finding: A18 18-SK-001 (major, HSE): descaling hazards held a placeholder ('H2S? (not expected)') and said hydrogen forms only on contact with Al/Zn; this contradicted A06.
decisions.reason: Fe + H2SO4 -> FeSO4 + H2 on carbon-steel tubes is basic acid-corrosion chemistry, and it gets worse when the inhibitor is depleted. The reviewer's text is applied, LEL monitoring and venting are added to details, instrumentation and the effect hazards, and dissolved-iron tracking is added as an inhibitor-depletion indicator. Now consistent with A06.

decisions.finding: A20 20-SL-401/402 (major, HSE): the slaker principle reversed 'drowning' (it said too hot drowns the lime).
decisions.reason: Lime-industry usage: drowning = too much water / low temperature, giving coarse low-surface-area hydrate; burning = too little water / overheating. The working principle, hazards, control and operating tips are rewritten, including the correct direction for water:lime ratio corrections.

decisions.finding: A19 19-UL-401 / 19-TK-401/402 (minor, HSE): the no-PWHT carbon-steel limit for 50% NaOH was stated as 50-60 degC.
decisions.reason: On the NACE SP0403 chart the Area A limit at 50% NaOH is ~45-50 degC, which is also consistent with A17. Text changed to <=45-50 degC metal temperature, with heating limited to tempered water or controlled low-pressure coils so there are no hot spots.

decisions.finding: Missing equipment A18 (mechanical): liquor (caustic inventory) storage tanks; 1.5-3 h tanks force a rate cut during a train descale.
decisions.reason: Added 18-TK-051/052 (2 x ~12,000 m3) and 18-PP-051..053. Sizing: one train out ~36 h means ~7,500 t of water not removed, so ~8,000-10,000 m3 of dilute-liquor storage plus a strong-liquor draw is needed. API 650 Annex M, with the PWHT approach per the owner rule.

decisions.finding: Missing equipment A20 (mechanical): third auxiliary boiler or uprated boilers.
decisions.reason: 20-BL-003 added (3 x 150 t/h package boilers); see the HRSG decision.

decisions.finding: Consistency (process): steam demand should rise to ~1.85-2.0 t/t once the gibbsite dissolution endotherm is included.
decisions.reason: Gibbsite dissolution is endothermic (on the order of ~+20-30 kJ/mol Al(OH)3, i.e. ~0.4-0.6 GJ/t Al2O3, ~30 MW). Combined with the corrected evaporator steam (112 t/h) and explicit deaerator steam (~45-50 t/h), A20 now designs for 450 t/h normal and 470 t/h design (~1.9-1.95 t/t). MP to A06 is ~190 t/h; the A06 owner should confirm.

decisions.finding: Consistency (mechanical/process): cooling water must rise to ~13,000-16,000 m3/h (A12 45-70 MW, A11 trim, A18 condensers).
decisions.reason: Duties summed: condensers 50-60, A12 ~60, A11 ~15, A19 oxalate 15-20 (also corrected upward), A15 product coolers 10-12, machinery ~10, total ~165-185 MW. Design 16,000 m3/h, 7 cells (6+1), 5 pumps (4+1); make-up and fresh water updated (~650 m3/h, ~2.7 m3/t).

decisions.finding: Consistency (process): spent-liquor routing between A11 and A18 must be decided.
decisions.reason: Decision: all spent liquor passes the A11 PL/spent interchangers (a 95-110 MW duty needs the full ~3,050 m3/h for a ~25-30 K rise) and reaches A18 at ~80-88 degC. Evaporator feed enters the effect-6 separator through a flash inlet. Re-doing the A18 heat balance showed the draft economy of 4.0-4.5 was not achievable with a ~5:1 liquor/water ratio in backward feed (each effect must heat the liquor ~13 K). LP steam was corrected to ~112 t/h, economy 3.6-4.0, and the feed tanks are now above the PWHT threshold.

decisions.finding: Consistency (process): process condensate tanks are owned by both A07 (07-TK-001) and A18 (18-TK-012).
decisions.reason: A18 takes ownership: 18-TK-012 is enlarged to ~1,200 m3 as the single plant process-condensate (hot wash-water) tank and also receives A07 flash condensate (~650 t/h total), with pumps 18-PP-023..025 (2+1). A07 keeps only its condensate pots/flash vessels, and 07-TK-001 should be deleted or renamed by the A07 owner.

decisions.finding: Consistency (HSE): washer 1 overflow C differs (A08 80-140 vs A19/A20 100-170 g/L).
decisions.reason: Aligned to washer 1 OF ~110-140 and washer 2 OF ~70-100 g/L, inside A08's band. This also exposed a liquor-chemistry error: washing does not change C/S, so carbonate in the causticiser feed is ~14-20 g/L, not 20-30. Causticisation was re-based to ~600 m3/h, ~6 t/h Na2CO3 removed (~25 kg/t), 4.2 t/h CaO, and steam heater duty corrected to 8-15 t/h (was 3-6).

decisions.finding: Consistency (mechanical/mining): lime demand differs (A17 30-80 kt/yr CaO vs A20 ~89 kt/yr quicklime).
decisions.reason: After the causticisation correction, lime falls to ~32 kg CaO/t, i.e. ~7.7 t/h CaO, ~8.6 t/h quicklime, ~71 kt/yr. A17 should set its import range to ~60-90 kt/yr. Silo cover becomes ~14 days.

decisions.finding: Consistency (all): bauxite factor and residue need single values.
decisions.reason: 2.65 t/t (640 t/h dry) adopted, and residue 285 t/h normal / 310 t/h design adopted (agrees with my 280-300 t/h balance).

decisions.finding: Consistency (mechanical/mining): refinery-to-port mode (8 km conveyor in A16/A17 vs 30-60 km rail in A20) and caustic receipt (pipeline in A17 vs rail/road bays in A19).
decisions.reason: A16/A17 own the export route, so the A20/plant-wide layout now uses the ~8 km covered conveyor. A19 caustic receipt is changed to the A17 ~8 km pipeline into 19-TK-401/402, with one road-tanker bay as back-up. Tank storage days corrected to ~20.

decisions.finding: Consistency (HSE): PWHT philosophy for caustic service is applied inconsistently.
decisions.reason: Stated one owner rule (PWHT at design temperature >=65 degC in Bayer liquor; 50% NaOH CS only <=45-50 degC; nickel alloy for hot concentrated caustic) and applied it to all A18/A19 tanks and vessels. The other areas should adopt the same rule. Chart boundary values are marked 'verify'.

decisions.finding: Consistency (mining): fuel basis (coal CFBC vs natural gas) affects port and site equipment.
decisions.reason: Natural-gas cogeneration is kept as the generic basis, because it is the cleaner, lower-CO2 option in published WA practice and is internally consistent across A15/A20. No coal-handling equipment is added. The coal alternative stays documented as an owner open question, not a design change.

decisions.finding: Self-identified during reconciliation: oxalate cooler duty (8-14 MW) and oxalate depletion (3-5 g/L) did not close the balances; 19-HX-201 had a placeholder ('titanium?').
decisions.reason: Heat balance (~350 m3/h x 1.3 t/m3 x 3.2 kJ/kgK x 40-45 K) gives 15-20 MW, so the design is now 2 operating + 1 spare wide-gap coolers. Depletion of 1.5-2.5 g/L matches the 0.6 t/h removal, and seed-wash oxalate was lowered to 5-10 g/L. Plates are SS 316L, and titanium is explicitly excluded because hot caustic attacks it.

open_questions: SOURCING LIMITATION: WebSearch was blocked again in this run (HTTP 403, 'feature not enabled for your organization'). All corrections rest on stoichiometry, mass and heat balances, and domain knowledge of standards and literature. Citations marked 'verify' (Light Metals, Hydrometallurgy, NACE SP0403 chart values, Alcoa patents and RTO/LBF reports, Alinta Pinjarra cogeneration, lime-supplier bulletins) need an SME or document check.

Evaporator economy: the stage-wise heat balance gives ~3.6-4.0 (112 t/h LP steam) for 6-effect backward feed with feed flash and 4-stage product flash. Ask a vendor (GEA, Andritz or similar Bayer FFE reference) whether a 7th effect, product flash extended to ~80 degC, or MVR on the cold effects is economic for this plant. Each would cut LP steam by ~15-30 t/h.

A11/A18 routing decision (all spent liquor heated to ~80-88 degC before evaporation): the A11 author should confirm the interchange outlet temperature and whether part of the spent liquor bypasses A11.

Digestion MP steam: A20 now designs for ~190 t/h (range 150-220), including the gibbsite dissolution endotherm per the process review. A06 must confirm with its own heat balance. If A06 adopts direct live-steam slurry heating, both steam and evaporation duty rise further.

Causticisation basis: the duty was re-based to ~25 kg Na2CO3/t on ~600 m3/h of washer 1 (+2) overflow. Carbonate generation depends strongly on bauxite organics and carbonate minerals; East Coast India-type ore sits at the low end and Darling Range-type at the high end (35-40 kg/t). Reactor temperatures and residences (R1 75-90 degC / 15-30 min; R2-R3 100-103 degC / 1.5-2 h) are still to be checked against licensor or Alcoa literature.

A08 interface: confirm washer 1 overflow C ~110-140 and washer 2 ~70-100 g/L, the ~600 m3/h side-stream draw, and the return of ~630 m3/h causticised slurry to washer 3 (with ~6.5-7.5 t/h extra solids).

Steam/power plant fuel: natural-gas cogeneration is kept. If the owner follows Indian practice (coal CFBC), A17 and A20 need coal import, a coal yard, ash handling, ESPs and a tall stack, and CO2 rises to ~0.8-1.0 t/t.

Power export of ~35-40 MW follows from the steam demand and GT size. The owner should confirm grid export rights. Otherwise smaller GTs (~20-25 MW) with more auxiliary-boiler steam reduce export at some loss of CHP efficiency.

Organics removal: confirm a rotary-kiln liquor burner with RTO versus a fluid-bed burner, wet oxidation, or omitting the LBF for low-organic East Coast ore (oxalate removal plus lime destruction only).
Liquor inventory tanks (2 x ~12,000 m3 at 80-100 degC): confirm the tank vendor's PWHT and inspection approach for large hot-caustic API 650 tanks, and the hold-up target (24-48 h).
Climate basis: tropical design wet bulb ~27-28 degC sets the cooling tower (7 cells), condenser vacuum and oxalate cooler outlet temperature. Confirm the site meteorology.
Electricity intensity (~230-250 kWh/t) is above the ~150 kWh/t average cited on Wikipedia. Verify against benchmarks; it depends on grinding, filtration type, calciner fans and the larger CW system.
